title: Evaluating a large language model-powered system for semi-structured interview in health research.
abstract: Objectives: Conducting qualitative health research with marginalized populations presents persistent challenges related to trust, disclosure, and resource constraints. Traditional in-person interviews can be costly and difficult to scale, while participants may hesitate to share sensitive experiences openly. This study assessed the feasibility and acceptability of a large language model (LLM)-powered conversational interview system as an alternative to semi-structured qualitative interviews with marginalized populations in a community-engaged health research context. Materials and Methods: We developed a web-based, LLM-powered interview system informed by a community-based participatory research framework. The system was tested with 28 caregivers of children with asthma living in subsidized housing. Postinterview evaluation sessions and researcher observation notes were analyzed to assess the system's feasibility and acceptability and identify usability, accessibility, technical, and implementation considerations. Results: Participants reported that the system was easy to use and appreciated its empathetic and nonjudgmental tone. They also rated the system positively for clarity, comfort, and accessibility, indicating that conversational artificial intelligence (AI) systems can be adapted to support qualitative data collection in underserved communities. Identified challenges i…

title: Revealing a multi-zone circumnuclear dust response in UGC 11487 through phase-resolved WISE W1--W2 diagnostics
abstract: Mid-infrared (MIR) flares trace dust reprocessing in obscured tidal disruption event (TDE) candidates, especially when the primary optical or ultraviolet flare is weak, missed, or strongly obscured. We investigate the phase-dependent W1--W2 evolution of the MIR-selected TDE candidate UGC 11487 (WTP14adeqka) and test whether its infrared behavior can be described by a single self-similar MIR response or requires a structured circumnuclear dust response. For the first time, we performed a phase-resolved analysis of the WISE/NEOWISE W1--W2 evolution of UGC 11487 (WTP14adeqka) over 2014--2024. We combined empirical W1--W2 timing, color, and flux diagnostics with phenomenological modeling and axisymmetric dust radiative-transfer calculations driven by hydrodynamically motivated fallback histories. We also constructed an aperture-matched ultraviolet-to-radio spectral energy distribution of the host galaxy. UGC 11487 exhibits a decade-long MIR flare characterized by a delayed and broader W2 response, color hysteresis, and systematic cooling from sim900 K to sim500--600 K. Observed-window positive-fluence centroids give a W2--W1 centroid offset of Δ t_ ̊m cent =224 d, corresponding to an effective differential response scale of 0.188 $, and the integrated IR energy is $(2.9--3.8) pc. The effective infrared luminosity reaches erg s -1 erg. A single fixed-color phenomenological component…

abstract: ABSTRACT This study aims to analyze the effect of earnings characteristics on the Market Value of energy sector companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) during the 2016–2025 period. This research employs a quantitative approach with a causal associative research design. The study uses secondary data obtained from companies' annual reports and year-end closing stock prices. The sample was selected using purposive sampling, resulting in 687 firm-year observations. Earnings characteristics are classified based on the relationship among Net Income, Cash Flow from Operations, and Total Accruals, which are represented by dummy variables. Data analysis was conducted using the Weighted Least Squares (WLS) regression method with the assistance of IBM SPSS Statistics. The results indicate that earnings characteristics in categories D1 and D2 have negative and statistically significant effects on Market Value compared to the reference category, with regression coefficients of -0.335 (sig. 0.028) and -0.472 (sig. 0.030), respectively. In contrast, Net Income and Cash Flow from Operations have positive and statistically significant effects on Market Value. Simultaneously, all independent variables significantly affect Market Value, with a significance level of less than 0.001. The Adjusted R-squared value of 0.267 indicates that the research model explains 26.7% of the variati…

title: The relationship between Twitter uncertainty measures and stock market returns during the COVID-19 crisis
abstract: Purpose This paper aims to explore how uncertainty captured through social media, particularly Twitter, affects global stock markets during the COVID-19 crisis. It focuses on whether the Twitter economic uncertainty (TEU) and Twitter Market Uncertainty (TMU) indices contain information that helps explain market behaviour in periods of stress. Design/methodology/approach The analysis relies on daily data from January 2007 to May 2023. This paper combines linear and nonlinear Granger causality tests (Diks and Panchenko, 2006) with the BDS nonlinearity test, and a Dynamic Conditional Correlation-Generalized Autoregressive Conditional Heteroskedasticity (DCC-GARCH) connectedness framework is used (Gabauer, 2020) to capture the dynamic transmission of volatility between Twitter-based sentiment indicators and 13 international financial markets. Findings The results highlight strong nonlinear causal effects from Twitter-based uncertainty measures to market returns. TEU and TMU indices appear to drive fluctuations in stock returns, particularly during episodes of heightened uncertainty. The DCC-GARCH analysis shows that TEU-ENG and TEU-USA act as net transmitters of volatility to markets such as Japan, Ukraine, China, Germany and even Bitcoin. Research limitations/implications As the study focuses mainly on the COVID-19 crisis, future research could extend the analysis to other stress …

title: The irrelevant responses and stock liquidity: dual validation evidence from the Chinese stock market using machine learning and large language models
abstract: Purpose As China’s capital market advances toward higher-quality development, the quality of corporate information disclosure and the transparency of managerial communication have become central concerns for investors and regulators. This study examines the relationship between managerial irrelevant responses during site visits and stock liquidity, and further investigates the underlying mechanisms through which such responses affect market liquidity. Design/methodology/approach Drawing on Q&A records from site visits to A-share listed companies in China, this study constructs a quantitative measure of managerial irrelevant responses using machine learning techniques. In addition, online scoring based on a large language model (GPT-4) is introduced as a complementary indicator. Using regression analyses, we estimate the impact of irrelevant responses on stock liquidity and conduct mechanism and subgroup analyses to ensure robustness. Findings We find that managerial irrelevant responses are significantly negatively associated with stock liquidity. Mechanism analyses suggest that increased investor attention to financial issues reflects heightened uncertainty about firms’ future prospects, thereby exacerbating illiquidity. Furthermore, evasive or ambiguous managerial communication reduces analyst coverage, deteriorates the external information environment and further suppresses …

Integrating capacity building, ethical finance and market access for smallholder empowerment: evidence from Tebar Hewan Kurban (THK) programme in Indonesia
abstract: Purpose This study examines the trilogy of community empowerment – an integrated model combining capacity building, ethical profit-sharing finance and guaranteed market access – as implemented through Indonesia’s long-running Tebar Hewan Kurban (THK) programme to enhance economic outcomes among smallholder livestock farmers. Design/methodology/approach A qualitative single-case study examines 28 years of programme experience through semi-structured interviews with 100 partner farmers, 5 farmer group leaders and 3 programme managers, complemented by document analysis and field observations. Resource dependency theory provides the primary analytical framework. Findings Case-study evidence suggests that farmers participating in the integrated THK programme experienced substantial economic improvements. Farmers reported a 269% nominal income increase, livestock mortality reduction from approximately 10 to 2%, and 94% reduced reliance on moneylenders (self-reported). Programme-reported purchasing prices consistently exceeded middleman rates by 14–28%. Five formal propositions extend resource dependency theory into pro-poor agribusiness contexts. Research limitations/implications Single-case design, purposive sampling and absence of a comparison group limit causal inference. Findings should be interpreted as suggestive, theory-building evidence rather than causal impact estimates. Fu…

title: Competitive Advertising and Market Inefficiency in the Dairy Industry: A Dynamic Bargaining Approach Using the Beggar-Thy-Neighbor Index
abstract: Abstract This study examines inefficiencies arising from advertising competition in the dairy industry, with particular emphasis on the dynamics of advertising effects, the presence of negative cross-effects, and the role of coordination mechanisms among firms. The central issue is that advertising, rather than creating net demand, often leads to business-stealing competition and beggar-thy-neighbor effects. To analyze this issue, a dynamic advertising framework is developed that incorporates advertising carryover and saturation. Within this framework, each brand’s advertising has not only a positive direct effect but also a negative effect on its competitors’ demand. The research methodology compares three decision-making scenarios – non-cooperative behavior, complete cooperation, and Nash bargaining – and introduces the Beggar-Thy-Neighbor Intensity Index as a measure of competitive inefficiency. The model is calibrated for two products, milk and cheese, and six leading brands in the Iranian market, and is estimated over the 24-month period from April 2023 to March 2025. The results indicate that, in the milk market, moving from the non-cooperative scenario to complete cooperation increases total advertising by approximately 46 %, while simultaneously reducing the Beggar-Thy-Neighbor Intensity Index from about 2.0 to 1.0; total industry profit increases by approximately 1.2 %…

title: Salmonella risks in wet market poultry systems of Bangladesh: food safety challenges, control gaps, and implications for trade and public health
abstract: Abstract Foodborne Salmonella remains a leading cause of bacterial gastroenteritis globally, and poultry products are consistently identified as a major transmission vehicle. The risk is particularly pronounced in developing countries where informal poultry marketing systems dominate and hygienic processing infrastructure remains limited. In Bangladesh, the rapidly expanding poultry sector plays a critical role in ensuring affordable protein supply and supporting economic livelihoods, yet food safety governance within wet market systems remains a significant challenge. Available evidence indicates that Salmonella contamination occurs throughout the poultry value chain in Bangladesh, with live bird markets (LBMs) serving as major contamination hotspots due to bird aggregation, on-site slaughter, poor sanitation, and lack of cold-chain management. The increasing prevalence of multidrug-resistant (MDR) Salmonella further intensifies the public health burden by increasing the risk of treatment failure and complicating antimicrobial stewardship efforts. Beyond domestic health implications, persistent food safety deficiencies may also limit Bangladesh’s ability to comply with international microbiological standards required for poultry trade, particularly regarding Hazard Analysis and Critical Control Point (HACCP) implementation, traceability, and antimicrobial resistance (AMR) moni…

title: Notified but Hazardous Cosmetics: Examining Gaps in Post-Market Legal Liability
abstract: This study examines the normative gap between the cosmetic notification mechanism, which places initial responsibility on business operators, and the civil liability regime, particularly in cases involving discrepancies in the formulation of mercury-containing cosmetics discovered after the products have obtained notification numbers and entered the market. This study employs normative legal research using statutory, conceptual, and comparative legal approaches to examine the legal framework for consumer protection in Indonesia and functionally compare it with the cosmetic supervision and liability system in South Korea. The novelty of this research lies in positioning post-notification formulation discrepancies in mercury-containing cosmetics as the central issue of legal liability, examining the integration of consumer protection law, technical supervision, and health-related criminal law, and using actual judicial cases as the basis for normative evaluation. The findings indicate that the primary problem does not stem solely from a legal vacuum, but also from the lack of clarity regarding business operators’ obligations to continuously ensure the conformity, safety, and quality of cosmetic formulations after products enter the market. Furthermore, the interaction among the relevant legal regimes remains insufficiently integrated, potentially creating legal uncertainty in det…

title: From meaning to mastery: how psychological climate fosters eco-friendly employees and proactive service stars
abstract: Purpose This study aims to investigate how hotel employees’ psychological climate is associated with two discretionary behaviours: voluntary pro-environmental behaviour (VPEB) and proactive customer service performance (PCSP). The authors developed a moderated mediation model to explain the mediating mechanism of experienced meaningfulness and the moderating role of interdependent self-construal (InterSC) in these relationships. Design/methodology/approach Data were collected in two waves from 603 employees in Macau’s four- and five-star hotels. The hypotheses were tested using PLS-SEM and conditional mediation procedures in SmartPLS 4, supplemented by a hotel-cluster-adjusted path analysis. Findings Experienced meaningfulness mediated the relationships between psychological climate and both VPEB and PCSP. Its effect size was medium for VPEB and small for PCSP. InterSC strengthened these indirect relationships by moderating the relationship between psychological climate and experienced meaningfulness. Practical implications Luxury hotels can simultaneously achieve service and sustainability excellence by fostering a supportive psychological climate. Specifically, management can implement practices that foster meaningfulness while recognising differences in employees’ relational orientations. Originality/value By applying social information processing theory, this study examines…

title: Promotion focus, growth i-deals and service creativity: a regulatory focus perspective
abstract: Purpose Given that content- and timing-based idiosyncratic deals (i-deals) are inherently heterogeneous across employees and contexts, this study shifts attention to motivation-oriented growth i-deals. Drawing on regulatory focus theory (RFT) and the ability–motivation–opportunity (AMO) model, the study seeks to examine the antecedents, outcomes, chain mediating paths and boundary conditions of growth i-deals. Design/methodology/approach Multiwave, multisource and multilevel data were collected from 600 frontline employees in 100 hotel and mall teams in China. A cross-level moderated mediation model was tested using multilevel path analysis in Mplus and 20,000 Monte Carlo simulations. Findings Four key findings have been obtained. First, promotion focus is positively associated with growth i-deals. Second, growth i-deals positively predict three AMO variables (creative self-efficacy, intrinsic motivation and perceived participation opportunity) that further promote service creativity. Third, team-level servant leadership moderates the main effect of promotion focus on growth i-deals. Finally, team-level servant leadership moderates the indirect effects of promotion focus on service creativity via the chain mediation path of growth i-deals and three AMO variables. The main effect and the indirect effects are stronger when team-level servant leadership is high rather than low. Pr…

title: Development of a specialised reproductive rheumatology consultation service: analysis of referral patterns across preconception, pregnancy, and lactation
abstract: Abstract Background Women with inflammatory rheumatic and musculoskeletal disease (iRMD) face unique challenges during preconception, pregnancy, and lactation. In 2024, a specialised consultation service was developed and implemented at the tertiary rheumatology centre of the Rheumazentrum Ruhrgebiet, Ruhr University Bochum, Herne, Germany, to address these specific needs. Methods Demographic characteristics, disease- and treatment-related data, reproductive status, referring physician, reasons for consultation, and recommendations for disease management were collected between 1 January 2024 and 3 April 2025. Results Overall, 57 patients were included; the mean age was 33.3 ± 4.4 years and the mean disease duration was 6.3 ± 4.8 years. Almost all patients (94.7%) had a confirmed diagnosis of an iRMD. 57.9% were planning a pregnancy, 40.4% were pregnant, and 1.8% were breastfeeding. At baseline, 21.8% were receiving csDMARDs and 50.9% were receiving bDMARDs. Glucocorticoid use was documented in 16.1%. Patients were referred by rheumatologists (35.7%), the in-house outpatient clinic (37.5%), general practitioners (14.3%), gynaecologists (10.7%), and the in-house inpatient clinic (1.8%). The most frequent reasons for consultation were patient concerns regarding pregnancy and medication safety. Consultation reasons differed descriptively between patients in the preconception period…

title: Mapping incivility research across financial services and other high-interaction service sectors: a bibliometric analysis of relational and thematic patterns
abstract: Purpose This study traces the evolution of incivility research across financial services and other high-interaction service sectors. It examines how the literature differs in its treatment of the forms, sources, associated outcomes, and thematic configurations of incivility. It also assesses the extent to which research reflects the transition toward digital service environments and identifies priorities for future research. Design/methodology/approach A bibliometric analysis was conducted on 1,259 documents indexed in Scopus and Web of Science, covering the period 1977–2025 and representing 517 scientific sources. Performance, citation, co-word, and thematic analyses were used to examine the field's development and compare its relational and thematic patterns across financial services, retail, hospitality, healthcare, and education. The search included incivility and adjacent forms of interpersonal mistreatment (e.g. bullying, verbal abuse) to map their relationships without treating them as conceptually equivalent. Findings The incivility literature has evolved from an early emphasis on internal workplace relationships in healthcare and education toward greater attention to customer-facing interactions in retail, hospitality, and financial services. The sectoral comparison reveals a relational divide in the literature. Retail and hospitality research primarily frames incivili…

title: Platform-integrated AI assistance and online medical consultation service quality: evidence from physician-month panel data in China
abstract: Objectives To examine the association between platform-integrated artificial intelligence (AI) assistance and online medical consultation service quality, considering consultation efficiency, conversation depth, and physician seniority. Methods We analyzed a 6-year panel of 77 physicians (5,544 physician-month observations) using fixed-effects regressions. Platform-observed online consultation service quality and efficiency are measured using entropy-weighted indices. Mediation analysis with Sobel and bootstrap tests, and conditional indirect effect models were conducted, followed by heterogeneity analysis across physician seniority. Results AI assistance use was positively associated with consultation quality (β = 0.666, p < 0.001) and consultation efficiency (β = 0.857, p = 0.002). An indirect association through efficiency was observed. This indirect association emerged only at medium and high levels of physician–patient conversation depth. Among experts, AI use was associated with efficiency and indirectly with quality; whereas among regular physicians, it was associated with quality but not efficiency. Conclusion Platform-integrated AI assistance was positively associated with online consultation service quality. These relationships vary with conversation depth and physician seniority, highlighting the importance of considering both interaction characteristics and clini…

title: Not perfect, but meeting a need: community-driven resilience in informal transport service ecosystems
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how inclusive transport provision is sustained within structurally constrained service ecosystems. Focusing on commuters with disabilities in Nigeria, it explores how strengths are mobilised across multiple actors under limited formal institutional support to sustain access and dignity. Design/methodology/approach The study draws on qualitative interviews with commuters with disabilities, informal transport providers and subject matter experts. Data were analysed using reflexive thematic analysis and abductive logic to enable iterative engagement between empirical insights and service ecosystem and strength-based perspectives. Findings Inclusion is sustained through community-driven resilience, a multi-actor, ecosystem-level process of resource mobilisation, enacted through cultural–moral activation and relational service adaptation. Cultural and moral expectations provide normative coordination, while trust, proximity and familiarity enable relational coordination and flexible service adaptation. These mechanisms enable ecosystem self-adjustment, although inclusion remains uneven and contingent. Research limitations/implications The study extends strength-based approaches from individual capabilities to ecosystem-level strength mobilisation and advances service ecosystem research by explaining how self-adjustment occurs through informal coord…

title: Digital transaction frictions in platform service ecosystems: coordination failures and consumer uncertainty
abstract: Purpose This paper aims to conceptualise Digital Transaction Frictions (DTFs) as recurrent, structurally embedded disruptions in platform-mediated service ecosystems and examines how coordination conditions shape consumer uncertainty, transaction-management effort and digital participation through service ecosystem theory and Transformative Service Research. Design/methodology/approach A qualitative study was conducted using semi-structured interviews with 40 participants, comprising 28 consumers and 12 organisational experts. Data were analysed through an abductive, Gioia-informed approach. Findings The findings identify three analytical elements: two ecosystem-level conditions, temporal drift and fragmented accountability and one consumer-level process, adaptive uncertainty. Together, these elements suggest how recurring instability in distributed service arrangements may shift uncertainty and transaction-management work onto consumers. Practical implications The findings suggest that platform operators and logistics partners could complement firm-level monitoring with shared diagnostics across the transaction pathway. Customer experience managers could also treat recurring friction as a signal of systemic misalignment rather than an isolated complaint. Originality/value The study positions DTFs as a complementary ecosystem-level construct that links coordination conditions w…

title: The Difficulties Pre-Service Mathematics Teachers Encounter in Their Statistical Investigations and the Role of Feedback
abstract: Conducting a successful statistical investigation process is considered an important dimension for data-driven reasoning and fundamental statistical skills. Pre-service middle school mathematics teachers need opportunities to engage in statistical investigations and develop the competencies required to implement this process in their future classrooms. However, pre-service mathematics teachers may encounter various challenges when conducting statistical investigations. This study aimed to examine how pre-service middle school mathematics teachers conduct statistical investigations and to identify the phases of this process in which feedback was most effective. The participants were 60 pre-service middle school mathematics teachers (20 groups) selected through convenience sampling. Data sources included pre-service teachers’ initial presentations of their statistical investigations, their final reports revised following feedback, and field notes taken by the researcher during their presentations. The data were analyzed using content analysis. The findings indicated that pre-service teachers experienced difficulties in formulating statistical investigative questions during the problem phase of the statistical investigation process, determining the sampling procedures and data collection tools during the plan phase, selecting analysis methods and visualization tools appropriate to…

title: Adult Care in a Pediatric Hospital: Patterns and Implications of an Internal Medicine Consult Service at a Children’s Hospital
abstract: OBJECTIVE Adults with childhood-onset conditions are increasingly admitted to children’s hospitals, yet many pediatric systems lack the infrastructure and expertise to manage adult-related medical needs. One approach to bridge this gap is the use of an adult medicine consult service. We aim to describe the demographics, clinical complexity, and consultation patterns of patients admitted to a freestanding children’s hospital and evaluated by an adult medicine consult service, which is a current gap in the literature. PATIENTS AND METHODS A retrospective descriptive cohort study was performed of admitted patients with a Hospital Medicine Adult Care (HMAC) service consult from July 2014 through June 2023. RESULTS Annual adult admissions increased over the study period, from 7.4% to 10.2% of all admissions. HMAC consulted on 1666 admissions for 1008 unique patients (median age, 27 years [range, 14–71 years]). The most frequent reasons for consult were venous thromboembolism prophylaxis (33.7%), age older than 25 years (21.2%), transition of care (7.6%), and hypertension (7.6%). HMAC physicians addressed a mean of 5.5 diagnoses per encounter. Patients averaged 3.6 admissions (range, 1–22) and 4.9 comorbidities (range, 0–21) each. title: Constructing inclusion in English-language government service pathways: a multimodal discourse analysis of interpretability for non-native users
abstract: Abstract English-language government websites are increasingly used to provide public-service information to international, migrant and multilingual users. However, access has often been approached from a technical perspective rather than through a discursive and multimodal approach. This article examines how inclusion is constructed in selected English-language government service pathways in Morocco, Portugal and Spain. Adopting a qualitative comparative design, it analyses six official pathways, one immigration or residency-related pathway and one criminal-record certificate pathway from each context, through multimodal discourse analysis and digital genre analysis. The analysis focuses on linguistic resources such as modality, agency, nominalisation and definitional support, together with procedural staging, visual hierarchy, salience, framing, navigation and language continuity across pathway layers. The findings show that potential interpretability is supported when procedural actions, institutional responsibilities, visual organisation and navigational transitions are made explicit and mutually reinforcing. It is constrained when guidance is document-heavy, administratively dense, fragmented across platforms or only partially mediated through English. The article conceptualises inclusion as multimodal interpretability: the extent to which institutional procedures are pote…

title: Examining the influence of the treating customers fairly concept on consumers’ purchase intention for non-life insurance products
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine the influence of Treating Customers Fairly (TCF) on consumers’ purchase intention for non-life insurance products in South Africa. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative, cross-sectional research design was used, using an online survey distributed through social media platforms. A total of 241 valid responses were analysed using structural equation modelling (SEM). Findings The study revealed contrasting effects of TCF standards on non-life insurance purchase intentions. Consumer willingness to acquire supplementary coverage increased by the first three TCF principles: organisational culture and governance structures, appropriateness of product offerings, and transparency in communications. These principles reduce perceived risk and uncertainty, thereby enhancing their confidence and willingness to proceed with a purchase. In doing so, they create favourable conditions that actively encourage consumers to make purchase decisions. Conversely, purchase intentions diminished when influenced by the following principles: advisory quality concerns, service delivery expectations, and post-purchase accessibility limitations. While these principles are essential, the observed decline in purchase intentions may potentially be explained by slower decision-making processes, increased perceived costs or psychological resistance arising from their strin…

title: Chemogenetics reveals a surprising role for GPR18 signaling in immunometabolic regulation of β cell activity
abstract: Pancreatic islet macrophages are important immunometabolic regulators of β cell function, particularly in obesity-associated type 2 diabetes. Previous studies have established that pancreatic islet macrophages communicate with β cells through either the release of cytokines and growth factors, or direct cell–cell contact. In this issue of the JCI , Singh et al. used chemogenetics to identify a Gq/AMPK pathway that remodels sphingolipid metabolism. This pathway links macrophages to β cells through a CD36-dependent mechanism that reduces insulin secretion. Surprisingly, the orphan GPCR GPR18 was identified as the receptor that engages this pathway. These findings expand our understanding in macrophage–β cell communication and identify GPR18 as a potential therapeutic target for type 2 diabetes.

title: Therapeutic mechanisms of art therapy in improving self-regulation in children with ADHD: a systematic review and integrated conceptual framework
abstract: Background Art therapy has been used as a non-pharmacological intervention for children with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), with previous studies reporting potentially beneficial outcomes across emotional, behavioral, attentional, and self-regulatory domains. However, comparatively little is known about the therapeutic processes through which participation in art therapy may contribute to self-regulation-related change. Objective This systematic review aimed to synthesize empirical evidence on art therapy interventions for children with ADHD, identify recurring candidate therapeutic processes associated with self-regulation-related outcomes, and integrate these processes into a preliminary hypothesis-generating conceptual framework. Methods Following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 guidelines, four electronic databases—PubMed, Scopus, the Web of Science, and PsycINFO—were systematically searched for studies published between January 2000 and May 2026. The final database search was conducted on 31 May 2026. In total, 13 eligible studies were included and synthesized using a qualitative thematic approach. Evidence related to candidate therapeutic processes was distinguished according to whether it was directly measured, explicitly reported or interpreted by the original study authors, or inferred during the re…

title: Hydrogen Bond Network Anchoring and Oxygen Vacancy Synergistic Regulation for High-Performance Aqueous Zinc−Ion Batteries
abstract: Abstract α-MnO2 possesses a unique 2 × 2 tunneling crystal structure and offers outstanding advantages such as high specific capacity and high operating voltage, making it a hot topic in research on cathode materials for aqueous zinc−ion batteries. However, its poor structural stability and intrinsic conductivity severely limit its electrochemical performance. Based on this, this study innovatively incorporated lightweight NH4+ into α-MnO2 to prepare NMO-x materials with different NH4+ doping levels. The results indicate that the N─H bonds in NH4+ form a hydrogen-bond network (N─H···O) with the framework oxygen atoms, effectively anchoring NH4+ and shielding the electrostatic repulsion between Zn2+ and O. Simultaneously, this induces the formation of oxygen vacancies, which suppress the Jahn−Teller distortion of Mn3+ and Mn dissolution, thereby significantly enhancing structural stability and ionic migration kinetics. Consequently, the optimized NMO-2 cathode material maintains excellent rate performance of 150 mAh g−1 even at a high current density of 5.0 A g−1, and retains a high capacity retention of 87% after 1000 cycles at a current density of 1.0 A g−1. This work has advanced research on the modification of MnO2 cathode materials and provided new insights for the design of high-performance aqueous zinc−ion battery cathode materials.

title: METTL8 orchestrates TFH cell differentiation through m³C-mediated TCF1 regulation in infection and cancer models
abstract: T follicular helper (T FH ) cells are critical for humoral immunity against infections and correlate with immunotherapy efficacy, whereas immune checkpoint inhibitor therapy can drive their aberrant expansion, underscoring the need to understand the regulators controlling T FH cell fate. However, the epitranscriptomic regulation of their differentiation remains poorly understood. Here, we identify the 3-methylcytosine (m³C) methyltransferase METTL8 as a key regulator of T FH cell differentiation in both viral infection and cancer. METTL8 was preferentially expressed in CXCL13 hi T FH cells, and its deficiency impaired T FH differentiation and germinal center responses in the lymphocytic choriomeningitis virus infection model and following anti–PD-1 immunotherapy in tumor models. Mechanistically, METTL8 exerted dual functions: it bound and stabilized Tcf7 mRNA through m³C modification, and it interacted with TCF1 protein to regulate chromatin accessibility and 3D genome organization at key T FH -associated loci, including Cxcr5 and Il6ra . Notably, ginkgolic acid treatment suppressed T FH responses without compromising the antitumor efficacy of anti–PD-1 therapy, an effect associated with METTL8. Collectively, our findings identify METTL8 as an epitranscriptomic regulator linked to RNA modification, TCF1-associated transcriptional control, and chromatin architecture during T FH …

A hierarchical adaptive Fourier-feature physics-informed neural network for radio-frequency capacitively coupled plasma discharges
abstract: Abstract Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) are difficult to train for radio-frequency capacitively coupled plasma fluid-Poisson systems because missing initial conditions, steep sheath gradients, and strongly imbalanced residuals can lead to unstable or nonunique reconstructions. We propose a Hierarchical Adaptive Fourier-feature PINN (HA-FPINN) for such coupled plasma models. The method combines Fourier feature mapping to improve the representation of small-scale sheath structures, sparse physical anchors to provide interior constraints, and a two-level adaptive weighting scheme to balance the PDE, boundary, and anchor losses as well as individual equation residuals. The framework is tested on an 8-equation helium discharge model and a 23-equation electronegative Ar / O 2 model. In the helium case, HA-FPINN reconstructs the space-time evolution of the main physical variables with 1 % anchors and converges for all tested network architectures, with convergence times of 110 – 246 s. In the Ar / O 2 case, HA-FPINN achieves stable reconstruction with 5 % anchors, whereas the non-adaptive FPINN and standard PINN fail to converge under the same setting. The best performance in both systems is obtained at the tested Fourier frequency parameter σ = 2.20 . Noise-injection tests show that HA-FPINN maintains the lowest reconstruction error in the helium case and preserves the main…

title: Political transactions, company filings, and the STOCK act
abstract: Purpose This paper aims to investigate whether the timing of US politicians’ equity transactions around corporate disclosures helps identify trades associated with abnormal returns. This paper examines whether political trading is more informative around specific types of corporate filings and whether the predictive value of such trading varies across periods of macroeconomic disruption and legislative reform. Design/methodology/approach Using disclosed congressional transactions from 2004 to 2021, the authors estimate trade-level models with politician, firm and year fixed effects. They compare purchases made within seven calendar days before key corporate filings (Forms 8-K, 10-K and 10-Q) and evaluate subsequent abnormal returns over a three-day window. They then consider all eligible Form 8-K filing dates and test whether political trading imbalances predict abnormal returns across different economic states and regulatory changes, especially before and after the passage of the STOCK Act. Findings This paper yields three main findings. First, purchases made within seven calendar days before a Form 8-K filing outperform the same politician’s other purchases by approximately 10 basis points over a three-day window. No comparable return effect is observed for purchases preceding Form 10-K or 10-Q filings. Second, political trading imbalances positively predict abnormal returns …

title: Coupled Regulation of Oxygen-Vacancy-Modified Near-Surface Structure and Interfacial Stability for High-Performance Li-Rich Mn-Based Cathodes
abstract: Abstract Li-rich Mn-based layered oxides (LRMOs) are prospective next-generation cathodes, delivering high specific capacities via coupled cationic and anionic redox. However, sluggish reaction kinetics, irreversible oxygen loss, and progressive interfacial structural degradation limit the practical application of LRMOs. Herein, a coupled strategy for regulating the near-surface structure and interfacial stability is developed using ammonium titanyl oxalate (ATO) as a multifunctional precursor. During thermal treatment, an approximately 10 nm Li2TiO3 coating layer forms to stabilize the cathode interface. Meanwhile, reducing gases released from precursor decomposition induce oxygen vacancy formation, whereas Ti incorporation suppresses excessive transition-metal (TM) reduction in the near-surface region, thereby alleviating the associated increase in Mn3+ content and Jahn–Teller distortion. Moreover, the coupled Ti and oxygen vacancy configuration enhances anionic redox reversibility, stabilizes the near-surface oxygen framework, and lowers the Li+ migration barrier, thereby improving Li+ transport and structural stability. The optimized ATO-2% cathode achieves an average initial Coulombic efficiency (ICE) of 90.07% at 0.1 C and a capacity retention of 88.1% after 300 cycles at 1 C. This work establishes a coupled regulation strategy for the oxygen vacancy-modified near-surface…

title: Indonesian Diplomacy in Europe: Navigating the EU Deforestation Regulation Through Roles, Scripts, and Discretion
abstract: Abstract Diplomatic practice remains underexplored in International Relations, particularly from the perspective of Global South diplomats. This study investigates how Indonesian diplomats in Europe navigate the EU Deforestation Regulation, focusing on how they manage information, interpret home-country directives, and exercise discretion. Drawing on International Practice Theory and Street-Level Bureaucracy, the analysis shows that diplomats enact layered performances across ranks, shifting between roles as bureaucrats, government representatives, and knowledge producers. Junior diplomats emphasize procedural responsibilities, while mid- and senior-level officials engage in mediation, informal lobbying, and coalition-building. Ambassadors coordinate these approaches by framing Indonesia’s position in high-level forums and ensuring internal coherence. Discretion operates not as defiance, but as strategic framing and timing within institutional constraints. The study introduces a layered and adaptive practice of diplomacy by showing how Indonesian diplomats reconcile Indonesia’s policy, development priorities, and economic interests with evolving global sustainability governance. These findings highlight the need for strengthened analytical capacity, formal recognition of discretionary competence, and more inclusive sustainability governance arrangements.

title: Multi-objective optimization of pixelated frequency selective surface radar absorbing composite using pareto-based genetic algorithm
abstract: Abstract This study proposes and experimentally validates a thin laminated pixelated frequency selective surface (FSS) radar absorbing structure (RAS) optimized using a Pareto-based genetic algorithm The unit cell was discretized into a 20 × 20 binary grid with octagonal symmetry to promote polarization-insensitive behavior. The binary pixel topology was optimized together with continuous design variables, including pixel length, sheet resistance, and second dielectric-layer thickness. Two absorption-coverage metrics were used in the optimization: X-band coverage as the primary target-band requirement and broadband coverage as the bandwidth-extension metric. The selected design had a pixel length of 1.25 mm, a sheet resistance of 45.6 Ω sq −1 , and a second dielectric-layer thickness of 2.31 mm, providing simulated absorption above 90% over 8.12–18.00 GHz. The fabricated specimen had a total thickness of 2.56 mm and an areal density of 3.60 kg m −2 . Free-space Thru–Reflect–Line-calibrated measurements showed absorption above 90% over 8.37–16.90 GHz for 0° polarization and 8.40–16.01 GHz for 90° polarization. The measured minimum reflection losses were −15.12 dB at 10.66 GHz and −15.56 dB at 10.77 GHz for 0° and 90° polarizations, respectively. A refined sheet-resistance sweep and 25-point sheet-resistance mapping indicated that the simulation–measurement discrepancy was mainly…

title: Analyzing the nexus between sustainability disclosure regulation and capital allocation efficacy: decoding the channel effects of financial reporting quality
abstract: Purpose Building on the global surge in sustainability legislation, this study aims to examine the nexus between environmental, social and governance (ESG) reporting laws and the capital allocation efficacy (CPAE) of regulated firms. The study also unveils the mediating role of financial reporting quality in transmitting the effect of sustainability regulation on CPAE. Design/methodology/approach Indian regulators have enforced the “Business responsibility and sustainability reporting” (BRSR) framework, which serves as an external shock for the research design. Accordingly, a sample of 976 listed companies from 2019 to 2025 is analyzed using a quasi-natural experiment approach with a difference-in-differences research design. The study also performs several robustness tests, including propensity score matching, a placebo test and alternative measurements of key variables. Findings The findings reveal a significant positive impact of ESG regulation on CPAE through the mediating role of improved financial reporting quality. The results suggest that ESG legislation enhances the quality and reliability of financial disclosures, reduces information asymmetry and thereby improves CPAE. Moreover, the findings indicate that the positive effect of ESG statutes is more pronounced among emission-intensive sectors. Research limitations/implications Given the limited research on the financi…

title: Fractional-order grey forecasting framework for cross-regional air quality early warning
abstract: Purpose This study develops an interpretable grey forecasting framework under limited information conditions. The framework supports air quality early warning across regions. It focuses on disturbed annual Air Quality Composite Index (AQCI) sequences and heterogeneous warning pressure across cities. Design/methodology/approach This study proposes S-HFGM(1,N), a Hausdorff fractional multivariable grey model with a single indicator buffer. The model integrates target sequence buffering, Hausdorff fractional accumulation and multivariable grey modelling. The framework uses AQCI association pressure for city screening and selects socioeconomic drivers. After validation, Monte Carlo simulations based on residuals quantify uncertainty. Warnings are then interpreted for specific pollutants. The application covers the Beijing–Tianjin–Hebei region. It uses observations from 2013–2022 for training and 2023–2024 for validation. The validated model produces projections for 2025–2030. Findings The model achieves an average validation mean absolute percentage error of 3.6861%, outperforming selected grey forecasting benchmarks. The baseline projections show different trends under gradual structural evolution. Beijing faces slight upward pressure. By contrast, Shijiazhuang and Tangshan continue improving. Handan and Xingtai follow a relatively stable trajectory despite persistent pressure. Th…

title: Forecasting primary healthcare resources in China using a grey convolutional multivariate self-memory combination model GMC-SM(1,n)
abstract: Purpose China is entering a moderately aging society, in which the demand for primary healthcare resources is characterized by small samples, multiple influencing factors and strong temporal dependence. This study proposes a novel grey forecasting approach to improve prediction accuracy and stability for primary healthcare resource demand under incomplete information. Design/methodology/approach Drawing on empirical data for primary healthcare institutions and beds in China, this study employs grey relational analysis to identify key driving variables and develops a grey convolutional multivariate self-memory combination model, denoted as GMC-SM(1,n), by integrating grey system theory with the self-memory principle and compares it with classical grey prediction models. Findings The proposed GMC-SM(1,n) model exhibits superior accuracy, with fitting and prediction MAPEs of 1.02% and 0.28% for institutions, and 1.93% and 0.82% for beds. The model also achieves lower root mean square error, mean absolute error and standard deviation of errors (SD) than comparative models, demonstrating strong robustness and an enhanced ability to capture multivariable coupling and temporal dependence with small samples. Practical implications The results reliably support dynamic resource allocation and long-term planning under population aging, offering practical reference value for policymakers. …

Explainable AI for tail-risk forecasting in cryptocurrencies: evidence from green and energy-intensive assets for risk-aware investment decisions
abstract: Purpose This study aims to develop an explainable deep learning framework for forecasting tail risk and volatility in cryptocurrency markets, with a particular focus on differences between energy-intensive and ESG-oriented digital assets. It aims to assess how volatility dynamics and downside risk exposure vary across environmental profiles and market regimes and how these differences can inform risk-aware investment decisions. Design/methodology/approach The proposed framework uses a quantile long short-term memory model to estimate predictive quantiles and Conditional Value at Risk (CVaR), enabling the modeling of asymmetric, fat-tailed and regime-dependent risks. The analysis focuses on four cryptocurrencies – Bitcoin and Litecoin (energy-intensive) and Algorand and Chia (lower-energy alternatives). The model integrates SHapley Additive exPlanations-based explainability and a regime classification (calm vs stress). Robustness is assessed using 20-, 40- and 60-day rolling evaluation windows, while predictive performance is evaluated through coverage rates, hit ratios and Kupiec and Christoffersen back testing procedures. Findings The results reveal substantial heterogeneity across the four cryptocurrencies rather than a uniform green-versus-energy-intensive ranking. Chia records the lowest Q50 root mean squared error (0.00149) and mean absolute error (MAE) (0.00119), whereas …

title: Forecasting endodontic outcomes from intraoral radiographs using a deep convolutional neural network
Applying economics-guided machine learning models to soybean oil price forecast
abstract: Purpose Forecasting soybean oil prices is difficult because price movements emerge from interacting supply, demand, inventory, trade and macro-financial forces, especially in import-dependent markets where external shocks can rapidly alter conditions. This study develops a comparative framework for integrating economic theory into physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) for soybean oil price forecasting. Design/methodology/approach These constraints are examined through five artificial neural network (ANN)-based models: a baseline ANN, PINN-A, PINN-B, PINN-C and a unified PINN-ABC model, evaluated not only for predictive performance but also for forecast robustness, interpretability and structural consistency. Findings Embedding economic theory into PINNs improves forecasting, but its effectiveness depends on the type of constraint imposed. Constraints that directly encode economically interpretable directional relationships contribute most, while combining multiple constraints creates trade-offs between structural richness and optimisation complexity. Research limitations/implications Economics-guided PINNs offer a promising bridge between flexible neural forecasting and theory-consistent commodity market analysis, supporting forecasts that are accurate, economically credible and decision-relevant. Originality/value Rather than treating forecasting as a purely data-driven tas…

title: Explainable Spatiotemporal Deep Learning for Extreme Rainfall Prediction Using Multi-Station Climate Data in Indonesia
abstract: Extreme rainfall prediction remains an important challenge for hydrometeorological disaster mitigation in Indonesia, where climate conditions and rainfall distributions vary considerably. This study evaluates four machine-learning models—Logistic Regression, Random Forest, HistGradientBoosting, and XGBoost—for classifying extreme rainfall events using multi-station daily climate data. The Climate Data Daily IDN dataset contains 589,265 observations from 173 stations over 2010–2020. Extreme events are defined using station-specific 95th-percentile (P95) thresholds calculated from the training data. A chronological split is used: 2010–2017 for training, 2018–2019 for validation, and 2020 for testing. Performance is assessed using accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, ROC-AUC, and PR-AUC. On the test set, XGBoost achieves 86.24% accuracy, an F1-score of 0.2304, ROC-AUC of 0.7346, and PR-AUC of 0.1689, whereas Logistic Regression obtains the highest recall (39.19%). SHAP analysis of XGBoost identifies previous-day relative humidity as the feature with the highest mean absolute SHAP value (0.4097), followed by previous-day rainfall (0.1661). These results constitute an explainable machine-learning baseline; no deep-learning architecture or explicit inter-station spatial relationship is evaluated in this study. The limited precision and recall indicate that the evaluated models are …

A novel framework for rapid short-term prediction of ship motions using an enhanced gradient boosting decision tree with dynamical evolution sequence
abstract: Abstract Accurate short-term prediction of ship motions is essential for selecting operational areas and time windows, which are critical for maritime safety and operational efficiency. Traditional physics-based methods provide high accuracy but are computationally expensive, limiting their use in onboard applications. To address this challenge, this study proposes a rapid short-term prediction method for ship motions. The method utilizes a dynamical evolution sequence (DES) to generate a more uniform sample set, replacing the conventional Latin hypercube sampling (LHS) in the gradient boosting decision tree (GBDT), thus enhancing model accuracy through improved input sampling. First, four test functions are used to validate and compare the original and improved GBDT models. Results show that the DES-based GBDT model consistently outperforms the traditional LHS-based GBDT model across all functions. Based on this, the enhanced model is used to develop a comprehensive set of surrogate models for all hydrodynamic coefficients required for six-degree-of-freedom (6-DOF) motion prediction, including added mass, radiation damping, and wave excitation force, comprising 84 submodels in total. This innovation reduces computation time from hours to approximately 10 s per operating condition. The feasibility of the proposed method is validated under two loading conditions for an offshore …

title: Advances in prediction of drug-target thermodynamics and kinetics: from molecular simulations to artificial intelligence
abstract: In the drug discovery field, drug affinity has long been considered the gold standard for designing small compounds with therapeutic activity. However, since the beginning of the 21st century, kinetic parameters, which are directly related to compound efficacy, have increasingly been recognized as central to the rational design of new drugs. However, such data are scarce, while the experimental determination of the association and dissociation rate constants, k on and k off , is costly and time-consuming. Molecular simulations, such as Molecular Dynamics (MD) calculations have been proposed to predict those kinetic constants, despite known limitations. With the rapid development of AI-based tools, researchers are now proposing advanced methodologies that leverage both data-driven learning from existing datasets and physics-based modelling through MD simulations. This review presents a critical overview of MD-based approaches for estimating protein-ligand binding free energies and rate constants. It then examines data-driven prediction methods and ML-assisted molecular simulations, with particular attention to validation and current limitations. Finally, it discusses the crucial need for new data with respect to the FAIR principles and methodological developments needed to further improve prediction quality.

title: An innovative GUI toolset for quick prediction of micro-scale RVE mechanical properties
abstract: Purpose The Micro-scale Representative Volume Element (RVE) Tool (MRT) and Quick Tool Model (QTM) were developed to rapidly and accurately analyze the effective elastic properties of microscale RVEs. Python code was developed to provide a simple and intuitive user interface. The effective elastic properties of composites with different fiber volume fractions (\(V_f\)) were calculated using the generated microscale models and compared with experimental results. The results demonstrated that the QTM significantly reduces computational time compared with the homogenization-based MRT model. Design/methodology/approach RVE, micro-scale, composite structure, structural analysis, homogenization, constitutive modeling. Findings The results demonstrate that the proposed MRT and QTM tools can accurately and rapidly predict the effective elastic properties of micro-scale RVEs. The QTM significantly reduces computational time compared to full homogenization-based FE models while maintaining high accuracy. Validation against experimental data and literature showed excellent agreement. Furthermore, parametric studies revealed that the random distribution of fibers, fiber shape deformation (up to ±15%), and rotation angles significantly influence the transverse elastic moduli and Poisson's ratios, whereas the longitudinal modulus (E1) remains relatively stable. The successful completion of 14…

title: Wear Prediction of Polymer Bearings for Industrial Booms
abstract: A simplified mathematical model was developed to estimate wear in polymer bearings for industrial boom systems under sliding conditions. Based on the Archard wear equation, the approach considers load and sliding distance as the primary input parameters. The results indicate that the model is suitable for describing the steady-state wear behaviour of the investigated tribosystem, while further refinements are required to accurately capture the running-in phase.

title: Risk factors and logistic regression-based nomogram prediction model for diabetic retinopathy in type 2 diabetes mellitus
abstract: Introduction Diabetic Retinopathy (DR) is a major cause of irreversible vision loss in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus (T2DM). Early identification of high-risk patients using readily available clinical tools is crucial. This study aimed to analyze risk factors for DR in T2DM patients and develop a practical nomogram prediction model based on common clinical and laboratory parameters. Methods A retrospective study was conducted on 379 T2DM patients (64 with DR) from a single center. LASSO regression (with the penalty λ chosen by the one-standard-error rule, λ.1se) was used for variable selection; the selected variables were entered into multivariable logistic regression and only those that remained independently significant were retained to construct the nomogram. Model performance was evaluated by discrimination (Area Under the Curve, AUC), calibration (Hosmer-Lemeshow test), and clinical utility (Decision Curve Analysis). Only internal validation (1000-sample bootstrapping) was performed; no external validation cohort was available. Results Five independent risk factors were identified: longer disease duration (OR = 1.27 per year), hypertension (OR = 3.56), elevated fasting plasma glucose (OR = 1.86 per mmol/L), higher glycated hemoglobin (OR = 6.38 per %), and hypertriglyceridemia (triglycerides ≥1.7 mmol/L, OR = 6.37). The nomogram showed good discrimination (AUC 0.922, 95% CI 0.8…

UDR-PREDICT: a malignancy prediction model for rapid diagnostic units
abstract: Abstract Objectives Hospital rapid diagnostic units (RDUs) assess outpatients with suspected serious disease, yet no validated tool estimates malignancy risk at the first RDU visit. We developed and internally validated UDR-PREDICT, a logistic prediction model with a derived integer score. Methods Retrospective analysis of a prospectively maintained registry of first RDU visits (2022–2025) in a Spanish tertiary hospital. The outcome was a final diagnosis of solid or haematologic malignancy. Candidate predictors available at referral were selected by least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO), refitted by logistic regression and shrunk. An integer score was derived with the Framingham points method. Both were validated by bootstrapping the full procedure and by internal–external cross-validation across calendar periods; 2025 served as an exploratory temporal test. Results Of 975 analysable patients, 147 (15.1 %) had malignancy. The model retained age, sex, abdominal mass, lymphadenopathy, pulmonary nodule and bone lesions. Optimism-corrected area under the curve (AUC) was 0.719 for the model and 0.721 for the score (calibration slopes 0.857 and 0.859). Across periods the pooled AUC was 0.693 (95 % CI 0.641–0.741) and the pooled calibration slope 0.737 (0.550–0.924). In 2025 (19 events) the AUC was 0.731 (0.618–0.826). Predicted risk rose from 3.9 % at 0 points to 64…

Factors associated with IgG antibody response following inactivated COVID-19 vaccination in children aged 3-17 years
abstract: Background The factors affecting the vaccine-induced humoral immune response in children's groups have not been fully clarified. This study takes COVID-19 vaccination as a model to determine the factors related to the IgG seropositivity of children aged 3 to 17 after vaccination with inactivated COVID-19 vaccine. Methods This single-center retrospective study included 1,706 children aged 3 to 17 who were vaccinated with at least one dose of inactivated whole virus COVID-19 vaccine between July 2021 and November 2022 (306 with one dose, 1,400 with two doses). The colloidal gold method was used to qualitatively evaluate the IgG antibody response. Data such as demographic characteristics, disease after vaccination, sports activities during vaccination, underlying diseases, medication, vitamin D supplementation and adverse reactions were collected through structured questionnaires. Univariate and multivariate logistic regression were used to identify factors related to seroconversion, and subgroup analysis was carried out on the two groups by age. Results In the adjusted two-dose cohort, compared with children aged 3–5 years, those aged 6–12 years (OR = 0.67, 95% CI 0.52–0.87) and 13–17 years (OR = 0.12, 95% CI 0.07–0.21) had lower odds of seroconversion. Post-vaccination illness (OR = 3.94, 95% CI 2.62–5.91), vitamin D supplementation (OR = 1.28, 95% CI 1.01–1.62), and adverse rea…

Soybean Response to Ultra-low Dicamba Exposure under Tropical Field Conditions: Effect of Application Timing and Tissue Dicamba Accumulation
abstract: Abstract Dicamba is an important tool for broadleaf weed management, but non-dicamba-tolerant soybean may be unintentionally exposed to ultra-low doses in tropical production systems where tolerant and non-tolerant cultivars coexist. This study evaluated the response of non-tolerant soybean to ultra-low dicamba doses (0–4.8 g ae ha–1) applied at four vegetative stages (pre-sowing, V1, V3, and V6) across five major soybean-producing regions of Brazil. Plant stand was not affected by dicamba exposure. Soybean injury increased with dose and growth stage, remaining below 2% in pre-sowing applications but reaching 50–63% at V3 and V6 at the highest dose. Yield responses followed the same trend: pre-sowing and V1 applications maintained yields similar to the check plots, whereas V6 was the most sensitive stage, with yield losses of 18 and 35% at 2.4 and 4.8 g ae ha–1, respectively. Tissue dicamba concentrations ranged from less than 8.7 ng g–1 in pre-sowing applications to 115 ng g–1 at V6 and were positively associated with injury (R2 = 0.61). Yield reductions were observed primarily at injury levels above approximately 30–40% or at tissue dicamba concentrations above 70–100 ng g–1. Overall, soybean sensitivity was influenced by developmental stage and tissue dicamba accumulation, in addition to nominal exposure dose alone. These findings provide a mechanistic framework for understa…

Procedure optimization and performance study of GTAW-WAAM ER2594 duplex stainless steel based on response surface methodology
abstract: Purpose The purpose of this study is to optimize gas tungsten arc welding (GTAW)-based wire arc additive manufacturing (WAAM) for fabricating ER2594 duplex stainless steel (DSS) thin-walled components and to correlate the resulting microstructures and mechanical properties with the optimized processing conditions. Design/methodology/approach Response surface methodology (RSM) with a three-factor, five-level experimental design was used to quantify the effects of welding current, welding speed and wire-feed speed on bead geometry (bead width and shape factor) and to develop a predictive model. Thin-walled components were then fabricated under the optimized parameters, followed by EBSD characterization of phase constitution and texture and room-temperature tensile testing. Findings Under the optimized parameters, thin-walled components were deposited uniformly with a machinable fraction > 90%. EBSD confirmed a ferrite–austenite duplex structure (43.6% ferrite and 56.4% austenite) with a pronounced < 001>//BD ferrite fiber texture and a more dispersed austenite texture. The tensile properties averaged 596.2 MPa in yield strength, 732.9 MPa in ultimate tensile strength and 39.3% in total elongation, indicating a favorable strength–ductility balance. Originality/value This work addresses the need for process optimization in GTAW-WAAM of ER2594 DSS, whose thin-wall formabili…

Understanding Consumer Responses to Sustainable Last-Mile Delivery: A Stimulus–Organism–Response Perspective from Vietnam
abstract: The article explores how perceived sustainability (PS) and perceived cost (PC) impact consumer attitudes (AT) and behaviors (IU) toward sustainable last-mile delivery modes (DM) in Vietnam’s e-commerce market, using the stimulus–organism–response (S-O-R) model. Data was collected through an online survey from e-commerce consumers in Vietnam. Exploratory factor analysis (EFA), confirmatory factor analysis (CFA), and partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) were conducted employing RStudio 4 and SmartPLS 4. The results demonstrate PS positively affects AT, whereas PC influences it negatively. Additionally, AT influences IU and actual choice of sustainable delivery methods. Nevertheless, the findings show an insignificant positive relationship between intention and behavior, emphasizing the gap between intention and behavior. The results suggest useful insights for Vietnamese business leaders and public officials. Companies may encourage green delivery methods by improving eco-friendly service awareness and presenting sustainable motives, whilst policymakers may reinforce such initiatives via facilities, legislation, and recognition programs. The article fosters the eco-friendly logistics operation in online retail literature through combining phycological and behavioral determinants in S-O-R framework. The study specifically underlines the gap between intentio…

title: Tracing emotion from movement to image: response profiles across expressive gestures and paintings
abstract: Introduction Emotional meaning can be inferred from facial expressions, body movements, and the static outcomes of expressive actions. We examined whether emotion-attribution profiles correspond across standardized facial expressions, videos of expressive painting movements, and the paintings produced by those movements. Methods One hundred adults rated each stimulus on seven emotion categories. Linear mixed-effects models assessed differentiation between the validated or artist-intended emotion and the remaining categories, whereas representational similarity analyses examined cross-format correspondence. Results Differentiation was strong for standardized facial expressions and was also evident for paintings and videos, although it was greater for paintings than for videos, with intended–non-intended differences of 4.06 and 2.21 points, respectively. Emotion-attribution profiles were more similar for matched than non-matched emotion pairs across all modality comparisons, with matched-minus-non-matched contrasts ranging from 0.32 to 0.57. Painting–Video correspondence was particularly strong for anger and joy and weaker for sadness, whose video showed a less selective attribution profile. Anger also showed the most consistent individual-level correspondence despite being associated with the most spatially constrained and least dynamic painting gesture. Discussion These proof-o…

title: Neurocognitive profiles structure heterogeneous treatment response to bumetanide in neurodevelopmental disorders: secondary analysis of a multiple baseline single-case experimental design
Identifiability and scaling limits of field sap-flow phenotyping: a two-season case study of the vapour pressure deficit response in maize and grain sorghum
abstract: The limited-transpiration phenotype, a plateau in transpiration above a threshold vapour pressure deficit (VPD), is invoked to explain why grain sorghum conserves soil water better than maize. Most evidence comes from controlled environments, where VPD is imposed, and radiation is held constant. We treat a two-season field dataset as a methodological case study and ask whether such a threshold is identifiable from stem heat balance records. We analysed sap-flow records from 37 plants (18 in 2024, 19 in 2025) of one sorghum hybrid (rainfed) and one maize hybrid (rainfed and irrigated). The records cover a dry and a wet postflowering season in the Pannonian Basin, Hungary. Management differed between seasons, so inference is restricted to contrasts within seasons. Midday flux (09:00 to 17:00) from measured records only was normalised within plant and season and modelled against daily maximum VPD, adjusted for window day and clearness index. No breakpoint was identifiable at day level in five of the six combinations of group and season; the sixth (corrected p = 0.03) sat at the edge of the search grid and did not recur with other integration windows. Bootstrap intervals for the breakpoint covered up to 57% of the sampled range, and a simulation recovered a full plateau in 12%–48% of replicates. The data neither locate a threshold nor exclude one. The adjusted demand slope was posi…

title: A statistical approach to demand estimation: evidence from fish consumption in Spain
abstract: Purpose Reliable demand estimation is often constrained by the short time series available in official household budget surveys, yet limited guidance exists on how to obtain robust elasticity estimates under such data constraints. This paper estimates own-price, cross-price, and income elasticities of demand for fresh and chilled fish in Spain, while also proposing a transparent and replicable empirical framework for demand estimation using short annual time series. Design/methodology/approach The analysis uses annual data from the Spanish Household Budget Survey for 2006–2015 and estimates parsimonious single-equation demand models under double-log specifications. Given the limited time dimension of the data, inference is strengthened through a comprehensive robustness strategy that combines bootstrap-based inference, first-difference estimation, leave-one-out (jackknife) sensitivity analysis, alternative functional forms, and standard diagnostic tests. This multi-method approach is designed to assess the stability of elasticity estimates in small-sample environments where asymptotic approximations may be unreliable. Findings Demand for fresh and chilled fish in Spain is found to be price elastic, with an own-price elasticity of −1.395. The estimated cross-price elasticity with respect to pork is positive (1.476), indicating substitution between fish and pork, while the income…

AI responsibility and the illusion of control: doctrines, gaps and the EU response
abstract: Purpose This paper aims to explore whether traditional liability doctrines can adequately address damages caused by the actions of artificial intelligence (AI) systems and whether AI systems themselves can be held accountable in cases of improper performance. In addition, the paper examines certain key aspects of the EU AI Act while considering what the law ought to be to fully accommodate the unique characteristics and consequences of AI systems. Design/methodology/approach This paper adopts a doctrinal legal analysis methodology, drawing on relevant legal sources, including legislation and academic literature. By identifying structural gaps, challenges and inadequacies in the current legal system, the analysis informs the need for legal reform. Findings Despite the increasing sophistication and self-learning capabilities of autonomous AI systems, current legal doctrines and legislative initiatives continue to conceptualise such systems as passive instruments. This persistent disconnect between technological advancement and existing legal frameworks underscores the need for early regulatory intervention during design and production, rather than waiting until technological outcomes have already emerged. It is also argued that an exclusive reliance on detailed documentation, risk assessments and compliance measures can be prohibitively costly, both economically and practically a…

title: Nursing management for patients with minor papilla stent placement after failed endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography cannulation: Two case reports
abstract: BACKGROUND Endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography (ERCP) is the standard intervention for pancreatic ductal drainage. Selective cannulation of the main pancreatic duct via the major papilla fails in 5%-10% of cases due to anatomic variants, particularly suspected pancreas divisum, and cannulation often occurs via the minor papilla. CASE SUMMARY This case report describes two patients (a 37-year-old female and a 71-year-old female) who presented with pancreatic ductal dilation and underwent ERCP for diagnostic and therapeutic purposes. In both cases, selective cannulation of the main pancreatic duct via the major papilla failed after repeated attempts; however successful minor papilla cannulation and pancreatic stent placement were achieved without intraprocedural or postprocedural complications, including post-ERCP pancreatitis, bleeding, or perforation at the 1-month follow-up. This report emphasizes the critical role of comprehensive nursing interventions throughout the perioperative period. CONCLUSION Preoperatively, nurses contributed to risk identification by thoroughly reviewing imaging and anatomical variations. Intraoperatively, they ensure seamless instrument preparation, timely device exchange, and steady guidewire stabilization, which are pivotal for procedural success. Postoperatively, a standardized “fasting-enzyme inhibition-fluid resuscitation” protocol w…

title: Classification and endoscopic management of pancreatic fistulas
abstract: Pancreatic fistula is a common and serious complication that may occur after pancreatic surgery, pancreatitis, trauma, or pancreatic intervention. It can lead to persistent external drainage, pancreatic fluid collections, infection, bleeding, nutritional depletion, repeated interventions, and sepsis. Endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography (ERCP) with transpapillary pancreatic duct stenting is widely used, but its effectiveness depends mainly on ductal continuity, leak location, successful stent placement across the ductal disruption, and the presence of disconnected pancreatic duct syndrome or associated collections. When ductal continuity is lost, the leak cannot be bridged, or mature collections and surgically altered anatomy are present, ERCP alone may be insufficient. In these situations, endoscopic ultrasound (EUS)-guided transmural drainage, EUS-guided pancreatic duct drainage, rendezvous techniques, fistula internalization, and combined approaches may provide alternative or complementary routes for internal drainage. This minireview summarizes current endoscopic strategies for pancreatic fistula and proposes an endoscopy-oriented classification framework to guide treatment selection.

When the model specification was held fixed, estimator choice did not change the substantive conclusion for this two-item measure: weight-related anxiety and self-reported weight-management goal non-attainment among undergraduates at a public university in Southwestern China
abstract: Background Weight-related anxiety has been widely studied as a correlate of weight-management goal non-attainment among university students, yet it remains unclear whether brief, floor-skewed anxiety measures yield estimator-dependent conclusions when maximum likelihood (ML) and weighted least squares mean- and variance-adjusted (WLSMV) estimation are compared. Holding the model specification constant, this study estimated the anxiety–outcome association and tested whether the two estimators reached the same conclusion. Methods We analyzed cross-sectional survey data from 754 undergraduates (71.4% female; mean age 20.66 years) enrolled at a public university in Southwestern China. Multiple logistic regression was used to identify factors associated with goal non-attainment. A nine-path manifest-variable recursive path model was then estimated under both ML and WLSMV using an identical specification, and direct and indirect associations were obtained from 5,000 bootstrap resamples (percentile 95% CIs), with all coefficients standardized. Results The two-item anxiety composite (range 1–6) showed a marked floor effect, with 39.4% of participants scoring at or below 2.0. In the logistic regression, weight-related anxiety was the strongest correlate of non-attainment (OR = 2.11, 95% CI 1.79–2.49, p < 0.001). title: Doing good or just looking good in the fashion industry? Motive attributions and the psychological mechanisms behind green trust
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how perceived greenwashing and internal and external motivations undermine green trust through two distinct psychological mechanisms: green skepticism and perceived brand hypocrisy. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative research design was employed using survey data collected from Generation Z consumers in Vietnam. Findings Perceived greenwashing increases both green skepticism and perceived brand hypocrisy, which are in turn negatively associated with green trust. Green skepticism and perceived brand hypocrisy operate as two distinct but parallel pathways (cognitive doubt and moral judgment) through which trust erodes, and these two mediating pathways are comparable in overall magnitude rather than one being dominant. Furthermore, perceived internal motivation reduces both green skepticism and brand hypocrisy, whereas perceived external motivation increases green skepticism and indirectly weakens green trust. Originality/value This study establishes green skepticism and perceived brand hypocrisy as empirically distinct yet co-occurring cognitive and moral pathways of green trust erosion, rather than treating skepticism as the default mediator. It further shows that internal and external motive attributions map asymmetrically onto these two pathways, refining how attribution theory and Expectancy Disconfirmation Theory are applied to sust…
