Unblocking the airway: direct neck lift for lymphedema-associated extrinsic stomal obstruction—a novel therapy for airway management: case report
abstract: Abstract Background Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is uncommon after total laryngectomy (TL) because airflow bypasses the pharynx and occurs exclusively through the tracheostoma. However, a mechanistically distinct form—extrinsic OSA—may occur when submental adiposity or lymphedema externally compresses the stoma. Case presentation A 61-year-old woman with prior TL developed nocturnal apneas and daytime somnolence from posture-dependent stomal obstruction caused by submental lymphedema and adiposity. Neck flexion produced complete external airway collapse despite tracheal lumen patency. She underwent ​direct​ excision neck lift involving direct skin and subcutaneous tissue excision, suprahyoid lymphadenectomy, submental lipectomy, lateral liposuction, midline platysmal plication, and Z-plasty closure. There were no complications. Over 20 months of follow-up she had near-complete resolution of nocturnal obstruction, improved breathing, a patent stoma in neck flexion, and improved cervicomental contour. Mild, infrequent obstruction persisted due to excess chest wall and breast tissue. Conclusions This case identifies extrinsic stomal obstruction as an underrecognized cause of OSA after TL and suggests that targeted soft-tissue debulking can restore airway patency when conservative measures fail. This represents the first documented case of successful surgical correction for extrin…

title: Axial Difference Cross-Correlation with System Modulation Reference for 3D Structured Illumination Microscopy
Bridging the Last Mile: A Necessity-Driven and Risk-Inversion Framework for FinTech Adoption in Emerging Markets
abstract: This study examines the roles of perceived risk and service trust in fintech adoption among rural shopkeepers in India and develops a necessity-driven adoption framework for institutionally constrained settings. Drawing on TAM, TPB, Institutional Theory, and the capability approach, it distinguishes perceived risk as an adoption trigger and service trust as a post-adoption sustainer. Using survey data from 274 shopkeepers and PLS-SEM, the results show that perceived risk positively influences both intention and actual usage, acting as a behavioral driver under institutional voids. In contrast, service trust is more important for sustaining long-term engagement than for initial adoption. Trust also weakens the effect of perceived risk on behavioral intention, reducing reliance on necessity-driven adoption. The study introduces a risk-inversion mechanism, showing that perceived risk can encourage adoption in constrained environments. Practical implications suggest that fintech providers should focus on trustbuilding and retention strategies, while policymakers should combine digitalization with digital literacy to ensure meaningful financial inclusion.

title: Good Forest Governance Principles In Protected Forest Management: A Comparative Study Of Indonesia And Brazil
abstract: Introduction: The management of protected forests plays a strategic role in maintaining global ecological stability, particularly in megadiverse tropical nations such as Indonesia and Brazil. However, implementing good forest governance principles such as transparency, accountability, and ecological justice remains challenged by regulatory overlaps and enforcement gaps. Purposes of the Research: This study explicitly aims to analyze and compare the legal frameworks, institutional structures, and implementation of good forest governance principles in protected forest management between Indonesia and Brazil. Methods of the Research: The novelty of this research lies in its comparative normative legal synthesis that bridges international environmental principles with domestic enforcement mechanisms, specifically contrasting Indonesia’s strict liability doctrine with Brazil’s constitutional social function of property and polluter pays principle. Using a normative legal methodology with statutory, conceptual, and comparative approaches, this study examines primary and secondary legal materials from both jurisdictions. Results / Main Findings / Novelty/Originality of the Research: The results demonstrate that Indonesia has integrated governance principles through Law Number 41 of 1999 and strict liability mechanisms, yet faces hurdles from sectoral legal disharmony and overlapping a…

abstract: The Regional Development Planning, Research, and Innovation Agency (BAPPERIDA) of West Sulawesi Province plays a strategic role in ensuring that regional development planning is well-directed, integrated, and aligned with regional priorities. However, its Regional Development Planning Index (IPPD) declined from 88.00 in 2024 to 82.25 in 2025, falling short of the 88.00 target. This study aims to analyze the quality of regional development planning at BAPPERIDA of West Sulawesi Province. A qualitative approach was employed, with data collected through interviews, observations, and document analysis. The analysis focused on three IPPN/IPPD assessment components: development planning synergy, planning quality, and the linkage between development and performance planning. The findings indicate that regional development planning is supported by structured mechanisms and systems, although its substantive quality requires improvement. Regarding planning synergy, document alignment and inter-agency coordination have been implemented, but challenges remain in data integration, fiscal capacity, sectoral ego, and stakeholder participation. In terms of planning quality, priorities, targets, and programs are established through analytical and cascading mechanisms. However, data consistency, research utilization, target accuracy, and outcome-oriented indicators need improvement. Regarding th…

title: The age–listening paradox: how managerial listening and conflict management shape workplace innovation?
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how a manager’s age relates to their listening abilities in the context of interpersonal workplace conflicts, and how these listening dynamics shape the workplace innovation climate. Design/methodology/approach Data was captured through an online survey (n = 220) and analyzed using PROCESS macros, followed by a post hoc qualitative study among senior managers (age > 45 yrs) to validate and explain the findings. The study is grounded in the theory of relational coordination and socioemotional selectivity theory to substantiate the research model and its hypotheses. Findings Results of our study suggest that (1) constructive listening ability of a manager positively influences workplace innovation climate, (2) collaborative conflict management acts as a mediator by influencing workplace innovation climate through constructive listening behavior, (3) interestingly, subordinates perception suggest that manager’s listening and conflict handling capabilities are weaker among older managers, which is associated with a less favorable workplace innovation climate. Practical implications The study highlights the need for organizations to develop managerial listening capabilities, particularly among mid- and senior-level managers, through targeted training interventions aimed at improving collaborative conflict management and fostering a supportive wo…

title: What makes platform work a good fit?
abstract: Purpose This paper aims to review the latest management developments across the globe and pinpoint practical implications from cutting-edge research and case studies. Design/methodology/approach This briefing is prepared by an independent writer who adds their own impartial comments and places the articles in context. Findings Appropriate fit between person and job is essential for both firms and employees in a platform work setting. This can be attained through a focus on developing the necessary skills and capabilities required to perform the role, while simultaneously taking measures to ensure that the job likewise satisfies the needs and requirements of the workers. Originality/value The briefing saves busy executives, strategists and researchers hours of reading time by selecting only the very best, most pertinent information and presenting it in a condensed and easy-to-digest format.

title: Editorial: Rethinking innovation management: four movements, a more connected perspective
Knowledge-sharing routines to promote knowledge value in co-innovation projects
abstract: Purpose Knowledge sharing is one of the main benefits attributed to participation in co-innovation projects. However, the literature has yet to explain which knowledge-sharing (KS) routines sustain knowledge value generation in such projects. This research investigates which combinations of KS routines generate knowledge value in co-innovation projects. Design/methodology/approach We conducted a qualitative comparative analysis (QCA) using data from 14 co-innovation projects documented by a focal company (Alpha). Alpha is a global developer of software solutions focused on companies of all sizes. Since 2010, Alpha has maintained 26 design and co-innovation centers worldwide, offering specific co-innovation services to support customers in leveraging technology, solving business challenges and creating measurable value. Findings Of the nine KS routines identified in the literature, seven combine to form four configurations that generate high levels of knowledge value. We call these configurations “innovative synergy”, “innovative interaction”, “innovative process” and “innovative result”. Research limitations/implications The research provides theoretical insights into combining KS routines that generate knowledge value in co-creation projects. Practical implications The study offers a practical guide for combining KS routines to foster knowledge value in co-innovation projects.…

title: Pastoral Leadership Transformation in Building Ministry in the Digital Era
abstract: This study aims to analyze the transformation of pastoral leadership in building church ministries in the digital era, with a focus on aspects of leadership, integrity, relationships, and the performance of the ministry team in the Wasior region, Papua. This research is motivated by various problems in church ministries, such as low involvement of the council and congregation, weak leadership assertiveness, inconsistency between words and actions, lack of communication, and the suboptimal use of digital technology. The study uses a qualitative explanatory approach with data collection through in-depth interviews with church ministry stakeholders. Data analysis is carried out through the stages of data reduction, data presentation, and drawing conclusions, accompanied by source triangulation to test the consistency of the findings. The results show that the effectiveness of church ministries is closely related to assertiveness, integrity, exemplary behavior, open communication, and the quality of relationships between pastors, councils, and congregations. The weakness of these aspects contributes to the decline in motivation, participation, and collaboration of the ministry team. This study concludes that a situational leadership model that integrates structural assertiveness, a close pastoral approach, member empowerment, and proportional use of digital technology is a relevant…

title: Penerapan Integrasi Lean Warehousing dan Employee Behavior untuk Meningkatkan Kinerja Operasional PT. CRP
abstract: PT CRP merupakan suatu perusahaan warehouse yang mendistribusikan karpet di Indonesia. Kelancaran operasional pergudangan ditentukan oleh kelancaran, efektif, dan efisien dari kegiatan-kegiatan yang terdapat pada sistem kerjanya dan diukur kinerjanya. Kinerja yang diukur adalah komplain pelanggan dan produktivitas sehingga mempersingkat waktu proses operasi sangat penting. Tahapan proses operasional meliputi receiving, put away, sales order, picking, packing, dan dispatching. PT CRP menghadapi tantangan untuk memperbaiki kinerjanya karena adanya hambatan, pemborosan di alur kerja operasinya, seperti pergerakan karyawan yang tidak perlu, waktu tunggu barang yang lama di setiap tahapan proses, adanya ekstra proses, kompetensi karyawan kurang, kurangnya koordinasi antarbagian, operator sering mengobrol, terjadi bullying, adanya penerimaan/pengeluaran barang secara bersamaan dan sebagainya. title: A Study of Blockchain Based Solutions towards Fraudulent Practices in Bangladesh
abstract: The objective of this study is to investigate how blockchain’s unique technological properties –immutability, cryptographic verification and decentralization- could be utilized to mitigate fraudulent practices in Bangladesh, with a particular emphasis on financial reporting fraud, LC fraud, payment fraud and tax evasion (especially VAT). This study employs an exploratory and qualitative methodology, obtaining secondary data from scholarly articles, handbooks and professional reports. Through critical analysis, this study evaluates blockchain’s potential in deterring fraud and identifies some major challenges associated with its implementation in Bangladesh. The findings highlight blockchain’s immense potential to mitigate fraudulent practices based on its distributed ledgers across multiple stakeholders, immutable audit trails and smart contract-based verification. In financial reporting, blockchain’s triple-entry accounting considerably reduces scope for financial statements manipulation; it has the potential to minimize LCrelated fraud by strengthening the authenticity of trade documents; it increases transaction security and integrity in both local and cross-border digital payment system; and in the field of taxation, it improves the traceability of documents and tax compliance. However, data privacy concerns, technological readiness and adoption costs are some challenges th…

title: More climate data is not enough: towards inclusive knowledge and action networks
abstract: Purpose This paper examines why increasing the availability of climate and weather data alone is insufficient to enable effective climate change adaptation and disaster risk reduction, particularly in low- and middle-income countries. It aims to identify the conditions required to make climate data actionable and to propose a more inclusive framework for knowledge and action. Design/methodology/approach The study adopts a conceptual, synthesis-based approach, drawing on existing literature and emerging practices in climate services. It integrates insights from research and implementation initiatives to develop six interrelated conditions that support the transformation of climate data into useable, context-specific knowledge. Findings The paper identifies six key conditions for making climate data actionable: community-centered co-production, inclusive participation, multi-stakeholder collaboration, integrated knowledge infrastructures, the use of climate storylines and strengthened local–global linkages. Together, these conditions enable more relevant and actionable climate information. Originality/value The paper contributes by synthesizing these conditions into a coherent framework and introducing the concept of “Knowledge–Action Networks.” This framework highlights the need to integrate technical, social and institutional dimensions, offering practical and conceptual value …

title: Analysis of Loss Prevention in Underground Mine’s Ore Delivery Operations Through the Implementation of an Integrated Remote Monitoring System on Fire Protection Equipment
abstract: Unintended discharges of fire suppression systems (FSS) on underground conveyor systems at PT Freeport Indonesia (PTFI) disrupted single-line ore delivery operations and resulted in substantial opportunity losses. Before this study, most FSS units were not integrated into a centralized remote monitoring platform, causing delays in incident detection, response, and operational recovery. This study examined the contribution of limited remote monitoring capabilities to prolonged downtime and quantified the reductions in operational downtime and opportunity losses associated with integrating FSS status monitoring into the existing AVEVA PI Vision dashboard. A quantitative, quasi-experimental pretest–posttest design was employed to analyze 48 verified discharge events, comprising 29 events in Phase 1 (2022–2023) and 19 events in Phase 2 (2024–2025). Data were obtained from the AVEVA PI System historian and evaluated using the prevention–appraisal–failure (PAF) cost framework. Statistical analyses included paired-samples t-tests and Wilcoxon signed-rank tests involving seven matched conveyor systems. None of the recorded discharges resulted from an actual fire. Mean downtime per event decreased by 37.4%, from 2.967 to 1.857 hours, while the matched-conveyor analysis indicated a 43.6% reduction (t = 5.2203, p = 0.00099; Wilcoxon p = 0.0078; Cohen's d<sub>z</sub> = 1.97). title: Injury patterns, management, and in-hospital outcomes of abdominopelvic gunshot wounds at a tertiary trauma center in Somalia: a retrospective cross-sectional study
abstract: Abstract Background Abdominopelvic gunshot wounds are an important cause of trauma-related morbidity and mortality in conflict-affected, resource-constrained settings. Contemporary data describing their epidemiology, management, and clinical outcomes in Somalia remain scarce, limiting evidence-based trauma system planning and context-specific surgical practice. Methods We conducted a retrospective cross-sectional study of consecutive patients presenting with abdominopelvic gunshot wounds to the emergency department of Mogadishu Somalia Türkiye Recep Tayyip Erdoğan Training and Research Hospital between 1 February and 30 June 2025. Demographic characteristics, injury patterns, diagnostic findings, management strategies, complications, and in-hospital outcomes were analyzed using descriptive statistical methods. Results A total of 154 patients were included; 141 (91.6%) were male and 108 (70.1%) were aged 21–40 years. On arrival, 88 patients (57.1%) were triaged as Orange and 57 (37.0%) as Red; 117 (76.0%) had a positive E-FAST examination. The abdomen was the primary anatomical injury region in 105 patients (68.2%) and the pelvis in 49 (31.8%). The small bowel was the most frequently documented injured intra-abdominal organ (n = 28, 18.2%). Operative management was performed in 87 patients (56.5%), and 104 (67.5%) received blood transfusions. At least one in-hospital complicatio…

title: Influence of CO 3 2- and SO 4 2- on the chloride binding capacity of AAMs with municipal solid waste incineration fly ash
abstract: Abstract Alkali-activated materials (AAMs) are widely used for the treatment of chloride-rich municipal solid waste incineration fly ash (MSWI FA). However, there is a lack of study on the influence of inevitable CO32- and SO42- from MSWI FA on the chloride binding capacity of AAMs. In this study, AAMs with different levels of internal Cl-, SO42- and CO32- were prepared to simulate the systems with MSWI FA to provide insights into the intricate competition of three anions for being bound by in-situ formed hydrotalcites (Ht) in AAMs. The results showed that at 5 wt% internal Cl-, CO32- reduced bound chloride by 0.81~3.4%, whereas SO42- increased it by 3.7~10.2%, and the influence of both anions decreased with prolonging curing time from 7d to 28d. Ht formation in AAMs with 3 wt% Cl- increased from 5.6 wt% to 6.3 wt% and to 7.1 wt% with the presence of CO32- and SO42-, respectively, while an increase in Cl- from 3 wt% to 5 wt% slightly varied the Ht content. Cold-water extraction for chloride binding capacity quantification varied the phase assemblage due to dissolution, and the optimal extraction time was 2h for powder samples. Spatial distribution of Ht was obtained by quantitative SEM-EDS hypermaps analysis, which revealed that Ca-Al Ht and Mg-Al Ht coexisted around GGBS, but Cl- and SO42- showed preference for intercalation into the Ca-Al Ht. title: Synergistic Molecular-Nano Engineering Enabling Ultralong-Cycling and High-Capacity Lithium Storage of Covalent Organic Frameworks
abstract: Abstract Lithium-ion capacitors (LICs) combine the high energy density of batteries with the high-power density of supercapacitors for potential advanced applications. As promising anode candidates for LICs, the practical application of covalent organic frameworks (COFs) is hampered by the intrinsically low electronic conductivity. Here, a “molecular-nano” dual-scale synergistic strategy is proposed to enhance the charge transport and utilization of active sites. At the molecular scale, three highly crystalized COFs (2,6-DAAQ-COF, 2,6-DAA-COF, and 1,4-DAAQ-COF) via donor-acceptor (D–A) structural design are synthesized to enhance the intramolecular charge separation and electron transfer processes. At the nanoscale, a three-dimensional conductive network is constructed by in situ compositing with carbon nanotubes (CNTs) to yield core-shell structured COF@CNT, which also effectively exfoliates COF layers and exposes active sites. Benefiting from the synergistic enhancement between intramolecular charge transfer and the macroscopic conductive network, the optimized 2,6-DAAQ-COF@CNT50 exhibits exceptional lithium storage performance, retaining a high discharge capacity of 1983 mAh g–1 after 1000 cycles at 1 A g–1. Furthermore, the electrode also exhibits excellent electrochemical performance at low temperature (–20 °C), retaining 220 mAh g–1 after 2000 cycles at 0.5 A g–1. The ass…

Compositional characterization and fouling mechanism of pipe scale in black-liquor evaporators of a kraft bamboo pulp mill
abstract: Abstract Pipe scale fouling in kraft bamboo black liquor evaporators reduces heat transfer efficiency and causes unscheduled shutdowns. Organic and inorganic deposits from a kraft bamboo pulp mill were characterized in this study. The scale is an organic–inorganic composite: 74.6 wt% inorganic (with elemental compositions of O 22.78 %, C 15.74 %, Si 10.99 %, Na 10.47 %, Al 8.41 %, Fe 3.04 %, Ca 1.82 %, S 1.14 %, and trace Mg/N based on OD scale) and residual organics (lignin 19.6 %, cellulose 4.8 %, and hemicelluloses 1.64 %). The crystalline phases include cancrinite, shortite, calcite, and enstatite, while the amorphous fraction is rich in aluminosilicates. The critical precursor for these components is silica, which originates from the bamboo culm; it condenses with Na + , Ca 2+ , and Al 3+ to form cancrinite and shortite under alkaline/high-temperature conditions. Simultaneously, alkali-resistant lignin–silicate complexes and micro-fibrillar cellulose act as nuclei that anchor inorganic crystallites to the steel wall. The revealed synergy between biogenic silica and pulping liquor provides a clear target for antiscalants based on Si-sequestration and dispersant chemistry.

abstract: Background Emergency medicine is characterized by urgency, criticality, severity, and diversity, which places high demands on undergraduate medical education. Traditional lecture-based teaching has limitations in developing students' advanced clinical competence and clinical transfer ability. Although virtual simulation and case-based learning (CBL) have demonstrated benefits in medical education, their combined application in emergency medicine teaching has not been systematically evaluated, especially based on artificial intelligence (AI). This study primarily aimed to investigate whether the integrated AI-powered virtual simulation combined with CBL could improve students' higher-order clinical competencies and clinical transfer ability, and secondarily to obtain empirical evidence to support the optimization of undergraduate emergency medicine teaching. Methods Third-year undergraduate students majoring in clinical medicine were selected as the research subjects and randomly divided into the control group and the experimental group. The control group adopted the traditional teaching method, while the experimental group adopted the AI-enabled virtual simulation combined with real emergency case teaching method. Development and EEG Assessment of a Virtual Reality Replica of a Prior Real Multisensory Environment Intervention
abstract: Multisensory environments (MSEs) are valuable therapeutic spaces for relaxation and stress relief, yet high costs and physical infrastructure limit accessibility. Immersive virtual reality MSEs (V-MSEs) offer a low-cost and scalable alternative to real MSEs (R-MSEs), but evidence is scarce. The aim of this study is an exploratory characterization of the electroencephalography (EEG) response to a V-MSE replica of a previous R-MSE intervention, using the original R-MSE data as a qualitative reference. After developing a V-MSE mirroring the original environment, 31 healthy participants underwent an adapted version of the protocol, and spectral and nonlinear features were computed from EEG recordings pre- and post-intervention. Analyses were performed within each environment, and comparisons between them remained qualitative. The alpha/beta ratio, negatively correlated with stress, was the only feature significantly increased in both conditions. In the V-MSE, frontal theta and the theta/beta ratio also increased significantly, whereas relative gamma power and Lempel-Ziv complexity decreased. Only in R-MSE, parieto-occipital alpha power rose significantly, whereas frontal delta power decreased. No feature changed significantly in opposite directions between settings. Evidence remains insufficient to establish V-MSEs as an alternative to R-MSEs, but this first EEG characterization of…

Sentani Folklore:A Reflection of Power Relations and Politics
abstract: This research proceeds from the premise that folklore not only represents the social life of the Sentani people but also serves as a discursive space where the community negotiates authority, legitimizes leadership, and voices criticism of power practices through symbols, metaphors, and cultural narratives. The study aims to analyze how power relations are represented in Sentani oral literature, identify the forms of political criticism embedded within it, and explain the function of oral literature as a mechanism of social control in indigenous life. A qualitative approach is employed, integrating the perspectives of the anthropology of literature and political literature. Folklore data—comprising folktales, oral chants, folk songs, and traditional expressions—were gathered through participant observation, in-depth interviews, and focus group discussions (FGDs) with tribal chiefs, community elders, and members of the Sentani community across various islands and villages in Lake Sentani between January and February 2026. Analysis was conducted using a hermeneutic approach, integrating theories of oral literature, Gramsci’s theory of hegemony, and Foucault’s theory of power to interpret the relationship between the texts and the socio-cultural contexts in which the folklore is produced and transmitted. The study posits that Sentani folklore constitutes a cultural arena serving n…

title: Contesting Presidential Power: Impoliteness Strategies in YouTube Comments on the Indonesian President’s Speech
abstract: The YouTube responses to Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto’s speeches have sparked extensive online discussions and criticisms, providing a useful site for examining how language is used to challenge political authority in the digital environment. This study examines the use of impoliteness strategies by YouTube users to challenge the presidential power in comments on the president’s speech. The study uses Culpeper’s framework of impoliteness and qualitative discourse analysis of 100 YouTube comments from a news video of President Prabowo’s speech. The analysis shows that the most common strategies are sarcasm or mock politeness, positive impoliteness and bald-on-record impoliteness. They are employed to challenge the president’s credibility, express political discontent and negotiate power relations in an online participatory environment. The findings suggest that YouTube comment sections act as sites in which users publicly contest political authority through linguistic practices. This study contributes to the growing body of research on impoliteness in computer-mediated communication by demonstrating the use of the impoliteness strategies in Indonesian digital political discourse.

title: Fuzzy logic driven real time fertiliser recommendation system with internet of things-integrated soil and environmental sensor suite
abstract: Precision nutrient management is essential for improving crop productivity while minimising fertiliser misuse, production costs and environmental impacts. This paper presents a low-cost, portable and real-time fertiliser recommendation system that integrates an Internet of Things (IoT)-based soil and environmental sensor suite with a fuzzy logic inference engine. The proposed system acquires key soil parameters, including nitrogen (N), phosphorus (P), potassium (K), pH and electrical conductivity (EC), along with environmental data and geolocation information. Sensor readings are calibrated and processed to estimate nutrient deficiencies and soil conditions. A fuzzy inference system utilises crop type, crop growth stage and nutrient deficiency percentages as inputs to generate crop-specific fertiliser recommendations for urea, diammonium phosphate (DAP), single super phosphate (SSP) and muriate of potash (MOP). An additional pH reclamation module recommends suitable amendments such as lime or gypsum. To enhance usability, a mobile application and Python-based dashboard were developed, enabling users with no prior agricultural expertise to select the crop and growth stage, deploy the sensor in the field and receive actionable recommendations, including fertiliser quantities, estimated costs and labour requirements. The system was validated using 100 soil samples collected from S…

title: The Digital Divide in Global Communication: Inequality, Governance, and the Contest for Narrative Power
abstract: The spread of information and communication technologies has made connectivity central to global communication, yet the benefits of this transformation are distributed unequally. This article examines the digital divide as a structural feature of contemporary global media rather than a mere gap in hardware access. Drawing on scholarship that treats the divide as a complex and dynamic phenomenon, it argues that the divide operates on at least three intersecting levels: access, usage and skill, and algorithmic and infrastructural power. It then traces how the divide is deepened by the politics of platform governance and by asymmetric control over digital content, and considers how these asymmetries become acute in armed conflict, where the ability to generate, moderate, and frame information is itself a weapon. The article concludes that bridging the divide requires not only connectivity and digital literacy but a redistribution of the power to produce and govern the global media environment.

title: Graph data-driven power flow model for offshore wind farm considering internal and external characteristics
abstract: Purpose Existing data-driven power flow modeling methods for offshore wind farms (OWFs) are only applicable to fixed external grid scenarios and ignore the imbalance of power flow samples, which severely restricts the fitting accuracy and application range of the model. To solve these defects, this paper aims to propose an optimized data-driven OWF power flow modeling method. It is committed to adapting to dynamic changes of internal and external operating conditions and solving the accuracy limitation caused by unbalanced samples, so as to improve the generalization and prediction accuracy of power flow prediction in complex working conditions. Design/methodology/approach This paper extracts hidden grid impedance information from historical power flow data to construct a new data set integrating internal and external characteristics of OWFs. Combining graph deep learning advantages and wind farm structural features, a multi-head graph attention network with Huber loss function is established for power flow fitting. Comparative verification proves that the proposed method can achieve accurate power flow prediction under variable working conditions and unbalanced samples. Findings Impedance of power grid has a significant impact on power flow distribution in the OWFs. By extracting the grid impedance characteristics from the historical power flow data (PFD), a new PFD set consid…

title: Proof of concept for a virtual serious game for the training of doctors and nurses: design and development of the GEMAS project
abstract: Background Traditional lecture-based education has shown limitations in engagement, knowledge retention, and skill transfer in healthcare training. Serious games and virtual simulations offer accessible solutions to enhance emergency medicine (EM) education. The GEMAS project (Gamificación en Enfermería y Medicina para el Aprendizaje por Simulación) was developed as a narrative-driven, browser-based serious game built around guideline-based diagnostic and therapeutic decision-making in common emergency scenarios, with separate pathways for physicians and nurses. This study aimed to describe its development and evaluate its usability, satisfaction, and short-term educational impact. Methods A pre–post single-center pilot study was conducted between June and November 2024 among physicians and nurses from a university hospital with no prior experience in serious games or high-fidelity simulation. Participants completed a single supervised, self-paced GEMAS gameplay session lasting up to 3 h. Educational outcomes were assessed using Levels I and II of the Kirkpatrick model: (1) satisfaction and usability through a 10-item Likert questionnaire and the System Usability Scale (SUS); and (2) knowledge acquisition via expert-reviewed pre- and post-intervention tests specific to each profession covering key emergency scenarios. Because the two tests were not equated, knowledge outcomes w…

Effect of low-power remelting process on the formed specimen of TC4 titanium alloy by selective laser melting
abstract: Purpose This study aims to investigate the SLM remelting process and improved the overall performance of the formed samples greatly. It provides a strategy for effectively manufacturing high melting point materials such as TC4 on machines with limited laser power. By designing the experiment of the low-power remelting process (LPRP), the difference between direct high power forming quality and low power forming quality is explored. Which provides new considerations for SLM low-power forming TC4 specimens. Design/methodology/approach This experiment is based on energy density. In the experimental parameters, to ensure the sum of the remelting process energy density and the volume process forming energy density was consistent. Using different volume laser powers and remelting laser powers to form samples. Findings The authors found that using LPRP can form specimens with good surface quality and density, and the metallographic structure is beneficial to the mechanical properties. This method can use low-power equipment to form high melting point materials, reduce excessive energy gradients, produce multiple α' phases, and improve the overall performance of the specimen. Originality/value The LPRP has the following advantages: 1) Reduces the excessive energy gradient to produce multiple α' phases; 2) Provides a strategy for effectively manufacturing high melting point materials su…

title: Reducing Cholesterol Content in Butter Products: Plant-Based Milk Analogues
abstract: Plant-based beverages can be used as an alternative aqueous phase (plasma) to reduce or completely eliminate cholesterol from butterlike products, specifically spreads. The article reviews physicochemical, biotechnological, and formulation methods for obtaining cholesterol-free products. Cereal, legume, and nut beverages were analyzed for their chemical composition, nutritional properties, energy value, vitamins, and minerals in comparison with cow’s milk. The sensory evaluation involved a qualified expert panel. The nutrient profile differed across the plant-based samples. The highest protein concentration was found in the soy beverages (up to 2.0 g/100 mL), but it remained lower than that of the cow’s milk control (3.0 g/100 mL). However, most plant-based samples demonstrated lower caloric values (25–60 kcal/100 mL) and contained neither cholesterol nor lactose. The oat, almond, and hazelnut beverages demonstrated the best sensory properties, featuring natural color shades and uniform textures, whereas the samples with added flavorings and colorants exhibited unbalanced profiles. The oat, almond, and hazelnut formulations were the most technologically and economically viable options for producing functional, cholesterol-free spreads with a custom-regulated composition. Priority areas for further research include the structure, mechanical properties, and emulsion stability of …

title: Classification of rice varieties using RGB images integrated with image-derived geometric traits based on deep learning models
abstract: Deep learning (DL) offers a promising approach for accurate, scalable plant classification. However, most DL studies on rice depend on seed images. In this study, we assessed leaf-based classification of nine rice varieties using red, green, and blue (RGB) images and geometric traits derived from these images at the vegetative stage, creating an image-guided feature integration model. The classification strategies included traits-based, RGB image-based, and combined RGB image and traits-based methods. For geometric trait measurements, six traits were calculated with the OpenCV module in Python. Classification was conducted at six growth stages: 13, 21, 23, 29, 33, and 35 days after sowing (DAS). Traits-based classification was performed using random forest and support vector machine models. For RGB image-only classification and RGB images combined with trait classification, four convolutional neural networks (CNNs): EfficientNetV2, InceptionV3, ConvNeXt-Tiny, and ResNet-50 were evaluated along with an Ensemble model of ResNet and EfficientNet. Traits-based classification achieved less than 0.5 accuracy at all stages. For RGB image-based evaluation, EfficientNetV2, ResNet-50, and ConvNeXt-Tiny gave an accuracy of 0.76 at 29 DAS, with the lowest being 0.43 for InceptionV3 at 13 and 23 DAS, and the highest 0.80 for Ensemble at 29 DAS. Similarly, for the trait integration method, t…

title: Ten key principles for reusable and transferable XR in European Industrial Virtual Worlds
abstract: Abstract Industrial Virtual Worlds promise gains in remote collaboration, efficiency, and safety, but a lack of reusability and standardization leaves the field fragmented, with XR solutions that scale and adapt poorly. We report the transfer of a collaborative XR system between two industrial projects: an initial project that built a 5G-based remote maintenance demonstrator, and a follow-up project on AI-supported work systems in the textile industry, in which three XR demonstrators were built. Across both, we observe frictions from shifting working conditions, hardware discontinuation, and unavailable source data. Finding that practitioners lack documented, transferable guidance for building reusable industrial XR, we contribute 10 principles, each stating how a recurring project component should be handled and placing it on a scale from customized through reusable to standardized. We position them within the Industry and Logistics domain and the Standardisation and Interoperability, Digital Twins, and Applied AI priorities of the Virtual Worlds Association’s Strategic Research and Innovation Agenda (SRIA) for European Virtual Worlds. Rather than proposing a new architecture or standard, our principles account for the practitioner-level decisions that determine whether reusable XR solutions are in fact reused – a necessary complement to European-level standardisation work.

title: Small-signal stability analysis of grid-forming and grid-following inverters in islanded microgrids
abstract: Abstract As power-electronics-based resources are increasingly adopted in distribution systems, their fast control dynamics and lack of inherent inertia can create stability challenges. This paper develops a unified state-space model of an islanded microgrid containing grid-forming virtual-synchronous-generator and droop-controlled inverters together with grid-following inverters operating in constant-power-reference mode. The grid-following model incorporates complete phase-locked-loop dynamics and bus-voltage coupling through dual Park transformations, allowing eigenvalue-based analysis of cross-controller interactions that are not observable in homogeneous-inverter studies. The results show that increasing virtual inertia can mitigate instability caused by high active-power droop gain only up to a critical value, beyond which effective damping degrades. The phase-locked-loop proportional gain must be coordinated with grid-forming parameters because it introduces an additional stability boundary. Although the virtual-synchronous-generator damping coefficient strongly affects grid-forming-only systems, it has a marginal influence on the dominant eigenvalues after grid-following inverters are introduced. Studies on a two-bus, three-inverter system and a modified IEEE 13-bus distribution system confirm the principal stability trends. The unified framework provides practical guid…

title: Trust formation across AI embodiments: how robotic, virtual, and embedded systems shape user behavior in healthcare
abstract: Purpose Trust in artificial intelligence (AI) systems shapes user behavior and technology acceptance, yet limited research compares how different AI embodiments influence trust formation. This study aims to examine how robotic, virtual, and embedded AI affect cognitive trust in healthcare contexts. Design/methodology/approach An experimental study was conducted to assess the effects of tangibility, transparency, reliability, task characteristics, and immediacy behaviors on cognitive trust across three AI embodiments. Participants evaluated healthcare scenarios involving robotic, virtual or embedded AI systems, and trust-related perceptions were analyzed across conditions. Findings Significant perceptual differences emerged across AI embodiments. Virtual AI was perceived as less tangible than robotic and embedded AI, while embedded AI was rated highest in technical intelligence but lowest in social intelligence. Despite these differences, overall cognitive trust did not significantly vary across embodiments. However, the mechanisms of trust formation were embodiment-specific. Reliability consistently predicted trust across all conditions. Transparency and immediacy behaviors enhanced trust in robotic AI, tangibility and social intelligence drove trust in virtual AI, and immediacy behaviors were especially critical for embedded AI. Originality/value This study advances AI trust r…
venue: Journal of Systems and Information Technology

title: Tecnologías y racionalidades en disputa: tensiones éticas, cognitivas y algorítmicas en la integración de la IA en la educación superior
abstract: The emergence of artificial intelligence (AI) in higher education raises ethical, pedagogical, and political challenges that exceed the instrumental level and point to the technological rationalities guiding its integration. The aim is to analyze the theoretical and practical tensions present in the literature published between 2022 and 2025. An analytical review was conducted, with a hermeneutic-interpretive analysis of 43 sources selected from 89 reviewed, organized around three axes: cognitive delegation, the reconfiguration of teaching work, and algorithmic bias as hidden curriculum. The findings show consensus on the transformative role of AI, but an uneven distribution of evidence, in which algorithmic bias is the least addressed dimension. The three tensions do not operate in isolation, but as expressions of a single dispute over the meaning of higher education. It concludes that integrating AI is a political and epistemic decision that demands critical pedagogies capable of contesting the rationalities at stake.

title: An in-depth observational and modeling analysis to explore long-range offshore wakes under different stability regimes
abstract: As wind energy areas continue to be built out worldwide, it is increasingly important to understand the implications of long-range wind farm wakes on wind energy generation. While gross capacity factors can be estimated, the impacts of upstream wind farm wakes on downstream energy production, especially under stable conditions, are largely unknown. A clear understanding of marine atmospheric boundary layer (MABL) stability in offshore regions is still evolving, as continuous high-resolution thermodynamic profiles in the MABL are uncommon. Given the relationship between stability and long-range (>50 km) offshore wakes, it is increasingly important to reliably estimate stability conditions in offshore regions. With the lack of consistent observations in and around offshore wind farms, it is necessary to rely on mesoscale models such as the Weather Research and Forecasting (WRF) modeling system to estimate stability and wake lengths. For this work we test WRF's ability to reproduce wake effects and potential losses using flight data over wind farms in the North Sea to evaluate its performance. As thermal stability is critical to understanding wake length, different metrics are evaluated to determine the best way to parameterize atmospheric stability from the WRF model. Results show that the bulk Richardson number derived from WRF can be used as a reliable metric to classify stabil…

title: The Role of Digital Marketing In Indonesia’s Energy Transition:Understanding Electric Motorcycle Purchase Decisions Through Influencer Marketing and Product Quality
abstract: Indonesia’s energy transition is increasingly reflected in transport electrification, including the expanding electric-motorcycle market. Yet purchase decisions remain shaped by more than policy incentives and charging infrastructure. This study re-examines three market-facing determinants—digital marketing, influencer marketing, and product quality—and evaluates their relationship with consumers’ purchase decisions. A quantitative survey was administered to 85 consumers who had purchased electric motorcycles. The questionnaire contained indicators for the four constructs and was assessed using validity and reliability tests, followed by multiple linear regression, partial significance tests, and a simultaneous F-test in SPSS. All measurement items exceeded the reported validity threshold (r-table = 0.213), while Cronbach’s alpha values ranged from 0.614 to 0.655, indicating acceptable internal consistency under the criterion used in the study. The reported regression results show that digital marketing and influencer marketing carry negative coefficients, whereas product quality carries a positive coefficient. All three predictors are statistically significant individually, and the overall model is significant (F = 26.959; p < 0.001) with R = 0.703, R² = 0.494, and adjusted R² = 0.475. The findings suggest that product quality is the most straightforward positive lever for str…

title: Postnatal Tsc2 loss disrupts neuronal development and synaptic integration in cortex
abstract: Introduction Tuberous Sclerosis Complex (TSC) is caused by dysregulated mTOR signaling and is associated with abnormal neuronal development, circuit dysfunction, and epilepsy. However, the developmental timing and mechanisms linking early Tsc2 loss to later network pathology remain unclear. Methods Here, we combined germline Tsc2 haploinsufficiency with focal postnatal deletion in excitatory cortical neurons to define the early cellular and circuit abnormalities that emerge following postnatal Tsc2 loss and precede the age of seizure onset reported in this model. Results Tsc2 loss produced a delayed, genotype-dependent neuronal hypertrophy that emerged by postnatal day 28 and paralleled the loss of TSC2 protein. Over the same developmental period, Tsc2 -deficient neurons exhibited persistent doublecortin expression together with altered NeuN expression. Notably, Tsc2 haploinsufficiency alone altered developmental trajectories, indicating that partial loss of Tsc2 can influence neuronal development independently of focal deletion. Circuit-level alterations emerged despite preserved interneuron density and positioning. Somatostatin interneurons exhibited selective hypertrophy in the two-hit condition, and inhibitory synaptic organization onto Tsc2 -deficient neurons was altered, with increased gephyrin scaffolding occurring alongside reduced somatostatin puncta density and unchan…

title: Successive Storage of Anions and Cations Empowering High-Energy-Density Wide-Temperature-Range Sodium Ion Batteries
abstract: Abstract Organic electrode materials have attracted considerable attention in sodium ion batteries in recent years, yet they still face challenges such as limited energy density, poor cycling stability, and performance degradation under extreme conditions. In this work, a new donor–acceptor (D–A) type monomer, TPA-PTO, based on pyrene-4,5,9,10-tetraone and triphenylamine units is developed, and the pTPA-PTO cathode is successfully constructed through in situ electropolymerization. The pTPA-PTO cathode could successively store Na+ and PF6–, which effectively mitigates concentration polarization and enhances structural stability. Moreover, the electropolymerization further suppresses dissolution and optimizes charge transport. Consequently, pTPA-PTO achieves a high energy density of 697.23 Wh kg–1 at 0.2 A g–1 and demonstrates excellent cycling stability over 1350 cycles. Furthermore, it exhibits long-term durability at 5 A g–1 for 10,000 cycles, with an ultralow capacity decay rate of only 0.0012% per cycle. In addition, the electrode maintains superior performance under high mass loading (7.13 mg cm–2) and across a wide temperature range (–20 to 60 °C). Finally, the pTPA-PTO||HC full cell retains 90% capacity after 2600 cycles at 3 A g–1.

title: Imaging-molecular integration in veterinary oncology: a perspective on evidence standards, validation, and translational readiness
abstract: Abstract Veterinary oncology increasingly generates imaging, pathology, and molecular data, but these layers are often interpreted in parallel rather than linked within clinically testable models. Radiogenomics is used here as a focused form of imaging-molecular integration, whereas multimodal artificial intelligence refers more broadly to models combining imaging, pathology, molecular, biomarker, and clinical variables. Quantitative imaging, radiomics, and pathomics can describe tumour morphology and spatial heterogeneity, whereas molecular biomarkers may provide biological context relevant to prognosis and treatment response. The key challenge is not to add more artificial intelligence to veterinary cancer diagnostics, but to determine when integration adds value beyond clinical, imaging-only, and molecular-only baselines. This Perspective proposes minimum evidence standards for veterinary oncologic radiogenomics and multimodal artificial intelligence, covering animal- and lesion-level linkage, preprocessing, data-leakage control, justified multimodal fusion design, clinically meaningful comparators, calibration, external validation, cautious interpretation of explainability outputs, and transparent reporting. Imaging-molecular artificial intelligence should be treated as a translational research programme, not an immediately deployable diagnostic product.

title: Implementing the energy data space through the OneNet connector
abstract: Abstract The energy sector is undergoing significant changes driven by the rise of distributed energy resources and the progression of digitalisation. This transformation generates vast amounts of data across heterogeneous stakeholders and platforms, creating the need for trusted data exchange while preserving data sovereignty. Data Spaces have emerged as a promising solution to address these challenges. This paper presents and analyses the OneNet Energy Data Space architecture and its implementation through the OneNet Connector and OneNet Middleware. The OneNet solution combines IDS and FIWARE technologies with harmonised Cross-Platform Services and semantic interoperability mechanisms to enable trusted and interoperable data exchange. Functional validation across multiple European demonstrators provided evidence of the feasibility of the OneNet approach for supporting interoperable energy services and flexibility markets, thereby supporting the energy transition.

title: Chemical Crosslinking and Phase Transitions in Refinery-Sourced Sulfur-Extended Bituminous Materials: Effects on Physicochemical and Rheological Properties
abstract: Abstract The upcycling of refinery-sourced elemental sulfur into heavy petroleum fractions (bitumen) represents a sustainable strategy for fossil energy resource management, yet achieving physicochemical stability requires precise control over sulfur reactivity during thermal co-processing. This study systematically investigates how thermal processing parameters govern the chemical crosslinking mechanisms, phase transitions, and rheological evolution of sulfur-extended bituminous materials. Using multi-scale characterization (DSC, fluorescence microscopy, FTIR) coupled with dynamic rheology, we demonstrate that processing conditions critically regulate the balance between physical sulfur dispersion and excessive chemical sulfurization. Moderate thermal processing (140 °C, 1 h) promotes a uniform granular sulfur dispersion and moderate formation of C–S and sulfone bonds. This optimally enhances the high-temperature viscoelastic stability of the binder while preserving its macromolecular mobility and stress relaxation capacity. Conversely, intensified thermal histories drive excessive sulfur polymerization and induce a morphological transition into dendritic crystalline domains. These complex structures act as internal stress concentrators within the rigid crosslinked network, fundamentally compromising the low-temperature flexibility and dynamic shear resistance of the heavy hyd…

title: Artificial intelligence aids multi-omics data integration in cancer drug discovery and development: from targets to drug synergy
abstract: Abstract The emergence of multi-omics technologies has enabled the integration of genomic, transcriptomic, epigenomic, proteomic, and metabolomic data to characterize the molecular complexity of cancer. Single-cell and spatial profiling further resolve intratumoral heterogeneity, cell–cell interactions, and the microenvironmental determinants of therapeutic responses. In parallel, artificial intelligence (AI) provides computational approaches for integrating these heterogeneous data types across target identification, drug response prediction, toxicity assessment, and drug-combination modeling. Across these domains, the available evidence indicates that multi-omics integration is most beneficial when the included layers provide complementary biological information; that single-cell and spatial omics analyses reveal treatment-resistant populations and niches but remain largely research-grade and thus not ready for routine clinical deployment; and that although foundation models support some representation-learning tasks, their advantages in perturbation-response prediction require confirmation via stringent evaluation. By distinguishing externally validated advances from retrospective proof-of-concept studies, we provide a practical framework for evaluating the translational readiness of AI-driven multi-omics tools in precision oncology.

Writing for justice: elementary teacher candidates' social justice integration in interdisciplinary units
abstract: Purpose This study investigates how teacher candidates (TCs) in two distinct teacher preparation pathways developed interdisciplinary literacy-rich social studies (SS) units, integrating writing and social justice themes. Design/methodology/approach Using a concurrent mixed-methods design, we analyzed 17 integrated English Language Arts and SS units produced by an elementary Bachelor of Science in Education (BSE) cohort and Master of Arts in Teaching (MAT) cohort for evidence of awareness, inclusive practices, critical practices and transformative practices. Findings The MAT cohort demonstrated more critical and transformative practices across literacy and SS integration, despite receiving no additional scaffolding. The BSE cohort tended to emphasize inclusive practices through text selection. Research limitations/implications Findings are drawn from two cohorts across two programs and may not be generalizable, though they provide insight into preservice teacher development. Practical implications Preparation programs can strengthen equity-focused practice by embedding scaffolds for anti-racist and transformative pedagogy within standards-aligned instruction. Social implications Supporting preservice teachers in socially just practice can advance equity in classrooms, addressing persistent opportunity gaps. Originality/value This study highlights how program type, diversity and…

title: Modeling and solving workflow scheduling problems on shared computing units with makespan and energy cost objectives
abstract: Abstract This research addresses the workflow scheduling problem on shared computing units. A set of interdependent tasks, originating from a workflow or project, requires processing by computing units such as virtual machines, while respecting precedence constraints and capacity restrictions, for example, in terms of virtual central processing units. The computing units may be heterogeneous or homogeneous in their capacities and cost rates. This problem arises in cloud environments that allow multiple tasks to share resources to improve utilization and reduce energy consumption in accordance with a race-to-idle strategy. We present different mathematical model formulations for this integrated model of workflow scheduling and vector bin packing: a mixed-integer program based on the pulse disaggregated discrete-time formulation, a mixed-integer quadratically constrained program, and a constraint programming satisfiability model, which can be further extended to related scheduling settings. The formulations are evaluated under a makespan objective and under a weighted-sum objective combining makespan and active-unit energy cost. Computational experiments with the Gurobi Optimizer and the CP-SAT solver show that the pulse-based formulation provides the strongest bounds and proves optimality most often, whereas the constraint programming formulation quickly finds high-quality incum…

title: Microwave-Driven Assembly of MTA–COF@CuCo2S4 Hybrid Architectures for High-Performance Water Electrolysis
abstract: Abstract The development of highly efficient and durable dual-functional electrocatalysts for overall water splitting is significant for renewable hydrogen production. This work depicts a novel MTA–COF@CuCo2S4 composite that was successfully fabricated by the integration of a cubic bimetallic sulfide CuCo2S4, with the porous COF matrix. The melamine–terephthalaldehyde COF matrix was successfully synthesized using a microwave-assisted method. Thus, the interaction between the two components makes it a novel electrocatalyst and shows an excellent electrochemical performance for both hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) and oxygen evolution reaction (OER) in alkaline conditions. At a current density of 10 mA cm–2, the composite MTA–COF@CuCo2S4 shows 61 mV (HER) and 260 mV (OER) overpotentials. Furthermore, the composite shows enhanced charge transfer kinetics and significant long-term durability under alkaline conditions, with no appreciable decrease in catalytic performance after 31 h. These findings suggest that the MTA–COF@CuCo2S4 electrocatalyst is a promising electrocatalytic material, highlighting the rational design of a COF-based electrocatalyst for renewable hydrogen production.

title: Numerical investigations of a novel offshore platform blast wall design using energy absorption devices at supports
abstract: Abstract Offshore blast walls are critical safety barriers designed to protect personnel and equipment from hydrocarbon explosions. Traditional designs often struggle to simultaneously satisfy code requirements for deflection limits and weld integrity under high-intensity blasts. This study proposes a novel offshore blast wall concept incorporating energy-absorbing support devices comprising polymethacrylimide (PMI) foam-filled sliding cores and rotational springs. The devices provide flexible support with adjustable translational and rotational stiffness, enabling controlled energy dissipation through foam crushing and spring mechanisms. Finite element analyses were performed to compare the proposed design with traditional Type 1 and Type 2 configurations under strength-level (SLB, 1 bar) and ductility-level (DLB, 3 bar) blast events. Parametric studies further investigated the influences of translational stiffness in the foam elastic range (Kt1), hardening stiffness (Kt2), rotational stiffness (Kr), and blast duration. Results demonstrate that the proposed design significantly outperforms traditional schemes: under SLB, it exhibits negligible plastic deformation (~1 mm vs. 7 mm and 4 mm for traditional designs); under DLB, it limits panel deflection to 167.7 mm (44% reduction) while maintaining support plastic strains at 4.54% (below the 5% rupture limit), whereas traditional…

title: АДАПТИВНА ФІЗИЧНА КУЛЬТУРА ЯК ЗАСІБ ФІЗИЧНОГО РОЗВИТКУ, СОЦІАЛІЗАЦІЇ ТА ІНТЕГРАЦІЇ ДІТЕЙ З ІНВАЛІДНІСТЮ
abstract: The article examines the theoretical foundations of adaptive physical culture as an important means of physical, mental and social development of children with disabilities. The relevance of the use of adaptive physical culture in the modern system of physical education, rehabilitation and inclusive education is substantiated; its importance for meeting the needs of children with disabilities in motor activity, physical development, health promotion, self-realization and social interaction is revealed. The main functions of adaptive physical culture are analyzed, in particular educational, developmental, creative, recreational and health-improving, hedonistic, socializing, integration. The relationship of physical culture activity with the formation of motor skills and abilities, the development of physical qualities, increasing the functional capabilities of the body, the formation of positive self-esteem and the acquisition of social experience is determined. Special attention is paid to the role of adaptive physical culture in the socialization and integration of children with disabilities into society, the development of communication skills and overcoming social isolation. The need for individualization of physical activity is emphasized, taking into account the age, health status, nature of the disorders, physical fitness and psycho-emotional characteristics of the child.…

title: Integration of Condition Index and Risk Score for Maintenance Prioritization of Educational Buildings A Component Level Case Study at Manado State Polytechnic, Indonesia
abstract: Maintenance of educational buildings is often constrained by limited budgets, incomplete condition data, and the absence of transparent maintenance prioritization procedures. This study developed and applied a maintenance prioritization model integrating the Condition Index (CI) and Risk Score (RS) to assess an operational higher education building at Manado State Polytechnic, Indonesia. A systematic visual condition assessment was conducted using 43 component-level observations across 16 rooms or zones and 12 building element categories. The model converted observed physical deterioration into an Element Condition Index (ECI), assessed risk impacts across five dimensions—safety, educational functionality, cost, comfort and health, and operational continuity—and classified building components according to their maintenance priorities. The results revealed a mean ECI of 47.82 and a mean Maintenance Priority Score (MPS) of 6.80, indicating the average condition of the inspected components rather than the overall structural safety of the building. However, the maximum ECI of 80.00 and MPS of 16.00 identified localized components requiring more immediate maintenance attention. Ceilings emerged as the highest-priority building element category within the inspected sample, followed by walls and columns. Components classified as very high priority were identified in rooms R. A112 and …

title: Energy and transport infrastructure is failing the people it serves
abstract: Abstract Low-carbon transitions are often judged by what gets built, but energy and transport systems can remain unusable or unsafe for large parts of the population. This Perspective argues that when research, policy, planning, and finance treat gender equality and social inclusion (GESI) as peripheral, infrastructure becomes selectively functional—delivered on paper but failing in practice—thereby undercutting sustainable development. We outline how exclusion predictably translates into three material risks: reduced national productivity, fiscal inefficiency, and increased climate vulnerability. We then argue that these risks are amplified in today’s political economy, as geopolitical fragmentation and shrinking development aid increase incentives to deprioritise inclusion even as resilience needs intensify. We conclude that GESI must be treated as a core planning process and identify future research priorities for making infrastructure delivery reliably translate into access. We write as a cross-sector group of researchers, policymakers, financiers, and practitioners because this is not a niche academic concern: the success of the energy and transport transition depends on renewable infrastructure being used, which depends on infrastructure being inclusive.

title: Incident-wavefront optimization for energy-efficient digital micromirror device projection
abstract: Abstract Digital micromirror devices (DMDs) are widely employed in maskless lithography, structured illumination, and programmable optical projection. However, the periodic micromirror array distributes the reflected optical power among multiple diffraction orders, only a fraction of which can be collected by projection optics with a finite numerical aperture (NA). Here, we propose a content-independent incident-wavefront optimization method for enhancing finite-NA energy collection in DMD projection. A physics-based differentiable diffraction model is established to describe the effects of the tilted micromirror aperture, periodic lattice, binary projection pattern, incident phase, and finite collection pupil. The incident wavefront is designed under the all-mirror-active state to redistribute optical energy from diffraction orders outside the pupil toward the NA region. Spectral decomposition and perturbation analysis identify conditions for transferring the all-on optimized wavefront to different binary patterns, enabling a single phase design to be reused across projection targets. Numerical simulations show that the NA collection efficiency increases from 27.33 to 71.20% for the all-on state. Experiments using a conjugate spatial light modulator—DMD system validate the predicted intensity enhancement across representative projection patterns. The proposed method provides a…

title: Natural Hydrogen Generation from Siderite–Brine Interactions: Experimental Insights into Temperature and Pressure Effects
abstract: Abstract Iron carbonates and oxides are considered potential contributors to subsurface hydrogen generation alongside the well-established serpentinization process. Among iron carbonates, siderite (FeCO3) has attracted considerable attention because of the presence of Fe2+ in its structure. However, previous studies have focused mostly on synthetic siderite, and the influence of temperature and pressure on hydrogen generation from natural siderite remains poorly constrained. In this study, hydrothermal experiments were conducted using a natural siderite-rich sample from the Georgina Basin, Australia, to quantify hydrogen generation under representative subsurface conditions. The experimental results revealed that temperature strongly controls gas generation, with no detectable H2 or CO2 at 70 °C after 60 days and substantial production of both gases at 200 °C. Under atmospheric pressure at 200 °C, H2 and CO2 yields reached 5.6 and 9.1 mmol kg–1 rock, respectively, increasing to 8.7 and 12.9 mmol kg–1 rock at 100 bar. XPS, XRD, and SEM analyses confirm partial oxidation of Fe2+, dissolution of siderite, and precipitation of secondary magnetite and iron oxides. These findings demonstrate that elevated temperature is essential for H2 generation, while increased pressure further enhances gas production from natural siderite-rich systems, supporting the evaluation of siderite-rich b…

title: Design to operation-built asset productivity and human well-being with digital twins
abstract: Although artificial intelligence (AI)-driven digital twins (DTs) are increasingly promoted for sustainable built asset management, there is limited empirical evidence of their full lifecycle application – particularly in emerging economy contexts that combine technical, environmental, and human-centric performance indicators. This study examines the integration of an AI-enabled DT system across the design, construction, and operational stages of ‘Nirmitee Tower’, a green-certified commercial complex developed by a mid-sized construction firm in Central India. Adopting a mixed-methods case study approach, the research collected triangulated evidence from system analytics, environmental performance metrics, semi-structured interviews, and post-occupancy surveys. Operational definitions were applied for key measures such as material waste, comfort score, and heating, ventilation, and air conditioning energy use, with baselines drawn from comparable pre-DT projects. Key findings include: a 21% reduction in project delivery time, a 35.9% decrease in material waste, a 28.3% reduction in annual energy use, a 21.1% reduction in water consumption, and a 32% improvement in occupant comfort scores. This study contributes by providing a validated, multi-dimensional assessment framework for AI–DT performance, by demonstrating a rare emerging market case of full lifecycle DT integration in a…
venue: Proceedings of the Institution of Civil Engineers - Engineering Sustainability

title: Deep Eutectic Green Solvent-Mediated Design of Irregular-Shape Palladium Nanostructure: A Potent Photocatalyst
abstract: Our work presents an integrated green nanotechnology for fabrication of Pd nanostructure (NS) utilizing the most environmentally benign and cost-effective green solvent, deep eutectic solvent (DES), of choline chloride and citric acid. The DES acts as a stabilizing agent during the reduction of Pd (IV) to Pd (0) particles by NaBH 4 . Characterization of the as-tailored particles via transmission electron microscopy revealed the formation of intricate, irregular, branched-shaped Pd NS owing to the fusion of smaller Pd spherical particles of size 15–40[Formula: see text]nm. The ensuing Pd particles were perfectly crystalline with high purity. These appealing irregular-shaped Pd NS were competent to photodegrade 85% of [Formula: see text][Formula: see text]ppm toxic fungicide hexaconazole during 21[Formula: see text]h and 71.86% of [Formula: see text][Formula: see text]M methylene blue (MB) dye in just 2[Formula: see text]h in aqueous medium. The photocatalytic feature of the Pd NS was attributed mainly to its efficient potential to generate hydroxyl reactive species upon irradiation with light.

title: Molecular mechanisms of male sterility in maize and genome editing-based precision design of hybrid seed production systems
abstract: Male sterility is central to modern maize hybrid seed production because it removes the need for manual emasculation, a labor-intensive and increasingly unscalable practice. This review critically synthesizes the molecular basis of cytoplasmic male sterility (CMS) and genic male sterility (GMS) in maize, focusing on mitochondrial-nuclear genome interaction, tapetal metabolic and developmental disruption, and the additional environmental sensitivity of genic systems (EGMS). In CMS, chimeric mitochondrial open reading frames impair mitochondrial energy metabolism, elevate reactive oxygen species (ROS), and trigger premature tapetal programmed cell death (PCD); nuclear pentatricopeptide-repeat (PPR) restorer-of-fertility (Rf) genes reverse this phenotype in a cytotype- and background-dependent manner. In GMS, hierarchical bHLH and MYB transcription-factor networks direct tapetal differentiation and sporopollenin biosynthesis by integrating lipid and carbohydrate metabolism, hormone signaling, and small-RNA pathways; in EGMS, these networks are further gated by temperature, photoperiod, and protein-quality-control mechanisms. IT is evaluated that genome-editing and synthetic-biology strategies for building precise, scalable sterility systems, distinguishing evidence by validation level. CRISPR/Cas9 is delivered as a transgenic cassette (Cas9, guide RNA and, usually, selectable or v…

title: Association between stage-specific sleep bout durations and obstructive sleep apnea severity: a variable-domain functional regression approach
abstract: The apnea-hypopnea index (AHI), the conventional metric of obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) severity, is typically studied using scalar summaries of sleep architecture, such as the total time spent in each sleep stage. Although clinically interpretable, these summaries fail to capture the temporal organization of overnight sleep-stage sequences and may obscure stage-specific associations with OSA severity. Modeling the stage-specific sequence of sleep bout durations captures how long each stage persists across successive bouts; however, because the number of bouts varies across individuals, these sequences are observed over subject-specific domains, limiting the applicability of conventional functional regression methods that assume a common observation interval. We therefore applied Variable-Domain Functional Regression (VDFR) to overnight polysomnographic data from the APPLES study ( n = 1, 103), treating the stage-specific sequence of sleep bout durations as a variable-length functional predictor of AHI. We compared three levels of sleep-stage granularity: five stages (Wakefulness, N1, N2, N3, and REM), three stages (Wakefulness, Non-REM, and REM), and binary staging (Wakefulness vs. Sleep). In stage-specific models, functional sleep-stage terms were significant across all staging granularities (all p -values < 0.001); longer Wake, N1, and N2 bouts were positively associated…

title: DESIGN OF A STATIC DUAL-CHANNEL WIND CATCHER FOR AIR SUPPLY AND EXHAUST
abstract: The study presents a static dual-channel wind catcher designed to simultaneously supply fresh air and remove exhaust air without moving components. Analysis of existing wind catcher designs showed that most solutions focus primarily on air supply and provide limited separation of supply and exhaust flows. The proposed “pipe-in-pipe” configuration was developed based on an analysis of ventilation grille and deflector calculation methods, equal inlet and outlet cross-sectional areas, and two-dimensional numerical modelling using Energy2D. Numerical and experimental investigations confirmed the functionality of the proposed design and revealed an interdependent relationship between channel dimensions and wind catcher height. An empirical linear relationship was derived to determine the optimal channel diameter ratio depending on wind catcher height. The proposed solution can be applied in new construction and building renovation using existing ventilation ducts, reducing reliance on mechanical ventilation.

title: CARBON FOOTPRINT AS A CRITERION FOR SELECTING EQUIPMENT SETS IN VARIANT-BASED DESIGN OF FOUNDATION CONSTRUCTION TECHNOLOGY
abstract: The article develops the variant-based design methodology for constructing underground parts of buildings by introducing an environmental criterion for evaluating equipment sets. The original methodology involves generating feasible structural and technological alternatives, selecting mobile crane sizes and number, and redistributing work among the machines. In the proposed approach, machine operating time, fuel consumption and CO₂-equivalent emissions are additionally determined for each equipment set. This enables alternatives to be compared not only by technological and economic indicators but also by carbon footprint. Particular attention is paid to the relationship between machine size, element consolidation, number of cycles and operating time. It is hypothesised that a smaller machine does not always give a lower carbon footprint, as lower specific energy consumption may be accompanied by more cycles and longer operating time.

title: Endovascular robotic-assisted system for cerebral angiography (ERASE): Rationale, design, and protocol of a multicenter randomized controlled trial
