Physics-constrained inverse neural estimation (PINE) of NO x emission spatial patterns from TROPOMI NO 2 columns over the North China Plain
abstract: Satellite NO 2 columns constrain where nitrogen oxides (NO x ) are emitted, but conventional inversions are costly or depend on existing emission products. We present physics-constrained inverse neural estimation (PINE), applied to NO x as PINE-NO x : a neural encoder maps Sentinel-5P/TROPOMI NO 2 columns to emissions, and a fixed, differentiable two-dimensional transport–chemistry decoder maps them back. We retrieve annual, monthly and overpass-time daily emission patterns over the North China Plain at 0.1° for 2023, with the annual total normalized to the EDGAR inventory; the observations adjust the daily relative pattern around this prior, which still sets the magnitude and large-scale structure. On 54 validation days used only to select the training epoch, the retrieved emissions raise the log-space spatial correlation between simulated and observed columns from 0.332 (EDGAR) to 0.856 (observation reconstruction, not emission accuracy). PINE-NO x places less emission than EDGAR in the strongest-emitting cells, but a synthetic test with known emissions gives a similar decrease, so this shift is primarily a structural artefact, most likely of this decoder, not an observed signal. Relative to MEIC, which the inversion does not use, 13.5 % of July emissions are placed in different 0.5° cells, against 18.5 % in the synthetic test and 20.5 % for EDGAR; January shows no clear gain…

title: Green fiscal policy, carbon emissions, and environmental sustainability: Evidence from Malaysia
abstract: This study examined the impact of green fiscal policy on carbon emissions and environmental sustainability for Malaysia, by using time series data from 1988 to 2020. The study employs the Autoregressive Distributed Lag (ARDL) model and the Error Correction Model (ECM) to demonstrate both short-term and long-term relationships between carbon emissions per capita and environmental taxes, energy consumption, green technological innovations, population density, and real GDP per capita. This paper also observed an inverted U relationship between economic growth and carbon emissions, which backed the Environmental Kuznets Curve (EKC) hypothesis. The results reveal evidence supporting the Environmental Kuznets Curve (EKC) hypothesis, indicating an inverted U-shaped relationship between economic growth and carbon emissions. In the short run, environmental taxes, energy consumption, and population density significantly increase carbon emissions. In the long run, economic growth and population density remain significant determinants of emissions, while green technological innovation shows a delayed but positive contribution to environmental sustainability. The findings suggest that green fiscal policy can play an important role in supporting Malaysia’s transition toward a low-carbon economy. However, stronger p…

title: Measuring uncertainty and prospects: evaluating blue carbon ecosystem measures in Taiwan
abstract: Taiwan has officially included marine carbon as part of its carbon offset framework in its greenhouse gas (GHG) emission reduction target, set at a level of a 23%–25% reduction by 2030, and net-zero carbon emissions by 2050. This analytical piece thus draws on a simple form of multicriteria analysis to evaluate the status of, and identify issues plaguing, the development of Taiwan’s blue carbon ecosystem (BCE) measures. The picture is quite murky. Contribution of marine carbon to GHG emission reduction is theoretically proven and officially included in Taiwan’s methodology for GHG emission reduction (theoretically proven impact). Subsequent follow-up on the development of Taiwan’s BCE measures is a worthy effort. However, the bureaucratic complex—comprising low bureaucratic capacity, caused by a conglomeration of the prevalence of the developmentalism mindset, overwhelming influences from high-energy-consumption industries, and the resulting fragmented view in policy design of Taiwan’s carbon dioxide removal (CDR) measures—has substantially impacted the development of Taiwan’s BCE measures. Given this reality, it would not be surprising if the effect of BCE measures were attenuated (attenuated effect), while the relevance exhibited in the policy outcome and original objectives remains weak (weak relevance). Policy flexibility and predictability of BCE measures have collaterally…

title: Orientation-Controlled In-Material Physical Reservoirs Based on Polymer-Wrapped Carbon Nanotube Nanofilms
abstract: Abstract Semiconducting polymer poly(m-phenylenevinylene-co-2,5-dioctoxy-p-phenylenevinylene) (PmPV)-wrapped single-walled carbon nanotube (SWCNT–PmPV) nanofilms were fabricated using the Langmuir–Blodgett (LB) method to investigate the effects of structural orientation on their electrical and reservoir computing properties. Polarized ultraviolet–visible absorption spectroscopy and atomic force microscopy revealed that repeated compression–expansion cycles during LB deposition produced highly oriented SWCNT nanofilms. The oriented films exhibited an anisotropic electrical response, pronounced hysteretic current–voltage characteristics, and enhanced generation of higher-order harmonics, while water adsorption further enhanced the current and nonlinear electrical response. In waveform generation tasks, the advantage of the highly oriented films was most pronounced for the sawtooth and sin(2ω) targets, which involve more complex waveform features and frequency components. Additional delayed-input reconstruction and nonlinear autoregressive moving average (NARMA) 2 tasks revealed enhanced fading memory and nonlinear temporal processing under humidified conditions, with the highly oriented film exhibiting a larger memory capacity and lower NARMA2 error than the less-oriented film. These results indicate that structural orientation, together with humidity-dependent electrical dynamic…

title: Regional variation in database-derived soil organic carbon and its associations with vegetation and the environment in the coniferous forests of the Greater and Lesser Khingan Mountains
abstract: Introduction Northeastern China’s conifer forests constitute important components of the world’s carbon cycle. However, whether soil organic carbon (SOC) is associated with the same environmental and biotic pathways across the Greater Khingan Mountains (GKM) and Lesser Khingan Mountains (LKM) remains unclear. Methods Using data from 282 plots in GKM and 334 plots in LKM, together with soil carbon data from CSDLv2, we conducted regional comparisons, Spearman correlations, and structural equation modelling to identify the environmental and biotic factors associated with SOC in GKM and LKM. Results We found that aboveground tree carbon stock (AGTC) was higher in LKM than in GKM (71.76 versus 55.81 Mg C ha −1 , but this difference was not significant ( p > 0.05). By contrast, SOC concentration was higher in GKM than in LKM (5.9 vs. 4.98 g/100 g; p < 0.05). The Spearman test showed that ectomycorrhizal trees (EcM_T) were positively correlated with SOC in both regions (LKM: r = 0.48; GKM: r = 0.46, p < 0.05). MAT had positive correlations in the LKM ( r = 0.3, p < 0.05) but negative correlations in the GKM ( r = −0.62, respectively, p < 0.05). Structural equation models further identified the positive total effects of EcM_T on SOC between GKM and LKM. MAT had the biggest total effect (−0.52, 37%) on SOC in GKM, while MAP had the strongest positive effect (0.28, 36%) in…

title: Continuous Molecular-Scale Welding of Carbon Nanotubes into Cellulose Yarns for Robust, Multisensory All-Textile Electronics
abstract: Abstract The seamless integration of electronic functionalities into sustainable textile architectures is foundational for next-generation wearable intelligence. However, achieving high electrical performance without compromising the inherent comfort and durability of natural fibers remains a persistent challenge. Herein, we report a continuous manufacturing strategy for robust conductive yarns via phosphoric acid-mediated molecular-scale welding technique. By precisely controlling the partial dissolution and in situ regeneration of cellulose chains, carbon nanotubes (CNTs) are architecturally “locked” within the reorganized molecular framework of yarns. This structural reconfiguration establishes a highly efficient, shielded charge transport network, yielding an outstanding electrical conductivity of 334.6 S m⁻ 1 at an ultralow CNT loading (11.2 wt%). The resulting Welded Cellulose/CNT Yarns (WCCYs) exhibit exceptional interfacial adhesion, delivering superior mechanical tenacity and laundry durability that surpass conventional coated fibers. Leveraging these synergistic properties, we demonstrate an all-textile, multisensory platform capable of concurrent, high-fidelity monitoring of biomechanical deformations, physiological signatures, and environmental stimuli (humidity and volatile organics). The WCCY-based system enables precise respiratory pattern tracking and fine-grain…

A supercapacitor-assisted cyclic battery recharging method for solar and wind power systems
abstract: The efficient use of solar and wind electricity in stand-alone power systems for remote facilities is limited during periods of reduced generation, when the source voltage may fall below the activation threshold of the charge controller. Under such conditions, direct battery recharging becomes impossible despite the availability of residual energy from the renewable source. This paper investigates a cyclic battery recharging method based on preliminary energy accumulation in supercapacitor modules and their subsequent discharge into the battery. The proposed approach was evaluated using a MATLAB/Simulink simulation model and a physical experimental setup with 166 F and 500 F supercapacitor modules and lead-acid batteries. The results show that preliminary energy storage in supercapacitor modules followed by controlled discharge enables additional battery recharging when the source voltage is insufficient for direct charging through the controller. For the 166 F modules, the duration of the complete first cycle was approximately 8.3 min, while for the 500 F modules it was approximately 28.5 min. Repeated cycles started from the residual voltage of the supercapacitor modules, which reduced the duration of the subsequent charging stages. The deviation between the simulated and experimental voltage characteristics did not exceed 3.5% in the most important operating regions and rema…

title: Peer versus teacher-assigned medical student grades
abstract: Background Teachers evaluate students’ academic progress and performance in the conventional education system. However, recent studies suggest that peer assessment offers a range of learning benefits and can effectively complement traditional sole teacher assessment. We evaluated the effectiveness of peer assessment alongside traditional teacher assessment in medical education. Methods Students were tasked with framing a set of questions for a chosen topic. A question paper was then created from the question bank. A pre-validated answer key with subdivisions of scores was prepared. Following the written examination, the answer key was displayed and used for the correction of anonymized answer papers, first by a peer and then by a teacher. This entire exercise was repeated for a different topic, providing comprehensive feedback. The scores allotted by the peers and teachers were then compared. Results On test 1, among the 94 students, the mean (standard deviation [SD]) score was 20.99 (4.30) for peer assessment and 20.72 (4.10) for teacher assessment. On test 2, the mean (SD) score was 22.22 (7.37) and 23.35 (5.81) for peer and teacher assessment, respectively. For each test, the correlation between peers and teacher grades was found to be 0.77 and 0.60. Conclusion Students are capable of designing a concise, valid, open-ended question paper. The difference in scores between the…

title: Five-year outcomes of machine perfusion versus static cold storage in controlled donation after circulatory death kidney transplantation: a binational cohort study
abstract: While hypothermic machine perfusion reduces delayed graft function (DGF) after kidney transplantation, its long-term benefits in controlled donation after circulatory death (DCD) are uncertain in real-world practice. We evaluated whether perfusion improves 5-year death-censored graft survival compared to static cold storage in DCD by benchmarking outcomes against those of donation after brain death (DBD). After analyzing the United Network for Organ Sharing and Swiss Transplant Cohort Study registries, we created a 1:1 propensity-score-matched cohort to balance baseline characteristics. Among 44,552 DCD recipients (34,739 with perfusion; 9,813 with cold storage) and 180,898 DBD controls, the matched 5-year death-censored graft survival rate was 84.8% with perfusion versus 87.4% with cold storage (hazard ratio 1.08; P = 0.19). Perfusion significantly reduced the rate of DGF (35.7% vs. 44.9%; P < 0.001), while the rates of primary nonfunction and acute rejection were comparable. Both DCD groups achieved long-term outcomes equivalent to those of the DBD cohort. In conclusion, while machine perfusion confers a substantial early reduction in delayed graft function, static cold storage continues to deliver excellent 5-year graft survival. Both strategies yield excellent long-term outcomes comparable to those of DBD transplants. Crucially, these findings support expanding DCD progr…

title: Confined intercalation and non-equilibrium joule heating conversion synergistically constructing SiOx@C composite for lithium storage
Four common lithium battery recycling methods: a mini review
abstract: Abstract The booming lithium battery industry has led to a surging accumulation of spent lithium batteries, posing a significant environmental and resource challenge. These end-of-life batteries are rich sources of valuable metals, including lithium, nickel, cobalt, and manganese. Against this backdrop, recycling lithium battery cathode materials has emerged as a research frontier of global importance. This comprehensive review delves into the current research landscape of commonly used lithium battery cathode materials, spanning lithium iron phosphate (LFP), lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide (NCM), lithium manganese oxide (LMO), and lithium cobalt oxide (LCO) cathode materials. Beyond mere description, it critically examines the multifaceted challenges plaguing spent lithium battery recycling, from technical and economic hurdles to environmental concerns. Furthermore, it proposes strategic future directions for advancing recycling technologies. By synthesizing existing knowledge and identifying research gaps, this study aims to provide robust theoretical foundations and practical insights to guide further exploration in the recycling of spent lithium batteries, ultimately contributing to the sustainability of the lithium battery industry and circular economy initiatives.

title: Large-signal stability analysis of reduced-order droop-controlled grid-forming inverters in islanded microgrids
abstract: Abstract Islanded inverter-dominated microgrids are vulnerable to large disturbances because power-electronic resources provide little inherent inertia. This study develops a tractable nonlinear model for assessing transient angle stability of parallel droop-controlled grid-forming inverters. A five-state nonlinear model of a two-bus microgrid is reduced to three states using a fixed-reference-bus approximation. Equilibrium consistency, linearized dominant modes, and transient trajectories are compared with the full-order model. A Lyapunov candidate is constructed to characterize the region of attraction, and phase portraits and fault simulations are used to evaluate power-measurement filter bandwidth and line resistance-to-reactance ratio. The reduced model reproduces the full-order equilibrium with voltage errors below 0.8 % and frequency errors below 0.07 %, while transient trajectory errors remain below approximately 3.2 %. Low filter cutoff frequencies increase the initial angle-deviation rate and values near 0.5 Hz lead to loss of synchronism. Increasing the line resistance-to-reactance ratio reduces synchronizing strength; trajectories diverge at ratios near 5.1, and post-fault recovery is lost at higher ratios. Additional simulations under varying loading conditions, droop gains, and static virtual impedance demonstrate good reduced-model accuracy under strong-reference…

Brand Experience Strategy in Building Wardah's Brand Awareness Through Skinverse Campaign
abstract: Brands with already high levels of brand awareness face challenges that differ from those of emerging brands, particularly in maintaining relevance and memorability amid increasingly intense competition. This study examines Wardah's brand experience strategy through the Skinverse campaign, which was conducted in 2024, 2025, and 2026, and its potential contribution to brand awareness. The study employs a qualitative approach with a case study design based on document analysis. Data were obtained from company press releases, 17 articles published by national online media outlets, and Top Brand Index data from 2022 to 2026. These sources were analyzed through deductive coding based on Schmitt's five Strategic Experiential Modules (SEMs). The findings reveal that Skinverse evolved from a science-based educational exhibition in 2024 to an artificial intelligence (AI)-powered skincare clinic in 2025, followed by a skin longevity clinic integrating skin health with lifestyle factors in 2026. Throughout this evolution, the experiential emphasis shifted from the Think module toward the Act module. The document analysis identified four potential mechanisms for strengthening brand awareness: the consistent use of the Skinverse campaign name as a distinctive brand asset; MURI (Indonesian World Records Museum) records and collaborations with experts as drivers of media coverage; personalize…

title: Establishment of simplified purification strategy for cancer antigen CA 15 − 3 from ascitic fluid of breast cancer patients
Rescuing declining schools: A data-driven turnaround strategy through a human resource management lens
abstract: This qualitative multiple-case study examines how data-driven decision-making and human resource management (HRM) were understood and used in three secondary schools experiencing decline. Data were drawn from semi-structured interviews with 15 participants, non-participant observations, and school documents. The findings identify four interrelated phases in the schools’ turnaround processes: data-based diagnosis, strategic intervention design, phased implementation, and continuous monitoring. Across the cases, documented practices included the use of performance information to identify school needs, professional development and coaching, performance feedback, staff collaboration, and monitoring of selected indicators. Participants’ accounts suggest that these practices may help connect organizational diagnosis with staff development and school-improvement planning. However, the study does not establish that HRM practices caused improvements in employee outcomes or sustained school recovery. The resulting human-capital-centered model should therefore be understood as an evidence-informed interpretation and a proposition for further application and evaluation, rather than a validated causal model.

title: Gender diversity as a strategic governance capability in the age of AI
abstract: Purpose This paper aims to reframe board gender diversity as a strategic governance capability rather than a symbolic initiative or universal performance lever. It explains inconsistent diversity–performance findings and clarifies when diversity may strengthen oversight in algorithmically mediated environments. Design/methodology/approach Drawing on structured evidence mapping and interdisciplinary research in corporate governance, leadership, efficiency economics, organizational demography and artificial intelligence (AI) governance, the paper develops a structured integrative conceptual synthesis focused on power, expertise–authority alignment and technological oversight. Findings Diversity effects are contingent rather than automatic. Board gender diversity is most likely to strengthen governance when three enabling conditions are present: representation thresholds that convert presence into voice, expertise aligned with authority and inclusive power structures that enable challenge. Under algorithmic complexity, these conditions may strengthen oversight of bias, explainability, privacy, cybersecurity, vendor dependence and technocratic capture. Practical implications Boards and policymakers should move beyond numerical representation to structural influence. Diverse directors should occupy consequential committees, have relevant expertise and decision rights and be supporte…

title: Configuring strategic action: a comparative study of top management teams and the microfoundations of strategy
abstract: Purpose This study examines how and why practitioners, practices and praxis (3Ps) become configured differently across contrasting organizational contexts. Through a comparative study of a university hospital and a private hospital, it investigates how organizational and institutional conditions shape practitioner agency, the function of formal and informal practices, the direction of strategic activity and the meanings attached to strategy work in reliability-seeking organizations. Design/methodology/approach We employ a qualitative comparative case-study design, drawing on 57 semi-structured interviews, archival documents and observational data from a state-affiliated university hospital and a privately owned hospital group located in Antalya, Türkiye. Data were analyzed through an abductive process combining inductive within-case thematic analysis with theoretically informed cross-case comparison. Findings Similar committees, reports, informal interactions and analytical tools produced distinct configurations of strategic action because authority, evaluative criteria, temporal pressures and knowledge were organized differently. In the university hospital, layered authority, professional legitimacy and long-tenured knowledge carriers combined custodial agency with institutional sensemaking; operational issues therefore moved upward for formal authorization, producing upward l…

title: Enhanced overload current suppression strategy based on adaptive voltage reference and hybrid feed-forward
abstract: Purpose This study is conducted to address overcurrent protection and transient voltage recovery in three-phase three-wire inverters. The primary objective of this study is to enhance the response speed of overload current suppression and prevent integrator saturation, thereby ensuring the operational reliability and rapid voltage restoration of stand-alone systems under extreme load conditions. Design/methodology/approach An adaptive voltage reference adjustment strategy is proposed based on real-time load impedance identification. The voltage reference is dynamically modulated through impedance estimation. Additionally, a hybrid feed-forward compensation mechanism is investigated to enhance the response speed during reference transitions and provide stability against abrupt load variations. Findings Simulation and experimental results demonstrate that the overload current is restricted within 0.5 fundamental cycles, with overshoot suppressed by over 50%. Furthermore, the voltage recovery time after overload clearance is notably reduced, and PI integrator windup is effectively eliminated, ensuring superior transient performance. Originality/value This work synergistically integrates impedance-based adaptive modulation with hybrid feed-forward compensation. Unlike conventional hard-clamping methods, the proposed strategy maintains control loop integrity and enhances the transie…

title: Building Direct-to-Consumer Capabilities in India: A Qualitative Study of Strategy, Scale, and Acquisition
abstract: Direct-to-consumer (D2C) brands have become central to India's consumer economy, reshaping how firms build brand equity, collect consumer data, and compete across digital and physical channels. Recent estimates place India's D2C market in the US$10–12 billion range in FY26, with forecasts toward US$60 billion by 2030, while Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities now account for a large share of new orders. At the same time, large FMCG firms are increasingly acquiring D2C brands to enter premium categories, access younger consumers, and obtain digital-first capabilities more quickly than they could build internally. This qualitative study draws on journal articles, annual reports, corporate press releases, and media coverage to examine how Indian D2C brands such as Minimalist, Wakefit, and Yoga Bar have scaled, and why incumbents are buying them. The paper argues that D2C should be understood as an organisational capability system rather than a simple sales channel, and that the current Indian market is entering a consolidation phase in which successful D2C brands are becoming strategic acquisition targets.

title: A River Ecosystem Restoration Strategy Based on Geological Characteristics and Environmental Quality in the Boyong River, Sleman
abstract: The Boyong River on the slopes of Mount Merapi exhibits high geomorphological dynamics and environmental quality due to the supply of volcanic material from repeated eruptions. This study aims to examine the geological and geomorphological characteristics, water quality, and riparian vegetation conditions along a ±2 km segment of the river as a basis for formulating ecosystem restoration strategies. Field observations were conducted through lithological identification, landform mapping, river cross-section measurements, analysis of water quality parameters (pH, temperature, TDS, DHL, and Fe), and evaluation of riparian vegetation. The results showed that easily eroded young volcanic breccia was the primary source of sedimentation, leading to channel siltation and slope instability. Variations in water quality reflect the influence of volcanic material weathering and high suspended sediment loads, while riparian vegetation exhibits uneven density, affecting bank stability. Integration of all parameters confirms the need for a restoration strategy based on sediment control, riparian vegetation enhancement, channel normalization, and sustainable water quality management.

title: The 2020 anti-power harassment law – boon or bane? Investigating its impact on Japanese listed firms
abstract: Purpose Recently, cases of abuse of authority and bullying in the workplace, known as “power harassment,” have been rising in Japan. In response to power harassment, the Japanese government enacted an anti-power harassment law in 2020, mandating firms to take measures to prevent and address this issue in the workplace. Considering the uniqueness and criticality of the anti-power harassment law, this study aims to investigate its effects on Japanese listed firms, focusing on employee well-being and firm performance. Design/methodology/approach Using panel data on approximately 2,400 firm-year observations for listed Japanese firms (2018–2021), this study combines financial, governance and employee-related data with adjustments for outliers. A difference-in-differences model with firm and year fixed effects is used to estimate the impact of the 2020 anti-power harassment law. Findings In addition to decreasing the paid leave take-up rate, the law increases firms’ market value. Moreover, employees voluntarily prioritize task involvement over downtime caused by heightened work engagement resulting from an improved workplace environment. Practical implications This study supports the mutual gains theory and focuses on a unique Japanese regulation, offering practical insights for foreign regulators and policymaking institutions. Originality/value This study focuses on a unique Japane…

title: Exploring Traditional and Contemporary Retail Factors Shaping Customer Perceptions of Organised Retailing in Thanjavur District, Tamil Nadu
abstract: Organised retailing in India’s semi-urban and district-level markets is shaped by both established store-based attributes and emerging technology-enabled attributes. This study identifies and empirically validates the traditional and contemporary factors that shape customer perception of organised retailing in Thanjavur District, Tamil Nadu. Data were collected from 536 respondents using a structured questionnaire comprising 40 traditional-factor items and 20 contemporary-factor items, together with measures of customer perception, satisfaction, loyalty and repurchase intention. Following data screening, reliability analysis, sampling-adequacy diagnostics and exploratory factor analysis with varimax rotation were performed on the 60 traditional and contemporary items. The Kaiser–Meyer–Olkin value (.853) and Bartlett’s test of sphericity (χ² = 9,898.742, df = 1,770, p < .001) confirmed the suitability of the data for factor analysis. Parallel analysis supported the retention of eight empirical factors, which together explained 45.62 per cent of the total variance and demonstrated acceptable-to-good internal consistency (α = .648 to .866). In line with the analysis, the originally hypothesised thirteen sub-dimensions eight traditional and five contemporary were not empirically reproduced; instead, the items regrouped into a more defensible eight-factor structure that largely sepa…

title: Prevalence of benzalkonium chloride tolerance in Listeria monocytogenes isolated from retail meats in Japan
Stitching innovation in fashion retail: a systematic review of barriers to digital technology adoption, including AI and marketing automation, in women-led SMEs
abstract: Purpose This study systematically reviews barriers to digital technology adoption, including artificial intelligence (AI) and marketing automation (MA), in contexts relevant to women-led small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in fashion and related retail, interpreted through the extended technology acceptance model (TAM++). Design/methodology/approach Following PRISMA 2020, a Web of Science search (2015–2026) retrieved 2,507 records. After screening and a two-reviewer eligibility assessment of 53 records, 25 studies were included. Their full texts were thematically analyzed in MAXQDA, and the resulting categories were interpreted through the three TAM++ thematic categories. Findings Eight categories were identified. Facilitating conditions, social influence, skill gaps/managerial expertise and financial constraints appeared in all 25 studies, followed by job relevance (24), perceived risk and privacy concerns (21), work-life/caregiving conflict (19) and digital trust/security (18). The categories span user, task and technological, social and environmental aspects. All eight also appeared in the 13 studies, including fashion businesses, where costs and task fit received greater emphasis. Research limitations/implications The evidence base is small and mainly concerns related digital technologies: two studies examine AI directly, none examine MA directly and four draw their s…

title: Reciprocal haptic cross-entropy links Gibsonian specification and Shannon uncertainty in human gait
abstract: Ecological psychology treats information as a relation that specifies an environmental source and its affordances, whereas Shannon theory quantifies uncertainty among alternatives. We propose a limited operational bridge between these views for haptic locomotion. Knee posture is represented by a finite helical axis reconstructed from consecutive thigh and shank marker configurations, and touch is represented by the ground reaction force line. Their canonical Klein product defines a signed reciprocal separation for every posture–touch pairing. Because the initial position of the knee axis family in the laboratory frame was unknown, one unconstrained three-dimensional translation was estimated from all synchronized pairs and interpreted as a coordinate boundary condition rather than an anatomical displacement. The verified analysis used 120 pairs (first knee transition index 29), yielding a translation of [33.585, −1296.928, −112.445] mm and a median post-registration line separation of 5.555 mm. Gaussian compatibility scores over the complete pairwise separation matrix produced a posture-to-touch cross-entropy of 2.993 nats. We correct an important mathematical point: with one-hot synchronized targets, this cross-entropy equals a Kullback–Leibler divergence and is distinct from the entropy of the predicted conditional distribution. Cross-entropy measures relative temporal specif…

title: Influential dynamic interactions of safe havens with facets of economic and monetary uncertainty
abstract: Purpose This study aims to investigate the dynamic causal connectedness that a range of innovative uncertainty measures presents with gold and silver prices. Design/methodology/approach Monthly data from January 1985 to January 2024 and averaged dynamic connectedness and network dynamic connectedness based on the advanced quantile-vector autoregression framework are used. Findings The impact that risk stemming from economic, monetary, fiscal or trade uncertainty has on precious metals is estimated. Gold and silver are found to behave as drivers of impacts in bear markets but as absorbers of spillovers in bull markets, especially silver. This also holds for economic policy uncertainty (EPU), which is succinctly the dominant form of risk and is mostly linked with monetary policy uncertainty. Fiscal and trade policies create risk in flourishing eras when absorbers such as silver, gold or EPU are most needed to mitigate uncertainty in markets. Originality/value This paper provides insights for policymakers and investors in normal and crisis periods.

title: A Method to Reduce the Factors Affecting Iodine Enhancement for Computed Tomography Contrast Optimization
abstract: Purpose: Iodine contrast enhancement is assessed using computed tomography (CT) number, though this value is not proportional to iodine concentration. This study develops a metric for iodine enhancement that is directly proportional to iodine concentration. Materials and Methods: Using studies previously reported in the literature, we parameterized the effect to create a correction for tube potential and patient-size-specific beam hardening on iodine CT number decrease. To validate the correction, we performed a study using different iodine concentrations, phantom sizes, and tube potentials. We also applied the correction to patient pulmonary angiogram data. Patients were grouped by tube potential [80, 100, 120, 140] (kV). Quantitative iodine contrast enhancement (Q-ICE) (ie, the difference between noncontrast and contrast-enhanced CT number) of the pulmonary artery (PA) was calculated. Pearson correlation coefficients are reported to characterize trends in PA Q-ICE across weight before and after correction. Results: The range of CT numbers measured for [10, 15] mg/mL iodine inserts was [290, 433] HU before correction, and [24, 36] HU after correction. Before correction, median PA Q-ICE enhancement was [662, 490, 263, 175] HU for [80, 100, 120, 140] kV, with a range of 487 HU observed across all measurements. After correction, the median PA Q-ICE enhancement was [366, 373, 285,…

title: Non-equilibrium condensation characteristics and suppression optimization in supercritical CO 2 compressor for hypersonic aircraft applications
abstract: Abstract In the supercritical carbon dioxide (sCO 2 ) closed Brayton cycle for hypersonic vehicle thermal protection, non-equilibrium condensation readily takes place near the compressor inlet, inducing aerodynamic degradation and flow instability. A numerical framework is established based on the Kantrowitz non-isothermal nucleation model and the Young droplet growth model, coupled with a Span-Wagner equation-of-state property database via user-defined functions. Validated against the Lettieri’s converging-diverging nozzle experimental data, the maximum relative error in condensation onset location is 3.58 %. The effects of mass flow rate, inlet pressure, and inlet temperature on condensation are systematically investigated, and an elliptical leading-edge optimization is proposed to suppress condensation. Results reveal that the dominant condensation mechanism shifts from near-critical thermodynamic driving to local expansion acceleration within 306–308 K. An elliptical leading edge with an aspect ratio AR = 5 delivers the optimal overall performance, attaining an approximately 3.5 % higher isentropic efficiency than the baseline case under design-point conditions. This study provides a reference for anti-condensation design of sCO 2 compressors.

title: Real-time manipulability optimization with whole-arm obstacle avoidance for redundant manipulators via projection neural dynamics
abstract: Online motion of a redundant manipulator in a cluttered workspace has to reconcile end-effector tracking with two further goals: keeping every link clear of obstacles and staying away from kinematic singularities. Existing reactive and task-priority schemes usually address these goals separately or sacrifice tracking once whole-arm avoidance is added; the non-convex manipulability measure further burdens joint-space optimization. This article proposes the obstacle avoidance manipulability optimization (OAMO) scheme. A first-order Taylor expansion of manipulability with Tikhonov damping removes the gradient instability near singularities; tracking, manipulability enhancement, and link-level avoidance are then assembled into a single quadratic program (QP) in joint-velocity space with joint-velocity/joint-acceleration box constraints and distance-activated half-space constraints; the QP is solved by a projection neural dynamics recursion with an analytical proof of global convergence to the Karush–Kuhn–Tucker (KKT) optimum. On a 6-degree of freedom redundant manipulator (UR5e in our simulation), three case studies are reported: fixed-position reconfiguration, closed-contour tracking, and an obstacle-laden spiral. They show that OAMO consistently raises manipulability, preserves link-to-obstacle clearance, achieves a 1 0 − 3 m -level mean tracking error, and runs at a millisecond-…

title: Three-dimensional shale-volume mapping using stochastic extended elastic impedance inversion and a probabilistic neural network in the Karina carbonate field
abstract: Characterizing carbonate reservoirs remains challenging due to high lateral and vertical heterogeneity, particularly related to Vshale content, which directly affects reservoir quality. Conventional approaches, such as acoustic impedance inversion, often fail to adequately resolve these complexities. This study focuses on the Baturaja Formation in the Karina Field, Sunda Basin, a carbonate reservoir characterized by thick facies and multiple growth cycles, where 3D heterogeneity significantly influences oil production. To address these challenges, an advanced workflow integrating Extended Elastic Impedance (EEI) inversion, stochastic inversion, and Probability Neural Network (PNN) was applied. The process began with seismic gather conditioning, chi-angle optimization, and EEI inversion. The vertical resolution of the inversion was further enhanced using stochastic inversion through structural modelling, variogram analysis, and sequential Gaussian simulation. The resulting EEI outputs were then employed as training data for PNN to predict 3D Vshale distribution. The integrated approach yielded a 90% correlation with well-derived Vshale, showing the effectiveness of EEI in direct Vshale prediction and the value of stochastic inversion in improving vertical resolution. PNN predictions identified low Vshale zones around paleo highs and other areas, confirmed against well logs, core…

title: Predictive Auto Scaling and Cloud Cost Optimization Using Machine Learning
abstract: Cloud applications experience fluctuating demand, requiring resource controllers to balance infrastructure cost against service performance. Reactive autoscaling changes capacity after monitored utilization crosses a threshold; predictive autoscaling attempts to provision resources before demand materializes. This paper evaluates a machine-learning-assisted autoscaling approach using a reproducible synthetic workload benchmark. A deterministic generator produces 40,000 five-minute observations with daily and weekly seasonality, autoregressive variation, noise, and burst events. Historical lag and rolling-window features support a 15-minute-ahead request-demand forecast. Persistence, Random Forest, histogram-based gradient boosting, and XGBoost are considered, with chronological train, validation, and test partitions. Across five random seeds, XGBoost obtains mean absolute error of 163.87 requests (standard deviation 1.97), root mean squared error of 208.83 (4.35), and coefficient of determination of 0.7373 (0.0086). In a separate single-seed controller replay, predictive scaling reduces normalized instance-hour cost by approximately 0.29% relative to a reactive threshold policy. However, the fraction of intervals above the 70% CPU proxy rises from 2.70% to 4.39%. These results show that forecast accuracy alone does not guarantee operational improvement. The benchmark is synthet…

title: EGGS-WG: an open source global gridded stochastic weather generator derived from ERA5-Land
abstract: A new open source and freely available stochastic weather generator, the ERA5-land Global Gridded Stochastic Weather Generator (EGGS-WG), is publicly available. This model offers several advancements over existing alternative stochastic weather generators, including the ability to simulate any terrestrial region of the planet, moving from simulating a single site to an entire gridded domain and increasing the temporal resolution of temperature simulation from daily to hourly. EGGS-WG is designed to be as low resource and portable as possible, ensuring ease of use for any potential end user. This paper describes in detail all of the principles that are used in the model design and code implementation. Preliminary tests are performed over five climatically distinct regions to confirm the ability of the model to reproduce the behavior of the ERA5-Land dataset. Precipitation occurrence rates and daily rainfall amounts are shown to be reproduced accurately by the model with a range of attributes investigated, including seasonality, spatial correlations and rainfall spells. However, some clear issues remain in the simulation of the most extreme precipitation values. Similar analysis is also performed for the air temperature and dew point temperature, showing stronger agreement than the precipitation data. EGGS-WG is designed with a focus on potential future developments, including su…

title: Harmonic Lyrebird Optimization with PyramidNet for Interested Region Selection-Based Image Steganography with Elliptic Curve Cryptography
abstract: Image steganography is the technique of embedding a hidden message inside an image file in a manner that makes the message difficult to detect. This technique enables covert communication by embedding data into the least significant bits of the image pixels, preserving the image’s overall appearance. Most of the previous research did not provide adequate protection against sophisticated attacks aimed at extracting or altering hidden information. Also, many existing algorithms did not adapt well to varying image characteristics or content, limiting their effectiveness. These issues are overcome by developing a new Harmonic Lyrebird Optimization Algorithm (HLOA) method to train the PyramidNet to identify regions of interest in cover images for steganography. Initially, the cover image is passed through a gridding process. Next, the cover image is converted into the frequency domain by applying the Discrete Cosine Transform (DCT). In the next step, the interested region selection is carried out by applying PyramidNet, which is fine-tuned by utilizing the designed HLOA. HLOA is the integration of harmonic analysis and the Lyrebird Optimization Algorithm (LOA). In the subsequent embedding stage, the secret image undergoes encryption. The result is subjected to inverse DCT, and the grids are then integrated to obtain the final embedded image. Later, in the extraction phase, the embed…

title: Optimization of the Support Vector Machine Algorithm for Chocolate Consumption Classification Using SMOTE and GridSearchCV
abstract: Extreme class imbalance can cause classification models to favor the majority class, resulting in an inadequate representation of model performance when accuracy is used as the sole evaluation metric. This study aims to evaluate the performance of the Support Vector Machine (SVM) algorithm using the Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE) and GridSearchCV for chocolate consumption category classification. The dataset consists of 1,885 observations from *Chocolate Consumption.xlsx*, a processed file derived from the *Drug Consumption (Quantified)* dataset available in the UCI Machine Learning Repository. It contains 12 predictor features and three target classes encoded as 0, 1, and 2. The class distribution indicates a substantial imbalance, comprising 32 observations in class 0, 67 in class 1, and 1,786 in class 2. The data were divided using a stratified train-test split with an 80:20 ratio. StandardScaler was applied for feature scaling, while hyperparameter optimization was performed using Stratified 3-Fold Cross-Validation with Macro-F1 as the model selection metric. Three configurations were evaluated: SVM with GridSearchCV, SVM with SMOTE, and SVM combining SMOTE and GridSearchCV. The test results show that the combined configuration achieved the highest Macro-F1 score among the three evaluated configurations, at 0.3370, with an accuracy of 89.66%, macro-preci…

title: Cross-Platform Content Operation of Children’s Science Popularization Journals: Characteristics and Optimization Strategies Based on Social Network Analysis
abstract: Against the backdrop of the National Action for Scientific Literacy of the People and the advancement of media convergence strategies, cross-platform operation serves as a vital avenue for children’s science popularization journals to overcome transformation bottlenecks and improve the effectiveness of science communication. Adopting social network analysis, this study selects 20 children’s popular science journals and 7 new media platforms to construct a journal-platform bipartite matrix. It examines the network characteristics and content synergy logic of cross-platform operation from three dimensions: core-periphery structure, centrality, and correspondence analysis. The results reveal a distinct core-periphery pattern in the network. Many journals suffer from weak intermediary capacity, unsystematic and undifferentiated platform deployment, insufficient operational depth, and low content adaptability. Accordingly, optimization strategies are proposed: implementing differentiated platform layout and establishing a hierarchical operation system, achieving precise content-platform matching, building cross-platform traffic interaction mechanisms, and strengthening journals’ operational capacity. This research provides references for children’s science popularization journals to develop a synergistic operation system with complementary functions across multiple platforms.

title: Does Conditional Covariance Outperform Empirical Covariance? A Study of Portfolio Optimization Techniques
abstract: This study analyses two academically utilised approaches of dynamic conditional correlation GARCH (DCC-GARCH) and historical/empirical covariance for covariance matrix estimation and their impact on portfolio optimization is studied during crisis periods. The researchers have collected data for a period of 9 months (i.e. the crisis period) of a multi-asset portfolio that is diversified across countries. This paper also compares different optimisation techniques to not only have a more robust comparison between results from the estimation of covariance matrix, but also to study which optimisation technique benefits the most from the change in covariance matrix estimation method and performs the best during the studied crisis period. It evaluates four strategies: mean-variance optimization (MVO), cluster risk parity (CRP), naïve risk parity (NRP), and equal weighting. The results indicate that DCC-GARCH based covariance matrix estimation provides a much better result for portfolio optimisation during the crisis period studied, and that max Sharpe portfolio optimisation technique benefits the most from said estimation method while CRP and NRP witness no benefit from the same. These results add to the existing literature showing the outperformance of DCC-GARCH in covariance estimation and highlights an additional nuance of variance in results based on which optimisation technique i…

title: Estimation of individual-tree DBH and allometry-derived biomass of Korean red pine using mask-based multimodal deep learning from UAV imagery
Pengembangan Model Regresi dan Machine Learning untuk Meningkatkan Akurasi Prediksi pada Data Multivariat
abstract: Purpose: This article develops a comparative framework for linear regression, regularized regression, and machine-learning models to improve prediction in multivariate datasets while maintaining transparent assessment of uncertainty. Design/Methodology: A methodological and analytical literature review examines ordinary least squares, ridge, lasso, elastic net, random forests, gradient boosting, and support vector regression. A reproducible experimental protocol is proposed using preprocessing pipelines, nested cross-validation, and MAE, RMSE, and R-squared; no unperformed empirical experiment is reported. Findings: Prediction quality depends on variable relationships, sample size, collinearity, nonlinear patterns, and validation design. Regularization can stabilize estimates when predictors are correlated, whereas nonlinear learners may capture interactions but require tuning and controls against overfitting and data leakage. Practical Implications: Researchers can apply the framework to select appropriate baselines, evaluate models on unseen data, assess subgroup performance, and report sensitivity before deployment. Originality/Value: The contribution is an integrated evaluation framework linking statistical interpretability, predictive accuracy, feature stability, reproducibility, and domain-aware decisions.

title: Transformational leadership and Senge’s learning organization disciplines: developing the integrable but not the integrator
abstract: Purpose Organizations must continuously learn and transform to survive, and transformational leadership (TL) is, in principle, a main driver of such change. Drawing on Bass’s (1985, 1990) TL model and Senge’s (1990) learning organization (LO) framework, this study aims to explore whether TL can develop Senge’s LO disciplines. Design/methodology/approach This inductive qualitative multiple-case study examines five Jordanian organizations exhibiting Senge’s LO disciplines, selected through purposive sampling, drawing mainly on 44 semi-structured interviews. Findings TL positively affects three of Senge’s five disciplines: personal mastery (PM), mental models (MMs) and shared vision (SV). However, it fails to develop the integrative discipline, systems thinking (ST). TL, therefore, cultivates key building blocks but not the integrator and cannot alone develop Senge’s. Practical implications Leaders can use individualized consideration (IC) to develop PM, intellectual stimulation (IS) to challenge MMs and idealized influence (II) to foster SV. They can also explore developing ST through IS. Originality/value This study offers a pathway toward developing LO disciplines through three contributions. First, this paper provides novel empirical evidence for three specific TL component–LO discipline linkages: II–SV, IS–MM and IC–PM. Second, this study identifies TL’s limited capacity to f…

title: Does in-class modality affect flipped learning? Designing a higher education flipped classroom using the 5E instructional model
abstract: Flipped teaching has been increasingly used in higher education. However, there is a lack of theory-driven design frameworks for educators, and questions remain on differences between conventional hybrid and fully online flipped classrooms. In the present study, the theoretically-founded 5E instructional model is discussed and implemented to design a higher education flipped classroom course in social science education. Then it is implemented in practice and over one semester with a quasi-experimental design (N = 113) to investigate potential differences in cognitive and affective processes between modalities (online vs. face-to-face in-class lessons). Students’ declarative and application-oriented knowledge acquisition, academic self-efficacy, social relatedness, and their course rating were measured with anonymous surveys and questionnaires. Overall, students only varied in declarative knowledge between modalities. Time predicted negative trends of course rating and social relatedness. In addition, academic self-efficacy was found to be predictive of overall differences in application-oriented knowledge acquisition and course rating. Course rating was predicted with the help of academic self-efficacy and social relatedness. However, student performance and course rating were not correlated. Adjustments to the original 5E model and comparisons against other implementations of …

“Pushing the wrong key:” marginalized older adults navigating scam encounters as critical data literacies
abstract: Purpose This paper examines how older adults from a low-income urban community who participated in a basic digital literacy course experienced online scams. The study aims to show how older adults interpret, navigate, and interrogate scam encounters in an educational context. It argues that scams are not the result of isolated bad actors but connected to the larger system of datafication. Further, teaching about online scams is an important aspect of critical data literacies. Design/methodology/approach This qualitative study draws from data collected over 18 months, including observation of the digital literacy course and 15 interviews. Using agential realism as a framework, data analysis focused on how the older adults made sense of scams as socio-material phenomena. Findings Findings explore three themes: “pushing the wrong key:” scams as emerging through the datafied body; “doing bad things,” scams as the manipulation of identities intensified through generative AI, and “no more than three minutes:” scams creating a need for never-ending vigilance and bureaucratic labor. Research limitations/implications Due to the relatively small sample size of this qualitative, community-based study, research results lack generalizability. Practical implications Implications provide specific examples of how older adults’ sense-making about scams, as emerging critical data literacies, can…

title: The effects of corrective feedback timing and explicitness on second language learning in video-based computer-mediated communication
abstract: Abstract Despite growing attention to the role of corrective feedback (CF) timing in face-to-face or text-based computer-mediated communication (CMC), little is known about how timing and feedback explicitness jointly affect learning in video-based contexts. This study examines the impact of CF timing and explicitness on Chinese EFL learners’ acquisition of the English “be” passive. 68 Participants were randomly assigned to one of five groups (immediate implicit, immediate explicit, delayed implicit, delayed explicit or no-feedback) and performed two communicative tasks conducted via synchronous video conferencing. Learning gains were measured through a pretest-posttest1-posttest2 design using an untimed grammaticality judgement test (UGJT) and an elicited imitation test (EIT). All feedback groups showed significant gains over time on both measures. For the UGJT, a significant interaction between feedback timing and explicitness was found at Posttest 1, although no pairwise contrast remained significant. The delayed implicit feedback group showed delayed gains over time. For the EIT, no significant adjusted group effects or interactions were found. These findings suggest that feedback timing and explicitness should be considered together and are consistent with the view that delayed feedback may promote explicit processing even when implicit in form.

title: Traditional Games and Sundanese Vocabulary Learning among Second-Grade Elementary School Pupils in West Java
abstract: Regional-language education can support children’s access to linguistic heritage by creating meaningful opportunities to understand and use local vocabulary. This study examined vocabulary test-score patterns among second-grade pupils who participated in traditional-game-based instruction and pupils who received conventional instruction. A quasi-experimental non-equivalent control-group design was conducted at SD GIS-PI in Garut, West Java, Indonesia. The sample comprised 91 pupils in three intact classes: 30 in the control class, 31 in experimental class 1, and 30 in experimental class 2. The intervention incorporated three Sundanese traditional games Oray-orayan, Cingciripit, and Nognogan within the theme Miara Lingkungan. A cognitive vocabulary test was administered before and after instruction. The control-class mean changed from 52.00 to 50.33; experimental class 1 increased from 51.94 to 56.45; and experimental class 2 increased from 62.67 to 68.00. Reported mean normalized gains were ?0.018, 0.075, and 0.133, respectively. These descriptive results show positive mean changes in both game-based classes and a small decline in the control class. Because the available statistical output contains inconsistent Mann–Whitney values and individual-level data were unavailable for reanalysis, no inferential significance claim is made. The study offers a context-specific account of …

title: Editorial: Trustworthy and explainable machine learning for human-aligned robotics and intelligent systems
Use of infrared thermography and machine learning to predict the infectious etiology of subclinical bovine mastitis in a robotic milking system
abstract: Abstract Mastitis is a major challenge for dairy production, and infrared thermography (IRT) is a promising non-invasive tool for monitoring udder health. This study evaluated whether thermal information obtained by IRT, combined with animal, production, and environmental variables, could be used in supervised machine learning models to predict subclinical mastitis (SCM) and its most probable infectious etiology in pasture-raised cows managed under a voluntary milking system. Eighty-nine lactating cows from a single herd underwent thermographic evaluation over six months, and milk samples from 530 mammary quarters were analyzed, of which 61 (11.5%) were positive for SCM. Mean (TMED), minimum (TCOLD), and maximum (THOT) udder surface temperatures, somatic cell count (SCC), milk composition, animal characteristics, and environmental data were used to develop a multilevel binary logistic model and a multinomial logistic model. The binary model, including SCC and TCOLD, showed an apparent area under the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve (AUC) of 0.96. However, using a ten-fold internal cross-validation, AUC decreased to 0.81 and sensitivity decreased from 0.90 to 0.33. The thermographic variables improved model fit modestly but significantly, whereas SCC accounted for most of the predictive information. In the multinomial model, apparent AUC values ranged from 0.78 to 0…

title: Digital Eye Strain in Online Learning and Remote Work: A Systematic Review of Prevalence, Risk Factors and Management Strategies
abstract: Background: Digital Eye Strain (DES) is a common ocular and visual complaint associated with prolonged use of digital devices. The widespread move to online learning and remote work has markedly increased screen exposure, which may place students and remote workers at greater risk. This systematic review assessed the prevalence, risk factors and management of DES in these populations. Methods: PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, Embase and the Cochrane Library were searched for studies published from January 2020 onward, with Google Scholar used as a supplementary source. Primary observational and interventional studies of individuals engaged in online learning, distance education, remote work or work from home were eligible if they reported the prevalence or severity of DES, associated factors or the effects of preventive or therapeutic interventions. Methodological quality was appraised descriptively against the domains of the Joanna Briggs Institute checklist for analytical cross-sectional studies. Because of marked heterogeneity, the findings were synthesized narratively. Results: Of 302 records screened, 28 full-text articles were assessed and five cross-sectional studies were included, all of students engaged in online learning (3,955 participants in total). No eligible study of remote workers and no interventional study was identified. In the three studies that defin…

title: DIGITAL ECOSYSTEM CULTIVATION AND RESEARCH CULTURE IN INSTRUCTIONAL LEADERSHIP: A DESCRIPTIVE STUDY OF PRIMARY SCHOOL ASSISTANT HEADTEACHERS IN SABAH
abstract: Digital transformation in primary schools calls for leadership practices that promote the purposeful use of educational technologies alongside systematic inquiry into teaching and learning. This study describes digital ecosystem cultivation and research culture cultivation as two dimensions of instructional competency among primary school assistant headteachers in Sabah, Malaysia. A focused descriptive analysis was undertaken using reported results from a quantitative, cross-sectional doctoral survey involving 423 assistant headteachers. The adapted instrument drew on the instructional domain of the Malaysian School Leaders Competency Standard 2.0 (KOMPAS 2.0), and descriptive statistics were obtained from the original study. Both domains recorded high self-reported ratings: digital ecosystem cultivation (M = 4.2228, SD = 0.39472) and research culture cultivation (M = 3.9665, SD = 0.40403). Among four instructional competency dimensions, digital ecosystem cultivation ranked second, whereas research culture cultivation ranked fourth. The difference of 0.2563 scale points is descriptive and was not tested for statistical significance. The pattern suggests a useful professional learning priority: complementing encouragement of digital technology with structured teacher inquiry, reflective evaluation and evidence-informed improvement. However, the data do not establish a relationsh…

title: THE EFFECT OF DIGITAL LITERACY AND SELF-EFFICACY ON COMPUTERIZED ACCOUNTING LEARNING OUTCOMES AMONG ECONOMIC EDUCATION STUDENTS
abstract: ABSTRACT The attainment of satisfactory learning outcomes in Accounting Computer coursework remains a persistent scholarly concern, as academic success in this domain is determined not solely by students' mastery of foundational accounting subject matter, but also by their capacity to effectively utilize digital technology and their level of confidence in their own academic capabilities. Deficiencies in digital literacy proficiency, compounded by inadequate self-efficacy, have been identified as significant impediments to students' ability to operate MYOB accounting software competently, with consequential adverse implications for overall learning achievement in Accounting Computer education. Therefore, this study aims to empirically examine the influence of digital literacy and self-efficacy on computerized accounting learning outcomes among undergraduate students in Economics Education. This study employs a quantitative research approach and involves 48 students selected through purposive sampling. The findings reveal that digital literacy and self-efficacy have statistically significant effects on students’ learning outcomes, both independently and collectively. The partial test results indicate that digital literacy has a positive regression coefficient of 0.485, with a t-statistic of 4.203, which exceeds the critical t-value of 1.679 at a significance level below 0.05. Sim…

title: Integrated neighbourhood health systems: defining the role of public health
abstract: Purpose Integrated neighbourhood health systems aim to bring together healthcare, social care and community resources to improve health outcomes in a defined local area. This article examines why public health approaches are central to neighbourhood health and how they can be incorporated in practice and applied in other settings. Design/methodology/approach Drawing on reflective, practice-based experience of integrating public health into a neighbourhood health system in Worcestershire, UK, the article sets out public health practice across three domains and presents a framework distilled from that practice. The approach is situated against existing research on public health and integrated care, with a focus on collaboration and role clarity. Findings Evidence suggests integrated care often remains overly focused on individual and clinical factors, despite the well documented influence of social determinants on health. Effective collaboration between public health and system partners can be constrained by cultural, conceptual and capacity barriers. A three-domain framework is proposed for public health input into integrated neighbourhood health systems: insight and intelligence, health improvement services and community engagement and development. In Worcestershire, service evaluations reported improvements across a range of participant outcomes, and the neighbourhood-level an…

title: Deinococcus wulumuqiensis-derived nanovesicles promote integrated tissue regeneration
Supramolecular Matrine-Proanthocyanidins Nanocomplex-Integrated Carboxymethyl Chitosan Hydrogel with Phenylboronic Acid Modification for Atopic Dermatitis Therapy
abstract: Abstract Atopic dermatitis (AD) is a chronic inflammatory skin disease featured by immune dysregulation, oxidative stress, and an impaired epidermal barrier. Oxidative stress and inflammation establish a self-sustaining vicious cycle that accelerates the progression of atopic dermatitis. However, few naturally derived self-assembled nanohydrogels have been developed to disrupt this reciprocal loop for the treatment of cutaneous AD. In this study, matrine (MAT) and proanthocyanidins (PAC), two Chinese medicine-derived molecules with inherent antioxidant and anti-inflammatory activities, co-assembled spontaneously into nanoparticles (PM NPs) in aqueous solution. Incorporation of PM NPs into the phenylboronic acid-modified carboxymethyl chitosan (CP) crosslinked network enhanced the mechanical strength of carboxymethyl chitosan, forming a composite hydrogel (CPPM). Spectral results verified that PM NP self-assembly was mediated by hydrogen bonding and π-π stacking. CPPM efficiently scavenged reactive oxygen species (ROS), suppressed the activation of the Ox-CaMKII and NF-κB signaling pathways, and activated Nrf2 to restore epidermal redox homeostasis. CPPM exhibited favorable moisturizing capacity, appropriate rheological properties, and mild ROS-triggered release to realize local therapeutic effects. In 1-chloro-2,4-dinitrochlorobenzene (DNCB)-induced AD mice, topical CPPM applic…

title: Integrated single-cell and bulk transcriptome analyses characterize CD8+ exhausted T-cell-associated prognostic features in colorectal cancer liver metastasis
abstract: Background Liver metastasis continues to be a critical factor contributing to adverse prognoses in colorectal cancer (CRC) and is significantly affected by an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME). While CD8 + exhausted T cells (CD8_Tex) are generally recognized as key elements in the attenuation of antitumor immunity, their precise functional role in colorectal cancer liver metastasis (CRLM) has yet to be comprehensively elucidated. Methods Single-cell RNA sequencing data from primary and metastatic lesions were integrated with bulk transcriptomic data from TCGA and GEO. Integrative bioinformatic analyses were used to characterize the biological features and clinical relevance of CD8_Tex cells in CRLM. In addition, the expression of key model genes was examined by RT-qPCR in colorectal cancer cell lines. Results We constructed a high-resolution single-cell atlas of CRLM. Based on genes upregulated in metastasis-associated CD8_Tex cells, we established a six-gene prognostic signature. This signature stratified patients into high- and low-risk groups with significantly different overall survival. Cell-cell communication analysis suggested enhanced interactions between fibroblasts and CD8_Tex cells in metastatic lesions, with APP-CD74 identified as a potential ligand-receptor interaction. Pseudotime analysis further suggested that key prognostic genes changed in parallel…

title: Editorial: Neuroadaptive brain-computer interface-driven robotic system for hand rehabilitation in stroke patients
An integrated analysis of the operational efficiency and network resilience of European railways
abstract: Purpose This study aims to use a unified assessment framework to examine the operational efficiency and resilience of ten European railway organizations. Efficiency reflects the productive performance of rail systems, while resilience captures their capacity to recover from disruptions, accidents and external shocks. The purpose is to compare operators using comparable metrics, identify vulnerabilities and discrepancies between efficiency and resilience and provide insights to improve network robustness. Examining both dimensions, the study aims to contribute to strategic planning and infrastructure investment across European Union (EU) railways. Design/methodology/approach The analysis applies four data envelopment analysis (DEA) models: CCR and BCC to assess efficiency and resilience. Inputs include network length, electrification, rolling stock, labor and operational expenditure. The outputs include passenger-km, train-km and revenue. Resilience uses safety-related undesirable outputs, fatalities, collisions, derailments, injuries and other accident indicators. Emergency expenditure serves as an additional resilience measurement. Ten EU railway operators are selected based on geographic, structural and regulatory homogeneity. Findings The results show that although some operators achieve full efficiency, resilience performance is more heterogeneous. Greece, Slovenia and Croa…

Lightweight segmentation model for real-time detection of multi-type façade defects using enhanced YOLOv12
abstract: Abstract Accurate segmentation of façade defects is essential for extracting visible damage regions and providing auxiliary information fourban infrastructure maintenance. However, existing detection methods based on bounding boxes often fail to delineate defect boundaries precisely, limiting their practical applicability. To address this challenge, this study proposes a lightweight instance segmentation model for real-time multi-type façade defect detection, built upon an enhanced YOLOv12n architecture. Three task-oriented modules are incorporated and adapted for façade defect segmentation: a Global Edge Information Transfer (GEIT) module that enhances boundary representation by integrating multi-scale edge features into shallow layers; a Hierarchical Attention Fusion Block (HAFB) that captures both local details and global semantics via parallel attention and re-parameterizable convolutions; and a Lightweight Shared Convolutional Segmentation Head (LSCSH) that improves efficiency and robustness through parameter sharing, scale adaptation, and group normalization. Experimental results show that the proposed model achieves 91.5% precision, 84.7% recall, 87.2% mAP@0.5, and 64.8% mAP@0.5:0.95, with a compact size of 5.1 MB and real-time speed of 201 FPS, demonstrating strong segmentation performance and deployment potential.

title: Understanding the Harpsichord Rattle
abstract: Harpsichord sound is recognised by its characteristic rattle, a noisy brittle sound at the beginning followed by the vocal cantabile part. Inhistorical descriptions, this idiomatic rattle seems to be appreciated as a contrast for more flowing and horizontal playing. Many historicaltreatises point out the importance of repeating the sounds or chords to emphasise and manipulate the valued croquant materiality of itssound.This article aims to investigate the expressive potential of this sometimes-rattling character of the harpsichord sound’s consonant-likebeginning by integrating historical, musicological and acoustic perspectives. It seeks to demonstrate how material characteristics andperformance practices contributed to the instrument’s distinctive sound and cultural significance in eighteenth-century music.The material turn of historical research has led scholars to move from abstract musical concepts to the tangible artefacts and practicesthat shaped past musical experiences. Recent advances in measurement techniques and computational modelling have enabled a moredetailed spectro-temporal characterisation of harpsichord sound and especially of its attack transient, allowing researchers to correlatespecific acoustic features with historical descriptions and performance practices.Ultimately, the study aspires to enrich both scholarly understanding and practical interpretation o…

title: A neuroanalytic multi-scale, multi-granularity decoupled distillation fuzzy classifier for interpretable epileptic EEG pattern detection
abstract: Introduction Electroencephalogram (EEG)-based recognition of epileptic seizures is a representative neuroanalytic pattern-detection problem at the intersection of artificial intelligence and computational neuroscience. Deep networks learn strong representations for this task but act as opaque function approximators, whereas Takagi-Sugeno-Kang (TSK) fuzzy classifiers express their reasoning as human-readable IF-THEN rules but have historically lagged behind deep models in accuracy. This study aimed to combine predictive strength with rule-level transparency. Methods A Multi-scale Multi-granularity Decoupled Distillation TSK Fuzzy Classifier (MMDD-TSK-FC) is proposed. One-dimensional convolutional neural networks (1D-CNNs) with different kernel widths are first trained as multi-scale teachers, so that both slow, trend-level and brief, transient-level EEG dynamics are captured. The temperature-softened outputs of each teacher are then transferred, through its own (decoupled) Kullback-Leibler distillation channel, to a TSK fuzzy student whose rule count is matched to the teacher's kernel width: wide kernels are paired with compact rule sets and narrow kernels with richer rule sets. A joint objective also penalises disagreement between each student and the ground-truth labels, and the predictions of the resulting multi-granularity students are fused by majority voting. The teachers …

title: Plasma fibronectin-1 and CCL18 as candidate markers of mechanically distinct regional lung injury in ARDS: a prospective physiological cohort study with exploratory multi-omics profiling
abstract: Introduction Mechanical power (MP) integrates the principal determinants of ventilatory energy delivery and is independently associated with mortality in acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), yet whether the intensity of mechanical energy delivery maps onto distinct regional lung injury patterns and generates a recognizable circulating molecular signature remains poorly defined. Methods We conducted a prospective physiological cohort study integrating quantitative chest CT (qCT), respiratory mechanics, and exploratory multi-omics profiling in patients with ARDS. Thirty patients underwent paired qCT and comprehensive respiratory mechanics assessment and were stratified into high-MP (>17 J/min, n = 11) and low-MP (≤17 J/min, n = 19) groups; a nested multi-omics sub-cohort of 20 patients (high-MP n = 7, low-MP n = 13) additionally underwent matched plasma proteomics, metabolomics, and peripheral blood mononuclear cell transcriptomics. Results After adjustment for static compliance, SOFA score, and CRP, MP remained independently associated with poorly aerated (b = 1.026, P < 0.001) and non-aerated lung fractions (b = 0.449, P = 0.009) on qCT, whereas driving pressure showed no independent association in the same models. In the multi-omics sub-cohort, supervised multi-block integration identified exploratory MP-associated candidate features organized into a structural ex…
