title: Integrating the Lesh translation model in e-learning to foster students’ numeracy skills
abstract: Although the Lesh Translation Model (LTM) has proven effective in addressing students' difficulties in translating mathematical ideas across representations, its application has so far been limited to face-to-face learning and its effectiveness when integrated into structured e-learning environments to improve students' numeracy skills has not been widely studied. This study aims to examine the effectiveness of integrating LTM into an e-learning platform (E-Numerasi) in enhancing students' numeracy skills compared to conventional instruction. This research uses a quasi-experimental pretest-posttest control group design and involves 119 eighth-grade students from two public junior high schools in Kuningan Regency, West Java, who were divided into an experimental group (n = 61) and a control group (n = 58). T-tests confirmed the equivalence of initial numeracy skills between the two groups prior to the intervention (p = 0.832). After the intervention, the experiment group obtained a significantly higher posttest mean score (M = 74.46) than the control group (M = 63.88), t(117) = 4.962; p < 0.001, supported by a moderate Normalized Gain (0.39) and a very large effect size (Cohen's d = 0.91). These results indicate that integrating the Lesh Translation Model into e-learning is significantly more effective in improving students' numeracy skills than conventional instruction.

Deep Q-network path planning with stratified sampling and prioritized replay
abstract: Deep reinforcement learning (DRL) has been widely adopted for mobile robot path planning in unknown and complex environments. However, existing DRL-based approaches suffer from two main limitations: sparse reward, which provides meaningful feedback only at terminal states, and experience heterogeneity, which reduces the efficiency of uniform sampling from the standard experience replay buffer due to the diversity of transition qualities stored within it. To tackle both issues at once, we propose SS-PER-DQN, a novel path-planning approach in which stratified sampling and a prioritized experience replay mechanism are incorporated into the Double Deep Q-Network. The memory buffer is divided into three priority layers based on temporal-difference error levels, with a dynamically varying sampling ratio between layers, and importance-sampling compensation to balance the sampling-distribution bias. A densely shaped reward function is additionally employed to expedite early exploration in the presence of sparsely rewarded actions in the environment. Experiments performed on Grid World and ROS Gazebo simulations show that the SS-PER-DQN is able to successfully plan paths at success rates of 94.5% and 89.0%, with a 24.5% and 21.8% reduction in path lengths, respectively, when compared to the traditional DQN algorithm, after convergence in approximately 53% fewer training episodes. Education Amidst Uncertainty: Strategic Leadership, Innovation, and Institutional Sustainability in the 21st Century
abstract: The twenty-first century has brought significant changes that have transformed educational systems worldwide. Rapid technological advancement, digital transformation, globalization, demographic shifts, artificial intelligence, public health crises, and evolving societal expectations have created complex challenges for educational institutions. These conditions require educational leaders to adopt strategic leadership practices that strengthen organizational resilience, encourage innovation, and promote institutional sustainability. This study presents a systematic literature review and thematic synthesis examining the relationship among strategic leadership, innovation, organizational resilience, and sustainability in educational contexts. Relevant scholarly studies were systematically identified, screened, and analyzed using academic databases, including Scopus, Web of Science, Google Scholar, and other scholarly sources. Guided by a systematic review approach and thematic analysis, the selected literature was examined to identify recurring patterns and emerging insights. The synthesis revealed five major themes: (1) increasing uncertainty and complexity in educational institutions; (2) strategic leadership as a driver of organizational adaptability; (3) innovation and digital transformation as catalysts for resilience; (4) collaborative governance and stakeholder engagement a…

title: Optimization of Dilute Acid Pretreatment of Waste Rice Straw for Enhanced Saccharification and Fermentation Yield
abstract: As a renewable alternative to fossil fuels, the production of bioethanol and biochemicals from lignocellulosic biomass has drawn significant interest. For biochemical conversion, pretreatement is the most crucial step, which removes biomass recalcitrance to improve cellulose’s accessibility for enzymatic saccharification and fermentation. This study investigated the potential of dilute sulfuric acid pretreatment of waste rice straw to produce building-block sugars and bioethanol. The study focused on optimizing several key parameters, including dilute acid concentration (60 mM), pretreatment time (30 minutes), pretreatment temperature (120°C), and liquid-to-solid ratio (5:1). This study also compared the efficiency of dilute acid pretreatment of rice straw with conventional dilute alkali and organosolv pretreatment techniques. The results showed that dilute acid pretreatment effectively dissolved a significant amount of hemicellulose under these circumstances, retaining 97.96% of cellulose in the solid substrate, which led to 64.28% glucose yield in enzymatic saccharification. The rice straw structure underwent morphological changes (i.e., cell wall rupture and changes in crystallinity) as the result of acid pretreatment, which were confirmed using SEM and XRD techniques. Furthermore, Saccharomyces cerevisiae fermentation trials showed that the total bioethanol yield was 78.7% …

title: Stochastic Model for Optimal Control of Water Resource Treatment under Random Disturbances
abstract: This study addresses the problem of optimal control of water resource treatment under stochastic uncertainty and random external disturbances. A mathematical model describing the dynamics of water pollution is developed in the form of a stochastic differential equation, which accounts for the influence of random environmental factors on the treatment process. The corresponding optimal control problem is formulated using a quadratic performance functional that characterizes the trade-off between minimizing the pollution level and reducing the costs associated with water treatment. The stochastic Pontryagin maximum principle is applied to derive the necessary optimality conditions for the control strategy. A numerical example is presented to demonstrate the applicability of the proposed model and to evaluate the resulting optimal control strategy under stochastic disturbances. The obtained results demonstrate the potential of the proposed approach for developing environmentally sound and economically efficient strategies for water resource management under uncertainty.

title: AI-driven multi-objective optimization of CNC machining parameters for enhanced surface finish and tool life
abstract: AI-driven CNC machining optimization requires balancing surface quality and productivity while avoiding unsupported integration of independently collected machining data. This study proposes a leakage-controlled, surrogate-assisted framework using two open datasets: a 27-condition turning surface-quality dataset and a 968-observation milling tool-life dataset comprising 14 tools. The datasets were analyzed independently, with no row-wise fusion or DOC–ADOC mapping. Cutting speed, feed rate, and depth of cut were used as controllable turning variables, while milling sensor and metadata features were used separately for remaining useful life (RUL) prediction. The selected Ridge surface model achieved LOOCV MAE = 0.1077, RMSE = 0.1383, and , while nested validation yielded , indicating limited out-of-sample generalization. The no-cycle RUL model achieved MAE = 23.44 cycles, RMSE = 31.39 cycles, and under leave-one-tool-out validation. NSGA-II significantly outperformed equal-budget random search in normalized hypervolume (0.7711 vs. 0.7421). Because the surrogate surface was statistically limited, continuous optimization was treated as exploratory. Final selection was therefore anchored to measured Pareto-efficient turning conditions. Equal-weight TOPSIS selected , , and , with measured and , as the balanced practical recommendation.

title: Constraint internalization through parametric reconstruction: A legality-aware framework for geometric optimization problems
abstract: Geometric optimization problems such as \(PA + k \cdot PB\) are commonly solved using reflection methods, projection techniques, or calculus-based optimization. In elementary treatments, these approaches often assume that signed algebraic expressions directly represent non-negative geometric distances across the entire real domain. When the variable extends beyond the traditional geometric boundary, this implicit assumption fails, creating what we describe as a representation legality gap. In this paper, we propose a parametric reconstruction framework that internalizes geometric admissibility constraints into the algebraic representation. Rather than partitioning the variable domain through piecewise case distinctions, we introduce an admissible auxiliary scaffold parameter \(L \ge x\) to decompose the objective function into a geometrically legal core path and an algebraically compensating residual. The auxiliary parameter \(L\) cancels identically in the reconstructed representation, ensuring global validity across \(\mathbb{R}\). We demonstrate this framework on a classical Hu Bugui-type optimization problem, establish the global minimum via dynamic projection inequalities, prove the exact invariance of the minimizer, and extend the…

title: Optimization and Automation as Efficiency Drivers: From Corporate Operations to Intellectual Property Management
abstract: In the context of the digital transformation of the economy, optimization and automation of business processes are becoming key factors in improving the efficiency of corporate governance. The article examines the relationship between the introduction of intelligent systems and the growth of operational efficiency using the example of two areas: automation of corporate operations and management of intellectual activity results. Based on the analysis of practical cases of the implementation of intelligent management systems in Russian companies, including the experience of large retail chains, the contradictory effects of large-scale algorithmization of managerial processes are revealed. Standardization and improvement of average operational efficiency indicators at the initial stages of digital transformation are accompanied by risks of leveling the unique competencies of managers and reducing the adaptability of organizations to changes in the external environment. The paper proposes a model of phased digital transformation, including inventory of business processes, implementation of SLA metrics, automation of time tracking, and formation of an intellectual property management system. Special attention is paid to the problems of registration and commercialization of intellectual activity results in educational institutions, where the lack of well-established business processe…

title: Integrated genetic and phenotypic characterization of doubled haploid lines in onion (Allium cepa L.)
abstract: Abstract Accurate identification of haploids, doubled haploids (DHs), and diploids is a critical step in the successful implementation of DH technology. This study aimed to establish a reliable framework for ploidy identification in onion by integrating flow cytometry, simple sequence repeat (SSR) marker analysis, stomatal characterization, and morphological evaluation, while assessing the potential of stomatal traits as a rapid and cost-effective screening approach. Flow cytometric analysis successfully distinguished haploid, diploid, and mixoploid regenerants based on nuclear DNA content, whereas SSR markers were used to confirm the homozygous nature of DH plants. Polymorphic SSR markers produced single-band profiles in DH plants, in contrast to the heterozygous banding patterns observed in donor plants, validating the genetic identity of DH regenerants. Significant differences were detected among haploid, DH, and diploid plants for all evaluated stomatal traits. Stomatal length, width, and index increased with increasing ploidy level, with diploid plants exhibiting the highest values, DH plants showing intermediate values, and haploid plants displaying the lowest values. Conversely, stomatal density showed a negative association with ploidy level, with haploid plants exhibiting the highest stomatal density and diploid plants the lowest. abstract: BACKGROUND Sodium taurocholate cotransporting polypeptide deficiency (NTCPD) causes persistent hypercholanemia and neonatal cholestasis, but its genotypic and phenotypic spectrum across ethnicities and geographic backgrounds remains poorly characterized. AIM To characterize the genetic architecture, biochemical trajectories, and genotype-phenotype correlations of NTCPD in a multi-ethnic pediatric cohort. METHODS In this case cohort study, we analyzed 125 patients with genetically confirmed NTCPD from Kunming Children’s Hospital (2020-2025). Longitudinal biochemical parameters were tracked, and multivariable regression was performed to assess genotype-biochemical relationships, adjusting for age, ethnicity, and geographic location. RESULTS The cohort comprised 69 male and 56 female patients (83 homozygous, 25 heterozygous, and 17 compound heterozygous). The c.800C>T variant was present in all compound heterozygotes, together with 11 additional variants (four likely pathogenic variants and seven variants of uncertain significance). The cohort comprised 73 Han and 52 individuals from ethnic minority groups, predominantly Yi and Hui, distributed across 15 prefectures. Biochemical profiles indicated self-limiting hypercholanemia, with total bile acid levels declining from 178.8 ± 60.9 µmol/L (0-2 months) to 141.2 ± 77.9 µmol/L (> 4 months, P = 0.0002). title: Probabilistic-temporal modeling of network security monitoring subprocesses for multi-stage attacks in IoT networks
abstract: Timely detection of a multistage cyberattack in an IoT network depends on the chosen monitoring architecture, execution time, and the transition behavior of subprocesses within that architecture. This paper introduces a probabilistic temporal model to evaluate an NSMS for both known and unknown multi-stage attacks. First, we introduce a conceptual monitoring architecture that organizes streaming-data processing, temporal analysis, attack classification, attack prediction, and response selection. The recurrent neural networks in the architecture form the basis of the implementation framework and are neither trained nor empirically analyzed. The evaluated contribution represents the NSMS subprocesses as a continuous-time Markov chain, where each state corresponds to a monitoring task and each transition rate is estimated from the respective mean processing time. We develop state-probability equations and use a specialized software tool to estimate the stationary probabilities and successful anomaly-detection probabilities. Numerical evaluations examine how delays in preprocessing, syntactic construction, encoding, classification, and prediction affect monitoring effectiveness. The analysis shows that the estimated probability of successful anomaly detection decreases as preprocessing and encoding time increases, underscoring the need to account for computational delay in time-cri…

title: Multi-agent generative AI ecosystems for cyber-physical systems in Industry 5.0
abstract: Cyber-Physical Systems (CPSs) are increasingly being implemented in critical industrial infrastructure, where complexity and interdependence are rising, posing significant cyber and operational risks. Traditional anomaly detection algorithms can be ineffective in capturing temporal dynamics, relational dependencies, and interpretable response requirements. The present paper proposes a multi-agent generative AI system to detect CPS anomalies and provide decision support by combining temporal feature encoding, relational modeling as graphs, supervised learning, and reasoning with an LLM. The architecture consists of detection, diagnosis, planning, governance, and human-in-the-loop validation agents. The framework is tested on the SWaT benchmark data. Findings indicate that the Autoencoder, LSTM, and 1D-CNN are more effective in terms of raw detection metrics, whereas the Random Forest provides more interpretable and agent-readable evidence to support the post-detection decision. Analysis of features and sensor family suggests the relevance of relational dependencies in characterizing anomalies. The multi-agent layer converts selected anomaly predictions into context-dependent explanations and governance-filtered recommendations to aid operator review, response planning, and process resilience. Overall, the framework supports transparent and human-supervised CPS anomaly management…

The Influence of Sales Promotion Content, Content Attractiveness, and User-Friendliness on Financial Decision Making through Imitation Intention
abstract: Purpose: This study examines the influence of sales promotion content, content attractiveness, and user-friendliness on financial decision making through imitation intention among social media users in Indonesia, particularly in the context of influencer marketing for Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) in the food and beverage sector. Research Method: This study uses a quantitative explanatory design with a cross-sectional approach. Data are collected through an online questionnaire using a five-point Likert scale and purposive sampling. Data analysis employs Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) using SmartPLS. Results and Discussion: The study proposes that sales promotion content, content attractiveness, and user-friendliness influence imitation intention and financial decision making. Imitation intention is also expected to influence financial decision making and mediate the relationships between promotional content characteristics and financial decisions. These relationships will be evaluated empirically. Implications: The findings are expected to help MSMEs and influencers develop promotional strategies that encourage informed financial decisions among social media users. title: Peran Financial self-efficacy dalam Memoderasi Literasi Keuangan Digital, Herding behavior, dan Perilaku Keuangan Mahasiswa
abstract: This study aims to analyze the influence of digital financial literacy and herding behavior on financial behavior, as well as to examine the role of financial self-efficacy as a moderating variable. The study sample consisted of economics education students from State University of Malang and State University of Surabaya. Data were collected using questionnaires. A quantitative approach was employed, utilizing multiple linear regression and Moderated Regression Analysis (MRA). The results indicate that digital financial literacy has a positive and significant effect on financial behavior, whereas herding behavior has a negative and significant effect. Moderation analysis reveals that financial self-efficacy strengthens the impact of digital financial literacy on financial behavior and weakens the impact of herding behavior on financial behavior. These findings suggest that enhancing digital financial literacy can foster better financial behavior, while the tendency to follow others' financial decisions can diminish the quality of financial behavior.

title: Financial ratio analysis to measure company financial performance
abstract: This study aims to analyze the financial ratios of PT. Kalbe Farma, Tbk. as a comprehensive measure of the company’s financial performance over the 2020–2024 period, a span that encompasses the COVID-19 pandemic, post-pandemic recovery, and a period of macroeconomic normalization. The financial ratios examined include the Liquidity Ratio (Current Ratio and Quick Ratio), Activity Ratio (Total Asset Turnover), Solvency Ratio (Debt to Assets Ratio and Debt to Equity Ratio), and Profitability Ratio (Gross Profit Margin, Net Profit Margin, Return on Assets, and Return on Equity). This study employs a descriptive-quantitative approach with secondary data sourced exclusively from the company’s audited consolidated annual reports and the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX). Data were collected through documentation techniques and analyzed using longitudinal financial ratio analysis methods. The results show that PT. Kalbe Farma, Tbk. consistently maintained a healthy financial condition across all four ratio categories throughout the observation period. Liquidity remained exceptionally strong, with the Current Ratio consistently exceeding 377%. The solvency structure was conservative, with the Debt to Assets Ratio never surpassing 20%. title: Financial Development, Foreign Direct Investment, Government Expenditure and Economic Growth in Sub-Saharan Africa: A Joint-Effect and Causality Analysis
abstract: Financial development, foreign direct investment (FDI) and government expenditure are well-established drivers of growth but are rarely studied together. This study examines their joint effect on economic growth in 45 Sub-Saharan African countries over 2002–2021, using correlation analysis, pairwise Granger causality tests and a six-step hierarchical fixed-effects panel regression with country-clustered standard errors. The predictors are jointly significant (F(6, 659) = 10.71, p < 0.001), though within-country explanatory power is modest (within R² = 0.089). Broad money (β = −0.097, p < 0.001) and interest rate spread (β = −0.017, p < 0.001) reduce growth, gross capital formation raises it (β = 0.081, p = 0.011), and domestic credit, FDI and government consumption have no significant contemporaneous effect; in a lagged specification FDI raises growth one year later (β = 0.078, p < 0.001). Granger tests show broad money and interest rate spread are bidirectionally related to growth, private credit is demand-following, and gross capital formation and government consumption Granger-cause growth without feedback. Growth within SSA economies responds to intermediation efficiency and productive investment rather than financial depth, and the FDI dividend materialises with a lag. The study recommends intermediation reform, investment promotion and rebalancing public spending toward c…

title: Penerapan Aplikasi BukuWarung untuk Meningkatkan Efisiensi Pencatatan dan Penyusunan Laporan Keuangan Pada UMKM di Condongcatur
abstract: Usaha Mikro, Kecil, dan Menengah (UMKM) memiliki peran penting dalam kegiatan ekonomi, tetapi sebagian pelaku usaha masih menghadapi kesulitan dalam mencatat transaksi secara lengkap dan konsisten. Kegiatan pengabdian ini bertujuan meningkatkan pengetahuan dan keterampilan dasar pemilik Soto Segar Gelatik serta Nasi Kuning & Nasi Uduk Bu Kris di Condongcatur, Sleman, dalam melakukan pencatatan transaksi melalui aplikasi BukuWarung. Kegiatan dilaksanakan pada tanggal 01 sampai 23 Oktober 2026 dengan pendekatan partisipatif-deskriptif. Tahapan kegiatan meliputi observasi dan wawancara, edukasi singkat mengenai pencatatan keuangan, pendampingan praktik penggunaan aplikasi, serta evaluasi setelah pendampingan. Hasil identifikasi awal menunjukkan bahwa kedua mitra memiliki kondisi yang berbeda. Soto Segar Gelatik telah mencatat penjualan secara manual, tetapi belum mendokumentasikan pembelian bahan baku dan biaya operasional secara menyeluruh. Sementara itu, Nasi Kuning & Nasi Uduk Bu Kris belum mencatat pemasukan maupun pengeluaran secara teratur. Oleh karena itu, pendampingan pada mitra pertama diarahkan untuk melengkapi pencatatan pemasukan dan pengeluaran secara digital, sedangkan pada mitra kedua difokuskan pada pengenalan alur pencatatan transaksi sebagai kebiasaan baru. title: Environmental Code Reform, Enterprise Abatement Outlays, and Stationary Industrial Emissions: Subnational Evidence from Kazakhstan, 2010–2025
abstract: Staggered industrial environmental codes pair multi-year preparatory monitoring windows with scheduled transitions toward best-available-technique permitting and progressive fee multipliers, raising an open mechanism question: do historically emission-intensive industrial regions adjust during early preparatory compliance through enterprise current abatement outlays and end-of-pipe pollutant capture, or does emission-intensity compression emerge as integrated-permit and fee-escalation thresholds arrive? Assembling a boundary-harmonized panel across all 16 consolidated parent regions of Kazakhstan from 2010 to 2025 (N = 256) around Environmental Code No. 400-VI (enacted January 2021, entering into general force July 2021, with Category I integrated permitting and scheduled fee multipliers commencing January 2025), we estimate exposure-gradient regressions with 9,999 null-imposed wild cluster bootstrap replications. Across 2022–2025, one standard deviation higher predetermined 2017–2019 stationary emission exposure is associated with no statistically resolved change in log real enterprise current environmental protection outlays (+0.0947 log points; clustered SE = 0.0869; bootstrap p = 0.3303) and statistically unresolved shifts in stationary pollutant capture shares (-0.0167; 95% bootstrap set [-0.0773, 0.0293]; p = 0.4876) and log captured tonnage (-0.0284; p = 0.8925). title: Socio-Demographic and Political Factors Associated with Attitudes Toward Electoral Reform in the Philippines, Indonesia, and Mexico
abstract: Public evaluations of electoral reform are shaped by social position, political affiliation, and assessments of electoral institutions. Objective: This review examines socio-demographic and political factors associated with attitudes toward electoral reform in the Philippines, Indonesia, and Mexico. A narrative thematic synthesis was conducted using 24 publication records designated in the author-supplied extraction worksheet. The evidence included quantitative studies, qualitative and descriptive studies, legal and institutional analyses, and secondary research. Perceived fairness, institutional trust, and representation were distinguished from expressed support for or opposition to reform. Evidence from Indonesia foregrounds political information, representation, and party or leader cues; Mexican studies emphasize partisanship, electoral integrity, and institutional trust; Philippine research contributes primarily institutional and voter-information context. Education appears relevant where measured, whereas chronological age and income are insufficiently assessed for robust cross-national comparisons. The evidence remains uneven in geographic coverage, study design, and outcome measurement. Electoral reform attitudes are best interpreted through the interaction of political alignment, access to information, and perceived institutional credibility. The available records do no…

title: The Role of Trust and Local Presence in Selling IT Outsourcing Services in the United States Market
abstract: The United States market for information technology outsourcing combines intense competition with long, multi-stage procurement, making price and technical skills weaker predictors of who wins a contract than they once were. This paper examines how trust and local presence shape the outcome of business-to-business deals for software development services in that market. The analysis draws on the management practice of a vendor that employs around 3500 people and sells primarily to clients in the United States and Canada, and it treats anonymized deal episodes as the empirical material. The argument develops in three steps. The first step maps the barriers that define the market, where buyers expect a provider to understand their business quickly and to work as if it were an internal team. The second step explains why clients reward the provider they trust the most, even when a cheaper option exists, and it shows how expertise, flexibility, and risk reduction combine into a single perception of dependability. The third step describes the shift toward an onshore model and a local office, opening segments that an offshore provider cannot reach and increasing conversion rates in large enterprise deals. The paper concludes that trust and local presence operate as primary competitive factors on the United States market and that providers who keep competing on price alone tend to stay …

Market concentration and market dependence of eleven exportable categories of chinese pungent vegetables
abstract: China is a major producer and exporter of pungent vegetables, including garlic, ginger, chili peppers, onions, scallions and mustard vegetables. Based on export data for 11 categories of Chinese pungent vegetables from 2015 to 2024, this study used CR4 and CR8 indices to measure export market concentration and market dependence coefficients. The results showed that the export value of Chinese pungent vegetables increased by approximately 73.49% in 2024 compared to 2015. Fresh leeks and other alliaceous vegetables, mustard vegetables, fresh chili peppers, onions and shallots showed relatively high export market concentration. Dried garlic and ground chili peppers were strongly dependent on the United States, whereas unground ginger showed a dual-core dependence structure in the Netherlands and the United States. The findings indicate that market diversification, product upgrading and risk monitoring are essential for improving the stability of Chinese pungent vegetable exports. Bangladesh J. title: Tensões entre mercado global, identidade nacional e reerguimento de fronteiras
abstract: Contemporary international relations reveal a scenario increasingly shaped by tensions between the integrative logic of the global market and the identity-driven forces fueling nationalism. Across the world, a renewed emphasis on physical and symbolic borders emerges as a reaction to the economic, cultural, and political uncertainties associated with globalization. This contradictory movement reflects the simultaneous advance of two historical vectors: on one hand, the consolidation of transnational flows of capital, technology, and information; on the other, the resurgence of discourses around sovereignty, economic protection, and cultural exclusion. While corporations and multilateral institutions extend their influence beyond nation-states, governments adopt defensive strategies based on restrictive immigration policies, trade barriers, and the reinforcement of national identities. This ambivalence highlights the crisis of the post-Cold War liberal global order, challenging ideals of interdependence and international cooperation. Moreover, the rise of populist leaderships in different contexts amplifies the political use of borders as symbols of control and autonomy in response to a perceived global inequality. The interplay between economic globalization and nationalist reaffirmation produces deep effects on global governance, regional stability, and human rights. Therefore…

title: Unraveling the Factors of Sustainable Market Competitiveness: Strategies of Digitalization, Circular Economy, Green Finance, and Gender Equality
abstract: ABSTRACT Despite the central role of digitalization, circular economy, green finance, and gender equality in the European Union (EU) sustainability and competitiveness agendas, the mechanisms through which these factors jointly shape sustainable market competitiveness remain insufficiently understood. Existing research has widely examined these factors in isolation, whereas rare attention has been given to their combined direct, mediating, and moderating relationships grounded in the dynamic capabilities view, ecological modernization, and feminist institutionalism theories across the EU member states. Hence, this study primarily aims to examine the direct association among the outlined factors. Secondly, it examines the mediating role of circular economy between digitalization and sustainable market competitiveness, the mediating role of circular economy between green finance and sustainable market competitiveness, and the mediating role of green finance between digitalization and circular economy. Third, it seeks the moderating role of gender equality between digitalization and circular economy, the moderating role of gender equality between digitalization and green finance, and the moderating role of gender equality between green finance and circular economy across the EU nations. To this end, the study extracted country‐year level data from Eurostat and the OECD for 2014–20…

title: An Investigation of Market Invariance for the Tokyo Stock Exchange
abstract: ABSTRACT We test the invariance‐of‐bet hypothesis from Kyle and Obizhaeva (2016) for the Tokyo Stock Exchange (TSE). The pooled regression coefficients of the logarithm of the number of trades on the logarithm of the product of volume and volatility range from 0.663 to 0.665, close to the theoretical value of two‐thirds predicted by the invariance‐of‐bet hypothesis. Using the TSE as a relatively clean benchmark, we further examine when the empirical two‐thirds relation deviates from its theoretical prediction. We find that deviations become more pronounced during extreme market conditions, for stocks facing more binding tick‐size constraints, and around the market open and close. Our results also suggest that measurement errors in transaction data can contribute to deviations from the two‐thirds relation.

title: Sustainability‐Related Information and Secondary‐Market Corporate‐Bond Spreads: Disclosure, Verification, and Contractual Commitment
abstract: ABSTRACT This study examines whether observable disclosure environments are associated with secondary‐market pricing in a global sample of corporate bonds containing a sustainable‐classified subset. Using corporate bonds from LSEG Workspace, the analysis relates option‐adjusted spreads to three dimensions of sustainability‐related information architecture: disclosure, external verification, and contractual commitment. Disclosure is negatively associated with option‐adjusted spreads in cross‐sectional specifications, but issuer fixed‐effects and within‐between estimates indicate that this association is primarily between issuers rather than within issuers. The principal zero‐versus‐positive Disclosure comparison has observed support among nonclassified bonds; classified bonds have no zero‐Disclosure observations. Moreover, the Disclosure Index ranges from 0 to 2 among nonclassified bonds and from 3 to 5 among classified bonds in the support sample, preventing a like‐for‐like comparison across classification groups at a common index value. Verification is positively associated with spreads in conventional joint specifications but is insignificant when recorded classification is included; its positive values occur exclusively among classified bonds in the support sample. Contractual commitment has sparse support. These findings describe conditional associations for outstanding bon…

title: Intermediate-Layer Governance and the Coupling of an Effective Market and a Proactive Government: A Mechanism-Based Analysis of Practices in the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area
abstract: Within the broader context of the "One Country, Two Systems, Three Legal Systems" framework, the cross-border flow of production factors among Guangdong, Hong Kong, and Macao has long faced a dual dilemma: high institutional convergence costs and the risk of market failure when governance remains laissez-faire. This paper argues that intermediate-level governance represents a third pathway to resolve this dilemma and achieve an effective synergy between an efficient market and an active government. Building upon transaction cost theory and drawing on the core institutional innovation practices within the Guangdong–Hong Kong–Macao Greater Bay Area, this study examines the mechanism and practical outcomes of intermediate-level governance, identifies the barriers to deepening such governance, and proposes pathways for improvement, thereby providing empirical insights for governance innovation in diverse institutional environments.

abstract: A mass circumcision social service initiative serves as a form of community-based healthcare, bringing essential medical services closer to the public. This activity, which provides circumcision services through a collaboration between professional organizations and the local government, was held to commemorate the 62nd National Health Day in 2026. It took place on November 14, 2026, in Bonto Tinggi, Tondong Kura Village, Tondong Tallasa District, Pangkep Regency. The event was organized by the Pangkep Regency branch of the Indonesian National Nurses Association (PPNI) in partnership with the Pangkep Regency Health Office. The initiative successfully delivered mass circumcision services, representing a joint contribution from professional organizations and the local government toward public healthcare. This cross-institutional collaboration serves as a vital approach to supporting the delivery of community-based health services.

abstract: Relevance. Personalized assistance is particularly important for adults with intellectual disabilities, who may require individualized support with daily activities, communication, and social interaction. Aim. To analyze the implementation of the personal assistant social service for people with intellectual disabilities, using the activities of the Shliakh Dobra (“Path of Goodness”) civic organization in the Uman territorial community as a case study, and to identify the organizational conditions needed for its further development. The empirical basis consists of information on assistant recruitment, the number of people receiving support, the organization of assistance, and service coordination. title: Evolution of a hospital-integrated online consultation service: a five-year descriptive study of utilization, expenditure, and insurance coverage
abstract: Abstract Background Online medical services are increasingly integrated into routine healthcare delivery, but evidence on the long-term evolution of hospital-integrated online consultation services remains limited. This study described changes in utilization, clinical scope, patient age distribution, expenditure composition, and medical insurance coverage over five years. Methods This retrospective repeated cross-sectional study used administrative outpatient data from a tertiary specialist hospital between 2021 and 2025. Annual utilization, age distribution, expenditure composition, and payment mechanisms were examined descriptively. An exploratory interrupted time-series analysis assessed changes in the monthly proportion of online consultations following the institutional implementation of expanded medical insurance mobile payment in June 2024. Results Online consultations increased from 62 in 2021 to 29,842 in 2025, accounting for 9.5% of total outpatient visits, while participating clinical specialties increased from 4 to 18. Across the full study period, in-person and total outpatient activity decreased by 13.8% and 4.7%, respectively, with most of the decline occurring in 2022. During the more comparable period from 2023 to 2025, online, in-person, and total outpatient activity increased by 58.3%, 3.0%, and 6.6%, respectively. The medication share of online-associated ex…

Context-aware forecasting of inter-firm competitive dynamics with graph learning and multi-agent reasoning
abstract: Abstract The evolution of competitive dominance in technology-intensive industries is shaped by complex interactions among research activity, media visibility, strategic disclosures, public attention, and market signals. Understanding these dynamics is critical for strategic intelligence, yet existing predictive models often treat firms as isolated entities and provide limited support for contextualizing long-horizon firm-to-firm competitive forecasts. Here, we introduce an integrated framework that captures the relational nature of market competition by extending our prior Bayesian Multivariate Time-series Graph Neural Network with a newly designed, post hoc, lookahead-free multi-agent reasoning layer. The framework infers inter-firm relational dependencies endogenously from multimodal signals to forecast latent firm competitiveness and pairwise competitive gap trajectories with quantified predictive uncertainty. To evaluate strategic plausibility, specialized persona-driven language model agents critique the forecasted trajectories across technological, financial, and regulatory lenses using retrieved evidence. Evaluated under a rigorous date-based temporal protocol with strictly withheld test horizons, the framework consistently outperforms competitive structural baselines and yields well-calibrated prediction intervals. title: Forecasting Respiratory Syncytial Virus Activity Using Seasonal ARIMA Models: Evidence from CDC Weekly Surveillance Data
abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) imposes seasonal operational pressure on paediatric care and hospital healthcare systems. This study evaluates whether weekly RSV test percent positivity data from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) National Respiratory and Enteric Virus Surveillance System (NREVSS) can support short-term forecasting of RSV transmission activity. The national weekly surveillance dataset spanning 3 January 2015 to 27 June 2020 was analyzed with four forecasting approaches: seasonal autoreggressive integrated moving average (SARIMA), non-seasonal autoregressive integrated moving average (ARIMA), exponential smoothing (ETS), and a seasonal naive benchmark model. Model predictive performance was validated via a 52-week chronological holdout sample and rolling-origin forecasts for 1–4 week ahead horizons. Multiple evaluation metrics were adopted, including root mean square error (RMSE), mean absolute error (MAE), symmetric mean absolute percentage error (sMAPE), directional accuracy, and peak-timing error. Exploratory time-series analyses verified prominent annual seasonality and short-term serial dependence embedded in RSV percent positivity time series. Among all candidate models, SARIMA yielded the smallest RMSE and MAE on the holdout dataset, and exhibited relatively robust performance as the forecast window extended. The overall findings demon…

title: Short-Term Forecasting of Weekly Dengue Cases in Singapore Using ARIMA and Fourier-ARIMA Models
abstract: In this paper, a clear case-only forecasting model is developed on weekly basis. Dengue in Singapore based on official surveillance data between 2012-W01 and 2026.W17. The paper questions whether the number of cases routinely reported can be useful on their own. Short-term warning information in cases when external covariates are not available or are delayed. Dengue Fever and Dengue Haemorrhagic Fever cases were aggregated on a weekly basis, converted with log(1 + cases), tested to be stationary, and modelled using Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average (ARIMA). And Fourier-ARIMA specifications. Candidate models were compared through residual diagnostics, information criteria, and recursive one-week-ahead validation on the final 10% of the series. ARIMA(4,1,0)+Fourier(2) was selected because it balanced point accuracy, residual adequacy, and parsimony. In the 75-week test period, the model achieved MAE of 11.6 cases and RMSE of 16.0 cases, while 90% prediction interval coverage was 80%. The framework is therefore potentially useful as interpretable and timely surveillance decision support for early warning and preparedness, but it should be combined with field intelligence and future calibration work.

The Role of Risk‐Neutral Moments in Forecasting Future Realised Variance: An International Perspective
abstract: ABSTRACT This paper estimates the predictability of future realised variance for eight stock markets using US‐listed proxy ETFs, based on their risk‐neutral variance, skewness, and excess kurtosis. Our evidence shows that risk‐neutral variance and skewness have a positive relationship with future realised variance, while excess kurtosis has a negative relationship. Results from various statistical tests for model comparison indicate that incorporating second and higher‐order risk‐neutral moments from specific market proxies, as well as aggregated moments across market proxies, into the HAR‐RV model enhances the predictability of future realised variance. The inclusion of these moments provides additional information, significantly improving forecasting power and reducing extreme underestimation. Moreover, portfolio allocation exercises demonstrate that these improvements can translate into economically meaningful certainty‐equivalent return gains.

BriefCensus: A short metering campaign that chooses permanent monitors for rooftop photovoltaic fleet estimation and forecasting
abstract: Most rooftop photovoltaic (PV) systems report no live generation, so operators estimate fleet output from a few monitors, yet the metering needed to choose those monitors remains unclear. BriefCensus chooses permanent monitors from a short temporary metering campaign. Its forward greedy search matches the capacity-weighted ratio of the campaign set with no fitted weights, so the estimate needs no refit when a monitor fails. Its outage filter removes campaign rows with under half of the capacity reporting, because such rows otherwise reward survival during data outages. A logged confirmation run on 16 UK regions, without the filter, passed its rule at four weeks and kept 0.68 of the one-year selection gain. With the filter, added after that run, four weeks kept 0.82 on 12 regions of unread systems and cut the error by 27% against random monitors at k = 10. An Australian hold-out agreed. In the retrospective forecast experiment, the largest gains from monitor selection occurred at 0.5 h and 1 h. The simulated campaigns support testing a one-month metering campaign in the field. Keywords: Rooftop Photovoltaics, Fleet Estimation, Reference Systems, Monitor Selection, Measurement Campaign, Short-Term Forecasting.

title: A Physically Interpretable Dual‐Encoder Cross‐Attention LSTM for Water Level Forecasting in Dam–Tide Interaction Systems
abstract: ABSTRACT Predicting the water level in real time in regulated tidal rivers is challenging because upstream dam releases and downstream tidal fluctuations act simultaneously, with their relative dominance shifting within an event. Attention‐based deep learning models for such systems have generally either mixed all forcings within a single encoder, meaning no forcing‐level attribution can be recovered, or distributed attention across variable–lag pairs in a self‐attention stream. This makes it impossible to read the relative influence of two named physical forcings. This study proposes a dual‐encoder cross‐attention long short‐term memory (LSTM) framework that separates the forcings at the encoder level rather than the attention level. Dam discharge and tidal stage are encoded by dedicated bidirectional long short‐term memory (BiLSTM) encoders. Attention is then applied at two levels: temporal cross‐attention with a per‐horizon query and channel attention normalized over the two forcings. When applied to the Gahwa River Basin, which is subject to releases from the Namgang Dam and tidal forcing from Sacheon Bay, the framework was evaluated across 12 flood events using event‐based cross‐validation. Predictions from 1 to 12 h ahead were benchmarked against those from a single‐encoder LSTM. The two models performed comparably at short lead times. Beyond 5–6 h, however, the baseline …

title: Hybrid Seamless Seasonal‐to‐Annual Forecasting for the Wind Energy Sector Over the Americas
abstract: Abstract Wind power generation is sensitive to atmospheric variability across seasonal to annual timescales, creating demand for climate information that is both skilful and temporally consistent. Here we develop a hybrid seamless seasonal‐to‐decadal forecasting framework for annual wind speed over the Americas. The hybrid system combines dynamical predictions from seasonal and decadal forecast systems with a statistical multilinear regression model driven by four large‐scale ocean–atmosphere variability indices. Temporal consistency is achieved by constraining decadal ensemble members according to their agreement with updated seasonal predictions, avoiding discontinuities when transitioning across forecast horizons. Results show that the hybrid framework provides skilful wind predictions in key wind energy regions of the Americas, including the Great Plains and northeastern Brazil, and in some cases outperforms dynamical‐only forecasts, while preserving forecast continuity across timescales. These findings demonstrate the potential of combining seamless dynamical predictions with statistical post‐processing for wind energy climate services.

title: Regime-Gated Feedback Adaptive Conformal Prediction for Financial Forecasting
abstract: Financial prediction intervals must respond to volatility clustering and abrupt shifts in forecast-error distributions. We propose regime-gated feedback adaptive conformal inference (RG-ACI), which combines volatility-normalized nonconformity scores, rolling calibration, a single online miscoverage-rate state and a causal short-to-long volatility-ratio gate. Building on the finance-specific score normalization of Chen et al., the method couples a retrospective coverage correction with an ex-ante volatility signal without introducing a second error-feedback state. On 20 simulated heavy-tailed, autoregressive stochastic-volatility paths with multiple regime transitions, RG-ACI attains 0.895 mean coverage and 0.894 crisis-period coverage at a nominal 90% target with low between-path dispersion, while volatility-normalized rolling calibration remains the most efficient interval in width and interval score. Component ablations separate the effects of error-rate adaptation, the volatility gate and feedback gain, and quantify the calibration–efficiency tradeoff of each. The contribution is an explicitly causal, single-state integration of feedback and regime gating together with a transparent analysis of its tradeoffs under designed distribution shifts.

title: Multicollinearity Problem in Prediction of Egg Albumen Index and Some Regression Methods
abstract: Research on Japanese quail (Coturnix coturnix japonica) eggs examined factors affecting albumen index prediction and evaluated the multicollinearity problem among egg quality traits. The study included egg weight, egg width, egg length, shape index, and Haugh unit as explanatory variables for predicting albumen index. Correlation analysis results showed a high positive relationship (r=0.85) between egg weight and egg width and a high negative relationship (r=−0.91) between egg length and shape index. Variance inflation factor (VIF) values ranging from 1.41 to 30.30 indicated the presence of strong multicollinearity within the dataset. To overcome the effects of multicollinearity, principal component regression (PCR) and penalty-based regression methods including Ridge, LASSO, Liu, and Elastic Net were applied. PCR analysis showed that the first two principal components explained 75% of the total variance, demonstrating the effectiveness of dimension reduction. Ridge regression stabilized coefficient estimates by retaining all variables, whereas LASSO controlled model complexity through coefficient shrinkage. Liu regression provided stable coefficient estimates under correlated variable structures, while Elastic Net combined L1 and L2 penalties to regulate coefficient selection. The comparison of model performance criteria demonstrated that PCR, Ridge, and LASSO regression model…

title: Applications of Deep Learning Algorithms in Protein Structure Prediction and Design
abstract: The three-dimensional configuration of a protein is important for its biological function, which is crucial in biological study and drug development. The progress of deep learning has greatly improved the prediction of protein structures. Especially, the AlphaFold series has increased the prediction precision and extended its use in the simulation of biomolecular complexes and drug discovery. This paper describes the latest progress in protein structure prediction and antibody design based on deep learning. The emphasis is on the enhancement and efficiency of the template-based method and the AlphaFold series. Furthermore, the practical applications of these methods in antibody engineering and drug discovery are illustrated by considering specific examples such as AbEgDiffuser for simultaneous sequence and structure design, and AlphaFold3 for the choice of covalent ligands. Experimental data indicate that deep learning can precisely forecast the protein structures and effectively improve the design and screening of potential substances, thereby offering new possibilities for rational drug design. In the future, more research should concentrate on predicting the conformational changes of proteins, designing novel antibody frameworks from scratch, and obtaining multiple drug-like properties at the same time.

Machine-learning-assisted prediction and optimization of tensile strength in particulate-filled polymer composites
abstract: Abstract Particulate-filled polymer composites (PFPCs) are characterized by high specific strength, good formability, and considerable design flexibility, making them key materials for rapid tooling in aerospace equipment manufacturing. In this study, metal-powder/resin composites were investigated, and a tensile-strength dataset comprising 45 independent experimental conditions was established. Three machine-learning regression algorithms, namely linear least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression, k-nearest neighbors (KNN), and support vector regression (SVR), were employed to develop tensile-strength prediction models. A fixed outer five-fold cross-validation procedure was used to obtain out-of-fold (OOF) predictions, while hyperparameters were selected through inner five-fold cross-validation within each outer training fold; a genetic algorithm (GA) was subsequently used to further optimize the SVR hyperparameters. The OOF RMSE, MAE, and R² values of SVR were 1.67 MPa, 1.32 MPa, and 0.882, respectively, and those of GA-SVR were 1.54 MPa, 1.21 MPa, and 0.901. With increasing particle volume fraction and particle size, the tensile strength initially increased and then decreased, whereas ball-milling time had a relatively limited effect. title: Physics‐Constrained Recurrent Prediction of Fatigue Stiffness Degradation in Composite Laminates Under Constant‐Amplitude and Two‐Stage Variable‐Amplitude Loading
abstract: ABSTRACT Composite structures are susceptible to fatigue damage under complex cyclic loading, and accurate prediction of stiffness degradation is important for structural condition assessment and life management. In this study, constant‐amplitude and two‐stage variable‐amplitude fatigue tests were conducted on four carbon‐fiber composite laminate configurations. A physics‐constrained sequential‐learning framework, termed PI‐LSTM‐VA, is developed for full‐curve stiffness degradation prediction. The model predicts a nonnegative degradation intensity and integrates it over an endpoint‐independent logarithmic cycle coordinate. A parameter‐supervised switch module represents additional posttransition degradation while preserving stiffness continuity. On four held‐out variable‐amplitude specimens, specimen‐mean MAE and RMSE were 0.008238 and 0.010016, respectively. RMSE decreased by 21.8% relative to the shared constrained baseline and by 39.2% relative to direct LSTM. Repeated specimen partitions confirmed lower average error, although dispersion increased and some predictions worsened. Separate five‐fold constant‐amplitude holdout tests yielded specimen‐mean RMSE of 0.015918 across 38 specimens and supported applicability within the investigated domain.

title: A Multi‑Objective Metaheuristic‑Driven Feature Selection Method for Body Fat Prediction
abstract: Accurate estimation of body fat percentage (BFP) is essential for obesity assessment and cardiovascular risk management. However, conventional anthropometric methods lack sufficient precision, while specialized body composition analyzers entail high costs that limit their widespread clinical adoption. This study proposes a multi‑objective metaheuristic‑driven feature selection framework that integrates an artificial neural network (ANN) with the Non‑Dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II (NSGA‑II) to optimize both predictive R2 and feature parsimony for BFP estimation. The proposed methodology is evaluated on a benchmark dataset comprising 252 individuals with 13 anthropometric predictors. A comprehensive baseline assessment is conducted using 16 machine learning algorithms, including six linear and ten non‑linear models. The hybrid ANN‑NSGA‑II framework identifies an optimal subset of six features, achieving a root mean square error (RMSE) of 3.4962 and an R‑squared (R²) value of 0.8311. These quantitative outcomes demonstrate that embedding a multi‑objective metaheuristic selection mechanism within an ANN architecture enables substantial dimensionality reduction while maintaining robust predictive performance. The proposed approach provides a cost‑effective and computationally efficient alternative for BFP prediction using only fundamental anthropometric measurements, thereby…

title: Genomic prediction of feed conversion ratio and breast muscle protein content across dietary protein regimes in Arbor Acres broilers using Genomic Best Linear Unbiased Prediction (GBLUP), BayesB, and Reproducing Kernel Hilbert Spaces (RKHS) models to diss
abstract: This study conducted genomic prediction of body weight gain and breast protein content in 500 Arbor Acres broilers across dietary protein regimes (18%, 21%, 24% CP) and water stress conditions (well-watered, moderate stress, severe stress). Birds were phenotypes for body weight gain, breast protein content, lysine, and methionine. Genotyping-by-sequencing generated 42,567 SNPs. Four genomic prediction models (GBLUP, BayesB, RKHS, BayesCπ) were evaluated using five-fold cross validation. RKHS achieved the highest prediction accuracies for breast protein (r=0.85) and body weight gain (r=0.72). a training population of 150-200 individuals were sufficient (r>0.65). eight QTL were identified, with overlapping but distinct positions on chromosomes 1A and 7A for yield and protein, suggesting tight linkage rather than pleiotropy. Genomic selection reduced cycle length from 5 to 2 years and improved cost efficiency by 45-52%. Top RKHS with 200 training individuals effectively improves breast protein without compromising yield under stress. It is recommended that NAPRI implemen genomic selection targeting QTL on chromosomes 1A and 7A, with RIL-289, RIL-089 and RIL-124 advanced as dual purpose lines.

title: Effect of Data Augmentation and Membership Functions on ANFIS-Based Tensile Strength Prediction of FDM-Printed PETG Parts
abstract: Fused deposition modeling (FDM) enables the fabrication of complex polymeric components; however, the tensile performance of printed parts is strongly influenced by processing conditions and can be difficult to predict when only a limited number of experimental observations are available. This study investigates the use of linear interpolation-based data augmentation combined with an adaptive neuro-fuzzy inference system (ANFIS) for predicting the tensile strength of FDM-printed polyethylene terephthalate glycol-modified (PETG) specimens. Layer thickness, infill density, and nozzle temperature were investigated using a Taguchi L9 experimental design, with three specimens fabricated for each condition and their mean tensile strength values used as the reference dataset. The experimental data were augmented in MATLAB using linear interpolation to generate datasets containing 200, 400, and 600 samples. Gaussian ANFIS models with three membership function configurations (M222, M333, and M444) were subsequently developed using 60/40, 70/30, and 80/20 training/testing ratios. Model performance was assessed using R2, MSE, and MEP, and a multi-criteria performance index was employed to determine the optimum configuration. The results showed that increasing the number of membership functions generally improved prediction accuracy, whereas increasing the augmented dataset size did not ne…

title: A comparison of machine learning models and established grading scales for hospital mortality prediction in non‐traumatic subarachnoid haemorrhage
abstract: Abstract Introduction Existing severity grading scales show limited ability to guide decisions in subarachnoid haemorrhage (SAH). Machine learning (ML) offers a promising alternative. We compared ML models against established scales—World Federation of Neurosurgeons (WFNS), Fisher, Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) and Acute Physiology and Chronic Health Evaluation (APACHE) IV—for predicting hospital mortality in Intensive Care Unit (ICU) patients with non‐traumatic SAH. Methods We collected relevant data from adults with non‐traumatic SAH admitted between January 2011 and March 2025. Two multivariable prognostic models were developed and compared across logistic regression (LR) and three ML algorithms (random forest [RF], artificial neural network [ANN] and eXtreme Gradient Boosting). Model 1 included demographics, GCS, radiographic findings, vasospasm, 5‐day interventions and APACHE IV scores, whereas Model 2 omitted APACHE IV. Model performance was assessed with area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) and area under the precision‐recall curve. Results Among conventional scales, APACHE IV discriminated best (AUROC 0.871, 95% CI 0.839–0.902), followed by GCS severity (0.804), WFNS (0.780), and Fisher (0.540). Model 1 achieved AUROCs ranging from 0.916 to 0.935 (ANN AUROC 0.935, LR AUROC 0.928), significantly outperforming individual admission scales. For Model 2 …

Strength–stiffness coupling mechanism governing grout‐rock interface performance and anchorage capacity
abstract: Abstract Interfacial shear strength ( τ p ) and shear stiffness ( k s ) at the grout‐rock interface (GRI) are key parameters governing load transfer and pull‐out resistance of fully grouted rock bolts. This study systematically investigates the shear behavior of the GRI under four grout material conditions, namely early high‐strength cement (EHC), EHC with 5% silica fume (SF), EHC with 10% styrene‐acrylate emulsion (SA), and EHC with 20% SA. Direct shear tests combined with digital image correlation (DIC) are conducted to characterize the macroscopic shear response and localized deformation of the interfaces. (1) The direct shear tests show that the incorporation of SF increases τ p from 7.7 to 9.1 MPa and k s from 15.5 to 22.5 GPa/m, whereas the addition of SA reduces these parameters to 7.3 MPa and 10.5 GPa/m at 10% SA and further to 5.7 MPa and 5.7 GPa/m at 20% SA; (2) The DIC results reveal that interfacial shear stiffness is closely associated with the extent of the localized deformation on the grout side. The deformation‐zone thickness decreases from 2.5 mm for EHC to 1.5 mm for EHC with 5% SF, but increases to 4.0 and 5.0 mm for EHC with 10% and 20% SA, respectively. A stiffer grout therefore results in stronger deformation localization and a higher k s , whereas a more deformable grout broadens the shear zone and reduces k s . Development of a School Partnership Management Training Module to Improve the Managerial Capacity of Senior High School Principals in Sekadau Regency
abstract: This study aimed to develop a valid, practical, and effective school partnership management training module to strengthen senior high school principals' managerial capacity in Sekadau Regency. It was motivated by low partnership management competence: all 21 principals were categorized as “Poor” or “Very Poor,” particularly in program implementation (45.2) and supervision and evaluation (42.8). This research and development design used a mixed-methods approach adapted from the five-stage ADDIE model: Analysis, Design, Development, Implementation, and Evaluation. Participants included five principals for interviews, seven for a focus group discussion, two expert validators, five principals for a limited trial, and ten for a broader trial. The module was evaluated using a four-point Likert-scale instrument. Quantitative data were analyzed using mean scores, N-Gain, and a paired-samples t-test; qualitative data were analyzed through the interactive model of Miles, Huberman, and Saldaña. The findings indicated that the module was valid, with feasibility scores of 82.3% from material experts, 79.5% from language experts, and 81.7% from instructional media experts, all “Very Feasible.” Its practicality score was 84.2% (“Very Practical”), with readability (88.0%) and ease of use (86.0%) as its strongest features. Effectiveness was demonstrated by an increase in the mean score from 48.…

title: No change in skeletal muscle oxidative capacity biomarkers after 6 weeks of twice‐weekly single‐leg cycle interval training in young active adults
abstract: Abstract Interval training (INT) of sufficient frequency, intensity and duration can increase biomarkers of skeletal muscle oxidative capacity in humans. Studies typically involve three to four sessions per week; however, the effect of reduced training frequency on this response is unclear. Most studies also do not include a non‐exercise control (CON) condition to account for the potential influence of extraneous, uncontrolled factors. We employed a single‐leg, counterweighted cycling model to investigate the effect of twice weekly INT for 6 weeks on biomarkers of skeletal muscle oxidative capacity including mitochondrial content and fibre capillarisation. Sixteen healthy active adults (6 males, 10 females; 22 ± 3 years; peak oxygen uptake: 36.1 ± 6.1 mL kg −1 min −1 ) performed INT with one leg and their contralateral limb served as a CON. INT involved 4 × 5‐min bouts at an intensity of 50%–60% W peak , interspersed with 2.5 min of recovery at 20% W peak . Muscle biopsy samples obtained from the vastus lateralis of both legs before and after the intervention revealed no differences in the primary outcome measure, citrate synthase maximal activity ( P = 0.350, time × leg interaction). There were also no differences in multiple markers of mitochondrial protein content or capillarisation (all P > 0.05), except NDUFB8 protein content, which increased post‐training in the INT leg o…

title: Mutation of Dengue Virus Envelope Protein and Mechanism of Cross-Host Transmission
abstract: Dengue virus spreads worldwide. Mosquitoes of the Aedes genus pass it to humans. The virus poses big risks to global public health. Its envelope protein, E protein, controls three key viral behaviors. It lets viruses recognize host cells, fuse cell membranes and live through changing environments. Most adaptive non-synonymous mutations appear on the gene that makes E protein. These amino acid changes reshape the protein’s 3D structure. This change lets dengue jump across different host species. This paper sorts out E protein structures and sites where mutations often happen. It explains how single amino acid changes affect virus heat resistance, receptor binding speed and intracellular replication. Mutated E proteins help viruses escape mosquito immune defenses. They also help viruses survive stress inside mammalian cells. This paper builds a full molecular path to explain how dengue shifts between mosquitoes and people. Current research has clear limits. Few studies measure how multiple mutations work together. Lab cell models cannot copy real infection environments. Long-term tracking of wild virus strains is rare. This work improves theories about dengue’s evolution in two hosts. It picks out key adaptive mutation sites. It offers theory support for epidemic early warning, broad-spectrum vaccine design and new antiviral drug research.

title: Biomechanical Load Characteristics, Injury Mechanism, Prevention and Intervention of Proximal Hamstring in Badminton Racket-Side Forward Lunge
abstract: The badminton racket-side forward lunge is a special step frequently used in the front court. During the landing buffer phase of this action, the proximal hamstring bears a relatively large centrifugal traction load, which is likely to cause tendon injury at the ischial tubercle, limiting daily activity and sports performance. This article systematically reviews the biomechanical load characteristics of the proximal hamstring during the badminton racket-side forward lunge, analyzes its specific injury mechanism, summarize and analyze the existing prevention and intervention strategies. The results showed that: in the landing buffer stage of the badminton racket-side forward lunge, the large flexion of the hip and knee joint form the bidirectional traction stress concentration effect on the proximal hamstring; Long term unilateral load accumulation and dislocation of the hip and knee motion sequence will further increase the risk of local injury; resistance and eccentric training and landing movement technology correction are the main damage prevention and control measures at present, and various external equipment can be used as auxiliary intervention measures. The existing research has some limitations, such as insufficient measured data, difficulty matching laboratory conditions to real-life badminton competition scenarios, and lack of long-term tracking. title: Molecular Mechanism of Alzheimer's Disease: Aβ -amyloid protein deposition, abnormal phosphorylation of tau protein and neurofibrillary tangles
abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a prevalent neurodegenerative disorder that seriously endangers the physical and mental health of the elderly population. Currently, the molecular pathogenic mechanism of this disease has not been fully elucidated, and there are limitations in clinical treatment methods, making it difficult to curb the progression of the disease at its root. This article systematically analyzed the interactive effects of the three core pathological mechanisms in AD, namely Aβ deposition, excessive phosphorylation of Tau protein, and neuroinflammation, and reviewed the advantages and disadvantages of traditional interventions, nano-delivery carriers, and nasal administration as new treatment technologies. The results show that the pathological process of AD is dominated by a multi-dimensional interactive network, and the APOE4 gene and chronic neuroinflammation play a key role in upstream regulation. Simply removing pathological proteins cannot stop disease progression, while targeted precise intervention such as p-tau217 and ceRNA regulatory networks show significant potential. This study clarified the multi-factor interwoven pathological regulatory mechanism of AD, complemented the cognitive limitations of single pathological research, and provided theoretical support for the development of early screening markers and precise targeted treatment. title: The Molecular Mechanism of HIF-2α-Mediated ADRN-MES Phenotypic Transition Under Hypoxia in Neuroblastoma Cells
abstract: Neuroblastomas are usually located in an area with poor oxygen supply inside the tumour; such an environment may promote metastasis and other serious behaviour in children. Tumor cells can switch between adrenergic and mesenchymal states to affect the clinical outcomes of young children.Hypoxia causes changes in the shape of cancer cells, the whole molecular signal pathway is still not known, and essential regulators that control these switches at different stages of cell growth have not been identified, Therefore,many crucial regulatory circuits still need to be studied. Based on the data of hypoxic cell lines, genetic knockdown assays and various molecular diagnostic methods were used to identify the metabolic pathways that cause structural changes in neuroblastoma under oxygen deprivation. HIF-2α is a switch that changes the expression pattern of the adrenergic signature genes into a mesenchymal one. PRRX1 and NOTCH3 are the secondary mediators that can decrease the production of native adrenergic mRNAs and promote the activation of a pro-tumorigenic mesenchymal feedback loop via HIF-2α. Currently, all of them are still at the level of laboratory cell culture and have not been validated by living mouse experiments or histopathological tests of real human tumour tissue. title: Dual‐Mechanism Suppression of Posterior Capsule Opacification by an MMP2/9‐Responsive Sulforaphane‐Eluting Intraocular Lens
abstract: ABSTRACT Posterior capsule opacification (PCO) is the most frequent complication of cataract surgery and is driven by the epithelial‐mesenchymal transition (EMT) of residual lens epithelial cells (LECs). The current standard of care, Nd:YAG laser capsulotomy, is reactive and carries well‐documented complications, underscoring the need for proactive pharmacological prophylaxis. Drug‐eluting intraocular lenses offer a localized delivery platform. Here, we developed a sulforaphane (SFN)‐eluting intraocular lens (GelMA‐SFN@IOL) by integrating SFN‐loaded gelatin methacryloyl (GelMA) microparticles onto the IOL haptics. The GelMA carrier was designed to respond to MMP‐2/9, which were upregulated in PCO‐associated capsular tissues. In vitro, MMP‐2 enhanced SFN release from GelMA‐SFN microparticles, supporting enzyme‐responsive release behavior. In TNFα‐stimulated HLE‐B3 cells, SFN suppressed LEC migration and EMT marker expression, accompanied by increased autophagic activity and reduced MMP‐2/9 expression. These findings suggest a potential feedback mechanism whereby SFN‐mediated MMP downregulation could reduce enzyme‐promoted carrier degradation and release as the pathological signal subsides. In a rabbit PCO model, GelMA‐SFN@IOL preserved capsular clarity and reduced aberrant LEC proliferation over 28 days, with no obvious histological abnormalities in the examined ocular tissues. …

title: Synergistic Mechanism of Functional Foods Rich in Active Peptides in Tumor Immunotherapy
abstract: Given that traditional tumor therapy is associated with recurrence risk and immunotherapy is limited by the tumor immune microenvironment, alternative adjuvant approaches are urgently needed. In this context, active peptide-functional foods have emerged as promising auxiliary resources, yet their synergistic anti-tumor mechanisms are still not well understood, necessitating further research. In this paper, the dual functions of active peptides in direct tumor suppression and bidirectional regulation of immunity were analyzed. The synergistic principle of inducing immunogenic cell death and activating systemic anti-tumor immunity was elucidated by Gramicidin S and its light-controlled derivatives. Four types of synergistic methods, including molecular modification, light-controlled administration, combination therapy, and nanocarriers, were summarized. It was pointed out that these peptides had problems such as lack of preparation standards and only stopping in vitro experiments. This study clarified the mechanism of active peptide combined with immunotherapy, and provided theoretical support for the development of anti-tumor active peptide food. title: STRENGTHENING THE CAPACITY OF THE BORNEO WASTE BANK THROUGH COMMUNITY-BASED OUTREACH IN THE BANJAR SERASAN NEIGHBORHOOD, PONTIANAK
abstract: The Borneo Waste Bank, which was established in 2014, has played a role in supporting waste reduction while also boosting community engagement. However, its management appears to be suboptimal, as the Waste Bank still faces challenges related to organizational governance and human resource capacity. These two aspects need to be addressed so that the Waste Bank’s management can improve in the future. The community service activity was conducted using a participatory outreach method, meaning that the material presented was not merely one-way communication; rather, the community was actively involved in discussions and in identifying issues. The activity was carried out in three stages: preparation, implementation, and evaluation. During the evaluation phase, the team distributed a questionnaire before and after the activity concluded, covering four main points: the level of understanding of the educational material, willingness to implement the material, an assessment of the activity’s benefits and expectations for the program’s sustainability, and gathering direct feedback for planning future activities. The results of the activity showed that the implementation process went as expected, with active participation from the community. All four aspects assessed by the team showed improvement. title: The Key Role and Potential Molecular Mechanism of HER2 (ERBB2) in Breast Cancer: A Bioinformatics Analysis Based on the TCGA-BRCA Database.
abstract: Breast cancer is one of the most common malignant tumors in women, with the HER2-positive subtype exhibiting strong invasiveness and poor prognosis. ERBB2, a key encoding gene of HER2, plays a crucial role in the development and progression of breast cancer, and its molecular mechanisms still require further in-depth analysis. This study, based on the TCGA-BRCA database, integrated transcriptome expression data, clinical information, and survival data to comprehensively analyze the molecular characteristics related to ERBB2. Differential expression analysis identified 334 significantly expressed genes, and GO and Hallmark pathway analyses revealed that they are mainly involved in the ERBB2 signaling pathway, estrogen response, and lipid metabolism. Further PPI network construction and module analysis revealed that ERBB2, GRB7, STARD3, PGAP3, and MIEN1 form a highly cohesive core functional module. Based on survival analysis, there is some correlation between ERBB2 expression and patient survival. The present study sheds lights on the synergistic interactions between ERBB2 and co-amplified genes in breast cancer, indicating that they may be involved in the synergistic progression of breast cancer and metabolic reprogramming. The results serve as a reference for the research of molecular mechanism of breast cancer that is positive to the HER2 receptor and screening for potential …
