title: SiC-embedded 3D carbon network microspheres derived from spray-dried granules for tunable microwave absorption
One Carbon Matters: Conformational Bending Stabilizes Ferroelectric Nematic Order and Enables Domain‐Modulated Antiferroelectric Smectic C Order
abstract: ABSTRACT Molecular design of ferroelectric nematics has primarily focused on optimizing highly polar rigid mesogenic cores, whereas the role of flexible aliphatic segments in regulating molecular conformation and polar ordering remains insufficiently understood. Here, we show that exchanging the positions of a methylene group and the ether oxygen within the linkage between a polar rigid core and an aliphatic tail (Ar‐O‐CH 2 ‐ versus Ar‐CH 2 ‐O‐) reshapes the molecular conformational landscape and profoundly influences the stability of the ferroelectric nematic (N F ) phase. Molecules with a stronger preference for bent, pear‐like effective geometries exhibit significantly enhanced N F stability, accompanied by reduced splay and bend elastic constants in the apolar nematic phase, and lower apparent activation barriers for dipolar reorientation. Further elongation of the flexible segment introduces competing packing motifs and gives rise to a domain‐modulated antiferroelectric smectic C (SmC AF ) phase. These findings establish conformational bending as a molecular‐shape parameter for controlling hierarchical ferroelectric and antiferroelectric liquid‐crystalline order, bridging the design principles of conventional bent‐core layered ferroelectrics with emerging rod‐like fluid ferroelectric materials.

title: Dissipation‐Decoupling‐Reorganization: Three Layer Response and Energy Matter Decoupling in the Urban Boundary Layer to Anthropogenic Heating
abstract: Abstract Coherent structure contributions to momentum, sensible heat, and CO 2 fluxes after anthropogenic heating were examined based on seven level turbulence observations from the Beijing 325 m meteorological tower. A three layer vertical structure was identified according to the 2017 data set: a near surface dissipation layer (8–15 m) marked by reduced CO 2 transport efficiency, organized coherent structures decreased significantly; a decoupling layer (47–80 m) characterized by divergent responses in the ejection and sweep contributions to heat and CO 2 fluxes; and an upper reorganization layer (200–280 m) featuring with recovered transport efficiency and a profile inflection point. This three layer pattern is most clearly expressed in 2017. Data from 2016 to 2015 show simplified two layer (decoupling and reorganization) without a distinct dissipation layer, indicating that the complete three layer response depends on background meteorological conditions. Our results provide a vertically explicit framework for understanding anthropogenic perturbations to urban turbulence transport process.

Layer‐by‐Layer Solvent‐Free Additive Manufacturing Enabling Controllable Ultrathick Electrode Coating for Lithium‐Ion Battery
abstract: ABSTRACT Dry electrode manufacturing is emerging as a transformative strategy for sustainable lithium‐ion battery production, yet achieving ultrathick electrodes with homogeneous microstructures, efficient electron transport, and high electrochemical utilization remains a fundamental challenge. Here, we report a solvent‐free, layer‐by‐layer additive manufacturing strategy that enables architecturally controlled ultrathick cathodes through molecular‐level coupling between reduced graphene oxide (rGO) and binder. During roll‐to‐roll hot pressing, molten binder infiltrates the rGO framework to form a continuous conductive binder network, uniformly bridging NMC811 particles to enhance particle adhesion, suppress binder aggregation, and establish efficient electronic percolation. This strategy enables precise control of electrode thickness (300–1000 µm) and areal loading (20–100 mg cm − 2 ) while eliminating solvent‐induced structural defects. The resulting multilayer cathodes, comprising up to five sequentially deposited layers, deliver a specific capacity of 230 mAh g − 1 at 0.1 C and an areal capacity of ∼10 mAh cm − 2 . The nearly linear increase in areal capacity with layer number demonstrates homogeneous conductive networks and efficient electrochemical utilization throughout the electrode thickness. Spatially robust pixel‐based mapping of biotic stress in Pinus nigra using unmanned aerial vehicle multispectral imagery and Random Forest
abstract: Abstract BACKGROUND Biotic stress threatens forest health, creating a need for rapid monitoring methods that complement field surveys. This study compared four original multispectral bands, five vegetation indices, and their combination for segmentation‐free, pixel‐based Random Forest mapping of healthy and unhealthy Pinus nigra canopies in Bingöl, Türkiye. Field and laboratory observations confirmed Dothistroma spp . and Tomicus spp . within the stand. RESULTS Unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) imagery with a ground sampling distance of 2.31 cm was evaluated using identical five‐block spatial cross‐validation partitions comprising 113 georeferenced trees (55 healthy and 58 unhealthy), each represented by mean predictor values from a manually delineated within‐crown sampling polygon. The combined model achieved the highest pooled overall accuracy (98.23%; Kappa = 0.9646). The vegetation‐index model achieved 97.35% accuracy and the highest area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (ROC‐AUC, 0.9991), with Optimized Soil‐Adjusted Vegetation Index (OSAVI) showing the greatest mean permutation importance. Exact McNemar tests detected no significant differences among models (all P = 1.000). title: Charging schedule as a design variable for active harmonic filter sizing in unbalanced low-voltage networks: when do optimisation and V2G add value?
Timed Elastic Band based trajectory planning and MPC based adaptive cruise control for car-like autonomous vehicle
abstract: This paper presents a hierarchical control architecture for a car-like autonomous vehicle. Lateral motion is handled by a Timed Elastic Band (TEB) local planner that repeatedly optimizes a short-horizon waypoint band, while steering is generated by a Pure Pursuit controller tracking the optimized local path. Longitudinal behaviour is governed by a model predictive control (MPC) based adaptive cruise control (ACC) that regulates speed and inter-vehicle distance in free-driving and car-following modes, explicitly respecting acceleration and braking limits and enforcing a minimum safety distance. Safety is addressed through constraint-aware planning and control: the TEB optimization penalizes proximity to obstacles and violations of lane boundaries using smooth penalty terms that support stable gradient-based updates, while the MPC-ACC embeds hard bounds and distance constraints to prevent unsafe following. The integrated stack is evaluated in representative driving scenarios, including lane keeping and car-following, and is benchmarked against the MathWorks Path Following Control System (PFCS) reference model to quantify tracking behaviour and constraint compliance under identical conditions.

Job Rotation as a Human Capital Strategy and Perceived Employee Performance in the Ghana Armed Forces
abstract: Objectives Job rotation is widely promoted as a human capital strategy, yet survey evidence from African armed forces is scarce. Anchored in Human Capital Theory, this study examines how three rotation-related dimensions of career mobility in the Ghana Armed Forces (GAF), namely military education and training, personnel transfers and peacekeeping deployments, are associated with perceived employee performance (productivity), and which implementation challenges personnel perceive Methods A cross-sectional questionnaire survey was administered to 390 serving personnel drawn from the Army, Navy and Air Force Results Personnel rated training and education most favourably (M = 4.04), peacekeeping missions moderately (M = 3.39), and personnel transfers at the scale midpoint (M = 2.95), with items on the transparency and fairness of transfers rated below neutral. In a multiple regression the three dimensions jointly accounted for 34.7 percent of the variance in perceived performance (R² = .347). Only training and education were significantly associated with performance (β = .57, p < .001); personnel transfers (β = −.04, p = .469) and peacekeeping deployments (β = .07, p = .184) were not. Insufficient career counselling (M = 3.89), long periods in a single role and the priority of institutional needs over personal career growth were the most strongly endorsed implementation challenges…

title: Digitalisation, Eco‐Innovation and SME Internationalisation: A Dynamic Capabilities Perspective
abstract: ABSTRACT This study integrates the digitalisation and dynamic capabilities literature to examine the relationship between digitalisation, eco‐innovation and internationalisation in small and medium‐sized enterprises (SME). Using data obtained from 300 SME owner‐managers operating in the United Kingdom, the findings suggest that digitalisation positively impacts eco‐innovation and consequently the nature of internationalisation activities. In addition, there is a moderating effect of internationalisation experience on the relationship between eco‐innovation and internationalisation. These findings highlight the pivotal role of eco‐innovation, digitalisation and international experience in enabling SMEs to thrive in international markets. Furthermore, the study offers empirical evidence of how SMEs dynamically develop digital resources, and internationalisation is an outcome of building such capabilities. The implications for practice and future research avenues are examined.

title: Leveraging Industry 5.0 for Sustainable Waste Valorization Planning: A Novel Decision‐Support Framework for Barrier‐Strategy Prioritization
abstract: ABSTRACT Accelerating urbanization and increasing waste generation pose significant challenges to sustainable development and underscore the need to effectively implement waste valorization systems. This study addresses critical gaps in thorough barrier and Industry 5.0‐integrated strategy identification for implementing sustainable waste valorization systems. This study develops an innovative decision‐making barrier‐strategy analysis tool, which extends Step‐wise Weight Assessment Ratio Analysis (SWARA) and Measurement of Alternatives and Ranking according to COmpromise Solution (MARCOS) within an Interval Type‐2 Trapezoidal Fuzzy Set (IT2TrFS) environment to capture a wider range of uncertainty for more accurate analysis. IT2TrFS‐SWARA facilitates holistic evaluations of implementation barriers, while IT2TrFS‐MARCOS prioritizes Industry 5.0‐oriented strategies. To validate this model, a case study of implementing advanced incineration‐based medical waste valorization was conducted. The results indicated “Inefficient process design for energy recovery mechanism” as the most significant barrier and “Integrate renewable energy as an energy source” and “Provide wearable safety‐monitoring IoT devices for workers” as most pivotal mitigation strategies. This tool can be extended to other urban sustainability domains, which support Industry 5.0‐enabled policy interventions for sustai…

title: A ordem e o caos: transições de poder na história antiga e medieval
abstract: The transition of power in Ancient and Medieval History was marked by dynamics of order and chaos that shaped civilizations and social structures. In Antiquity, political changes often occurred through military conquests, the collapse of empires, and the rise of new leaderships, as seen in the Persian, Roman, and Greek empires. Stability, often illusory, was disrupted by internal wars, popular uprisings, and external invasions. In the medieval period, the fragmentation of power after Rome's fall led to decentralization and feudalism. In this context, vassalage relationships and the Church's influence played central roles in political and social reorganization. The struggle for hegemony among European kingdoms, Muslim expansion, and the Crusades exemplified how distinct forces shaped power transitions in this era. Thus, the history of these two periods is a narrative of continuous reconfiguration, where stability was often preceded or followed by chaos and instability.

abstract: ABSTRACT Qur'an memorization learning in nonformal education requires instructional strategies that promote accurate recitation, memorization fluency, long-term retention, and learner motivation. This article aims to examine educators' instructional strategies for improving the quality of Qur'an memorization through three interconnected dimensions: planning, implementation, and evaluation. The study employed a qualitative literature review approach with descriptive qualitative analysis through a literature search conducted in October 2026 using Google Scholar, Garuda, and DOAJ. The review analyzed seven relevant scholarly articles published between 2023 and 2024. The synthesis identifies three essential dimensions of effective instructional strategies. First, learning planning involves assessing learners' initial abilities, establishing realistic memorization targets, selecting appropriate methods, and designing evaluation procedures. Second, instructional implementation integrates tahsin, talaqqi, wahdah, and muraja'ah with individualized guidance, motivational reinforcement, and active learner participation. Third, learning evaluation emphasizes memorization accuracy, fluency, tajwid compliance, retention, and continuous formative feedback. The discussion also highlights the importance of family involvement and supportive learning environments in strengthening memorization pr…

title: Marketing Communication Strategy Through Social Media Content based on Local Wisdom to Increase the Added Value of Indonesian Coffee Brands (Study on Conservation Coffee Brands Based on Local Wisdom)
abstract: The coffee industry is a significant sector in Indonesia, contributing to both domestic production and consumption. However, challenges such as declining production due to climate change, limited agricultural land, and increasing global competition have encouraged coffee businesses to adopt more innovative marketing strategies. One emerging approach involves social media marketing communications that incorporate local cultural values and traditional knowledge. This study aimed to explore the social media marketing communication strategies employed by Indonesian coffee businesses, particularly those incorporating local wisdom, and examine their implications for brand value. A descriptive qualitative approach employing a holistic single-case study design was adopted. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews with consumers and coffee business owners who actively incorporated local wisdom-based content into their marketing strategies. The findings indicated that such content fostered emotional connections with consumers, enhanced brand awareness and engagement, and strengthened brand loyalty. These findings highlight the strategic potential of integrating local cultural values into social media marketing communications to enhance brand differentiation, strengthen perceived brand value, and support long-term business sustainability in Indonesia's coffee industry

title: Traceability as a Quality Cue: How Consumers Respond to Product‐Level Information
abstract: ABSTRACT Food supply chains have become longer, more fragmented and less visible to the people at the end of them, leaving consumers unable to verify the safety, provenance and ethical credentials of what they buy and firms unable to demonstrate them credibly. Against this background of growing supply chain complexity and consumer uncertainty, we examine whether traceability information functions as a quality cue in meat consumption and how it influences purchase intentions. Focusing on electronic identification (eID)‐enabled lamb traceability in Australia, we employ a multi‐study, mixed‐method design. Study 1 ( n = 10) explores consumer perceptions through in‐depth interviews. Study 2a conducts a pilot, whereas Study 2b uses a Facebook A/B field experiment to test behavioural responses in a natural setting. Study 3 ( n = 402) applies an online experiment to test a moderated mediation model. Qualitative findings show generally favourable attitudes, linking traceability to quality, safety and assurance. Whereas the field experiment shows no significant behavioural effect, the controlled experiment demonstrates that traceability increases purchase intention via perceived product quality, with stronger effects for highly involved consumers. Findings suggest that traceability can serve as a strategic, institutionally verified quality signal but that its effectiveness is conditional…

title: SAÚDE MENTAL DOS PROFISSIONAIS DE ENFERMAGEM: A PRÁTICA DO AUTOCUIDADO COMO ESTRATÉGIA DE MELHORIA
abstract: A saúde mental dos profissionais de enfermagem tem recebido atenção diante das condições de trabalho marcadas pela sobrecarga, pressão emocional e contato frequente com o sofrimento humano. Este trabalho tem como objetivo analisar de que forma a prática do autocuidado contribui para a melhoria da saúde mental dos profissionais de enfermagem e identificar estratégias utilizadas para promover o bem-estar mental desses trabalhadores. Trata-se de uma revisão integrativa da literatura, com abordagem qualitativa e caráter descritivo e exploratório. A busca dos estudos foi realizada na Biblioteca Virtual em Saúde (BVS), entre maio e julho de 2026. Como resultados foram analisadas 13 publicações, os achados apontaram que a sobrecarga, as jornadas extensas e as condições inadequadas de trabalho estão relacionadas ao estresse ocupacional e ao desgaste emocional dos profissionais. Entre as práticas de autocuidado identificadas, destacam-se a atividade física, o descanso, o relaxamento e o apoio social. As estratégias individuais apresentaram contribuições para o bem-estar mental, especialmente quando associadas ao suporte institucional e à melhoria das condições de trabalho. Conclui-se que o autocuidado contribui para a promoção da saúde mental dos profissionais de enfermagem. Sua associação com medidas institucionais de acolhimento, apoio psicológico e condições adequadas de trabalho fav…

title: Valoración actuarial del reaseguro no proporcional en seguros de automóviles: Aplicación de la tarificación del Burning Cost
abstract: En el mercado asegurador es fundamental contar con mecanismos para mitigar los riesgos asociados a la intensidad de los siniestros. En este proceso interviene un agente clave, el reasegurador, quien proporciona cobertura ante eventos inesperados. En este contexto, el presente trabajo aborda la modalidad no proporcional de los contratos de reaseguro, en particular Excess Loss y Stop Loss, centrándose en su tarificación mediante la metodología Burning Cost. Asimismo, se aplican distintas técnicas de triángulos de run-off para analizar la sensibilidad en la estimación de la prima de reaseguro. El estudio se basa en una cartera real (modificada) de seguros de automóviles perteneciente a una aseguradora con reconocimiento a nivel nacional.

title: POLA ASUH ORANG TUA DAN PERILAKU SIBLING RIVALRY PADA ANAK USIA DINI: TINJAUAN LITERATUR
abstract: ABSTRACT Sibling rivalry in early childhood is manifested through jealousy, competition for parental attention, quarrels, and rivalry between siblings. This study aims to (1) analyze the relationship between parenting styles and sibling rivalry behavior and (2) examine parenting styles and family factors associated with such behavior. This article employs a structured literature review guided by the PRISMA 2020 reporting principles. The literature search was conducted in October 2026, covering publications from 2012 to 2025, and analyzed 18 relevant publications consisting of empirical studies, reviews, and meta-analyses. The findings were synthesized using a narrative-comparative approach. Meta-analytic evidence indicates that authoritative parenting is negatively associated with sibling conflict (r = −0.201), whereas neglectful, inconsistent, permissive, and authoritarian parenting styles are positively associated with it. Other studies highlight the importance of differential parental treatment, age gaps, child characteristics, autonomy support, and parental mediation of conflicts. Publications on family education further reinforce the implications of communication, family interaction, and prosocial behavior development, although they do not directly examine sibling rivalry. These findings suggest the need for warm and consistent parenting that is fair and responsive to chil…

title: Bacterial DnaK Promotes CHIP‐Mediated GPX4 Degradation: A Bone‐Targeted DNAzyme–Nanozyme Strategy for Repair of Infected Bone Defects
abstract: ABSTRACT Staphylococcus aureus infection impairs bone repair, but how bacterial proteins disrupt osteogenic progenitors remains unclear. The bacterial chaperone DnaK promotes glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4) degradation in bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs), accompanied by lipid peroxidation, ferroptotic injury, and impaired osteogenic differentiation. GPX4 protein turnover increases without a change in Gpx4 mRNA abundance. A candidate E3‐ligase screen identifies the C terminus of Hsc70‐interacting protein (CHIP) as a mediator of this response. Catalytically inactive CHIP attenuates DnaK‐associated K48‐linked GPX4 ubiquitination, while CHIP knockdown preserves GPX4 and osteogenic proteins in primary BMSCs. To target bacterial DnaK and host oxidative injury, a bone‐targeted deoxyribozyme (DNAzyme)–nanozyme platform (DMPA) combines a dnaK ‐targeting DNAzyme with manganese hexacyanoferrate, polydopamine, and alendronate. In infected cultures, DMPA reduces bacterial dnaK transcript and DnaK protein abundance and improves BMSC redox balance and matrix mineralization. In a mouse model of infected tibial defects, DMPA promotes bone regeneration. These findings link bacterial DnaK to host GPX4 degradation through CHIP and establish a bone‐targeted DNAzyme–nanozyme strategy that combines bacterial DnaK suppression with redox regulation to promote repair of infected bone defects.

title: Rethinking Paradoxical Tensions in the Transition Toward Circular Business Practices: A Systematic Literature Review
abstract: ABSTRACT As central actors in the transition toward a circular economy, firms face multiple tensions when implementing circular business practices, often resulting in paradoxical situations. Although paradox scholars increasingly call for a systems perspective to capture the full complexity of wicked problems, the extent to which systems thinking informs research on paradoxes in firms' transition toward circular business practices remains unclear. We address this gap through a systematic literature review of 42 peer‐reviewed articles published between 2018 and 2025 and indexed in Scopus and Web of Science. We examine the implicit assumptions underlying the reviewed studies, drawing on the three core elements of systems: hierarchy, interconnections, and emergence. To structure the analysis, we classify paradoxical tensions across four analytical levels—macro, interorganizational, organizational, and individual. Based on recurring patterns in the literature, our review identifies four implicit assumptions that constrain a more systemic understanding of paradoxes in firms' circular transition: (1) Paradoxes largely exist in isolation from one another and (2) remain stable over time, (3) within the organizational level, strategy is the key element shaping paradoxes, and (4) individual actors, and their perceptions and experiences of paradoxes, play a limited role in shaping firms' …

title: An In Situ Amorphous Thermoconversion Strategy for Macroscopic Glass Heterojunctions
abstract: ABSTRACT Heterojunction fabrication has long been constrained by the stringent lattice‐matching requirements between dissimilar components, limiting the accessible material combinations and processing routes. Here, we report an amorphous thermoconversion strategy for constructing hybrid glass heterojunctions in situ. In this approach, structural competition among liquid phases derived from distinct metal–organic hybrid halide crystal structures generates divergent luminescence across amorphous phases, giving rise to a new family of halide glass heterojunctions. These hybrid halide glasses display excitation‐dependent and time‐gated persistent luminescence that is color‐tunable across a 160 nm wavelength window, a property that enables direct optical visualization and confers broad photonic versatility. Beyond their optical attributes, the resulting macroscopic glass heterojunctions exhibit well‐defined mechanical rigidity and arbitrary processability, supporting spatially resolved fluorescence and persistent luminescence outputs alongside one‐dimensional (1D) optical waveguiding at losses that surpass those of state‐of‐the‐art crystalline counterparts. Therefore, this work delivers the demonstration of macroscopic heterojunctions in halide supramolecular glasses and establishes a scalable route to multi‐channel, low‐dimensional optical waveguide for information storage and encr…

title: Divergent Smoke Transport and Subseasonal Responses Under Uncertainty in Smoke Injection Height in the 2017 Pacific Northwest Event
abstract: Abstract Wildfire smoke injection height (IH) is closely linked to aerosol vertical distribution, long‐range transport, radiative effects, and aerosol‐meteorology interactions. The Unified Forecast System coupled with the second‐generation NASA GOCART aerosol scheme currently lacks explicit plume‐rise parameterization, confining biomass burning emissions to the boundary layer. This treatment misrepresents extreme events like the 2017 Pacific Northwest (Pacific Northwest event) wildfires, which injected smoke into the upper troposphere and lower stratosphere. We used idealized sensitivity experiments within fully coupled subseasonal‐to‐seasonal (S2S) configurations to examine differences in smoke evolution among simulations with prescribed IHs (surface‐to‐500 hPa and surface‐to‐200 hPa) and the default boundary‐layer injection. Our results demonstrate that simulations with elevated injection better reproduce lofted smoke layers and associated long‐range transport pathways. Crucially, we find that simulations with different IHs show pronounced, delayed divergences in coupled meteorological fields. While aerosol and atmospheric differences among the simulations are modest in the first 2 weeks, they become more pronounced during weeks 3–4. By this period, simulations with varied prescribed IHs show substantial local differences in near‐surface temperature (ranging from −7.7 to +8.3…

title: Prioritizing Accounting Conservatism Strategies under Financial Constraints: An Integrated Fuzzy MCDM Framework for Enhancing Financial Reporting Quality
abstract: Conservative accounting strategies are essential for businesses to enhance the quality of their financial reporting. However, businesses with limited managerial and financial resources cannot implement all these strategies simultaneously; therefore, it is necessary to determine which conservative accounting strategies should be prioritized. The primary objective of this study is to identify the most suitable conservative accounting strategies for firms operating under resource constraints. To achieve this, an integrated multi-criteria decision-making model based on fuzzy logic is employed. First, expert evaluations are modeled using spherical fuzzy sets. Second, the LOPCOW technique is used to calculate the importance weights of the criteria. Third, conservative accounting strategies are prioritized using the CoCoFISo method. This study offers a distinct perspective to the literature by addressing conservative accounting not merely in terms of influencing factors, but as a strategy selection problem amidst limited resources. The findings demonstrate that an uncertainty-responsive conservative accounting framework is the optimal strategy for accounting conservatism, while stakeholder and creditor protection emerges as the most important criterion.

title: An integrated financial statement analysis and valuation method for stock investment decisions: Evidence from PT Bank Syariah Indonesia
abstract: This study aimed to examine the role of financial statements in supporting stock investment decisions by integrating financial performance analysis with Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) valuation method. Focusing on PT Bank Syariah Indonesia (BSI) during the period from 2020 to 2023, the study adopted a quantitative descriptive method using financial ratios and valuation analysis. The results showed consistent growth in assets, revenue, and net profit, as well as improvements in profitability ratios such as Return on Assets (ROA) and Return on Equity (ROE), reflecting enhanced operational efficiency. The valuation results further indicated that the Bank’s stock was undervalued, as the estimated intrinsic value exceeded market price, suggesting potential investment opportunities. These results outlined the importance of applying an integrated analytical method that combined fundamental and valuation analysis to support moreeffective and informed investment decision-making.

Detecção de fraudes em transações financeiras com Machine Learning: uma revisão da literatura
abstract: The growing digitalization of financial transactions has significantly increased the occurrence of fraud, making its detection a central challenge for banking institutions and payment companies. Given the limitations of traditional rule-based systems, machine learning has gained a prominent position in recent scientific literature. This study aimed to analyze, through a narrative literature review, the main machine learning techniques applied to fraud detection in financial transactions, with emphasis on credit cards. The research, qualitative and exploratory in nature, was based on the critical analysis of eight scientific works published between 2018 and 2026, found in databases such as IEEE Xplore, Scopus, ScienceDirect, and Google Scholar. Results indicate the recurrent use of ensemble algorithms, such as Random Forest and boosting, alongside classical models, such as Logistic Regression, Decision Trees, and Support Vector Machine, with no universally superior algorithm. The extreme data imbalance is addressed through undersampling, SMOTE and its variants, and decision threshold adjustment. It was also found that metrics such as F1-Score, AUC-ROC, and the area under the precision-recall curve are more suitable than accuracy alone, and the tension between opaque models and the right to review automated decisions set out in the Brazilian General Data Protection Law was discus…

Generative AI and the Evolution of Mortgage Underwriting: Measuring and Mitigating Racial Disparities
abstract: Abstract Mortgage underwriting is entering a new phase of technological change as general-purpose generative AI tools begin to appear in mortgage origination workflows. We develop an audit framework to evaluate how large language models process mortgage applications. Using real HMDA applications, we experimentally manipulate borrower race, race proxies, and credit quality, and prompt leading commercial LLMs to make approval and pricing recommendations. LLMs recommend more denials and higher interest rates for Black applicants than otherwise identical white applicants, with disparities largest for riskier loans and persisting when race is signaled through names or locations. A simple instruction to avoid bias substantially reduces disparities when race is explicit, partially reduces the name-based pricing gap, and does little against the geographic pricing gap. In matched HMDA–Freddie Mac data, race-blind LLM recommendations correlate with actual lender pricing and subsequent delinquency, though the delinquency association operates largely through observed credit scores. The results show how AI auditing can inform mortgage underwriting governance before general-purpose models become more deeply embedded in origination workflows.

title: Carbon emissions regulation, input-output networks, and firm dynamics: The case of a low-carbon-zone pilot in China
abstract: Abstract Input-output linkages among sectors and firms are largely overlooked when assessing regulatory policies. Using a carbon emissions regulation in China as an example, we find that the regulation facilitates the transition to green technologies and reduces entry and carbon emissions in the regulated sectors with large carbon emissions. We also find unintended spillovers via the input-output network, resulting in more entry and innovation in the downstream sectors; and less entry and innovation in the upstream sectors. These facts can be rationalized by a firm-dynamics model with input-output linkages. The results of quantitative exercises are substantially different when taking input-output linkages into account.

Robust Failure Handling Mechanism for Fog Computing Using Fuzzy Logic
abstract: Fog computing is an emerging computing paradigm suitable for time-sensitive and real-time Internet of Things (IoT) applications. The devices in the Fog environment are autonomous and not exclusively dedicated to Fog application processing. Due to that, the probability of device failure in the Fog environment is high compared with other distributed computing paradigms. Thus, handling failure in Fog is crucial to ensure successful application execution. Several techniques are available in the literature to handle failure, such as checkpointing and task migration, each of which works well in cloud based enterprise applications that mostly deal with static or transactional data. These failure-handling methods are not applicable to highly dynamic Fog environments. In contrast, this work focuses on solving the problem of managing application failure in the Fog environment by proposing a composite solution (combining fuzzy logic-based task checkpointing and task migration techniques with task replication) for failure handling and generating a robust schedule. We evaluated the proposed methods using real failure traces in terms of application execution time, delay and cost. Average delay and total processing time improved by 56% and 48%, respectively, on an average for the proposed solution, compared with the existing failure handling approaches.

Finding the right balance: a framework analysis of staff and service user experiences of moving to remote drug and alcohol support during the COVID-19 pandemic
abstract: Abstract Background Dependence on alcohol and other substances contributes significantly to poor health globally. Deaths associated with substance use have increased since the COVID-19 pandemic and providing effective support for recovery is critical. The pandemic required an unprecedented change to recovery services for substance use, from in-person care to mainly telephone and online support. The study described here forms part of a wider evaluation and was one of the first to explore the move to remote models of recovery services. Methods This was a multi-method qualitative study, employing in-depth interviews, focus groups, text-based asynchronous interviews, digital timelines and creative vignettes. Framework analysis was undertaken, with focus on service user out-of-pocket expenses as part of a health economic evaluation. A Public Involvement group, including people with experience of substance use, supported study design and analysis. Staff ( N = 36) and drug and alcohol service users ( N = 28) in an English city participated in one or more of the data collection methods. Findings were shared with staff and service users, and their input shaped the final analysis. Results Most participants wanted to retain remote services alongside in-person provision, post-pandemic. Remote delivery was not appropriate for everyone however, and not all aspects of service delivery work re…

title: Cerebra: A computationally efficient framework for accurate protein structure prediction
abstract: Abstract Remarkable progress has been made in the field of protein structure prediction. Representative methods like AlphaFold and RoseTTAFold achieve prediction accuracy close to experimental structural determination, but at the cost of heavy computational consumption for model training. In this work, we propose a new framework, Cerebra, for improving the computational efficiency of protein structure prediction. In this network architecture, multiple sets of atomic coordinates are predicted parallelly and their mutual complementarity is leveraged to rapidly improve the quality of predicted structures through a new attention mechanism named path synthesis attention (PSA). Consequently, Cerebra markedly reduces the computational consumption, achieving evident acceleration on both model training and inference, in comparison to OpenFold, the academic version of AlphaFold2. When evaluated on the CAMEO 2025 dataset, the Cerebra model trained on a limited number of GPUs shows comparable performance to the published OpenFold model that has been thoroughly optimized using a plethora of computational resources. Moreover, ablation studies confirm that the PSA mechanism efficiently accelerates the network convergence, suggesting its potential in handling the many‐body effects of protein geometries in graph‐based models. Finally, the fast inference of Cerebra effectively assists hallucinat…

When the grid overflows: a novel probabilistic framework to assess the success of storing excess electricity as heat in high-temperature ATES (HT-ATES) systems
abstract: Abstract Increasing shares of variable renewable electricity (VRE) are creating more frequent periods of surplus electricity, increasing the need for flexible options that can absorb and use this excess generation. One option is to convert surplus electricity into heat, but its effective use requires storage when heat production and demand do not coincide. Because heat demand remains concentrated in the colder months, long-duration seasonal thermal storage is needed to bridge this temporal gap. High-temperature aquifer thermal energy storage (HT-ATES) is one technology capable of providing this seasonal storage function. This study develops a demand-oriented operational probability of success (PoS) framework for evaluating whether HT-ATES can convert historically observed surplus electricity into useful seasonal heat. The Neubrandenburg system in Germany was used as a physically grounded reference case. Historical German electricity data from 2015 to 2022 were represented through empirical four-week surplus distributions and coupled to a chronological Monte Carlo inventory model accounting for charging availability, well thermal throughput, adopted storage limit, and thermal recovery. The model first generated a distribution of achievable seasonal heat delivery, which was then evaluated against alternative heat-demand targets. PoS is therefore expressed as the probability that …

title: Assessing DASHAT through the New Public Service Lens: A Qualitative Documentary Analysis
abstract: Public service innovation does not by itself demonstrate democratic citizen influence. Dapur Sehat Atasi Stunting (DASHAT), an Indonesian community-oriented nutrition initiative, provides an opportunity to distinguish between program intentions, reported implementation, citizen participation, and documented influence over service decisions. This study examines how documentary evidence portrays DASHAT’s alignment with the seven New Public Service (NPS) principles, with particular attention to citizen participation across four stages of co-production: commissioning, design, delivery, and assessment. The study employed qualitative documentary analysis using directed qualitative content analysis. Thirteen evidence units were extracted from eight selected DASHAT-related documents and mapped deductively to the seven NPS principles. The four stages of co-production served as complementary analytical categories. The analysis distinguished program intentions, reported implementation, empirical findings, and recommendations to establish appropriate boundaries of interpretation. The documents provide evidence of service provision, attention to vulnerable groups, community empowerment, and capacity-building activities. A specific menu-planning activity indicates citizen participation in service design. However, the reviewed sources provide less conclusive evidence of citizen influence over…

title: The lesson planning knowledge of pre-service science teachers
abstract: This study assessed lesson planning knowledge and final teaching demonstration performance among pre-service science teachers at Central Bicol State University of Agriculture–Pasacao Campus during the second semester of academic year 2025–2026. Using a quantitative descriptive-correlational design, the study covered all 82 fourth-year Bachelor of Secondary Education major in Science interns. Data were obtained through a 24-item five-point Likert-scale lesson planning knowledge questionnaire and the Pre-Service Student Teaching Demonstration Evaluation Form. Weighted means, one-way analysis of variance, and Pearson product–moment correlation with t-tests were employed. Respondents were classified as having Very High Knowledge in writing lesson plans (4.52), competencies required to write a lesson plan (4.50), and assessment and assignment (4.59), and Very Knowledgeable in creating lesson objectives (4.46). Knowledge did not significantly differ across the four dimensions (p = .233). All seven final teaching demonstration parameters were rated Outstanding Performance, with means from 4.55 to 4.67; differences among performance parameters were not significant (p = .705). Positive statistically significant correlations were reported between all four knowledge dimensions and seven performance parameters (r = .317–.772). The findings support targeted enhancement in objective writing,…

title: Governance of Professional Allowance Payments to Certified Non-Civil-Service Teachers with Inpassing Equivalence at Private Madrasahs: An Analysis of Legal Certainty and Fairness Following the Removal of Length of Service as A Criterion
abstract: This article examines the legal and governance framework for determining Teacher Professional Allowance (TPG) amounts for certified non-civil-service teachers with inpassing equivalence at private madrasahs in Indonesia, focusing on the treatment of length of service. Using normative legal research with statutory, conceptual and case approaches, it analyses relevant legislation, ministerial regulations, technical guidelines and Supreme Court Decision No. 55 P/HUM/2024. The analysis identifies a lack of alignment across three regulatory levels: higher-level legislation recognises length of service as an element of salary equivalence; Minister of Religious Affairs Regulation No. 4 of 2025 does not expressly mention it; and Director General Decision No. 665 of 2026 excludes it from the calculation. This inconsistency creates risks to legal certainty, proportional distributive justice, transparency, accountability and administrative effectiveness. The article argues that technical guidelines should not negate elements recognised by higher-level norms and proposes a six-stage governance model comprising integrated data collection, hierarchical verification, an operational definition of length of service, transparent calculation, an objection mechanism, and audit and evaluation. The study is normative and does not assess actual implementation in individual regions.

title: The Role of Customer Satisfaction In Mediating The Effect of Service Performance and Perceived Value On Customer Loyalty: Evidence From A B2B Outsourced Cleaning Service In A Pharmaceutical Manufacturing Setting
abstract: Outsourced facility services have become a strategic component of operations in Indonesia's highly regulated pharmaceutical industry, where cleanliness is not a cosmetic concern but a compliance requirement embedded in CPOB, WHO Prequalification, ISO 9001:2015, and ISO 14001:2015 standards. This study examined why an outsourced cleaning-service provider operating exclusively for a single pharmaceutical client since 2013 recorded 38 client complaints between November 2025 and January 2026, of which 66% concerned Service Performance and Perceived Value, and asked whether Customer Satisfaction mediates the effects of these two constructs on Customer Loyalty. Prior research has largely tested this chain in consumer-facing settings, leaving the business-to-business, compliance-driven pharmaceutical outsourcing context empirically unexamined. A quantitative, explanatory cross-sectional survey collected primary data from 355 employees of PT Bio Farma (Persero) Pasteur, Bandung, drawn by simple random sampling from a population of 3,096 and analyzed using PLS-SEM in SmartPLS. All eight hypotheses were supported at the 5% significance level. The model explained 74.0% of the variance in Customer Satisfaction and 68.3% of the variance in Customer Loyalty. Service Performance showed the strongest association with Customer Satisfaction (β = 0.543; f² = 0.901), while Customer Satisfaction sh…

title: Innovative Self-Efficacy and Social Identification as Drivers of Service Innovation Engagement and Innovation Performance in Digital SMEs
abstract: Digitalization provides opportunities for small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) to improve their services and strengthen innovation performance. However, realizing these opportunities depends not only on technology adoption but also on individual confidence and social relationships that encourage innovation. This study examines the effects of innovative self-efficacy and social identification on service innovation engagement, as well as the effect of service innovation engagement on innovation performance among digitally enabled SMEs in Surabaya, Indonesia. Using a quantitative explanatory survey approach, the study applies partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) to test the proposed relationships. The findings indicate that innovative self-efficacy and social identification positively influence service innovation engagement, with social identification demonstrating a stronger relationship. Furthermore, service innovation engagement positively influences innovation performance. These findings highlight the importance of individual confidence, a sense of belonging to business communities, and active involvement in service innovation. This study extends service innovation research to digitally enabled SMEs and offers practical implications for strengthening innovation practices and competitiveness.

Enhanced CO 2 Capture in Type III Porous Liquids via Steric Solvent Structure Regulation
abstract: Abstract Porous liquids (PLs), an emerging class of materials, combine the abundant porous structure of solid adsorbents with the rapid mass-transfer and fluidity properties of liquid adsorbents, showing great potential for CO2 capture. In this study, a targeted solvent structure regulation strategy was proposed to fabricate three sterically hindered solvents for PLs, including the conventional imidazolium ionic liquid [EMIM][NTF2], amino-functionalized ionic liquid [AEMIM][NTF2], and amino-hydrogen-bond bifunctional deep eutectic solvent [EMTA], which were blended with MOF-801 to construct three types of MOF-801-based PLs containing permanent micropores. A set of characterizations and molecular dynamics simulations were employed to confirm the successful synthesis of MOF-801-PLs. Meanwhile, the adsorption performance of MOF-801-PLs for CO2 in mimetic flue gas was evaluated, and the MOF-801-EMTA-PLs exhibited great adsorption capability of up to 1.378 mmol/g, higher than that of MOF-801-AEMIM-PLs (0.541 mmol/g) and MOF-801-EMIM-PLs (0.498 mmol/g). Furthermore, density functional theory (DFT) calculations and grand canonical Monte Carlo (GCMC) simulations were used to observe the CO2 adsorption mechanism. This study verifies that tuning solvent molecular structures is a feasible strategy for the design of advanced PLs.

One-Year Participation in A School-Based Yoga Program and Changes in Children’s Self- Regulation and Laceration-Related School Infirmary Visits
abstract: School-based interventions that support children’s psychological and physical functioning are needed to promote healthy development. This study examined changes associated with a year-long yoga program implemented as part of routine elementary school education in Japan. The Asa (morning) Yoga program was implemented during Monday morning homeroom sessions from April 2024 to March 2025 at one public elementary school. Data from 201 children for whom informed consent was obtained were analyzed. Psychological functioning was assessed before and after the intervention, and monthly visits to the school infirmary due to lacerations and bruises were examined across four study periods. Post-intervention scores were significantly higher for difficulty with self-control and difficulty with goal-oriented motivation. Visits to the school infirmary due to lacerations differed significantly across study periods, with fewer visits during January–February than during April–June. No significant pre–post changes were observed in quality of school life, and no significant differences were observed in visits due to bruises. Participation in a year-long, school-based yoga program was associated with changes in selected aspects of children’s psychological functioning and laceration-related infirmary visits. COVID Diaries, U.S. Media Response to COVID Vaccination Program, December 2020 to September 2021
abstract: Abstract We present a curated dataset of U.S. news coverage of the COVID-19 vaccination rollout to support research on media communication during a public health emergency. The dataset contains 5,317 unique URLs from 20 nationwide, open-access media outlets, spanning December 2020 (Phase 1a allocation) through September 2021 (broad availability and emerging mandates). Outlets were selected based on a survey of 489 U.S. adults identifying their primary sources of information about the vaccination program. For each publication, we provide outlet, date, headline, original URL, and a permanent link. These records capture the contemporaneous media environment in which individuals sought information and made decisions about COVID-19 vaccination. The dataset enables analyses of topical emphasis, framing, and agenda-setting across outlets and over time, and provides a resource for reproducible research on audience segmentation, economic drivers of content, and editorial retention strategies during the COVID-19 vaccination campaign.

title: Thermal response during erbium laser-assisted removal of ceramic crowns and laminate veneers: a scoping review
abstract: Abstract This review aimed to systematically map and synthesize the available evidence regarding the thermal effects of laser-assisted debonding of ceramic crowns and laminate veneers on the dental pulp and to identify current knowledge gaps. Following the Joanna Briggs Institute methodology and the PRISMA-ScR guidelines, the scoping review was conducted after preliminary screening identified limited and heterogeneous evidence for a systematic review. PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched through June 2026. Two independent reviewers screened eligible studies and extracted data on laser parameters, irradiation protocols, restorative characteristics, debonding performance, and thermal outcomes. A total of 63 records were identified, and 10 studies met the eligibility criteria and were included in this scoping review. Er, Cr: YSGG was the most investigated laser, followed by Er: YAG. The included studies evaluated the debonding of lithium disilicate and zirconia laminate veneers and full-coverage crowns. Considerable heterogeneity was observed in laser parameters, ceramic materials, restoration thicknesses, and outcome assessment methods. Intrapulpal temperature change and debonding time were the most frequently reported outcomes, with most studies reporting temperature increases below the commonly cited historical thermal threshold for irreversible pulp damage. To reveal the evolution and underlying mechanisms of these characteristics, this study investigated the microscale adhesion and macroscale mechanical response of the asphalt–aggregate interface induced by UV aging of asphalt. Subsequently, the microscale interfacial work of adhesion was quantified by AFM measurements and surface free energy theory, whereas the macroscale viscoelastic and tensile responses under dynamic shear and uniaxial tensile loading were assessed using an improved frequency sweep test with aggregate substrates and pull-off tests, respectively. Finally, the intrinsic linkages among the microscale properties of asphalt, the microscale interfacial adhesion, and the macroscale mechanical response were examined using Pearson correlation analysis. title: Colocalization between bone loading and metabolic activity in the human tibia in response to acute exercise
abstract: Abstract Bone strain and remodeling are important factors affecting bone strength. Better characterizing the relationship between these factors in response to acute loading will improve our understanding of bone metabolism in relation to daily physical activities. The purpose of this study was to evaluate colocalization between finite element-estimated bone strain and [18F]sodium fluoride ([18F]NaF) positron emission tomography (PET) imaging-estimated bone remodeling in the tibial diaphysis in response to acute exercise. We hypothesized that the exercise-induced change in standardized uptake values would be greatest in regions of higher strain. 26 participants underwent bilateral PET-magnetic resonance imaging (PET-MRI) scans before and after a bout of stair ascent and descent exercise. Finite element analysis was performed to calculate principal strain distributions in the tibial diaphysis. [18F]NaF standardized uptake values (SUV) were calculated from pre- and post-exercise PET data and mapped to the tibial surface. Mean pre-exercise and exercise-induced change in SUV were calculated and compared between regions defined by strain percentile. Both normalized mean pre-exercise and exercise-induced change in [18F]NaF SUV increased with maximum principal strain in a pattern suggesting an exponential relationship. title: Recurrent features of stress response in the unicellular zygnematophyte Mesotaenium: intracellular inclusions and vacuoles forming upon UV
abstract: Abstract The Zygnematophyceae, the closest algal relatives of land plants, many of which are unicellular, must manage environmental stress responses largely cell-autonomously, making them powerful models for dissecting the ancestral cellular toolkit underlying plant terrestrialisation. In this brief report, we revisit UV-B time-course experiment data on the unicellular zygnematophyte Mesotaenium endlicherianum , in which UV-B irradiation triggered a significant accumulation of terminal vacuoles. We re-analysed the corresponding RNA-seq data with a new focus on genes associated with vacuolar biology and lipid metabolism. Within 2 h of UV-B onset, homologs of genes linked to vacuolar functions in land plants were differentially expressed: transcripts of putatively lytic enzymes (a papain-like cysteine protease and two GH38 alpha-mannosidases), of a metal tolerance protein and of two AHK1-like histidine kinases increased, whereas those of the tonoplast H⁺-pyrophosphatase AVP1, the Ca²⁺/H⁺ antiporter CAX5 and the phosphatidylinositol 3-phosphate 5-kinase FAB1A decreased. Lipid-related transcripts indicated a shift from membrane lipid biosynthesis towards lipid turnover, including the induction of a SUGAR-DEPENDENT 1-like triacylglycerol lipase. abstract: Aim: This article examines the role of artificial intelligence (AI) in four core management accounting functions: cost analysis, budgeting, management control, and decision-making. Method: A structured literature review synthesizes findings from systematic reviews, case studies, experiments, a dissertation, and professional reports to distinguish demonstrated predictive benefits from broader claims about organizational performance. The review is limited by the absence of a complete database export and a study-specific PRISMA flow; it should therefore be read as a structured synthesis of accessible literature rather than a fully reproducible systematic review. Results: Machine-learning models can match or exceed human estimates in selected cost-estimation tasks when adequate historical data are available. In budgeting, machine learning can improve prediction accuracy, but predictive accuracy alone does not establish causal effects or guarantee appropriate resource allocation. In management control, digital tools support more timely and anticipatory monitoring, although the available evidence does not always isolate the effect of AI itself. For decision-making, the usefulness of AI depends on data quality, model explainability, user trust, professional competence, and the preservation of human accountability. title: Analysis of Causes and Risk Mitigation for Delivery Delays Based on On-Time In-Full (OTIF) Data in Non-Cement Distribution Using RCA and FMEA Methods at PT XYZ
abstract: Delivery punctuality is an important indicator of logistics service performance, yet non-cement distribution at PT XYZ still experiences delays. On Time In Full (OTIF) data from May to July 2026 recorded that only 54.64% of 14,986 shipments were delivered on time. This study aims to determine the on-time delivery rate, identify the dominant causes and root causes of delay, and determine mitigation priorities. The methods used were Pareto diagram, Root Cause Analysis (RCA) with fishbone and 5 Why, and Failure Mode and Effect Analysis (FMEA), with Severity, Occurrence, and Detection rated by two respondents. The Pareto results show that long parking time (49.9%) and unloading schedule (41.1%) caused 91.0% of the delays. RCA identified the root causes as the absence of a standard maximum stopping time, a joint arrival scheduling mechanism with receivers, a procedure for communicating estimated arrival, and a cargo readiness confirmation procedure. Based on FMEA, the highest Risk Priority Number (RPN) belongs to the absence of a joint arrival scheduling mechanism with receivers (336), followed by the absence of an estimated arrival notification procedure (168) and a standard maximum stopping time (120). Joint arrival scheduling with receivers should be the priority for improvement.

title: AI-DRIVEN INNOVATION AND ORGANISATIONAL TRUST IN AI: THE MEDIATING ROLE OF KNOWLEDGE TRANSPARENCY IN FAMILY-OWNED SMES
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly viewed as a driver of organisational innovation through its capacity to generate and recombine knowledge. However, the relationship between AI-driven innovation and organisational trust in AI remains insufficiently understood. Drawing on organisational trust theory and the knowledge-based view of the firm, this study examines the mediating role of transparency of AI-generated knowledge in linking AI-driven innovation to organisational trust in AI. Using cross-sectional survey data collected from managers and executives of family-owned SMEs and analysed through structural equation modelling, the study identifies positive associations among AI-driven innovation, knowledge transparency, and organisational trust in AI. The estimated indirect effect is consistent with the proposed mediating role of knowledge transparency, although the research design does not establish causality. The study contributes to innovation and knowledge research by examining perceived knowledge transparency as a link between AI-driven innovation and trust. It also offers managerial insights into the potential relevance of making AI-generated knowledge understandable and open to discussion.

title: Transformation of Business Communication Model in Crisis: Rebranding of Warung New Bahari into Ekspresss Bahari
abstract: This study examines the transformation of the business communication model in the franchise crisis experienced by Warung New Bahari (WNB), which underwent rebranding into Ekspresss Bahari (WEB) and succeeded in maintaining only 30 of 125 outlets in the Jabodetabek region. Using a qualitative approach with a case study design, data were collected through in-depth interviews with 12 informants, participatory observation of 8 outlets, business document analysis, and two focus group discussions. Findings reveal that there is a structural disjunction between the implementation of Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) technology and the Cultural Intelligence (CQ) of organizational actors, manifested in seven forms of communication gaps. The transformation of the communication model was designed through three phases—restart-up, reconcept, and rebranding—by integrating CQ into every layer of business communication. The recommended communication model integrates ERP as a strategic communication platform, CQ as the core competence of organizational actors, and Artificial Intelligence (AI) as an operational enabler. The novelty of this research lies in bridging the studies of ERP, business communication, and cultural intelligence in the context of crisis, downsizing, and rebranding of franchise-based MSMEs.

title: Implementasi PLTS–PLN dengan Automatic Transfer Switch pada Penerangan Gedung Parkir (Implementation of a Solar PV–Grid System with an Automatic Transfer Switch for Parking Garage Lighting)
abstract: Parking garage lighting needs an uninterrupted power supply, but solar PV output varies with irradiance and weather. This study implements a solar PV–PLN system with an Automatic Transfer Switch (ATS) for lighting on the seventh floor of the Universitas Pamulang Viktor parking building, and examines how far the field test records support conclusions about battery backup and energy contribution. The system consists of three 550 Wp PV panels, a 60 A MPPT controller, a 48 V 50 Ah battery, an inverter with a 1,500 W continuous rating, and a 63 A two-pole ATS, serving 75 LED lamps of 18 W each (1,350 W). Observations ran for seven days, 09:00–21:00 WIB, with readings every 30 minutes on the PV, battery, and PLN sides. The load was activated in three scenarios (12, 40, and 75 lamps) without controlled repetition. The system was assembled and supplied the lighting load. The design requirement of four hours at full load is 5.4 kWh, while the battery’s usable AC energy is only about 1.82 kWh (80% DoD, 95% inverter efficiency), equivalent to roughly 81 minutes. Transfer to PLN was observed at around 18:30, when battery voltage approached 45 V. Daily PV output was recorded at 275–446 W. On the first day, battery current differed substantially between instruments (11.86 A and 22.12 A), and ATS transfer time and actual irradiance were not recorded. title: PERFIL CITOPATOLÓGICO DO COLO DO ÚTERO EM MULHERES ATENDIDAS NA ATENÇÃO PRIMÁRIA DO CENTRO-NORTE DE RONDÔNIA
abstract: O câncer do colo do útero permanece relevante problema de saúde pública, especialmente na região Norte do Brasil. Este estudo analisou o perfil epidemiológico, assistencial e citopatológico dos exames realizados em mulheres residentes em Jaru-RO, entre 2020 e 2025, bem como a associação entre faixa etária e desfechos. Trata-se de estudo observacional, retrospectivo, descritivo, analítico e transversal, com dados do SISCAN/DATASUS (n=10.537). Utilizaram-se estatísticas descritivas e inferenciais (qui-quadrado de Pearson e Exato de Fisher; p<0,05). Houve maior frequência de exames entre 40–44 anos (15,76%), predominância de mulheres autodeclaradas amarelas (41,32%) e realização majoritária para rastreamento (99,51%), com 80,90% de citologia prévia normal. As amostras foram predominantemente satisfatórias (99,27%), com representatividade da zona de transformação em 77,60%. As lesões intraepiteliais foram pouco frequentes (LSIL: 0,47%; HSIL: 0,23%), com predomínio de exames sem alterações (99,29%). Na análise bivariada, não houve associação entre faixa etária e adequabilidade da amostra (p=0,351). title: The Economic Impact of Hosting International Sports Mega Events (2015- 2025): A Systematic Narrative Review
abstract: The hosting of the Olympic Games, FIFA World Cup and other sport mega-events is always touted as an economic imperative, with the expectation of an economic boost from the event, job creation, investment in the City's infrastructure, and the creation of a legacy that will last for years to come. The effects on these topics are scattered in the fields of economics, urban studies, tourism management and sociology, however. Research studies were searched from 2015 to 2025 in the two literature databases we used, Semantic Scholar and PubMed Central (PMC), to determine the impact of sport mega-events on the economy. After screening, 31 studies met the inclusion criteria and were quality assessed using the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool (MMAT) of 1052 records identified. The three main findings were found using thematic synthesis. First, the hosts might have positive non-market benefits (reputational or “psychic” benefits), which may be unevenly experienced across low-income and minoritized groups. Second, structural negative or negligible aggregate financial impacts are typical in most major events like the Olympics, the FIFA World Cup and Formula 1. Thirdly, small and medium events tend to create small and medium economic impact locally but with uncertain benefits. title: Invisible Wounds: Structural Violence and Institutional Power in 4.48 Psychosis and Cleansed
abstract: This paper examines Sarah Kane's plays Cleansed (1998) and 4.48 Psychosis (2000) through the lens of structural violence and institutional power. Drawing on Johan Galtung's concept of structural violence as indirect harm embedded in social systems, it argues that Kane depicts "invisible wounds", psychological, emotional, and existential traumas inflicted by oppressive institutions such as psychiatric facilities and authoritarian regimes. In Cleansed, the institution manifests as a site of physical torture and identity erasure, reflecting broader societal mechanisms of control over non-normative bodies and desires. In 4.48 Psychosis, violence is internalized, critiquing the medical-industrial complex's failure to address mental suffering. Through fragmented dramaturgy and graphic imagery, Kane exposes how institutional power perpetuates harm, urging audiences to confront complicity in these systems. This analysis synthesizes trauma theory, Postdramatic theatre, and feminist critiques to illuminate Kane's contribution to experiential.

title: A Dynamic MILP Framework for Multi-Stage Food-Grain Supply Chain Optimization: A Case Study of Jharkhand’s Public Distribution System
abstract: Food-grain supply chains involve several activities such as procurement, processing, transportation, storage, and distribution. In the Public Distribution System (PDS) of India, these activities are closely connected because procured paddy has to be processed in rice mills before the milled rice can be stored and distributed to different demand locations. This study develops a dynamic Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP) model for a four-stage food-grain supply chain consisting of procurement centres, rice mills, warehouses, and PDS distribution points. The model considers milling recovery, period-wise milling capacity, procurement availability, route activation, warehouse capacity, inventory balance, demand fulfilment, opportunity cost, and shortage penalty. Transportation costs are calculated from inter-node distances using the applicable Jharkhand Government transportation-rate structure. The model is tested through computational experiments using the East Singhbhum network and is further examined using observed procurement-stage data and a calibrated downstream representation of the Seraikela-Kharsawan district network. For the East Singhbhum simulation, the total system cost decreases from INR 76,102,850.08 under the baseline allocation to INR 75,105,464.62 with the proposed MILP, giving a reduction of 1.31%. title: Kinerja Energi PLTS 1.650 Wp untuk Penerangan Parkir dengan ATS (Energy Performance of a 1,650 Wp Solar PV System for Parking Lighting with an Automatic Transfer Switch)
abstract: This study evaluates the energy performance of a nominal 1,650 Wp solar photovoltaic (PV) system installed to support lighting on the seventh floor of the Universitas Pamulang parking building and connected to the PLN grid through an Automatic Transfer Switch (ATS). Measurements were recorded every 30 minutes from 09:00 to 20:00 Western Indonesian Time over seven days, covering voltage, current, power, energy, and battery state of charge. The summary data report an average PV output power of 351.714 W, while average PLN power on days with an active lighting load was approximately 1,508.990 W. The daily PV energy values listed in the tables range from 0.237 to 0.460 kWh, averaging 0.342 kWh. However, these energy summaries cannot be consistently reconstructed from the full interval data and are therefore not used to quantify PLN energy reduction. A single comparison between the KWS-302 monitor and an AVO meter gives relative differences of approximately 0.88% for voltage and 17.89% for current; current-measurement accuracy is consequently not considered validated. Design calculations indicate a 1,350 W lighting load requiring 5.4 kWh for four hours of operation, whereas the 48 V, 50 Ah battery at an 80% depth of discharge provides a theoretical 1.92 kWh DC, or about 1.82 kWh AC assuming 95% inverter efficiency. title: Exact optical soliton solutions on continuous-wave backgrounds for a coupled fourth-order nonlinear Schrödinger system in weakly birefringent optical fibers
abstract: We investigate exact optical soliton solutions for a coupled fourth-order nonlinear Schrödinger system governing pulse propagation in weakly birefringent optical fibers. Three complementary analytical methods — the generalized exponential rational integral function method (GERIFM), the [Formula: see text]-expansion method, and the tanh-coth method — are systematically applied to derive 12 distinct families of exact solutions, including bright, dark, singular, and combined soliton structures on non-vanishing continuous-wave backgrounds. The mathematical validity of all solutions is confirmed by direct substitution into the governing equations and the reduced ordinary differential equation. Graphical analyses in two and three dimensions demonstrate the temporal stability and robust propagation characteristics of representative solutions. The results provide a theoretical foundation for the design of ultrafast optical communication systems, mode-locked fiber lasers, and nonlinear photonic devices in which fourth-order dispersion and birefringence effects are significant.

title: Development of A Real-Time Monitoring and Overcurrent Protection System For Industrial Air Compressors
abstract: Compressors are vital equipment in the manufacturing industry that generate pressurized air to support various production processes. A common issue encountered in compressors is elevated operating temperatures and premature component failure caused by delayed replacement of consumable spare parts, such as oil, filters, and maintenance kits. This study aims to design and implement an Arduino Nano-based monitoring system for operating temperature, electric current, and running hours to support predictive maintenance routines on compressors. The system integrates a temperature sensor, a current sensor, and an hour meter with an Arduino Nano as the central controller, coupled with a buzzer alarm for early warnings whenever operating parameters exceed predefined threshold limits. The current sensor was evaluated by comparing system readings against a clamp meter across five electrical load variations, showing an average deviation of 0.09 A with a maximum error of 8.11%. Meanwhile, the temperature sensor testing against a ThermoGun as a reference instrument yielded measurement discrepancies of 1–3 °C under ambient and heated conditions. Furthermore, the system successfully provided real-time alerts whenever temperature, current, or operating hours exceeded set limits. The results demonstrate that the developed system reliably and effectively monitors compressor health as an economica…

title: Clinical characteristics and endoscopic management of inflammatory fibroid polyp of the gastrointestinal tract
abstract: BACKGROUND Inflammatory fibroid polyps (IFPs) are rare lesions of the gastrointestinal tract. Knowledge regarding the endoscopic and clinical characteristics of IFPs remains limited. AIM To investigate the clinical and endoscopic characteristics of IFPs and evaluate the outcomes of endoscopic resection (ER) for IFP management. METHODS This retrospective analysis enrolled a consecutive cohort of patients who received ER for IFPs at our institution between March 2014 and December 2024. We collected and analyzed their clinicopathological characteristics, endoscopic findings, and long-term follow-up outcomes. RESULTS A total of 108 consecutive patients were included (59 females, 54.6%), with a mean age of 54.6 ± 10.7 years. The median lesion size was 10 mm (range 5-50 mm). Most lesions were located in the stomach (70/108, 64.8%), followed by the large intestine (36/108, 33.3%); one lesion was found in the esophagus and one in the duodenum. All 108 patients successfully underwent ER, with no severe adverse events reported. Both the en bloc resection rate and the endoscopic complete resection rate were 99.1%. Three of 108 patients (2.8%) developed recurrent lesions postoperatively. A comparative analysis of gastric and colorectal IFP patients revealed significant differences in lesion size, endoscopic techniques, and operative time. abstract: Abstract Peri-implant biomaterials are commonly compared as isolated antimicrobial technologies, although their clinical relevance depends on linked requirements spanning prevention and treatment. Preventive approaches must preserve tissue integration and future cleanability; once disease develops, treatment must provide access to and disruption of mature biofilm, preserve or recover implant-surface competence, control destructive inflammation, support defect-specific regeneration, and enable durable maintenance. This structured critical review proposes a six-gate framework that evaluates preventive surfaces, decontamination methods, local delivery systems, host-directed materials, and regenerative adjuncts against those downstream requirements. Human peri-implant evidence was prioritized for treatment claims. Animal studies, clinically representative in vitro models, simplified implant models, and indirect oral-biofilm or general materials evidence were considered separately. The synthesis shows that mechanical and surgical strategies have the most direct clinical evidence, but no decontamination protocol has shown consistent, durable superiority across clinical settings. Reconstructive biomaterials can improve radiographic defect fill in selected defects, but their additional benefit for composite disease resolution remains uncertain. title: Unraveling the Intrinsic Interfacial Chemistry of Fluoroethylene Carbonate on Lithium Metal Anodes via a Solvent-Free Model System
abstract: Abstract Fluoroethylene carbonate (FEC) is a widely used film-forming additive for stabilizing lithium metal anodes (LMAs), yet its intrinsic interfacial chemistry remains elusive because its reactions are coupled with those of solvents and Li salts in conventional electrolytes. Herein, a solvent-free, dry-processed poly(ethylene oxide)-based solid polymer electrolyte (PEO@Dry) is developed as a platform to isolate the interfacial reactions of FEC without interference from traditional liquid organic solvents. PEO@Dry retains the intrinsic interfacial reactivity of PEO and LiTFSI while eliminating solvent-derived interference. FEC is found to undergo a spontaneous chemical reaction with Li metal before electrochemical reduction, producing a dense LiF-rich solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) that is subsequently reinforced by organic species derived from the electrochemical reactions. The resulting SEI exhibits a well-defined composition and robust structure, leading to an enhanced interfacial stability and electrochemical performance. Comparative research with a DME-based liquid electrolyte reveals that FEC (DME@FEC) follows distinct reaction pathways depending on its solvation state. abstract: BACKGROUND Spontaneously ruptured hepatocellular carcinoma (rHCC) carries high early mortality following emergency hemostatic procedures like transarterial embolization (TAE) or transarterial chemoembolization (TACE). Existing prognostic models lack accuracy, particularly by omitting morphological risk factors such as tumor protrusion. AIM To develop and validate a novel scoring system that integrates quantitative tumor protrusion with clinical parameters to improve 30-day mortality prediction. METHODS This retrospective cohort study included consecutive patients with rHCC treated with emergency TAE/TACE between January 2007 and December 2024. Three quantitative protrusion metrics (percentage, maximum diameter, and area) were compared for predictive performance. Inter-observer reliability was assessed using intraclass correlation coefficients. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify independent predictors of 30-day mortality. A weighted scoring system was derived from regression coefficients and internally validated using bootstrap resampling (1000 iterations). The model’s discriminative ability was compared to the model for end-stage liver disease and Child-Pugh scores using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) and DeLong’s test. Realizing personalized prediction for the reversal of chronic hepatitis B-associated liver fibrosis through machine learning
abstract: Although long-term antiviral therapy can reverse liver fibrosis in a considerable proportion of patients with chronic hepatitis B, treatment response differs markedly among individuals, and reliable methods for predicting who will benefit remain lacking. Conventional clinical tools such as liver stiffness measurement and the aspartate aminotransferase-to-platelet ratio index were originally dewsigned for cross-sectional staging rather than longitudinal prediction, and their ability to capture the dynamic process of fibrosis reversal is limited. In this opinion review, we discuss how machine learning (ML) may help address this unmet need. We focus on three areas where ML has shown early but encouraging results: Quantitative analysis of images using ML, integration of pathological and clinical data through multimodal models, and dynamic prediction of treatment response based on serial measurements during antiviral therapy. In our view, the greatest value of ML lies not in replacing existing assessment tools but in complementing them, particularly through the early identification of patients who are unlikely to achieve fibrosis reversal with antiviral therapy alone.
