title: The Influence of Cholesterol on the Mechanism of Stabilization of Phospholipid Bilayers by Sucrose
abstract: Abstract Sugars are widely utilized to preserve cells during desiccation and freezing because their addition results in a decrease of the main phase transition temperature of phospholipid bilayers. This has been explained by two opposing models: the water replacement hypothesis, involving direct sugar–phospholipid interaction at the bilayer interface, and the hydration forces explanation, involving an entropy-driven phase transition with sugar molecules accumulating away from the bilayer interface. However, biological membranes contain substantial sterol content, and the influence of cholesterol (CHOL) on these mechanisms remains poorly defined. We conducted molecular dynamics simulations of sucrose (SUC) interactions with pure 1,2-dioleoyl-sn-glycero-3-phosphocholine (DOPC), 2DOPC:1CHOL, and 1DOPC:1CHOL bilayers at full hydration and under dehydration. SUC expanded bilayers, reduced lipid tail order, and formed direct hydrogen bonds with DOPC headgroups, with the strongest protective effect observed under dehydration. CHOL condensed the bilayers and limited SUC-driven expansion, producing a saturation-limited response at high SUC concentration. SUC remains interfacially associated at low concentration but increasingly accumulates in the interbilayer aqueous region at high concentration, particularly under dehydration conditions. Thus, CHOL modulates the magnitude of SUC-mediat…

title: Xiao Chai Hu Decoction ameliorates doxorubicin-induced cardiotoxicity through an Akkermansia muciniphila–associated gut–heart mechanism
abstract: Abstract Background Doxorubicin (DOX) induces cardiotoxicity partly through ferroptosis. Xiao Chai Hu Decoction (XCHD) has anti-inflammatory and organ-protective activities, but its effects on DOX-induced cardiac injury and the gut–heart axis remain unclear. Purpose This study investigated whether XCHD attenuates DOX-induced cardiotoxicity through gut microbiota remodeling, with particular emphasis on the contribution of Akkermansia muciniphila and the downstream involvement of BMP10-associated ferroptosis. Methods Male C57BL/6 mice received DOX (5 mg/kg/week for 4 weeks; cumulative dose, 20 mg/kg) and XCHD (5–20 g/kg/day). Cardiac function, myocardial injury, histopathology, iron accumulation, and ferroptosis-related indices were evaluated. Cardiac transcriptomics and fecal 16S rRNA sequencing were combined with antibiotic-mediated microbiota depletion, fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT), and A. muciniphila supplementation to assess microbiota involvement. H9c2 cells treated with XCHD-containing serum and subjected to BMP10 knockdown were used to examine the downstream role of BMP10. Results XCHD improved cardiac function and reduced myocardial injury, fibrosis, iron accumulation, and ferroptosis-associated alterations. Transcriptomic analysis identified BMP10 as a candidate downstream factor suppressed by DOX and restored by XCHD. In H9c2 cells, XCHD-containing serum atte…

Analysis of Attitude Toward Green Financing in Support Net Zero Emission by 2060 Based on the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB): A Perspective from MSMEs
abstract: Net Zero Emission (NZE) 2060 has become Indonesia’s national aspiration to achieve a carbon-neutral economy by 2060 that the banking sector has reinforced its role as a key catalyst in promoting environmentally sustainable economic activities, particularly through the provision of green credit, financing, and investment. This study examines the behavior of green MSMEs toward Green Financing in supporting NZE 2060 based on the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB). The research focuses on green MSMEs located in four districts/cities in the Special Region of Yogyakarta (DIY), aiming to analyze the determinants of their behavioral intention to access Green Financing. The study applies the 10-times rule sampling technique and collects primary data from 62 respondents using a Likert scale (1–5) questionnaire distributed via Google Forms. Data were analyzed using SmartPLS 4.0. The findings reveal that Attitude does not significantly influence Behavioral Intention among green MSMEs actors in accessing Green Financing.

title: Beyond Energy Nationalism: Contractual Lock-In, Gas Export Diversion, LNG Trading Hubs, and Asymmetric Energy Security in Indonesia Singapore Natural Gas Relations
abstract: This qualitative literature review examines the economic, contractual, infrastructural, and environmental consequences of diverting Indonesian natural gas exports from Singapore toward domestic users. It distinguishes Indonesian pipeline gas from shipborne liquefied natural gas (LNG), Singapore-based LNG trading and transshipment, and final Singaporean gas consumption. Using recent peer-reviewed literature and contemporaneous official information, the study critically assesses claims that a small temporary supply reduction implies negligible bilateral dependence or that export interruption necessarily triggers financial default and gas flaring. The synthesis identifies asymmetric but conditional vulnerabilities: Singapore may replace a limited pipeline shortfall through diversified procurement, while Indonesian producers can face revenue and financing risks if domestic offtake or contractual settlement is inadequate. Conversely, a connected and creditworthy domestic customer may create significant economic value through greater electricity reliability and industrial activity. A conceptual framework links physical flows, gas sales agreements, project-finance covenants, infrastructure absorption, political credibility, and methane outcomes. The study concludes that sound resource nationalism requires reconciled gas-flow accounting, scenario-based netback and welfare analysis, con…

Bimolecular Homolytic Substitution Catalysis with a Europium Photocatalyst for Single Functional Group Cross-Coupling
abstract: Abstract Lanthanide photocatalysis has emerged as a promising alternative to precious-metal systems due to its earth abundance, low toxicity, and unique photophysical properties. However, reported lanthanide-based photocatalysts have primarily focused on the generation of reactive radical species, with limited ability to control product selectivity in bond-forming processes. Here we report a single europium-cryptate catalyst that enables selective C(sp3)–C(sp3) cross-coupling of benzyl chlorides by combining single-electron transfer-driven radical generation with bimolecular homolytic substitution reactivity. The reaction proceeds through a Eu(II)-benzyl intermediate that initiates single-electron transfer to form a benzyl radical, followed by SH2 with a Eu(III)-benzyl species to forge the cross-coupling product. Our findings provide a mechanistic framework for designing selective C(sp3)–C(sp3) cross-coupling reactions using lanthanide metals, paving the way for the broader application of lanthanide-based photocatalysts in organic synthesis.

Advancing Psychrophilic Anaerobic Digestion of Cattle Manure through Microbial Adaptation, Bioaugmentation and Pathways to Reliable Low-Temperature Biogas: A Critical Review
abstract: ow-temperature anaerobic digestion of cattle manure can recover methane, but slow conversion and delayed start-up can limit reliable energy delivery. This critical narrative review examines biochemical constraints, microbial adaptation and bioaugmentation, performance measurement and translation to useful energy. International evidence is synthesized, with the Ngorongoro Conservation Area of northern Tanzania serving as a motivating application context. The synthesis identifies coordination of hydrolysis, syntrophic conversion and methanogenesis as central to methane onset, production rate and stability. Cold-adapted inocula and targeted consortia can improve methane recovery in selected controlled systems, but differences in substrates, inocula, dosing and reactor operation restrict cross-study comparison and field extrapolation. Combined microbial and carbon amendments require controls that distinguish biological effects from additional substrate contributions. Reliable interpretation also requires explicit solids accounting, gas volume reference conditions and separation of measured recovery from modeled asymptotic potential. Higher methane recovery alone does not establish improved pH stability, methane fraction or microbial persistence. Net energy and economic benefits of these interventions remain insufficiently resolved because methane gains must be assessed alongside pr…

title: Uncertainty-aware planning of hybrid renewable and conventional distributed generation using a novel optimization framework
abstract: Abstract With the increasing integration of distributed generation (DG) units based on renewable energy into power distribution networks, advanced planning models are required to guarantee smooth integration and enhanced network performance. In order to reduce investment costs while lowering line losses and improving voltage stability, this study proposes an optimization planning model for the optimal placement and sizing of DG units. A novel hybrid algorithm, the Improved Genetic Moth Swarm Algorithm (IGMSA), combining the Genetic Algorithm (GA) and an improved Moth Swarm Algorithm (MSA), is introduced to address the complex DG placement problem under renewable-generation uncertainty. This method considers systems with variable renewable energy sources (RESs), including photovoltaic (PV) panels, wind turbines (WT), and their combinations with fuel cells (FC), with uncertainties modeled using the Point Estimate Method (PEM). Three hybrid configurations; namely PV/WT/FC, PV/FC, and WT/FC, are simulated and optimized on the IEEE 33-bus and IEEE 119-bus distribution systems. Comparative analysis demonstrates the superior performance of the proposed IGMSA against the standard GMSA and other optimization algorithms, yielding competitive Pareto-optimal solutions with an improved balance between exploration and exploitation. Results indicate that the proposed approach can effectively …

title: Naïve Bayes integration with Markov chain and cellular automata for modelling urban land use change
abstract: Abstract Away from the conventional Logistic Regression (LR) technique, this study presents a novel Naïve Bayes (NB) integration with Markov Chain (MC) and Cellular Automata (CA) for modelling urban land use change. Although NB is a simple parametric algorithm similar to the Logistic Regression (LR), previous studies have shown that it can outperform the LR when the features are independent, and the dataset is small and highly dimensional, such as land use datasets. In this experiment, NB was used to classify land use into urban and non-urban classes. The training data, test data, and validation data were extracted from the land use data. The training and test datasets were used to train and evaluate the NB; while the validation data was used to validate the CA prediction. The NB probabilities, transition probabilities from the MC model, neighbourhood interaction, and transition rule from the CA model were combined to determine the evolution of each cell in the prediction. Land use drivers were derived from Landsat-5 Thematic Mapper (TM, 1984), Landsat-7 Enhanced Thematic Mapper Plus (ETM+, 2000), and Landsat-8 Operational Land Imager/Thermal Infrared Sensor (OLI/TIRS, 2020) imageries. Binary urban scenarios (urban and nonurban cells) were modelled using twelve salient urban land use drivers. Urban transitions from 1984–2000 to 2000–2020 were used to predict the urban state in …

title: Design of Fibril-Forming and Cell-Adhesive Peptides Conjugated with Non-Natural Functional Groups Based on Molecular Descriptors
abstract: Abstract We developed a molecular descriptor-based strategy for designing fibril-forming and cell-adhesive peptides conjugated with non-natural functional groups for biomaterial applications. Twenty-one peptides were prepared by introducing one of the 20 standard amino acids at the N-terminus of the fibril-forming core sequence NFGAIL. Their fibril-forming properties were evaluated by thioflavin T fluorescence, circular dichroism, and ζ-potential measurements. Principal component analysis (PCA) classified the peptides according to their fibril-forming characteristics, and correlation analysis identified the molecular descriptors PCD and IC1 as parameters associated with fibril formation. Cell adhesion assays revealed regions in the PCA distribution associated with enhanced cell adhesion. Based on these relationships, peptides conjugated with non-natural functional groups that were not included in the original peptide library were designed and experimentally evaluated. Several designed peptides exhibited enhanced cell adhesion while retaining fibril-forming properties. In particular, a peptide conjugated with acridine carboxylic acid showed cell adhesion 9-fold higher than that of IAPP(22–27) and 1.7-fold higher than that of gelatin after purification. These results demonstrate that molecular descriptors extracted from a limited experimental peptide dataset enable the rational d…

title: Computational Design of a Molecular Pulley for Nanoscale Force Transmission
abstract: Abstract Molecular machines are promising tools for precision nanomachining because they can deform structures at the nanoscale without chemical damage. However, a clear engineering design framework has not yet been established. Practical use requires proper material selection, confirmation of physical feasibility based on molecular interactions, and realistic design guidance. Here, we examine cyclodextrins threaded on flexible hydrogel polymers that act as both sliders and rotational joints while attaching to each other and to surfaces. Molecular dynamics simulations show that this system can operate as a molecular pulley and allow for the evaluation of different scalable geometries and their performance. We demonstrate that pulley mechanisms, such as force direction change and force amplification, can be used to control the elastic deformation of nanopatterned solids.

Exploring Microbial Biotransformation of Electro-Homoeopathic Plant Constituents and Its Relevance to Diabetes Mellitus
abstract: Diabetes mellitus is a complex metabolic condition characterized by insulin resistance, β-cell dysfunction and chronic inflammation and host–microbial interactions. Plant preparations are composed of several phytochemicals that are known to have a wide range of biological effects and bioavailability in the gut, which could significantly be influenced by the gut microbiota. Microorganisms in the intestine have the enzymic capacity to break, hydrogenate, reduce, dehydroxylate, and hydrolyse natural substances, producing metabolites with different characteristics than their parent substances. Electro-Homoeopathy is a system of botanical medicine that uses plant essences in complex medicines, but so far, there is not much information about the microbial biotransformation of the plant matter components of these medicines. A perspective review of potential relationships between microbial degradation of components of Electro-Homeo plants and mechanisms related to diabetes, focusing on the case of Hydrastis canadensis and the component berberine. Conversion of berberine to dihydroberberine by the intestinal bacteria offers a mechanistic rationale. Phenolic compounds, polyphenols, microbial metabolites, short-chain fatty acids, bile acid signalling, intestinal barrier function, inflammation and insulin sensitivity are also taken into account in the review. title: Halotolerant PGPR Enhances Growth and Floral Performance of Rosa chinensis Under Saline Stress
abstract: Roses are susceptible to salinity stress, which has a substantial impact on their growth and the visual quality of their flowers. The growth and visual quality of ornamental plants are closely associated with their ability to tolerate abiotic stressors. In recent years, the use of plant growth-promoting rhizobacteria (PGPR) has emerged as a potential strategy for improving the growth and quality of ornamental plants in stressful environments. Therefore, the present study was conducted to identify commercially available PGPR species that could be used to develop salt stress tolerance in ‘Surkha’ roses for commercial production. We evaluated three salinity levels (3, 5 and 7 dS m⁻¹ NaCl), applied alone or in combination with one of two PGPR genera. Compared with the corresponding non-inoculated treatments at the same salinity, inoculation with Bacillus spp. at 3 dS m⁻¹ produced a significant increase in leaf area and numerical improvements in several other growth and floral traits; effects of Pseudomonas spp. and of both genera at higher salinity levels were generally small and non-significant. The non-saline control generally showed the highest values for most traits. abstract: Maqolada heterogen tarmoq sharoitida ishlovchi ko‘p foydalanuvchili virtual borliq (VR) tizimlarida bashoratli ekstrapolyatsiya (dead reckoning) asosidagi holat kompensatsiyasini ma’lumot uzatish ustuvorligi bilan birgalikda modellashtirish masalasi qaralgan. Pozitsiya va kvaternion ko‘rinishidagi aylanishni qamrab oluvchi 6DoF og‘ish o‘lchovi, og‘ishni o‘z ichiga olgan ustuvorlik funksiyasi, yuborish oralig‘i hamda qabul qiluvchi tomondagi holat kelishuvi sxemalari rasmiylashtirilgan. Chegaralangan tezlanish farazida ekstrapolyatsiya xatosi ma’lumot yoshining kvadratiga mutanosib ekani, aylanish uchun Grönwall tengsizligiga asoslangan yuqori baho, paket yo‘qotishini hisobga olgan holda ma’lumot yoshi chegarasi va og‘ish hadi kiritilganda xatoning o‘z-o‘zini cheklash xossasi isbotlangan. abstract: The development of Generative Artificial Intelligence has facilitated the creation and modification of digital visual works, including Virtual YouTuber character designs. This convenience raises legal issues when character designs resulting from the creativity of creators are used, imitated, modified, or commercially exploited without authorization. This study aims to analyze the forms of legal protection available to Virtual YouTuber character designers against commercial exploitation based on Generative Artificial Intelligence and to examine the application of Intellectual Property Rights regulations to such issues. This research employs normative legal research using a statutory approach and a conceptual approach. The legal materials consist of primary, secondary, and tertiary legal materials, which are analyzed qualitatively through library research. The results indicate that Virtual YouTuber character designs that fulfill the requirements of copyrightable works are protected by copyright, including moral and economic rights, and their commercial utilization requires the authorization of the creator or rights holder. The use of Generative Artificial Intelligence to produce works by taking or reproducing expressive elements from protected character designs may constitute a copyright infringement, particularly when such works are commercially exploited without authorization. …

title: Food Sovereignty in an Age of Geopolitical Fragmentation: Corporate Power, Global Supply-Chain Vulnerabilities, and the Reconfiguration of Indonesia’s National Food Politics
abstract: Global food politics connects agrifood production and consumption to geopolitical conflict, corporate concentration, trade governance, climate instability, and contested claims over food sovereignty. This qualitative literature review examines how those transnational forces influence Indonesia’s national food-policy orientation, especially its renewed emphasis on domestic production, public reserves, postharvest infrastructure, price stabilization, and village cooperatives. Drawing interpretively on peer-reviewed journal literature published during 2020–2026 and triangulating policy claims against official Indonesian regulations, the review identifies seven interconnected arenas of power: knowledge and seed technologies; agricultural inputs; trade and logistics; finance and corporate organization; rule-setting; narratives and information; and land, procurement, and territorial distribution. Findings indicate that external shocks expose real vulnerabilities, but neither autarky nor indiscriminate import liberalization provides a sufficient response. Indonesia’s institutional challenge is to combine domestic productive capacity with diversified external sourcing, accessible nutritious diets, protected smallholder livelihoods, accountable reserves, ecological safeguards, and meaningful local participation. The review develops a conditional-sovereignty framework that treats autonom…

title: Preselected voltage vector strategy integrated with virtual flux-based predictive direct power control for AC/DC rectifier
Evaluasi Kinerja dan Keandalan Operasional Rectifier pada Catu Daya Telekomunikasi (Performance Evaluation and Operational Reliability of Rectifiers in Telecommunication Power Supply Systems)
abstract: This study aims to evaluate the electrical performance of a rectifier system in a telecommunication power supply and analyse power supply continuity during module failures. Voltage, current, and output power were measured over seven days at four load points, while failure records were reviewed based on six months of operational history. The results show that the output voltage ranged from 54.04 to 55.13 V, with total output power ranging from 28.03 to 29.62 kW and averaging 28.91 kW. The summed current across the four load points ranged from 510.04 to 542.93 A. Compared with the reference rating of 3,600 A, this represents 14.17–15.08%; however, interpretation of the loading level requires verification of the actual system configuration. Operational records show one rectifier module failure with a reported handling time of 72 hours, without interruption of the power supply because the other modules continued supporting the load. These findings indicate relatively stable electrical output and power supply continuity during the recorded module failure. However, quantitative reliability assessment requires additional data on the number of active modules, operating hours, and total system downtime.

title: A Quasi-Experimental Study to Assess the Effectiveness of a Virtual Reality Distraction Technique on Reducing Pain During Painful Procedures Among Children in a Selected Hospital
abstract: Pain during procedures is a common and distressing experience for hospitalised children. Repeated needle procedures, venepuncture, intravenous cannulation, injections, wound care and other brief interventions may produce fear, anticipatory anxiety and behavioural distress, which can make cooperation more difficult. Virtual reality (VR) distraction uses an immersive digital environment to direct attention away from the procedure and may reduce the amount of attention available for pain processing. This review examines the theoretical basis, clinical use and research evidence for VR distraction in children undergoing painful procedures and presents a practical quasi-experimental framework for assessing its effectiveness in a selected hospital. Evidence from randomised and quasi-experimental studies suggests that immersive distraction can reduce self-reported pain and, in many settings, observable distress. The likely benefit is influenced by age, developmental level, previous procedural experiences, type and duration of procedure, headset acceptability, content preference and the quality of usual care. A proposed study can compare pain scores in an experimental group receiving age-appropriate VR distraction plus routine care with a comparison group receiving routine care alone. Pain should be measured using an age-appropriate validated scale, while demographic and procedural char…

title: The Digital Commons and the Infrastructural Power of Generative AI
abstract: Abstract The use and construction of generative AI reshape how information flows in society and who controls it. This paper investigates these changes and assesses their potential repercussions for the future of our shared information infrastructure. The findings elucidate an emergent social dilemma in which the use and construction of generative AI tend to degrade and compete with our existing infrastructure, while also layering atop the commons new infrastructure that is, by its current design, centralised and mediated. Yet, alternative futures that preserve the collective nature of our infrastructure remain possible. As a first step toward such futures, this paper concludes by exploring interventions to promote a decentralised and unmediated generative commons.

title: Far-red light can power biological nitrogen fixation in cyanobacteria
abstract: Abstract Nitrogen fixation is one of the most energetically expensive biological reactions shaping the biosphere. Here, we demonstrate that some heterocyst-forming cyanobacteria can perform this process solely with low-energy far-red light, after undergoing a light acclimation response known as far-red light photoacclimation (FaRLiP). Although FaRLiP has been shown to drive oxygenic photosynthesis beyond the visible spectrum in some cyanobacteria from shaded terrestrial habitats, it was unknown whether it could also support growth in nitrogen-poor environments. In this study, we focused on heterocyst-forming, nitrogen-fixing cyanobacteria carrying FaRLiP genes from various habitats. Based on transcription, protein, and enzymatic activity assays, we demonstrate that FaRLiP does support growth in the absence of combined nitrogen sources. This includes a strain lacking far-red Photosystem II, though it was energy-limited and required additional sugar input. Bioinformatic analyses revealed that this reduced FaRLiP gene cluster variant is transcribed in nitrogen-fixing symbiotic cyanobacteria in natural environments. Together, these results indicate that nitrogen fixation can be powered by low-energy photons, likely facilitating cyanobacterial growth in resource-limited microbial mats as well as shaded symbiotic environments. The Effect of Balance Funds and Regional Original Revenue on Regional Financial Performance through Capital Expenditure in Medan City
abstract: Regional autonomy demands local fiscal independence, where Local Own-Source Revenue (PAD) and Balancing Funds are expected to drive Regional Financial Performance, with Capital Expenditure as a mediator. This study aims to analyze the direct and indirect effects of Balancing Funds and PAD on Regional Financial Performance through Capital Expenditure in Medan City. This explanatory quantitative research uses Medan City Government time series data from 2007-2024. The path analysis method was applied using EViews software. The results reveal that PAD positively and significantly affects Capital Expenditure and Financial Performance. Conversely, Balancing Funds have a negative and significant effect on Financial Performance and an insignificant effect on Capital Expenditure. Capital Expenditure positively affects Financial Performance but fails to mediate the relationship between the two independent variables and Financial Performance. In conclusion, fiscal independence through PAD is the primary lever for financial performance, while reliance on central transfers potentially weakens it.

title: The Effectiveness of Problem-Based Learning in Enhancing ‎Science Literacy ‎Skills and Conceptual Understanding in Science and ‎Social Studies among ‎Sixth-Grade Elementary School Students ‎
abstract: Problem-based learning (PBL) is frequently proposed to strengthen scientific literacy and conceptual understanding, but small school-based comparisons require careful interpretation. This study describes a non-equivalent-group, pretest–posttest comparison involving 38 sixth-grade students from two public elementary schools in Bogorejo, Blora, Indonesia. Nineteen students in one school received PBL-oriented instruction and 19 students in another school received conventional instruction. The revised analysis uses aggregate figures available in the original report; individual-level records and the original statistical output were unavailable for verification. Reported posttest means were higher in the PBL-school group than in the comparison-school group for scientific literacy (78.16 vs. 62.37) and conceptual understanding (80.00 vs. 64.21), with a descriptive difference of 15.79 points for each outcome. The source report also listed normalized gains of 0.709 vs. 0.490 and 0.727 vs. 0.516, respectively; these gains could not be reproduced without individual data and a documented calculation procedure. Because the original inferential tables do not validly establish an independent between-school effect, statistical significance is not asserted in this revision. The observed pattern is compatible with the pedagogical rationale for PBL but cannot isolate an intervention effect from s…

title: Predicting awareness of where facility-based abortion services can be accessed among women in Ethiopia using explainable machine learning
abstract: Abstract Access to safe abortion care remains a significant public health concern in low- and middle-income countries, where unsafe abortion contributes substantially to maternal morbidity and mortality. In Ethiopia, although abortion is legally permitted under specific circumstances and facility-based abortion services are available, awareness of where these services can be accessed remains limited. Evidence on predictors of such awareness remains scarce. Therefore, this study aimed to predict women’s awareness of where facility-based abortion services can be accessed in the community and identify its key predictors using nationally representative data. Data from 8,894 women participating in the 2019 Performance Monitoring for Action (PMA) Ethiopia survey were analyzed. The data were stratified into development (80%) and independent test (20%) sets. Within each training fold, imputation, categorical encoding, Boruta feature selection, and SMOTENC were performed before model fitting to minimize information leakage. Eight supervised machine learning algorithms were developed and compared using repeated stratified 10-fold cross-validation with five repeats. Grid-search hyperparameter tuning was performed for the selected model using the development data. title: Myhill–Nerode Quotient Learning for Continuous Observation–Action Spaces via Kernel Maximum Mean Discrepancy
abstract: Model-free identification of the minimal world-model of a bounded agent in a POMDP has been made tractable in the finite setting by Myhill–Nerode quotient learning: a permutation G-test on fixed-policy continuation histograms clusters histories into continuation-equivalence classes. With continuous observations and actions the continuation alphabet is infinite and the G-test is undefined. We extend quotient learning to 𝒪 × 𝒜 ⊆ ℝ^(d). Histories are keyed by coarse quantile bins; for every pair of bins the continuation laws are compared with a kernel maximum mean discrepancy (MMD) permutation test on raw continuation vectors under Benjamini–Hochberg control, and bins whose test does not reject are merged by union–find. title: Enhancing AI Feedback Systems: Lessons Learned from a RAG Implementation Study
abstract: This study investigates the impact of Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) on graduate students' perceptions of AI-generated feedback in a cyber-social learning environment. Using a non-equivalent cohort comparison quasi-experimental design, the research compared survey responses from Fall 2023 (n=96) and Spring 2024 (n=86) before and after implementing RAG. Participants engaged in iterative project cycles involving AI feedback, peer reviews, and instructor evaluations. Results revealed significant improvements in perceived feedback quality (p < .001, d = 0.41) and usefulness (p < .001, d = 0.51) following RAG implementation, while perceptions of actionability remained unchanged (p = .68, d = -0.05). Hierarchical regression analyses identified educational level as a positive predictor of quality and usefulness perceptions, whereas age and location negatively predicted actionability, and educational level positively predicted it. These findings suggest that RAG enhances the contextual relevance and perceived value of AI-generated feedback, particularly for advanced students. However, the lack of improvement in actionability highlights a persistent challenge in AI feedback systems. The study recommends integrating RAG with human support and developing targeted interventions to improve feedback literacy and implementation, especially for less advanced students and older learners.

title: Real-time cognitive load estimation from language in interactive learning environments
abstract: Abstract Cognitive load is a foundational construct in learning. Yet, most adaptive educational systems continue to depend on behavioral traces or physiological instrumentation to infer learners’ mental effort, limiting their scalability and ecological validity in open-ended learning contexts. This paper introduces a language-based framework for turn-level, real-time, and non-invasive cognitive load regulation in interactive learning environments. We present the Cognitive Load Estimate from Language (CLEL). This metric synthesizes eight linguistically grounded indicators into a unified estimate of cognitive load derived directly from learners’ written explanations. Building on this metric, we develop the Cognitive Load-Adaptive Multi-Agent Tutor (CLAMAT), a multi-agent instructional architecture in which specialized LLM-based agents coordinate adaptively through a cognitive-load-aware orchestration mechanism. Empirical evaluation with undergraduate learners performing explanatory tasks shows a strong association between CLEL and self-reported mental effort. Teacher evaluations favour CLAMAT feedback in clarity, helpfulness, and perceived adaptivity. Students also show an overall pre–post score improvement after receiving feedback from both systems, although the design does not isolate their respective contributions to learning. These findings demonstrate the promise of language…

abstract: Penelitian ini bertujuan meningkatkan kemampuan numerasi murid melalui penggunaan Problem Based Learning (PBL) dalam materi satuan panjang dan berat pada pelajaran Matematika kelas III sekolah dasar. Penelitian ini dilakukan dengan metode Penelitian Tindakan Kelas (PTK) yang dilakukan selama dua siklus dengan murid berjumlah 30. Setiap siklus memiliki alur pembelajaran yang sama yaitu perencanaan, aksi, pengamatan, dan refleksi. Data dikumpulkan melalui tes, observasi, dan dokumentasi selama pembelajaran. Hasil penelitian yang didapat memperlihatkan terdapat perkembangan hasil penilaian murid siklus I senilai 2.331 dari maksimal skor 3.240 atau 71,94% berkategori cukup, yang berkembang pada siklus II yaitu senilai 2.694 atau 83,15% berkategori baik. Nilai rata-rata pada aspek kognitif berkembang dari 72,67 menjadi 83,33. Perkembangan aspek-aspek yang dinilai dalam penelitian ini mengungkapkan bahwa penggunaan model pembelajaran PBL dapat memberikan hasil yang baik dalam pembelajaran Matematika materi satuan panjang dan berat. Model PBL dinilai mampu menjadi solusi bagi murid dalam mencerna konsep matematika, menyelesaikan masalah sehari-hari, diskusi, dan masalah kontekstual lainnya. Maka dari itu, PBL dinilai memiliki potensi dalam meningkatkan kemampuan numerasi murid sekolah dasar.

title: Islands in the Machine: A Systematic Geographic Assessment of Insular Territories in Video Games
abstract: Islands occupy a privileged position in human imagination and in the geography of the real world. As circumscribed, ecologically distinct, and often isolated territories, they concentrate geographic diversity into bounded spaces that invite exploration, narrative, and control. These same qualities make islands recurrent settings in video games, where the island serves simultaneously as a spatial container, a design convenience, and a cultural signifier. Yet despite the ubiquity of island environments in interactive media, no systematic attempt has been made to assess how faithfully video games represent the specific geographic properties that define insular territories. This paper presents the first comprehensive geographic analysis of island representation in video games. Drawing on a catalogue of 125 titles spanning multiple genres, platforms and release decades, a seven-block variable framework is developed, covering insularity, geomorphology, climate, hydrography, biogeography, human elements, and spatial scale, and computing an Island Geographic Fidelity Index (IGFI) for each title. Restricting the main analysis to 96 genuinely insular games and using 28 continental titles as a comparative reference, a mean IGFI of 42.2 (SD = 10.8) is found on a 0–100 scale, with Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024 serving as a benchmark reference at 98.8. Results show that insularity recognit…

title: Discrimination of ranges of closely related RNA targets using CRISPR-based detection assay developed using machine learning-based optimization
abstract: Abstract Early detection and identification of pathogen strains are crucial for mitigating infectious disease threats, including those posed by closely related zoonotic variants. A key limitation of current molecular detection approaches is their narrow focus on individual targets, which can delay recognition of outbreaks caused by closely related but non-identical pathogens. Here we report a two-channel CRISPR/Cas13a detection assay capable of discriminating between SARS-CoV-2 and a panel of twelve closely related zoonotic sarbecoviruses using a compact duplex assay format. Guide RNA sets with tunable specificity were designed using a two-stage machine learning pipeline: initial candidate filtering with a pre-existing RuleFit model, followed by retraining on 382 sarbecovirus-specific in vitro data points to refine the mismatch threshold from 4 to 6 mismatches for target exclusion. The optimized assay achieved proof-of-concept three-way classification of synthetic RNA targets into: (1) SARS-CoV-2, (2) the closest known near-neighbor BANAL-236, and (3) remaining zoonotic near-neighbors, with a limit of detection of 15–150 fM for synthetic RNA targets. This approach provides a practical framework for surveillance-oriented detection that identifies not only a specific pathogen but also its closest relatives, provided that system-specific validation and model retraining are include…

title: Improvement in phase-C students’ writing skills of pantun following the implementation of differentiated instruction within a deep learning approach
abstract: This study examined changes in Phase-C elementary school students’ pantun writing skills following the implementation of differentiated instruction within a Deep Learning approach. The study employed a quantitative approach using a one-group pretest–posttest design involving 30 fifth-grade students at Al Kautsar Islamic Elementary School in Krian, Sidoarjo. Data were collected through pantun writing assessments, classroom observations, and documentation. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, the Shapiro–Wilk test, a paired-sample t-test, and N-Gain analysis. The findings showed an increase in the mean pantun writing score from 68.40 on the pretest to 84.70 on the posttest, representing a mean improvement of 16.30 points. The paired-sample t-test indicated a statistically significant difference between pretest and posttest scores (p < .001), while the N-Gain score of 0.52 indicated moderate improvement. These findings suggest that students’ pantun writing skills improved following the implementation of differentiated instruction within a Deep Learning approach. However, because the study did not involve a comparison group, the observed improvement cannot be attributed exclusively to the instructional intervention. The findings provide preliminary empirical evidence regarding the implementation of differentiated instruction in pantun writing instruction.

Results: BPW Ar Risalah is effective as a benefit distributor (distributive effectiveness): targeting is perceived as accurate, distribution is generally on time with one compensated delay, and monitoring is conducted periodically according to the type of beneficiary. Social assistance of IDR 500,000 per month, scholarships of IDR 1,500,000 per semester, and income of IDR 1,500,000 per month contribute to meeting living needs, education, and income stability, with job creation as the most transformative benefit. However, transformative effectiveness cannot yet be fully concluded: beneficiaries' understanding of the concept and mechanism of productive waqf remains limited, the benefit amounts are supplementary, and monitoring does not yet measure impact. A Two-Phase Framework for Cryptocurrency Portfolio Construction Under Deep Uncertainty: A Hybrid Approach Based on RR-DEA and Robust Optimization
abstract: Abstract Investment decision-making is a challenging problem in financial engineering, particularly when investors are presented with multiple investment options. The decision paths become more complex in the space of digital assets, where investors are faced with a huge number of assets to select from, before even deriving optimal allocations. Within virtual space, the market for cryptocurrencies is gaining traction among investors, especially due to its potential for substantial returns and diversification. However, the market for cryptocurrencies presents unique challenges due to its inherent volatility and uncertainty, underscoring the need for a robust and structured investment framework to guide decision-making. Noting this gap in the literature on cryptocurrency investment, we introduce an innovative two-phase framework for cryptocurrency portfolio construction, designed to address the complexities and uncertainties inherent in cryptocurrency markets. In a two-phased analysis, we start with a Robust Ratio Data Envelopment Analysis (RR-DEA) to screen and preselect the most efficient cryptocurrencies from a pool of available assets, followed by the application of a Robust Goal Programming (RGP) optimization procedure to allocate weights based on the investor’s risk preferences, return targets, and other relevant financial goals. title: OPTIMIZATION OF BATH TEMPERATURE FOR ELECTRODEPOSITED NiFeWMoMn HIGH-ENTROPY ALLOY THIN FILMS
abstract: In this study, NiFeWMoMn high-entropy alloy thin films were successfully synthesized using the electrodeposition method by varying the bath temperature. The structural, morphological, corrosion, magnetic, and compositional properties were systematically investigated using X-ray diffraction (XRD), Field-emission scanning electron microscopy (FESEM), Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS), electrochemical tests, and Vibrating-sample magnetometry (VSM). XRD analysis confirmed the formation of a solid solution with a refined crystalline structure, showing the smallest crystallite size and lower dislocation density at 75 ∘ C. FESEM images revealed uniform and dense surface morphology at this temperature, while EDS confirmed the presence of all intended elements with a more balanced atomic distribution. Electrochemical corrosion studies showed that the sample coated at 75 ∘ C exhibited the lowest corrosion rate and the highest polarization resistance, indicating superior corrosion resistance. Magnetic measurements showed that coercivity increased with temperature 75 ∘ C was identified as the most favorable temperature for achieving a uniform coating, improved corrosion resistance, controlled magnetic behavior, and enhanced structural properties.

title: Integrated population genomics and phenotypic analyses reveal geographic structure and signatures of recent positive-selection underlying insecticide resistance in Anopheles arabiensis from The Gambia, West Africa
abstract: Abstract Insecticide resistance in malaria vectors is spreading, with newly identified resistance markers raising operational challenges and threatening malaria reduction. Anopheles arabiensis is an important vector in The Gambia; however, the molecular basis of its insecticide resistance remains poorly understood. We observed signals of population structure between coastal and inland An. arabiensis populations in The Gambia, indicating restricted gene flow likely influenced by environmental variation. Pyrethroid and DDT resistance were widespread. However, the prevalence of both phenotypic and genetic insecticide resistance differed between coastal and inland populations. For instance, the Vgsc-L995S and Vgsc-L995F substitutions conferring pyrethroid and DDT resistance were more frequent in coastal populations and were associated with markedly higher phenotypic resistance to these insecticides. We also identified increased frequencies of copy number variation at Cytochrome P450 (Cyp6aa/p, Cyp9k1) and carboxylesterase (Coeae2-7 g) metabolic resistance markers in coastal An. arabiensis. Some observed gene amplifications were unique to Gambian coastal populations, suggesting their independent evolution. title: HierWoodNet: HierStyle multi-scale semantic style transfer method for Chinese woodblock painting
abstract: Abstract Woodblock painting, a traditional Chinese intangible cultural heritage, is known for its vivid colors and distinctive textures. However, modern lifestyles and declining cultural inheritance have led to risks of style loss and discontinuity. AI-based image style transfer offers a promising avenue for preserving and creating woodblock art. However, existing methods struggle with semantic feature extraction, style consistency, and color modeling in this domain. To address these challenges, we propose a hierarchical woodblock style transfer network. Our approach introduces a Content-Aware Positional Encoder based on the Transformer architecture, which enhances multi-scale feature representation and global structural perception. This helps preserve content during style transfer. We further present a HierStyle Encoder that learns rich, hierarchical style features from data, enabling fine-grained control over the transfer process and improving semantic and textural coherence. A progressive decoder integrates multi-stage upsampling with cross-layer connections to preserve semantic structure while injecting detailed style features. Finally, the ChromaNova Color Decoder dynamically optimizes color representation through a multi-dimensional color loss function that considers both color contrast and distribution differences. Quantitative experiments show that our method achieves t…

title: A specialized microbiome enriched in nitrification and halogen cycling potential resolved from multi-omics investigation of a Caribbean suboxic and acidic marine sinkhole
abstract: Abstract Background The Luymes Sinkholes, located on the Luymes Bank northwest of Saba, represent a unique marine environment characterized by distinct biogeochemical gradients. Most noticeable is an acidic (pH ≈ 6.25) and suboxic (O2 < 60 µmol/kg) submerged ‘lake’ at ~ 220 m depth exhibiting extreme deviations from standard oceanographic patterns, including elevated inorganic carbon, nitrate, and phosphate, and a lower temperature (20.3 ºC vs 26.4 ºC). To determine how the microbiome within the submerged acid lake adapted to these unique conditions, we collected 59 coupled samples of size-filtered (0.22 µm) planktonic microbes for shotgun metagenomics and solid-phase extracted dissolved organic matter for untargeted metabolomics from 21 stations at depths ranging from 2 to 600 m during a 10-day research cruise in December 2019. Results We identified a distinct microbial community within the submerged acid lake different from the non-acidic sinkholes, with increased abundances of Nitrospinota , Thermoproteota , Planctomycetota , and Actinobacteriota . We also found three enriched classes of dissolved compounds within the submerged acid lake: (1) large, (2) low-polarity, and (3) halogenated metabolites, including iodides and halobenzoic acids. Correlations between microbial taxa and metabolite classes show potential links between nitrifying archaea and halogenated compound cycli…

abstract: Pemberdayaan ekonomi jemaat melalui pelayanan gereja membutuhkan pengelolaan yang terarah dan berkelanjutan, bukan hanya penyediaan bantuan dan fasilitas usaha. Penelitian terdahulu telah membahas pemberdayaan ekonomi melalui pengembangan potensi lokal, bantuan modal, pelatihan, dan pemanfaatan aset gereja. Namun, kajian yang mengintegrasikan fungsi pengelolaan program ekonomi berbasis pasar dengan faktor pendukung, penghambat, dan dampaknya terhadap pemberdayaan ekonomi jemaat masih terbatas. Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis pengelolaan Pasar Obor, mengidentifikasi faktor pendukung dan penghambat, serta menganalisis dampaknya terhadap pemberdayaan ekonomi jemaat di GKI Ekklesia Klasaman, Kota Sorong, Papua Barat Daya. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif deskriptif dengan pemilihan informan secara purposif. Data dikumpulkan melalui wawancara, observasi, dan dokumentasi, kemudian dianalisis secara deskriptif. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa pengelolaan telah mencakup fungsi perencanaan, pengorganisasian, penggerakan, dan pengawasan, tetapi belum terintegrasi secara optimal karena keterbatasan pedoman operasional, pendampingan usaha, dan evaluasi perkembangan peserta. abstract: Excessive fruit set in European (Prunus domestica L.) and Japanese (Prunus salicina L.) plum trees necessitates thinning to optimize crop load, enhance fruit quality, and reduce manual hand thinning. This study evaluated the efficacy of the ethylene precursor 1-aminocyclopropane-1-carboxylic acid (1-ACC) as a chemical thinning agent for the European plum cultivar ‘Vibrant’ and the Japanese plum cultivar ‘Early Golden’. Treatments were applied at full bloom (FB) and at the fruitlet stage (8-10 mm diameter) using 1-ACC concentrations of 150, 300, and 450 mg·L⁻¹. Horticultural measurements included crop load, yield, fruit size distribution, fruit quality, phytotoxic effects, and crop value. Applications of 1-ACC effectively reduced crop load, with FB applications producing greater thinning responses than fruitlet-stage applications. Increasing application rates resulted in decreased yield and crop value, while average fruit weight increased. No hand thinning was required in both years of the study due to poor pollination in the ‘Early Golden’ orchard and atypical fruit drop unrelated to 1-ACC treatments following early fruit development in the ‘Vibrant’ orchard; therefore, commercial thinning was not required. Thinning responses varied by cultivar and application timing, underscoring the importance of cultivar-specific thinning strategies. Ethylene evolution following 1-ACC applic…

title: Relationship Between Perceived Stress and Student Incivility Among College Students: A Cross-Sectional Study
abstract: Student incivility has become an increasing concern in higher education because of its adverse effects on classroom climate, teaching effectiveness, and students' academic experiences. Psychological stress has been recognised as a potential factor influencing uncivil behaviour. This study evaluated the relationship between perceived stress and student incivility among college students and investigated whether perceived stress significantly predicts student incivility. A quantitative, cross-sectional research design was followed, and data were collected from 219 college students using structured questionnaires measuring perceived stress and student incivility. Descriptive statistics, reliability analysis, Pearson's correlation, and simple linear regression were performed using Jamovi. A statistically significant positive relationship was identified between perceived stress and student incivility. Regression analysis showed that perceived stress significantly predicted student incivility, although it explained only 4% of the variance in uncivil behaviour. Significant gender differences were observed in both perceived stress and student incivility. Rather than presuming an automatic, uniform progression from student stress to behavioural misconduct, this study provides a nuanced, methodologically transparent evaluation that underscores the sensitivity of stress–incivility dynamics…

abstract: Purpose: The study explored role of project monitoring mechanisms in enhancing performance of Public-Private Partnership (PPP) infrastructure projects in Kenya. Policy puts a lot of emphasis on the need for monitoring along the project lifecycle; however, many PPP projects continue to display inefficiencies pointing towards weak monitoring systems. Materials and Methods: Data were collected from 252 respondents representing government agencies, private consortia, and project management units across 103 PPP projects. Regression analysis was used to test relationship between project monitoring mechanisms and project performance. Findings: Project monitoring had a statistically significant but weak positive influence on project performance (β = .014, p < .005). The positive but not so profound effect suggests that the monitoring frameworks that exists are largely compliance-oriented rather than the one that drives performance in the project environment. Implications to Theory, Practice and Policy: The study recommends institutionalizing real-time monitoring, feedback systems, and adoption of digital data tools to strengthen accountability within PPP infrastructure projects in Kenya. abstract: Abstract Background The reintroduction of exercise pulmonary hypertension (EPH) to the pulmonary hypertension (PH) definition by the European guidelines underlines the importance of examining the hemodynamic response to exercise during right heart catheterization. Because the standard exercise modality of cycle ergometry (CE) is not universally accessible, we compared its hemodynamic effects with those of dynamic single-arm exercise (AE) in patients undergoing right heart catheterization (RHC). Methods 50 consecutive patients with indication for RHC were enrolled. Hemodynamic parameters were assessed at rest, followed by randomized exercise periods with an intervening rest phase. Thermodilution was used to determine cardiac output. The intensity of the AE was patient-determined, whereas CE was conducted at a fixed work rate ranging from 10 to 50 watts, based on the patient’s physical status. Oxygen uptake (VO₂) was estimated using the reverse Fick principle to compare relative exercise intensity between modalities. EPH was defined by an mPAP/cardiac output slope > 3 mmHg·L⁻¹·min⁻¹, and exercise-induced left heart disease by a rise in PAWP from ≤ 15 mmHg at rest to > 25 mmHg during exercise. title: The Effect of Financial Literacy and Financial Planning on the Financial Control Ability of MSMEs
abstract: Financial control is a critical managerial function for MSME sustainability because it enables owners to compare actual outcomes with plans, identify deviations, and take corrective action. This study examines the associations of financial literacy and financial planning ability with financial control ability among MSMEs. A cross-sectional quantitative survey was conducted using purposive sampling of 91 MSME owners or managers who completed 24 five-point Likert items. Variable scores were calculated as item means and analyzed using multiple linear regression, supported by reliability assessment, residual diagnostics, and HC3 robust standard errors. Mean scores for financial literacy, financial planning, and financial control were 4.615, 3.892, and 4.369, respectively. Financial literacy (B=0.332; β=0.331; p<0.001) and financial planning (B=0.317; β=0.655; p<0.001) were positively associated with financial control. The model was significant, F(2,88)=136.829; p<0.001, with R²=75.67%. However, financial control reliability was low (α=0.424), and residuals were non-normal. The findings suggest that financial planning has a stronger standardized association with financial control than financial literacy, although interpretation should remain exploratory because of measurement-quality limitations and the observational design.

title: Addressing mental health among incarcerated individuals through financial education: evidence from prison-based programs
Financial Technology dan Inklusi Keuangan Masyarakat Pedesaan: Tinjauan Literatur Sistematis atas Manfaat, Hambatan, dan Kebijakan
abstract: Differences in financial service use between urban and rural areas suggest that the expansion of financial technology (fintech) does not necessarily lead to meaningful inclusion. This study synthesizes the roles, benefits, barriers, and policy priorities of fintech for rural communities through a systematic literature review and narrative thematic synthesis of ten core publications from 2021–2025. A reconciled selection flow reports 309 records, 102 duplicates, 95 records excluded during screening, 56 reports not retrieved, 46 reports excluded after eligibility assessment, and ten included studies. The literature suggests that digital payments and financial services may reduce geographical and transaction-cost barriers, while their effects on poverty, productivity, and welfare are highly context- and design-dependent. Most available evidence is national-level or conceptual; direct rural household-level evidence remains limited. Recurring barriers include connectivity, financial and digital literacy, trust, data security, and product suitability. The synthesis proposes a sequenced policy agenda encompassing digital infrastructure and local agents, practice-oriented literacy, context-sensitive services, consumer protection, and outcome-based evaluation. The evidence does not justify a universal numerical claim about poverty reduction.

title: Institutional Perspectives on Youth Digital Vulnerability in Lampung, Indonesia: Problematic Information, Cyber Financial Fraud, and a Community-Based Resilience Model
abstract: This study examines institutional perspectives on youth digital vulnerability in Lampung Province, Indonesia, focusing on problematic information, cyber financial fraud, and community-based prevention. Using a qualitative descriptive approach, data were collected through face-to-face, semi-structured interviews with purposively selected representatives from 13 organizational units across provincial and municipal government, police, territorial defense, social resilience, and digital-governance institutions. Documented interview records were analyzed thematically and contextualized using policy and connectivity documents, alongside provincial cyber-governance evaluations covering 2022–2025. The analysis generated four themes: youth vulnerability within an unequal digital environment; problematic information and cyber financial fraud as converging risks; a layered institutional response and its implementation constraints; and a proposed community-based youth digital resilience model. Institutional informants linked youth digital vulnerability to unequal connectivity, uneven information-verification capacity, and limited digital-safety awareness. Problematic information and cyber financial fraud were described as distinct but related risks that may exploit trust, emotion, urgency, and limited verification. Institutional accounts identified complementary functions in public communi…

Density of Subminimum Wage Usage and Labour Market Consequences for Workers with Disabilities in the United States
abstract: Section 14(c) of the Fair Labor Standards Act allows for workers with disabilities in the United States to be paid below the federal minimum wage. Using Current Population Survey data and 14(c) certificate employment data from the U.S. Department of Labour, this article investigates whether the density of 14(c) employment has labour market spillovers for workers with disabilities. Logistic regressions suggest individuals with disabilities living in states with more active 14(c) certificates are less likely to be participating in the labour force and to be employed. Regional concentrations of 14(c) certificates may be related to weakened regional differences in bargaining power of workers with disabilities. JEL Codes: J14, K31, J31

title: Characterization, Epidemiology, and Host Range of Alternaria solani f. sp. lactucae , the Causal Pathogen of Alternaria leaf spot of lettuce
abstract: An undescribed leaf spot disease was first seen on lettuce grown in coastal California in 2023. Caused by a species of Alternaria , the symptoms were round to irregular, gray green to brown leaf spots having concentric rings; these symptoms were distinct from those of other known foliar diseases of lettuce in the state. Inoculation experiments showed that 15 different cultivars of iceberg, romaine, green leaf, red leaf, and butterhead lettuce types were susceptible. When 22 non-lettuce crops in seven plant families were inoculated, this Alternaria sp. caused disease on only endive, potato, and tomato. Conidial morphology of the lettuce pathogen resembled that of the potato early blight pathogen, A. solani . When an A. solani isolate from potato was inoculated onto potato and lettuce, the potato developed severe early blight, but the lettuce remained symptomless. In 8- to 11-month-old Petri plate cultures, the lettuce Alternaria sp. isolates formed microsclerotia; when inoculated onto lettuce, the microsclerotia caused the leaf spot disease. Whole-genome sequencing and calculation of average nucleotide identity indicated that the lettuce Alternaria sp. and A. solani isolates clustered together, although the lettuce isolates were distinct from the potato pathogen and represented a new forma specialis , A. solani f. sp. lactucae , within the A. solani species complex. We present a…

abstract: The global transition from fossil-fuel-based electricity systems to renewable energy sources is essential to achieving sustainable development and reducing grid dependency. This study investigates residential energy consumption behavior within a solar-battery-grid architecture using the proposed GridSolarMatch framework. System monitoring data were obtained through a dedicated data logger operating with Module Version No.: LSWS_01_2421_SS_00_00.00.00.06, ensuring high-resolution and reliable time-series measurement of solar generation, battery operation, and grid interaction. GridSolarMatch employs a transparent, rule-based dispatch strategy that prioritizes solar energy utilization, regulates battery charging and discharging via explicit state-of-charge (SOC) dynamics, and uses the grid as a fallback resource during energy deficits. Time- of-Use electricity tariffs are incorporated to evaluate tariff-aware operational behavior without relying on forecasting or computationally intensive optimization solvers. The result demonstrates effective battery buffering, reduced grid dependency during peak tariff periods, and controlled SOC cycling that preserves battery longevity. Analysis of grid import behavior, battery state-of-charge profiles, and a cumulative sustainability-cost objective function confirms that the framework enhances renewable self-consumption while moderating long …

Induction of Growth and Sporulation in Colletotrichum capsici Inciting Turmeric Leaf Spot
abstract: Background: Turmeric (Curcuma longa L.) is a globally significant spice, also referred to as the “golden spice.” India is the world’s largest producer of turmeric, accounting for 80% of the global production. Turmeric is utilized in the preparation of food, as a colouring agent in textiles and as a component of confectionaries and medicine. Turmeric is also employed to treat human and animal diseases due to its antimicrobial and anticancer properties. The plant is susceptible to a variety of fungal, bacterial, viral and nematode diseases. Leaf spot, which is caused by Colletotrichum capsici, is the most significant fungal disease. It results in a substantial decrease in yield as a result of the loss of photosynthetic area. Methods: The growth of C. capsici, the influence of light sources on growth and sporulation, the utilization of carbon and nitrogen sources and the effect of organic manure extract on growth were all examined in this experiment. Result: The maximum radial mycelial growth was achieved on potato dextrose agar and potato dextrose agar plus host leaf extract media, with diameters of 90.00 and 87.00 mm, respectively. The pathogen demonstrated exceptional conidial production during a seven-day period of continuous darkness and three hours of darkness followed by 21 hours of light. Sucrose was determined to be the most effective carbon source among the five distinct…

title: Forecasting volatile electricity prices in the Australian National Electricity market using machine learning
abstract: Abstract The growing integration of variable renewable energy Sources have intensified price volatility in the Australian National Electricity Market (NEM), creating operational challenges for market operators, traders, and battery energy storage systems (BESS). Short-term electricity price forecasting is important for arbitrage, market operation, and participation in ancillary services such as Frequency Control Ancillary Services (FCAS). The evaluation presents a Comparative evaluation of eight forecasting models: Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average (ARIMA), Seasonal Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average with Exogenous Regressors (SARIMAX), linear regression, exponential smoothing, XGBoost, Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks, and Prophet with and without an exogenous demand regressor, using historical price data from New South Wales (NSW). Five-minute-ahead forecasting performance is assessed across selected stable, volatile, and rapidly fluctuating periods. XGBoost achieves the lowest mean validation MAE (0.040) and highest mean validation $$R^2$$ (0.949) among the evaluated models, and retains the best performance on the held-out test set. The findings support the use of market information in the evaluated forecasting models.

title: Formation of State Policy on Professional Orientation as a Factor in Mitigating the Personnel Shortage in the Labour Market
abstract: This study compared career guidance in Kazakhstan with Germany and Finland and identified policy implications for improving education–labour market links. It combined documentary analysis, cross-national comparison, media content analysis and a survey of 42 respondents in Kazakhstan. Germany emphasised employer participation and workplace-integrated vocational training, while Finland provided continuous guidance across educational and employment transitions. Kazakhstan has adopted elements of both models, but coordination, labour market alignment, training options and school-based guidance remain limited. Survey findings also indicated gaps in school guidance provision. Stronger coordination among schools, employers, and employment services could improve continuity and employment relevance.

title: Festa e mercado
abstract: No presente texto discutimos a política dos eventos festivos e da produção de seus públicos. A partir de uma abordagem etnográfica, cruzamos o acompanhamento de festas universitárias LGBTQIA+ em São Carlos, município do interior do estado de São Paulo, com os megaeventos de Madonna e Lady Gaga realizados no Rio de Janeiro, tomando-os como situações privilegiadas para observar transformações nas formas de organização, consumo e ocupação da cidade em uma leitura mais sistêmica. Argumentamos que esses eventos integram a paisagem urbana contemporânea e são simultaneamente espaços de consumo e acontecimentos públicos, com relações de interdependência. Embora incorporem práticas inclusivas, que envolvem o reconhecimento da democratização do acesso e das diferenças, a naturalização dos processos econômicos de profissionalização, empresarização e segmentação dos públicos para viabilização do lucro, rearticula desigualdades. Demonstramos que a ampliação do acesso dos públicos não elimina as diferenciações e hierarquias, que reaparecem nas formas de trabalho, nos modos de circulação das pessoas, nas possibilidades de consumo e nas dinâmicas dos espaços. Ao analisar essas diferentes escalas empíricas, buscamos conjugar interesses teóricos comuns na compreensão das relações entre mercado e diferenças sociais na produção de identidades coletivas, experiências e desigualdades. title: Inclusive Agribusiness Models for Smallholder Farmers: Value Creation, Market Integration and Equitable Benefit Sharing
abstract: Inclusive agribusiness is increasingly proposed as a means of connecting smallholder farmers to remunerative markets while improving the distribution of benefits within agricultural value chains. Yet participation, commercial upgrading and equity are analytically distinct outcomes, and improvements in one do not reliably secure the others. This critical narrative review examines the institutional designs, value-creation mechanisms and distributional consequences of contract farming, producer organisations, coordinated value chains, sustainability certification and digitally mediated market services. Peer-reviewed theoretical, observational, quasi-experimental, experimental and review evidence was assessed with attention to selection, counterfactual validity, contract governance, heterogeneity and geographical transferability. The evidence indicates that coordinated marketing can reduce transaction costs, support quality upgrading and improve access to inputs or information. Nevertheless, observed income gains are contingent on crop characteristics, procurement reliability, bargaining conditions and who is able to enter and remain in a scheme. Stronger causal evidence exists for particular contractual and information interventions than for the broader claim that inclusive business models routinely reduce inequality. Commercial standards may provide price or market advantages whi…

title: Do guard dogs really need protecting? Tibetan perspectives and practices of Tibetan Mastiff conservation after the market collapse
abstract: Following the collapse of the Tibetan Mastiff (TM) market in China in the mid-2010s, conservation of the breed has become a laissez-faire field dominated by competing grassroots actors. Drawing on twenty-four months of multi-sited ethnography in Tibetan pastoral communities, breeding farms, and enthusiast networks, this article compares how Tibetan intellectuals, enthusiasts, and pastoralists in Machu (Gansu) understand whether TMs need conservation, who should be responsible for it, and by what method. Because the TM is neither a wildlife species nor a standardised breed, what stakeholders seek to sustain is a working pastoral lineage and the interspecies lifeway through which guarding capabilities are cultivated. I argue that these positions are best distinguished through three concepts routinely conflated in everyday speech: guarding, protection, and conservation. Tibetan intellectuals use the TM as a metaphor for Tibetan dispossession but rarely offer practical proposals. Tibetan enthusiasts, despite claiming Tibetan custodianship, equate conservation with protection through controlled breeding farms, reproducing the paternalistic rescue logic critiqued by Abu-Lughod. Pastoralist conservationists in Machu instead seek to restore the conditions in which guard dogs can guard once again, although certain pastoral dog-keeping practices such as long-term tethering and misconcept…

title: Digital Platform Entrepreneurship, Gendered Care Responsibilities and Labour Market Inclusion in India
abstract: Women’s labour force participation in India remains persistently low, shaped not only by limited employment opportunities but also by the unequal distribution of unpaid domestic and caregiving work. This study examines the role of women-led platform entrepreneurship in promoting an inclusive labour market by addressing the care burden and enhancing female labour force participation. It asks how digital transformation has enabled platform entrepreneurship, how platform entrepreneurship shapes women’s entry and terms of participation, whether platform entrepreneurship accommodates, relieves or intensifies care, how it relates to inclusive growth, and what constraints limit these outcomes. The paper adopts a conceptual and analytical approach, drawing on existing literature and descriptive analysis of Time Use Survey (TUS), 2024. It compares gender differences in participation and average time spent per participant in employment, unpaid domestic and caregiving activities across sixteen major states: Andhra Pradesh, Assam, Bihar, Gujarat, Haryana, Himachal Pradesh, Karnataka, Kerala, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Odisha, Punjab, Rajasthan, Tamil Nadu, Uttar Pradesh and West Bengal. The findings indicate that the gender gap is associated with unequal allocation of unpaid work as much as with differential access to employment, with notable variation across states. title: Market Penetration of a Premium Dairy Brand through General and Modern Trade: Exploratory Field Evidence from Pune, India
abstract: A premium dairy brand entering an established city market has to win over two very different people: the neighbourhood retailer in general trade (GT) and the shopper in modern trade (MT). This paper reports an exploratory field study of Sid’s Farm, a dairy brand that sells on laboratory testing and quality, carried out during a two-month on-the-job training placement in Pune (May–July 2026). I draw on a recorded retailer funnel from Wakad (53 retailers approached), a brand-availability audit of those same 53 outlets, and field observation of customer interactions, freezer merchandising and two sampling activities at a modern-trade store in Baner. Reading the evidence through Ansoff’s market-penetration logic, the AIDA model and retailer relationship management, I find five things. First, 77.8% of interested retailers (21 of 27) placed a first order, yet only 39.6% of everyone approached did. Second, 13 of the 21 first-order retailers (61.9%) were recorded as reordering, while 6 had stopped. Third, Govind and Amul were present in 94.3% and 88.7% of audited outlets, so entry means competing for shelf space that is already taken. Fourth, the main GT barriers were price, demand uncertainty, margin and cold-chain-related spoilage, while MT shoppers pushed back on price, loyalty and low visibility. Fifth, high-protein curd and paneer drew stronger interest in a fitness-adjacent store…

abstract: Background Community learning centers ( Pusat Kegiatan Belajar Masyarakat , PKBM) are Indonesia’s main providers of second-chance upper-secondary (Package C) education, yet little is known about how their learning services develop learners’ 21st-century skills. This study examined whether learning service quality develops learners’ critical thinking, creativity, collaboration, and communication (4C skills) directly or through tutor competence. Methods A cross-sectional survey was completed by 354 final-level Package C learners drawn by proportional geographic stratification from 4,530 learners in urban, coastal, and highland PKBMs in South Sulawesi, Indonesia. Adapted, expert-reviewed instruments measured the three constructs, and data were analyzed with partial least squares structural equation modeling using 5,000 bootstrap resamples. Results The measurement model met reliability and validity criteria, and full collinearity tests indicated that common method bias was unlikely. Learning service quality predicted tutor competence (β = 0.545, p < 0.001), and tutor competence predicted 4C skills (β = 0.548, p < 0.001), whereas the direct effect of service quality on 4C skills was not significant (β = 0.170, p = 0.146). The indirect effect was significant (β = 0.298, 95% confidence interval 0.188 to 0.408), indicating indirect-only (full) mediation; the model explained 43.1% of th…

title: CONTENT MARKETING DIMENSIONS AND CUSTOMER PATRONAGE OF QUICK-SERVICE RESTAURANTS IN CALABAR, NIGERIA
abstract: This study examined the effect of content marketing on customer patronage of quick-service restaurants (QSRs) in Calabar, Cross River State, Nigeria. Specifically, it assessed the effects of informational content marketing, visual content marketing and social media content marketing on customer patronage. A cross-sectional survey design was adopted, and primary data were collected from customers of purposively selected QSR outlets using a structured questionnaire. The sample size was determined using the Topman formula, resulting in 369 questionnaires being administered, of which 328 were returned and found usable, representing a response rate of 88.9%. The data were analysed using descriptive statistics and multiple linear regression with the Statistical Package for the Social Sciences (SPSS). The regression model was statistically significant (F = 35.640, p < .001), explaining 24.8% of the variation in customer patronage (R² = .248). The findings revealed that informational content marketing (Beta = .163, p = .010), visual content marketing (Beta = .288, p = .001) and social media content marketing (Beta = .372, p = .002) each had a positive and statistically significant effect on customer patronage. Social media content marketing recorded the strongest relative contribution, followed by visual and informational content marketing. The study concludes that content marketing is…

State Capacity and Environmental Regulation: The Case of Air Pollution in La Oroya, Peru (1922–1927)
abstract: This study evaluates the Peruvian state’s resolution of the La Oroya emissions conflict (1922–1927), assessing whether it demonstrated state capacity by incorporating environmental considerations and effectively implementing the measures adopted. Using a historical-institutional approach based on the qualitative analysis of historical sources—bulletins and reports of the Corps of Mining Engineers of Peru (CIMP), established in 1902 to manage mineral resources, official bulletins of the Ministry of Development, and secondary literature—the analysis applies Carpenter’s concept of bureaucratic autonomy (legitimacy, organizational capacity, and political differentiation) to examine the CIMP’s role during its first decades. The results show that, despite its political support, legitimacy, and technical capacity, the CIMP’s bureaucratic autonomy was constrained on the criterion of political differentiation. Its Report on La Oroya’s Emissions (1926) identified the problem and proposed technical solutions, but the CIMP lacked the authority to enforce them: the Cerro de Pasco Copper Corporation complied only partially, installed filters only between 1936 and 1942, and purchased much of the affected land at low prices. In La Oroya, the resolution favored corporate interests over environmental and community concerns, reflecting Peru’s broader trend of prioritizing economic growth over env…
