title: Identifying dynamical network markers of financial market instability
abstract: Abstract Market instability has been extensively studied using mathematical approaches to characterize complex trading dynamics and detect structural change points. This study explores the potential for early detection of market instability by applying the Dynamical Network Markers (DNM) theory to order placement and execution data from the Tokyo Stock Exchange. DNM theory identifies indicators associated with critical transitions as their precursors in high-dimensional financial market systems of many interacting elements. In this study, market participants are identified using virtual server IDs from the trading system, and multivariate time series representing their trading activities are constructed. This framework treats each participant as an interacting element, thereby enabling the application of DNM theory to the obtained time series. The results indicate the presence of DNM-related patterns associated with large price movements on a daily time scale. These findings demonstrate the applicability of the DNM framework to market participant behavioral data and provide a basis for understanding mechanisms of instabilizing dynamics in financial market systems. The study could inform potential future developments of DNM-based early warning indicators through the identification of appropriate forecasting horizons and time scales as well as the incorporation of multiple aspect…

title: DDA-BNN v1.0: a morphology-aware surrogate model for the optical properties of black carbon-containing particles
abstract: Black carbon (BC) is the most strongly absorbing component of atmospheric aerosol and significantly impacts Earth's energy balance. The optical properties of BC-containing particles depend on particle-level variability in size, chemical composition, and internal morphology. Such particle-level details are not easily represented in large-scale atmospheric models. Existing parameterizations typically assume idealized particle geometries (e.g., homogeneous spheres or concentric core–shell spheres) and homogeneous mixing, which can yield biased predictions and provide no quantitative estimate of model-form uncertainty at the single-particle level. In this work, we present a probabilistic framework for predicting the optical properties of individual BC-containing particles using a hybrid Bayesian neural network (BNN) model trained on discrete dipole approximation (DDA) simulations. The hybrid BNN is a flexible combination of deterministic and Bayesian layers allowing for more realistic treatment of particle optical properties and quantification of uncertainty. The hybrid BNN model predicts extinction efficiency, single-scattering albedo, and asymmetry parameter and returns predictive uncertainty that can be decomposed into aleatoric (data-driven variability) and epistemic (uncertainty due to limited training coverage) components. We show that the hybrid BNN outperforms homogeneous-s…

title: Detection of TeV emission during early afterglow from poorly localized gamma-ray bursts with ground-based IACTs
abstract: Gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) are among the most luminous and rapidly evolving transients in the Universe. While space-based instruments have extended GRB observations up to energies of ∼100 GeV, the detection of very high-energy (VHE; E>100 GeV) emission from ground-based telescopes, especially during prompt and/or the early afterglow phases, remains challenging. These difficulties arise from the rapid temporal decay of GRB afterglows, strong attenuation by the extragalactic background light, observational latency, and the typical poor sky localization provided by MeV detectors such as Fermi/GBM. In this work, we investigated the prospects for detecting TeV (∼100 GeV--1 TeV) emission from poorly localized GRBs by adopting optimized follow-up strategies based on rapid tiling of large localization regions. We simulated a realistic population of GRBs informed by more than 15 years of Fermi/GBM and Swift/XRT detections and recent progress in the afterglow emission modeling. Using these simulations, we evaluated the detectability of GRB early afterglows by the next-generation imaging atmospheric Cherenkov telescopes, which are equipped with larger fields of view, as a function of latency, exposure time, and observational strategy. Our strategy can significantly enhance the detection rate; for instruments such as ASTRI and LACT, it increases by up to a factor of two compared to strategies…

title: Deep learning models for ADITYA-U MHD equilibrium
abstract: Abstract This work presents an integrated deep learning framework for rapid magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) equilibrium estimation in the ADITYA-U tokamak. A free-boundary equilibrium database containing 100,760 cases was generated using the pyIPREQ Grad–Shafranov solver from experimentally derived operating conditions spanning 766 ADITYA-U plasma discharges, with constraints representative of circular limiter plasmas near the flat-top phase. The database was used to develop a cascaded framework for predicting scalar equilibrium quantities, 1d safety factor profiles, and 2d poloidal flux profiles. Dense neural networks, principal component analysis (PCA), convolutional neural networks (CNN) and physics-informed neural networks (PINN) were investigated within this framework. The error propagation, cross-models consistency and ablation study of Grad–Shafranov residual were performed for the proposed framework. Across the test dataset, the models achieve median mean absolute errors of 1 × 10 − 2 for the safety factor profile and 2 × 10 − 3 for the normalized poloidal flux profile. The largest model requires approximately 1ms per equilibrium inference on a multi-core CPU. The results demonstrate the potential of the framework as a fast surrogate for equilibrium analysis, experiment planning and real-time plasma control applications for ADITYA-U experiments.

title: Prediction of lncRNA-protein interacting pairs using LLM embeddings based on evolutionary information
abstract: Interactions of long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) with proteins is responsible for numerous cellular processes, including transcriptional regulation, chromatin remodeling, cell differentiation, and intracellular signaling. Several computational methods have been developed for predicting lncRNA–protein interaction (LPI) pairs; however, many existing approaches were developed using earlier versions of interaction databases, potentially limiting their applicability to more recently characterized interactions. In this study, we developed a sequence-based framework for LPI prediction using a large non-redundant dataset comprising 128,374 interacting and an equal number of non-interacting pairs. Initially, similarity-based approach BLAST was tried which had poor discriminative power, due to low sequence similarity between sequences. Subsequently, we developed convolutional neural network and machine learning models using sequence-derived features and protein language model embeddings. The CatBoost model integrating Dinucleotide Autocorrelation (DACC) features for lncRNAs and ESM-2-t30 embeddings for proteins achieved an AUC of 0.929 on the training dataset and 0.692 on the homology-aware validation dataset. These results demonstrate the potential of combining sequence-derived features and protein language model representations for LPI prediction while highlighting the challenges associa…

title: Multi-scale simulations of wind farm impacts on nighttime near-surface temperature in complex terrain
abstract: Various studies have shown that wind turbine wakes can induce temperature variations. Investigating these effects near the ground is particularly important for assessing their potential impact on vegetation and human activities. In this study, the multi-scale Meso-NH/SURFEX/EOL modeling framework, which includes coupled atmosphere, land-surface and actuator models, is used to evaluate the impact of the Ensemble Éolien Catalan wind farm on ground and near-surface temperatures, as well as terrain-specific flow dynamics during a stable nocturnal radiative cooling event associated with frost risk in nearby vineyards. The simulations are performed using nested domains to dynamically downscale the atmospheric conditions from the operational weather forecast AROME-1.3km to a horizontal resolution of 5 m, allowing explicit representation of turbine wakes through rotative actuator disk representation. Turbine-induced meteorological variations are quantified by comparing simulations performed with and without the actuator model. The results reveal that near-surface meteorological responses arise from the combined influence of individual turbine wakes and the large-scale impact of the wind farm, which modifies the flow dynamics and temperature field. In the wind farm, a mean near-surface warming of approximately 0.4 °C is found, with localized temperature increases reaching up to 1.6 °C i…

title: Modeling individual nearby radio galaxies as ultra-high-energy cosmic-ray accelerators
abstract: Abstract Nearby radio galaxies are among the most promising candidates for the acceleration of ultra-high-energy cosmic rays (UHECRs). In this work, we develop a physically motivated, source-resolved framework to quantify the contribution of the three nearest Fanaroff–Riley Class I (FR-I) radio galaxies – Centaurus A, Virgo A, and Fornax A – to the UHECR flux measured by the Pierre Auger Observatory. Acceleration spectra derived from detailed jet-acceleration models are combined with numerical simulations of extragalactic propagation, while the more distant radio-galaxy population is treated as a continuous background. By fitting our simulation exclusively to the measured UHECR energy spectrum, we determine the relative contribution of each source and constrain the fraction of jet power converted into UHECR luminosity. We find that a small number of nearby radio galaxies can account for the highest-energy UHECR flux with acceleration efficiencies of order $$10^{-3}$$ 10 - 3 – $$10^{-2}$$ 10 - 2 , while the background contribution remains subdominant. Some resulting scenarios yield mass-composition trends broadly consistent with observations at the highest energies and predict distinct levels of secondary neutrino fluxes. These results demonstrate that physically grounded, source-specific modeling of nearby radio galaxies provides a physically motivated contribution to the inter…

title: From academic excellence to market attractiveness: explaining the transformation gap in higher education institutions
abstract: Purpose This study examines why academic performance does not necessarily translate directly into market attractiveness in higher education institutions. Drawing on capability, institutional and signaling perspectives, it frames this disconnect as a transformation gap: an explanatory condition in which internally generated academic value requires strategic and relational mechanisms to become externally recognized market value. The transformation gap is not treated as a separate latent construct. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative explanatory design was used with 300 strategic-level academic and administrative respondents in Indonesian higher education. Four reflective constructs – academic performance (AP), strategic positioning (SP), relational signaling (RS) and market attractiveness (MA) – were assessed using Partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM). The reported evaluation includes reliability and convergent validity, heterotrait–monotrait ratio (HTMT), collinearity, R2, Q2, f2 and bootstrapping with 5,000 resamples. Findings Academic performance was not significantly related to market attractiveness directly (β = 0.07, t = 1.12, p > 0.05), so H1 was not supported. Academic performance was positively related to strategic positioning (β = 0.41, t = 6.85, p < 0.001) and relational signaling (β = 0.38, t = 6.10, p < 0.001). Strategic positi…

title: HEATING CHARACTERISTICS OF A SOLAR-CO₂ AIR SOURCE HEAT PUMP COUPLED SYSTEM WITH VALLEY-ELECTRICITY HEAT STORAGE
abstract: Taking the heating system of a rural household in Yinchuan as the research object, a simulation model of a solar-CO₂ air source heat pump heating system was developed based on TRNSYS, and its operation from November to March of the following year was simulated and analyzed. The results show that the system can reliably satisfy the indoor winter heating demand of rural households, with heating temperature fluctuating little and remaining stable at approximately 18.0 ℃. Regarding the electricity consumption of the coupled system, the energy use of the space-heating pump and the heating circulation pump rises in step with the extreme-cold heat load in winter, showing a pronounced negative correlation with outdoor temperature; in contrast, the energy consumption of the solar collector pump is governed solely by solar irradiation and remains stable throughout the entire heating season. Over the whole heating season, the collector harvested 6,276.26 kWh of heat and the air source heat pump delivered 6,359.19 kWh, the two contributions being nearly equal, with the total heat output of the heat pump slightly exceeding that of the solar collector. The carbon emissions of the solar-coupled heat pump heating system are only 1,433.94 kgCO₂, equivalent to 24.5% of those of a coal-fired boiler (the highest-emitting option), demonstrating remarkable energy-saving and emission-reduction effect…

Assessment of the alignment between Nutri-Score and the NOVA classification before and after the Nutri-Score algorithm update: analysis of 450 food products from the Polish retail market
abstract: Abstract Background Nutri-Score is one of the most widely used front-of-pack nutrition labelling (FOPNL) systems in Europe. Whereas Nutri-Score assesses nutritional quality, the NOVA classification categorises foods according to the extent and purpose of processing. An updated version of the algorithm was introduced to improve alignment with current dietary recommendations and reduce favourable ratings assigned to highly and ultra-processed foods. This study aimed to assess the alignment between Nutri-Score and the NOVA classification before and after the algorithm update, and to analyse changes in the classification of food products available on the Polish retail market. Methods A total of 450 food products available in Polish supermarkets and representing various food categories were analysed. Products were classified according to the Nutri-Score algorithm (before and after the 2023 update) and the NOVA classification system. A healthfulness classification based on Part B of the KomPAN questionnaire and supplementary author-defined criteria was used to assess changes in Nutri-Score ratings before and after the algorithm update across products with different healthfulness profiles. Results Agreement between Nutri-Score and the NOVA classification increased following the algorithm update (ρ = 0.571 after the update vs. ρ = 0.518 before the update). title: Nonconviction Arrests and Labor Market Trajectories
abstract: Abstract In this Article, I examine whether nonconviction arrests—one of the least severe forms of formal criminal justice contact—destabilize labor market trajectories. Using longitudinal data from the National Longitudinal Survey of Youth 1997 (NLSY97) and individual fixed-effects models, I isolate the relationship between nonconviction arrests and labor market outcomes among adult men. I find that a nonconviction arrest is associated with a 7.5% point increase in the likelihood of employment disruption in the following survey period. In the longer term, nonconviction arrests are associated with hourly wages that are approximately 10.5% lower and significant reductions in access to employer-provided health insurance (5.1% points) and retirement benefits (8.7% points). Reduced access to benefits appears to be related to lower rates of full-time employment. Given Black men’s disproportionate exposure to nonconviction arrest, these findings suggest that arrest practices may contribute to racial disparities in labor market outcomes.

title: Under the “Light Wellness” Consumer Trend—A Study on Consumer Purchase Intentions and Market Expansion Strategies for Functional Snacks
abstract: This study examines consumer purchase intentions and market expansion strategies for functional snacks within the “light wellness” trend. It reviews relevant theories and the market landscape, combining questionnaire surveys with empirical analysis. Using SPSS and Stata, the study conducts reliability and validity tests, exploratory factor analysis, correlation analysis, regression analysis, and robustness tests. Findings show that perceived value—comprising functional, hedonic, symbolic, social, and conditional dimensions—positively influences purchase intention, with functional value exerting the strongest effect; health concern positively moderates this relationship, and sub-sample regressions confirm robustness. Firms should advance market expansion through product innovation, value communication, scenario building, and channel synergy.

title: FROM GENERATED INFORMATION TO INTERNATIONALIZATION KNOWLEDGE: GENERATIVE AI, ABSORPTIVE CAPACITY AND SMES’ MARKET ENTRY DECISIONS
abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) can reduce the cost of acquiring information about foreign markets and generating alternative strategies for small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). Greater information availability does not necessarily improve decision quality, however. This conceptual paper uses a narrative literature review and adopts absorptive capacity as its main theoretical perspective, alongside the Uppsala internationalization process model, to examine the role of experiential knowledge and business networks. The unit of analysis is a specific market entry decision involving a defined product, target market, and entry mode. The paper distinguishes information-processing efficiency, decision quality, and business performance. It proposes that generated content requires value recognition, evidence verification, and contextual integration to support a decision. Proportionate resource commitments and feedback from action may then support the development of reusable knowledge. These processes are connected through feedback rather than a fixed linear sequence. The strategic value of GenAI depends on the fit between the speed of information generation and organizational verification capacity, knowledge embedded in transaction relationships that is difficult to codify, and the incorporation of feedback into organizational routines. Three propositions address the re…

title: Governança de mercado nas plataformas digitais: uma análise do Código de Ética dos aplicativos de delivery
abstract: O presente trabalho objetivou analisar como o Código de Ética e Conduta do aplicativo iFood atua como mecanismo de governança no mercado de delivery por plataforma. A metodologia empregada foi a análise de conteúdo, que possibilitou construir dimensões de análise e articular a ligação entre o arcabouço teórico e o objeto empírico. Os resultados mostram a existência de estruturas de governança nas plataformas, o que questiona se elas são ferramentas para os estabelecimentos comerciais ou estruturas regulatórias. A conclusão é que os mecanismos observados impõem formas de governança, o que abre uma lacuna relevante para o aprofundamento do tema.

title: Entre o velho e o novo: sociabilidades, poder e mudanças no processo de realocação do Mercado Público de Oitizeiro, João Pessoa-PB
abstract: O presente artigo tem como objetivo analisar as transformações nas sociabilidades, nas relações de poder e nas dinâmicas sociais decorrentes do processo de realocação do Mercado Público de Oitizeiro, em João Pessoa–PB. Mais do que avaliar a eficácia administrativa da mudança, busca-se compreender os significados atribuídos por feirantes, consumidores e demais usuários ao deslocamento do mercado, entendendo-o como um evento social e histórico que impacta redes de relações, práticas cotidianas e estruturas simbólicas consolidadas ao longo de décadas. Sua metodologia é de caráter etnográfico e interpretativo, fundamentada na perspectiva da “descrição densa” de Clifford Geertz, realizada a partir de observações de campo nos dias de feira, através de conversas informais com feirantes e frequentadores, além de registrar conflitos, gestos, narrativas e mudanças nas interações sociais. O estudo dialoga com referenciais teóricos de Georg Simmel, Marshall Sahlins, Victor Turner, Max Gluckman, Eric Wolf e Fredrik Barth, articulando conceitos como sociabilidade, evento histórico, drama social, fronteiras sociais e relações de poder. E com isso, os resultados indicam que a realocação do mercado desencadeia tensões, conflitos e reconfigurações nas redes de sociabilidade, caracterizando-se como um “drama social”, nos termos de Turner. A decisão da gestão municipal, percebida como verticalizad…

title: Stock market prediction and trading strategy optimization with S4-integrated deep learning architectures: a comparative study of hybrid fusion mechanisms
abstract: Purpose The accurate prediction of stock market movements remains a challenging task due to the non-stationary, noisy and highly volatile nature of financial time series. While deep learning models such as Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks, Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) and Transformer have demonstrated promising results, they often struggle to capture both long-term dependencies and short-term fluctuations efficiently. To address these limitations, this paper introduces al hybrid framework that integrates the Structured State Space Sequence (S4) model with three fundamental deep learning architectures via tailored fusion mechanisms. Design/methodology/approach Specifically, we propose (1) LSTM-S4, a parallel architecture with attention-based fusion and skip connections; (2) MLP-S4, a serial embedding model that enables temporal modeling for MLP; and (3) Transformer-S4, a tandem structure that combines global attention with local temporal pattern extraction. Extensive experiments are conducted based on real-world data from six Chinese stocks covering diverse sectors and market conditions. Findings The results demonstrate that the S4-integrated hybrid models outperform their base counterparts and existing baseline models in terms of predictive accuracy measured by RMSE, MSE, MAE and $Rˆ2$, as well as simulated investment returns. Notably, we design a practical trading strateg…

Statistical Modeling of the Drop Strength of Cotton Fiber-Reinforced Paper Composites Using Response Surface Methodology
abstract: . In the present work, a statistical model for the height to failure of cotton fiber-reinforced paper composites subjected to MIL-STD-810G 516.6 drop tests was developed using response surface methodology. The independent variables considered were the density ( ρ ) and alkali treatment time ( t ). The Minitab 22.1.0. statistical software was used for modeling and both linear and non-linear effects were considered. The effect of treatment time was mostly insignificant at the lower densities. However, the effect of variables on the response was in the order of ρ 2 > ρ > t 2 > t . The lowest response (height to failure) was observed in the low-density region (< 0.10 g/cm³), likely due to insufficient material available to accommodate the stress. However, the maximum response was observed at the extended alkali treatment time (4.5 hr. < t < 6.3 hr.) and higher fiber density (0.25 g/cm 3 < ρ < 0.27 g/cm 3 ). The density dominated over the treatment time for the response output. Furthermore, increasing treatment time enhances the response up to a certain point. Once the optimum response was achieved, the response began to decrease slightly with further increases in either density or treatment time. The misalignment and failure of the reinforcement, followed by matrix fracture, were the primary failure mechanisms for composites under the drop test.

abstract: Purpose This study investigates the root causes of Indonesia's teacher distribution crisis, examining the upstream-downstream paradox where a surplus of education graduates coexists with critical teacher shortages in public schools. Design/methodology/approach Employing a Multi-Level Governance (MLG) framework, this qualitative case study analyzes data from 21 key stakeholders, including central and local government officials, university lecturers and teachers. The primary interview data are reinforced by secondary data triangulation from 2021–2024 national recruitment records. Findings The analysis reveals that the shortage is not a supply issue but the result of specific “governance gaps.” These include Fiscal Gaps (local reluctance to hire due to regional allowance costs), Objective Gaps (political patronage), Accountability Gaps (phantom vacancies) and Policy Gaps (fragmented silos). Stakeholders perceive current collaborative efforts as “merely ceremonial” rather than substantive. Research limitations/implications The primary policy focus is 2021–2024, while supply-demand trend analysis draws on national data from 2012 onwards. Long-term policy dynamics may still evolve. Non-state actors in teacher governance were beyond the scope and remain an opportunity for further research. abstract: Bladder cancer is a heterogeneous malignancy with variable immune infiltration and limited response rates to immune checkpoint blockade. HLA-DQB1, a major histocompatibility complex class II gene involved in antigen presentation, may participate in tumor immune regulation. However, its expression pattern, prognostic relevance, immune microenvironmental associations, and immunotherapy-related significance in bladder cancer remain incompletely characterized. Transcriptomic and clinical data of bladder cancer were obtained from TCGA-BLCA. HLA-DQB1 expression was compared between tumor and normal tissues, and its association with overall survival was evaluated using Kaplan–Meier and Cox regression analyses. Single-sample gene set enrichment analysis was used to estimate immune-cell infiltration. Correlations between HLA-DQB1 and immune checkpoints, antigen-presentation genes, and immune-related modules were assessed using Spearman correlation analysis. Differential expression analysis between HLA-DQB1-high and HLA-DQB1-low tumors was performed using limma, followed by GO and Hallmark GSEA. External validation was conducted using GSE13507. Immunotherapy-related analyses were further performed in the IMvigor210 atezolizumab-treated urothelial carcinoma cohort. abstract: Abstract Purpose of Review Allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) is a therapy for hematological malignancies and inherited disorders. However, graft-versus-host disease (GVHD) remains a major cause of morbidity and mortality. Mesenchymal stromal cells (MSCs) have emerged as a cellular therapy because of their immunomodulatory and tissue-repair properties, although clinical responses have been inconsistent. This review examines evidence supporting MSC use for GVHD, focusing on treatment timing, disease stage and severity, patient characteristics, MSC product properties, and biomarkers predicting response. Recent Findings MSCs modulate innate and adaptive immunity, including T cells, B cells, natural killer cells, dendritic cells, and macrophages, through paracrine mediators, extracellular vesicles, and cell-cell interactions. Clinical studies have reported activity in GVHD prophylaxis and treatment, particularly in selected patients with steroid-refractory acute GVHD (SR-aGVHD), whereas randomized studies have not consistently demonstrated benefit across unselected populations. The clinical development of remestemcel-L provided important translational evidence, culminating in FDA approval of remestemcel-L-rknd (Ryoncil) in December 2024 for pediatric patients aged 2 months and older with SR-aGVHD, the first FDA-approved MSC-based therapy for GVHD. Wastewater-based epidemiology during New Zealand's COVID-19 elimination response: real-world public health impact and economic evaluation
abstract: ABSTRACT After more than a year without community transmission, a localised outbreak of COVID-19 occurred in Auckland, New Zealand, in August 2021. The response to this outbreak was supported by wastewater-based epidemiology (WBE) with over 5,000 wastewater tests from 217 locations across New Zealand. This study provides specific real-world examples of the use of WBE to detect pathogen circulation and to provide supporting evidence that transmission was absent or limited in a community, and how this can directly influence public health actions. Evidence of community transmission via positive wastewater tests informed the escalation of public health responses, while early identification of infection in communities with no known cases enabled targeted interventions that contributed to effective control and pathogen elimination from a community. The economic benefits of these responses, quantified in millions of NZ dollars per day, highlight the value of WBE at low disease incidence and emphasise the importance of detection patterns in interpreting results and supporting communication to the public regarding infection risk. WBE can be a highly impactful and cost-effective public health tool in the response to disease incursions. Pandemic preparedness must include plans for selecting appropriate WBE sampling locations and ensuring the capacity to analyse sufficient samples rapidly.

abstract: Diffuse leptomeningeal glioneuronal tumor (DLGNT) represents a rare central nervous system neoplasm predominantly observed in pediatric patients. Most cases pursue an indolent clinical course; nevertheless, a small subset demonstrates high-grade histology together with craniospinal dissemination and carries a dismal prognosis. We describe a 6-year-old girl presenting with recurrent vomiting and obstructive hydrocephalus. Initial neuroimaging revealed cerebellar cystic lesions and diffuse leptomeningeal enhancement, which was initially misinterpreted as infectious meningoencephalitis. Tumor biopsy was declined by the patient’s family at initial consultation, and ventriculoperitoneal shunt placement was performed for hydrocephalus relief. One year after shunt surgery, craniospinal magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) documented substantial tumor progression, with corpus callosum infiltration and vertebral body signal abnormalities. Subsequent biopsy established the diagnosis of DLGNT with high-grade histological features, with a Ki-67 proliferation index of approximately 80%. DNA-methylation profiling assigned the tumor to the DLGNT-MC2 molecular subclass. Additional molecular findings included KIAA1549::BRAF gene fusion, 1p deletion, 1q gain, and 17q gain, with an intact 19q and no 1p/19q codeletion. Comparative Effectiveness of Hormonal Replacement Therapy Versus Integrative Non-Pharmacological Interventions in the Management of Menopausal Syndrome: A 24-Month Longitudinal Analysis
abstract: Background: Menopausal syndrome substantially diminishes health-related quality of life in midlife women globally. Hormone replacement therapy (HRT) has long been the standard of care for symptom management; however, long-term safety concerns—including elevated risks of breast malignancy, cardiovascular events, and venous thromboembolism—have prompted growing interest in holistic, non-pharmacological alternatives. Direct longitudinal comparative data across Southeast Asian populations remain scarce.Objective: To evaluate and contrast the efficacy of HRT versus a structured integrative intervention programme on symptom severity and quality of life over a 24-month follow-up period.Methods: This prospective, comparative longitudinal study enrolled 500 women aged 45–60 years presenting with moderate-to-severe menopausal syndrome across six Type B hospitals in Indonesia between January 2023 and December 2025. title: Organising under uncertainty: how startup investors construct value through sensemaking
abstract: Purpose This study examines how early-stage investors construct startup value under conditions of uncertainty. Drawing on a sensemaking perspective, it explores how investors interpret and integrate resource, leadership and contextual cues into coherent valuation judgements of venture potential. Design/methodology/approach Utilising a semi-structured interview approach, qualitative data were generated from seven startup investors in Malaysia, capturing experiential reflections and evaluative reasoning. An iterative interpretive analysis was conducted, with computational text analysis used for supplementary pattern-checking and visualisation. The themes are presented as interconnected dimensions of investors' valuation narratives. Findings The findings illustrate that valuation is constructed through a dynamic sensemaking process in which investors integrate five interrelated dimensions: operational discipline, customer and market focus, technological capability, product–market viability and team and leadership. Investors complement available financial information with interpretive narratives that connect internal capabilities, leadership and external conditions into coherent assessments of venture potential. title: Comparison of Financing Risk Indicators (NPF, CAR, FDR, and CKPN) as Outcome Signals of Risk Management Between Bank Syariah Indonesia and Bank Muamalat Indonesia in 2021-2024
abstract: Backgrounds: The growth of Islamic banking in Indonesia requires effective financing risk management to maintain financing quality and stability. Objectives: This study compares financing risk outcomes, used as signals of risk management performance, between Bank Syariah Indonesia (BSI) and Bank Muamalat Indonesia (BMI) in 2021–2024, based on the Non-Performing Financing (NPF), Capital Adequacy Ratio (CAR), Financing to Deposit Ratio (FDR) and Allowance for Impairment Losses (CKPN) ratios. Methodology: A quantitative descriptive-comparative approach was applied to secondary data from the banks’ annual reports and financial statements. Findings: BSI’s NPF fell from 2.93% to 1.90%, while BMI’s moved from 0.67% to 3.35%; both stayed below the 5% OJK limit. BSI’s FDR rose from 73.39% to 84.97%, whereas BMI’s remained between 38.33% and 47.14%. BMI had a higher CAR (23.76% to 32.70%) than BSI (20.29% to 22.09%). BSI’s financing risk outcomes were therefore more consistent. Conclusions: BSI’s financing risk outcomes were more consistent, but the ratios cannot confirm how risk management was implemented, and the findings are descriptive, covering two banks over four years without significance tests. title: Lessons From the Development and Assessment of a Community Participative Mental Health and Substance Policy Agenda in the Bronx, NY
abstract: ABSTRACT Context: In 2025, the Bronx, one of New York City (NYC)'s Boroughs, experienced the largest mental health and substance use disparity in NYC. Program: The goal of this practice report is to describe and evaluate the 2025 community-centered policy agenda proposed by a community collaborative named the # not62 campaign. The campaign has fostered constructive partnerships over 2 decades to improve the Bronx's residents' well-being. Implementation: Experts in health services, social work, and behavioral health used measures of legitimacy, feasibility, and government support to assess each policy agenda item, with the purpose of assisting in prioritizing the agenda items and supporting long-term community engagement. Policy Agenda items ranged from supporting more educational and training initiatives for Bronx Youth in the health care field to health education campaigns to reduce stigma and monetary incentives to ensure patient compliance with treatment. Evaluation: Results from the evaluation indicate that the initiatives with the greatest potential for success at the present time are those related to improving and expanding access to mental health services through existing NYC-funded programs and investing in higher education in academic programs related to the health service workforce. title: A UAV-based real-time detection system of flowering nectar plants using a lightweight deep learning model
abstract: Abstract Purpose Timely knowledge of flowering status and peak blooming periods in transferred areas is crucial for migratory beekeepers to make informed management decisions. Traditional manual field surveys are labor-intensive, time-consuming, and unsuitable for frequent monitoring. Current monitoring approaches using Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAV) rely on offline processing and require complex data analysis by specialists, making them impractical for beekeepers to implement in apicultural settings. Given the short time window for capturing flowering events, especially for species with short florescence periods, an accurate, fast monitoring solution is needed. We developed a UAV-based real-time investigation prototype leveraging edge-intelligence computing for nectar flower detection of Rhus chinensis in complex mountainous field conditions. Methods An improved, high-precision, and lightweight deep learning model based on YOLOv5s was proposed. The model was optimized with acceleration strategies during deployment to reduce inference time. Results Experimental results showed that the proposed model for flower detection achieved a mean Average Precision (mAP) of 89.5 and an inference speed of 56 frames per second (FPS). After applying acceleration strategies during model deployment on the edge computing device, the processing throughput reached 192 FPS with a mAP of 89.2; a 3.1…

title: Feeling the gap: cognitive-affective divergence in SME managers' Industry 4.0 and sustainability narratives
abstract: Purpose The study investigates how small- and medium-sized enterprise (SME) managers perceive and emotionally engage with environmental and social sustainability in the context of Industry 4.0 adoption. Using semi-structured interviews combined with multimodal sentiment analysis (speech prosody and emotional language), we aim to uncover implicit hesitancy, dissonance, and conceptual fragmentation that traditional methods fail to detect, thereby offering new insights for policy design and corporate social responsibility research in structurally disadvantaged regions. Design/methodology/approach The manuscript employs a mixed-methods design integrating semi-structured interviews with multimodal sentiment analysis. Twenty SMEs in Southern Italy, selected through structured sampling, participated in interviews exploring Industry 4.0 investments, environmental practices, and social sustainability. Recorded interviews underwent (1) thematic and content analysis for explicit responses, and (2) Hume AI-based prosody and emotional language analysis to detect implicit emotional engagement. This dual approach captures both declared positions and underlying affective reactions, enabling the identification of dissonance between cognitive awareness and emotional investment across environmental and social sustainability dimensions. Findings Environmental sustainability is widely recognized (9…

title: The application of Fourier series in forecasting construction project completion: a case study
abstract: Purpose Predicting project completion time is a crucial aspect of construction management for mitigating delays and supporting effective project control. However, existing forecasting methods still rely on extensive historical data and lack optimality in capturing the cyclical and non-linear patterns of project progress. Therefore, an accurate and adaptive prediction model is required to support decision-making under conditions of limited data. Accurate prediction of construction completion remains challenging due to the cyclicality and nonlinearity of progress data, especially when historical datasets are frequently scarce or unavailable. This study develops and validates Optimum Fourier Series–Polynomial Regression (Optimum.FSPR), a hybrid prediction model designed to provide reliable completion forecasts under conditions of data scarcity or high volatility. Design/methodology/approach The Optimum.FSPR technique integrates Fourier Series (FS) to model cyclic patterns with Polynomial Regression (PR) to capture nonlinear long-term trends. Model performance is evaluated using weekly project progress data, with Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average (ARIMA), eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) serving as benchmark models and Mean Absolute Error, Mean Absolute Percentage Error and Root Mean Squared Error as evaluation metrics. Additionally, 2,00…

title: Creating a palliative care skills training for health care professionals in allogeneic haematopoietic stem cell transplantation recipients: symptom management to end-of-life care
abstract: Abstract Background Allogeneic haematopoietic stem cell transplantation (allo-HSCT) presents a complex procedure with curative intent in haematological disorders, but is associated with high toxicity. Acute graft-versus-host disease (GvHD) and infections are early complications with high mortality, while fatigue and chronic GvHD contribute to significant late morbidity. Our preceding study revealed substantial palliative care needs, including patients’ uncertainty and existential fears, alongside Health Care Professionals (HCP) reported uncertainty and call for further training in addressing these challenges. Methods To address these needs, we developed and piloted a one-day training for HCPs, based on Brown’s Design Thinking principles, covering symptom management, end-of-life care, patients’ and family caregivers’ perceived life threat, and goals-of-care discussions. The training, led by a palliative care specialist, was held in three 6-8 h sessions with a total of 28 participants. It was delivered through various learning modules, interactive components, and group discussions. The programme was evaluated at three time points (pre-training, post-training, one-month follow-up) using self-confidence and practice transfer surveys, complemented by open feedback, and analysed descriptively. Results At one month post-training, participants reported increased self-confidence across …

title: Nonlinear Complexity Features Add Nothing beyond the Power Spectrum in Motor-Imagery BCI: A Surrogate-Controlled Reassessment
abstract: A significant amount of research in the field of Motor-Imagery (MI) brain–computer interfaces have shown that nonlinear and higher-order features-such as fractal dimensions, entropies, detrended fluctuation analysis, variational-mode complexity, Phase–Amplitude Coupling (PAC), and bispectrum/bicoherence-enhance the decoding of sensorimotor rhythms. However, the past studies have drawn their conclusions based on within-session cross-validation, per-subject tuning, fusion over a spatial–spectral baseline, and the absence of a surrogate control. The present study poses a more focused and testable question: do these features contain information that goes beyond that provided by the power spectrum when assessed fairly? Using the BCI Competition IV datasets 2a and 2b (18 subjects) under the official independent-session protocol, a single matched shrinkage-LDA classifier is applied to decode fifteen families of features, each family is subjected to an Iterative Amplitude-Adjusted Fourier Transform (IAAFT) surrogate test, and all the families of tests are corrected for multiple comparisons. The results are clear. Nonlinear-7 achieves 0.576 compared to 0.691 for plain band power on dataset 2a and 0.668 compared to 0.735 on dataset 2b; when compared to a filter-bank CSP and Riemannian ensemble, the additional value of the surrogate-corrected nonlinear and PAC candidates is only +0.0000 C…
venue: International Journal of Electrical and Electronics Engineering

title: Impact of maternal positioning on maternal comfort and fetal magnetic resonance imaging quality in a 75-cm bore system
abstract: Abstract Objectives To compare maternal comfort between the supine and left lateral positions during fetal MRI and to assess fetal brain image quality with a conventional body array coil vs. a super-flexible coil on a 75-cm bore system. Methods In this prospective study, 50 women with singleton pregnancies (gestational age 25–36 weeks) referred for suspected fetal brain abnormalities underwent MRI on a 75-cm bore 3.0-T system. Each was scanned in both the supine and left lateral positions (order randomized) and rated comfort for each on a five-point Likert scale. Fetal brain images were analysed as three within-subject conditions: supine with conventional coil, supine with super-flexible coil, and left lateral with super-flexible coil. Image quality was assessed subjectively and objectively using repeated-measures analyses. Results Comfort scores were higher in the left lateral position than supine (4.2±0.8 vs. 3.8±0.9; p=0.031), particularly in late pregnancy. Subjective image quality did not differ significantly among conditions. In the primary positional contrast (super-flexible coil held constant), the left lateral position yielded significantly higher SNR in 17 of the 20 brain regions and higher CNR in six of the eight regions (all q <0.05 after false-discovery-rate correction), with differences most pronounced in late pregnancy (15 of 28 metrics remained significant after…

title: Perceived benefits of sustainable fashion: the role of warm glow for other- and self-benefit framing on online consumption intentions
abstract: Purpose Despite the relevance of perceived self-benefits in fashion brand advertising, combining other- and self-benefits still frequently backfires. The current paper explores how sustainable online fashion branding influences consumption intentions when emphasizing other-benefits (sustainability) combined with different affective self-benefits, i.e. intrinsic benefit (good feeling of helping others) and image-benefit (social esteem) through intrinsic and extrinsic dimensions of warm glow feelings. The moderating role of consumers’ value orientations is additionally examined. Design/methodology/approach Findings of two multi-factorial experiments among a total of 482 participants reveal that by advertising different affective self-benefits alongside the other-benefit of sustainability, fashion brands may elicit both intrinsic and extrinsic warm glow. Findings Specifically, added image-benefits may help to elicit extrinsic warm glow, while added intrinsic benefits induce intrinsic and extrinsic warm glow. However, the positive effect of benefit framing is contingent on personal values, with enhancement and transcendence orientation explaining differences in consumer reactions. Originality/value This research offers novel insights into the interplay of other- and self-benefits in sustainable fashion marketing by addressing consumers' affective reactions. Moreover, the results co…

title: The power of perception: the impact of inclusivity policies and diversity climate on employee well-being
abstract: Purpose The purpose of the current study is to assess the relationship between employees' perceptions of inclusivity policies and employee well-being (i.e. life satisfaction, job satisfaction, turnover intentions and work–life balance). Moreover, we also examine diversity climate as a potential mediator of this relationship. Design/methodology/approach Drawing on the model of inclusive organizations and the signaling theory, we hypothesized that positive perceptions of inclusivity policies would relate to better employee well-being through a more favorable perception of diversity climate. The sample consisted of 361 faculty and staff from a large Southeastern university. A single-level path-analytic mediation model was used to test hypothesized relationships due to the negligible between-college variance. Findings The results revealed that positive perceptions of inclusivity policies were associated with a more positive diversity climate which, in turn, enhanced certain well-being outcomes – life satisfaction, job satisfaction, turnover intentions and work–life balance. Further, diversity climate mediated the relationship between employees' perceptions of inclusivity policies and employee well-being. Our results highlight the importance of not only implementing inclusive policies but, also ensuring that employees perceive them as fair and effective. Originality/value The curren…

Land acquisition reform and schedule performance of highway projects: evidence from India's RFCTLARR Act
abstract: Purpose Land acquisition is widely recognised as one of the most delay-prone activities in infrastructure project delivery. This study empirically evaluates whether transparent and fair land acquisition reforms improve schedule performance of publicly procured infrastructure projects, focusing on India's Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement (RFCTLARR) Act. Design/methodology/approach The analysis is based on a dataset of 481 completed highway projects implemented between 2000 and 2019, covering both pre- and post-reform periods. Mean comparison analysis, ordinary least squares (OLS) and seemingly unrelated regression (SUR) models were employed to examine the association between the reform and the three indicators of schedule performance: estimated unit time, actual unit time and time overruns, while controlling for project-specific, governance and state-level factors. Findings The results consistently show that projects implemented after the RFCTLARR Act had lower estimated and actual unit times and significantly lower time overruns. These findings suggest that enhanced procedural fairness, through improved compensation mechanisms, mandatory social impact assessments and structured rehabilitation and resettlement measures, is associated with reduced uncertainty, disputes and execution risk, thereby improving project sc…

title: Pengaruh Beban Perkuliahan dan Fleksibilitas Jam Kerja terhadap Produktivitas Kerja Mahasiswa Pekerja di Universitas Pamulang
abstract: This research investigates how academic workload and working-hour flexibility relate to the work productivity of employed students at Pamulang University. A quantitative associative method was applied, involving 35 respondents selected through purposive sampling. Primary data were obtained through questionnaires using a five-point Likert scale and processed through multiple linear regression analysis, classical assumption testing, partial and simultaneous hypothesis testing, and the coefficient of determination. The findings reveal that academic workload has a negative relationship with work productivity, although the effect is statistically insignificant, as indicated by a significance level of 0.446. Meanwhile, working-hour flexibility demonstrates a positive relationship but does not have a significant effect, with a significance value of 0.097. The simultaneous test also indicates an insignificant effect of both independent variables, with a significance value of 0.236. Furthermore, the R² value of 0.086 indicates that the research variables account for 8.6% of the variation in work productivity, while the remaining proportion is associated with other factors beyond the research model.

title: A dual artificial neural network core PRNG on FPGA driven by a novel 4D hyperchaotic system with hidden attractor
Food insecurity as a source of supply chain risk? An alternate perspective on a vicious cycle
abstract: Purpose The objective of this paper is to provide a perspective on food insecurity as an antecedent and enabling condition of supply chain risk. The goal is to scope a research landscape for evaluating this relationship and to encourage future research in this underexplored direction. Design/methodology/approach Building on extant literature on food security and supply chain risk management, we conceptualize food insecurity as a social condition that generates or intensifies existing supply chain risks. Findings We provide a framework and propositions to explore the mechanisms through which food insecurity may become operationally consequential across the micro-meso-macro levels. We also discuss different interventions for mitigation. Practical implications Using real-world examples, we illustrate how the impact of food insecurity-related disturbances may affect supply chain performance. We discuss reactive, active, and proactive interventions involving business decision-making and policymaking. Originality/value We explore an underexplored pathway of how food insecurity affects supply chain performance. We position food insecurity not only as an outcome but as an antecedent of supply chain risk.
venue: International Journal of Physical Distribution & Logistics Management

title: Sustainability disclosure: transparency or smoke and mirrors?
abstract: Purpose This study aims at advancing the theory of managerial intent and strategic choice with regards to disclosure transparency that companies adopt in sustainability reporting under mandatory disclosure regulations. It investigates whether, and how, corporate performance and governance mechanisms influence the transparency of sustainability reports. Design/methodology/approach The study provides an analysis of sustainability reports published by Italian listed companies, following the implementation of the European Union (EU) Directive 2014/95/EU on sustainability disclosure. Both textual and quantitative analysis are conducted to classify disclosure strategies and to investigate the relationship between transparency levels, corporate performance indicators, and governance structures. Findings The results of this study indicate that firms operating within mandatory disclosure settings do not consistently align the tone of their reporting with their underlying performance and, thus, tone may be used strategically, potentially to obscure unfavourable performance or to manage stakeholder perceptions. Furthermore, the analysis highlights substantial deficiencies in the readability of corporate disclosures. Originality/value This study advances knowledge on the categorization of transparency disclosure strategies. It enhances understanding of the importance of linguistic choices …

title: Social fashion identity: definition, scale development and empirical validation
abstract: Purpose This study contributes to the conceptualization and measurement of how consumers use fashion to express multiple social identities. It aims to conceptualize social fashion identity, develop and validate its measurement scale and establish its dimensionality, reliability, convergent, discriminant and nomological validity. Design/methodology/approach Across two studies, social fashion identity is conceptualized, and a scale was developed and validated in a step-by-step process following Churchill (1979) and DeVellis (1991) procedures. Study 1 focused on construct conceptualization, item generation and scale validation, whereas Study 2 examined the nomological validity. Findings This paper validated the social fashion identity scale as a reliable two-dimensional construct consisting of fashion identity expression and fashion-based group belongingness. Social fashion identity was distinct from fashion consciousness and product involvement, positively associated with fashion consciousness, and positively related to consumers' willingness to pay more for fashion items. Practical implications The social fashion identity scale offers fashion companies a tool to segment their clients, enabling more personalized customer experiences within the fashion market. Furthermore, the findings can contribute to the effectiveness of fashion brands' product development, marketing and pricin…

title: Internal audit quality and earnings management: the roles of competence, independence, and work performance
abstract: Purpose This study examines whether internal audit quality (IAQ) is associated with lower income-increasing discretionary accruals and improved financial reporting quality (FRQ) in an emerging market with uneven regulatory enforcement. Design/methodology/approach Survey-based measures of internal audit (IA) competence, independence and work performance are combined with archival data from non-financial firms listed on the Dhaka Stock Exchange. FRQ is proxied by signed discretionary accruals from the performance-adjusted modified Jones model (Kothari et al., 2005), and interaction models examine variation across reporting-pressure and governance conditions. Given the cross-sectional design, the findings are associational rather than causal. Findings Higher IAQ is associated with lower income-increasing discretionary accruals. Competence is the attribute primarily associated with this relationship, whereas independence and work performance show no separate association once modelled jointly. The association is stronger among loss-making firms but weaker where audit committee independence is high, a pattern consistent with substitution between IA and audit-committee monitoring, though the interaction is only marginally significant. Evidence on audit committee financial expertise is weaker and is treated as suggestive. Practical implications In emerging markets, the findings highlig…

title: Three-dimensional computational evaluation of water-to-air mass stopping power ratio for therapeutic helium-, carbon-, oxygen-, and neon-ion beams and its application to patient-specific quality assurance
abstract: Abstract Objective. Current dosimetry protocols recommend a constant water-to-air mass stopping power ratio, s w,air , of 1.126 with an uncertainty of ±1.5% for light ions, irrespective of ion species and energy. This study aims to develop a computational framework to calculate three-dimensional s w,air distributions of helium-, carbon-, oxygen-, and neon-ion beams for patient specific quality assurance (PSQA), and to systematically investigate spatial variations in s w,air under clinically relevant conditions. Approach. A computational framework was developed to calculate three-dimensional s w,air distributions based on the Bragg-Gray approximation, together with three-dimensional dose distributions for treatment planning. The framework was validated against published datasets for a mono-energetic carbon-ion beam. Treatment plans were generated using helium-, carbon-, oxygen-, and neon-ion beams for rectangular targets with varying spread-out Bragg peak (SOBP) widths and depths, as well as for bone and soft tissue, head and neck, and ocular cases. The corresponding s w,air distributions were calculated in a water phantom and compared with the recommended value of 1.126. Main Results. The mean s w,air within the target increased for shallower targets with narrower SOBP widths. For all ion species, s w,air increased toward the distal end of the SOBP, with larger variations obser…

title: Bridging marine ESG practices and smart technologies: toward sustainable and accessible travel experiences
abstract: Purpose This study investigates how marine environmental, social, and governance (ESG) practices and smart tourism technologies (STTs) jointly shape tourists’ perceptions, attitudes, and behavioral intentions in accessible tourism. Design/methodology/approach A two-study structural equation modeling approach was adopted. Study 1 analyzed 689 valid responses from an ocean leisure sample to examine the effects of ESG practices on travel attitudes through perceptions of a friendly environment and destination image. Study 2 analyzed 690 valid responses from a tourism sample to investigate the mediating role of STTs in the relationship between travel attitudes and travel intentions, as well as the moderating role of perceived risk. Findings ESG practices positively influence travel attitudes through perceptions of a friendly environment and destination image. Travel intention strengthens the relationships between ESG practices and perceptions of a friendly environment and between perceptions of a friendly environment and travel attitudes. STTs positively mediate the relationship between travel attitudes and travel intentions. Furthermore, perceived risk strengthens the positive relationship between travel attitudes and STTs but weakens the relationship between STTs and travel intentions. Originality/value By integrating the Stimulus–Organism–Response framework with the Theory of Pla…

title: Uncertainty-aware possibilistic load forecasting for smart grid energy conservation
abstract: Overview efficient electricity usage management in the presence of deep uncertainty is critical for modern power systems with a high renewable share. We present a fuzzy interval regression framework that represents load observations as triangular fuzzy numbers and estimates α-cut interval forecasts without requiring a full probability distribution. The original eight-hour example is retained only as a transparent calculation: at α = 0.5, the corrected two-weight fit gives an in-sample empirical coverage of 83.3% and a mean interval width of 2.164 MW; these values are descriptive and are neither confidence levels nor predictive validation. To provide out-of-sample evidence, the method was additionally evaluated on the public Taylor half-hourly electricity-demand series for England and Wales (4,032 observations), using the first 3,360 points for estimation and the final 672 points for testing. For the one-step model, the mean absolute error (MAE) was 429.1 MW, the root mean square error (RMSE) was 574.5 MW, and the mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) was 1.45%. The residual-calibrated, time-of-day triangular spreads had an empirical coverage of 91.7% at α = 0.5 and a mean interval width of 1,804.4 MW. An example of demand-response data is given in the form of a 1 MW effort to reduce base load at four defined hours. Assuming a marginal rate of 0.7 tCO₂/MWh, this gross avoided em…

title: Artificial Intelligence (AI) Driven Forecasting of Value Added Tax: A Case Study of the Tanzania Revenue Authority
abstract: This study set out to assess the applicability of Artificial Intelligence (AI) models in forecasting Value Added Tax revenue, with a focus on the Tanzania Revenue Authority. In assessing the applicability, the historical trends and performance of VAT collection were used to develop AI models to forecast monthly VAT revenue, thereafter providing recommendations for improving VAT forecasting through the adoption of AI technologies. The study utilised time series for the period of January 2021 to December 2024, constructing a dataset covering 48 months. The variables under the data set are: VAT revenue statistics, which provide detailed transactional records of VAT collections across three main categories: imports, purchases, and sales. The granular daily entries are aggregated to obtain monthly totals, creating a coherent time series that is suitable for statistical modelling and forecasting purposes. Other variables include the Consumer Price Index (CPI), GDP and inflation rate. Five forecasting models, SARIMAX, Elastic-Net, XGBoost, CNN-LSTM, and SNaive, were basically applied in predicting VAT revenue. All models under testing performed at different levels, with XGBoost performing better with the lowest MAE TZS 150 billion, RMSE TZS 205 billion and MAPE 275%, demonstrating its effectiveness in capturing non-linear patterns and handling outliers in VAT revenue data. The Elastic…

title: An Integrated Explainable Machine Learning Framework for Cell-to-Pack Imbalance Prediction in Electric Vehicle Battery Systems
abstract: This study presents a machine learning framework for predicting cell-to-pack imbalance in electric vehicle batteries. A set of battery attributes that affect battery performance, including State of Charge (SOC), State of Health (SOH), temperature (including ambient temperature and humidity), and cabin temperature, were used to make this prediction. The collected battery data were pre-processed to improve prediction performance. Three preprocessing methods were used: (i) Variational Mode Decomposition (VMD); (ii) deep denoising autoencoders, and (iii) feature selection using minimum Redundancy Maximum Relevance (mRMR) mutual information. This preprocessing step removes noise from the dataset and identifies useful information for prediction. Cell-to-pack imbalance prediction was performed using three interpretable machine learning models: (i) an Explainable Boosting Machine (EBM); (ii) fuzzy regression; and (iii) RuleFit. These models provide transparent predictions and help in understanding the factors responsible for battery imbalance. Models were evaluated on an independent 20-sample test set held out from the 100-record dataset. Among the three interpretable models, Fuzzy Regression achieved the strongest predictive performance (R² = 0.998), followed by RuleFit (R² = 0.976), while EBM achieved a lower R² of 0.201 on this independent test set despite providing detailed feature…

title: Theoretical Prediction of Tensile Strength Property of Fiber Metal Laminates
abstract: This study estimates the theoretical tensile strength properties of Carbon Fiber Reinforced Aluminium Laminates (CARALL) fiber-metal laminates (FMLs) for two stacking configurations like Type 1 (aluminum outermost: A|C|A|C|A) and Type 2 (carbon-fiber outermost: C|A|C|A|C) that are taken from the experimental data in literature. For achieving this purpose, two complementary approaches Metal Volume Fraction (MVF) and Classical Laminate Theory (CLT) are adopted. Tsai-Hill / von Mises Criteria are applied for first ply failure and progressive failure. The results indicated that for Type 2, CLT method predicts 728 MPa tensile strength, which is in good agreement with experimental value — an under-prediction of only 6%. The MVF Rule of Mixtures provides a reliable upper bound: +7% for Type 2 and +22% for Type 1 composite samples, respectively. In addition, for CLT progressive failure analysis, 90° CF ply transverse cracking (matrix failure) — FPF at ~463-472 MPa for both types while Aluminum layer yielding/failure — occurs after FPF due to load redistribution, but 0° CF fibre fracture — ultimate failure event, dominant load-bearing mechanism.

title: Machine learning-based prediction of overall survival after lung SBRT using clinical, dosimetric, and radiomics features: a multicenter study
The effects of incomplete vibrational accommodation and finite-rate surface catalysis on peak heat flux prediction of hypersonic compression corner
abstract: Abstract In high-enthalpy shock tunnels, gas molecules are excited to higher vibrational and chemical energy states. However, rapid expansion and acceleration through the nozzle leave insufficient time for vibrational deexcitation and recombination, leading to significant gas–surface interaction effects on wall heat transfer. This research utilizes computational fluid dynamics (CFD) to study the influence of vibrational accommodation and finite-rate catalysis on flow field structure and peak heat flux in hypersonic compression corner flows under thermochemical nonequilibrium free-stream conditions, characterized by low-to-medium Reynolds numbers and high Mach numbers. The results indicate that vibrational accommodation and finite-rate catalysis have a negligible influence on the structure of the flow separation bubble. However, both significantly affect the peak heat fluxes, which can be decomposed into three components: translational-rotational heat flux, vibrational heat flux, and catalytic heat flux. More importantly, a validated theoretical method is proposed to predict the peak heat flux by accounting for the effects of incomplete vibrational accommodation and finite-rate catalysis. Furthermore, the proposed theoretical framework suggests an equivalence relation between the vibrational accommodation coefficient and the catalytic coefficient, indicating a quantitative inter…

title: A cascade deep learning network for simultaneous prediction of dose and linear energy transfer in proton therapy of prostate cancer
abstract: Abstract Objective. Prediction of dose-averaged linear energy transfer (LETd) may facilitate LET-aware evaluation of proton therapy plans. This study developed a cascade deep learning framework for simultaneous three-dimensional prediction of dose and LETd distributions for conventional dose-based optimization (DoseOpt) and LETd-incorporated optimization (LETOpt) in prostate intensity-modulated proton therapy. Approach. A total of 150 patients with prostate cancer were included, each with DoseOpt and LETOpt plans. Planning CT images and anatomical structure masks were used as inputs. The cascade network transferred an intermediate latent representation from the dose prediction pathway to the LETd prediction pathway. Stepwise, multitask, and anatomy-only LETd (only-LET) networks served as comparators. Model performance was evaluated using five-fold cross-validation. Main results. All dose-predicting models showed high spatial agreement, with cascade Dice similarity coefficients of approximately 0.93, 0.96, and 0.95 for the 50%, 75%, and 95% prescription isodose volumes. No significant differences in structure-specific dose errors remained after false discovery rate correction. The cascade model achieved the lowest global LETd mean absolute error (MAE) for DoseOpt and LETOpt, 0.108 ± 0.025 and 0.111 ± 0.025 keV μ m −1 , respectively, significantly lower than those of the multitas…

title: Spatiotemporal patterns and machine-learning prediction of malaria risk across Africa, 2000–2024
Diagnostic prediction models for metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease and related fatty-liver phenotypes among patients with type 2 diabetes: a systematic review
abstract: Objective To systematically summarise and critically appraise multivariable diagnostic prediction models for MAFLD and related fatty-liver phenotypes in adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). Methods Eight databases (four international and four Chinese) were searched from inception to May 2026. Two reviewers independently screened studies and extracted data using the CHARMS framework. Risk of bias and applicability were assessed with PROBAST. Because of substantial clinical and methodological heterogeneity, results were synthesised descriptively rather than pooled. Results Eighteen diagnostic studies (study-level: 7 MAFLD, 8 NAFLD, and 3 MASLD) reporting 52 distinct diagnostic model specifications were included. No eligible prognostic studies or prognostic models were identified. Studies on NAFLD and MASLD are regarded as indirect supporting evidence; their performance evaluations neither were combined nor directly compared with the MAFLD model. Feng Leyi et al. (2024) used samples recruited from the same hospital at different times, but the validation period came before the development period, thus the independence of the participants could not be confirmed. It was not classified as an independent external validation. The remaining studies reported significant development-set performance or internal validation; No study provided clear independent external validation. BMI…

title: Melting temperature prediction method for mold flux based on transfer learning algorithm
abstract: Abstract To establish an accurate predictive model for the single hot thermocouple technique (SHTT)-measured melting temperature, a transfer learning strategy was introduced. The proposed model learns general relationships between mold flux composition and melting behavior on the large hemisphere-method dataset in the pre-training process and retains them in the feature-extraction layers. Fine-tuning the output layer with limited SHTT data then adapts the model to SHTT measurements, alleviating the accuracy bottleneck associated with direct training on a small SHTT dataset. The results show that the coefficient of determination ( R 2 ) and mean squared error (MSE) of the pre-trained model (Hemi_MLP) on the test set are 0.87 and 1,268.65, respectively. It provides effective general knowledge of mold flux melting behavior for the subsequent fine-tuning task. The fine-tuned model (SHTT_MLP) achieves 0.99 R 2 and 187.6 MSE on the SHTT test set, which has the best performance among the comparison models. The Shapley Additive Explanations analysis shows that the determination of the SHTT_MLP for the influence of each component on the melting temperature of mold flux is consistent with prior knowledge. Additionally, the SHTT_MLP primarily completes the fine-tuning process by strengthening its sensitivity to CaO/SiO 2 and CaO/Al 2 O 3 .

title: Development and external validation of a pre-drainage prediction model for moderate-to-severe gallstone-related acute cholangitis
abstract: Abstract Background Acute cholangitis may rapidly progress to sepsis and organ dysfunction, making early severity assessment essential. However, few practical tools are currently available based on routine pre-drainage data. This study aimed to develop and externally validate a pre-drainage model for identifying moderate-to-severe gallstone-related acute cholangitis. Methods This two-center retrospective study included 159 patients in the training cohort and 119 in the external validation cohort. Tokyo Guidelines 2018 Grades II–III defined moderate-to-severe disease. Candidate variables measured within 24 h of admission and before drainage were selected using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression and refitted using multivariable logistic regression. Performance was assessed by bootstrap resampling and external validation. Results The four-predictor model included the direct-to-total bilirubin ratio, ln-transformed systemic inflammatory response index, red cell distribution width, and serum calcium. Apparent and optimism-corrected areas under the curve were 0.823 and 0.777, respectively. The external area under the curve was 0.871 (95% confidence interval, 0.804–0.937), but the model overestimated absolute risk (calibration intercept, − 0.828). Exploratory intercept-only recalibration reduced the Brier score from 0.158 to 0.137. Decision curve analysis sugge…

title: Coupled Abrasive and Fatigue Wear Modeling of Blanking Punches for Prediction of Wear Using Linear and Nonlinear Wear Models
abstract: Repeated blanking operations cause progressive degradation of punch edges, leading to dimensional inaccuracies, burr formation, and premature tool failure. This study proposes a coupled abrasive–fatigue wear modeling framework for estimating the lifetime of punches under long-term repeated blanking process. Abrasive wear was modeled using a modified Archard wear formulation, whereas fatigue-induced wear was represented using an extended Lemaitre damage model capable of capturing cyclic damage accumulation within the elastic regime. An adaptive finite element framework incorporating wear-driven geometry updating and element deletion techniques was developed to simulate progressive punch edge degradation during repeated blanking operations. The proposed methodology was applied to an AISI D2 punch and AISI 430 sheet metal under long-term cyclic blanking conditions. The results of finite element analysis demonstrated that the conventional linear wear model predicted gradual wear evolution, whereas the coupled nonlinear wear model effectively captured accelerated wear propagation after approximately 300,000 blanking cycles due to fatigue-induced material detachment. The predicted wear depth evolution showed good agreement with the experimental results, with a maximum relative error below 7%. In addition, the proposed wear update method using accumulated cycles enabled faster wear pr…

title: An edge-conditioned convolution model for carbon flow rate prediction under source-load uncertainty
abstract: Introduction The realization of China’s dual-carbon goals relies on accurate and fine-grained carbon emission modeling of the new-type power systems. Conventional carbon calculation methods are designed for traditional power systems and rely on deterministic power flow calculations. This makes it difficult to capture the impacts of source–load uncertainty on the carbon flow rate under high renewable penetration. Methods This paper proposes a carbon flow rate prediction model based on Edge Conditioned Convolution (ECC) to account for source–load uncertainty. First, a carbon flow rate calculation framework is established by incorporating the full lifecycle carbon emissions of renewable generators and a network loss allocation mechanism. This mechanism combines upstream and downstream power flow tracing to allocate network losses between the generation and consumption sides using an allocation coefficient. Second, an ECC-based carbon flow rate prediction model is developed to incorporate branch attributes into information aggregation through edge-conditioned convolution weights. A physics-informed loss function is adopted to encourage the conservation of the carbon flow rate. Furthermore, by using Sobol sequences and Inverse Transform Sampling (ITS) algorithms to generate multi-scenario data sets, the application scenarios of the prediction model are extended to power systems with…

abstract: Purpose The prime objective of this study is to examine the impact of different service quality dimensions, namely, reliability, tangibility and physical environment, on halal purchase intention among the customers of fast-moving consumer goods (FMCG). This study also examines the mediating effect of customer satisfaction along with the moderating impact of word of mouth on the path of customer satisfaction and purchase intention. Design/methodology/approach The data were obtained through FMCG-purposive sampling by distributing questionnaires to FMCG customers. A total of 647 questionnaires were surveyed, and the questionnaires were self-administered. Of these, 347 were valid and considered for analysis using variance-based structural equation modeling (PLS) to test the hypothesis. Findings The study’s results reflected that service quality is important in creating customer satisfaction. In the same way, the physical environment where customers are provided with services and service quality reliability are also key to generating customer satisfaction. In terms of the indirect results, Service quality reliability, physical environment and service quality tangibility are positively associated with halal purchase intention through the mediation of customer satisfaction.
