title: Detection of candidate acoustic biomarkers for Parkinson's disease using an explainable machine learning composite spectrogram approach
abstract: Introduction Speech abnormalities are common in Parkinson's disease (PD), and machine learning (ML) offers a potential framework for objective and scalable speech-based diagnostics. This study introduces an explainable ML pipeline that leverages a novel vowel articulation-based composite input to detect PD and identify candidate phoneme-level biomarkers. Methods Two publicly available datasets of PD speech recordings were analyzed. Sustained vowel articulations were converted into log-mel spectrograms either individually or as a composite image by vertically concatenating a set of vowels per subject. Processed spectrograms were used to train ML models, with performance assessed using repeated random subsampling with five participant-level 80:20 splits and bootstrapped area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC). A support vector machine, logistic regression, and random forest trained on conventional acoustic features served as baselines. Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM) was applied to quantify model attention across vowel regions. Results A total of 150 participants (49.3% PD) were included. After adjustment for age, sex, and dataset, cepstral peak prominence and harmonics-to-noise ratio were significantly higher in PD, particularly for the vowel /u/. The ML model achieved an average AUROC of 0.895 using individual vowels and 0.890 using …

title: Sequential deep embedded clustering with dynamic autoencoder
Innovative Process for Cellulose Acetate Recovery from Cigarette Butts by Means of Natural Deep Eutectic Solvents
abstract: Abstract This work investigated a waste product of environmental concern, cigarette butts, as a potential source of cellulose acetate. It is estimated that there are 967 million smokers worldwide who produce approximately 6 trillion cigarette butts each year, causing a direct environmental impact. The proposed approach aimed to transform this polluting waste into a high-value material, recovering pure cellulose acetate from cigarette butts for reuse in a variety of applications. Developing an effective and environmentally friendly recovery method was very challenging. This was achieved by using different types of natural deep eutectic solvents (DES), which are a class of innovative solvents that combine the properties of ionic liquids and organic solvents. They are known for their sustainability and versatility. The efficiency of the various DES employed was evaluated using thermogravimetric analysis, nuclear magnetic resonance, inductively coupled plasma optical emission spectroscopy, scanning electron microscopy and Fourier-transform infrared analysis. Based on the results obtained, the most effective DES was identified as that consisting of choline chloride and levulinic acid, which allows clean cellulose acetate to be recovered with a yield of up to 93%.

title: The effect of climate policy uncertainty and geopolitical risks on foreign tourism activities in India
abstract: Purpose While existing literature emphasises economic factors to examine tourism demand, growing uncertainties in recent years have shaped international tourism. Hence, this study examines how climate policy uncertainty (CPU) and geopolitical risks (GPR) affect India's inbound tourism demand. Design/methodology/approach We use foreign exchange earnings from tourism (FEET) and foreign tourist arrivals (FTA) to study India's tourism demand from abroad over the period 2003M1 to 2019M12. We employ a nonlinear autoregressive distributed lag model to identify asymmetric short- and long-run effects and a time-varying Granger causality analysis to capture evolving causal dynamics. Findings The empirical results reveal significant nonlinear and state-dependent dynamics. CPU exerts a persistent negative effect on tourism demand, suggesting regulatory risk surrounding climate-related policies and weakening destination attractiveness. However, GPR exhibits short-lived, episodic effects, altering perceived safety during global and regional crises. The findings suggest that India's tourism sector is more sensitive to CPU than to GPR in the long run, because CPU alters the anticipated cost of future travel and tourism investment. Our results can be understood through the combined lenses of real options, expectations and risk perception theory. Research limitations/implications The findings in…

title: Optimization of post‑stroke rehabilitation: data from own clinical study of the possibilities of impact on indicators of the International Classification of Functioning
abstract: Aim: Improving the effectiveness of therapeutic and rehabilitation measures in patients during the late recovery period and with the consequences of a cerebral infarction. Methods: The results of treatment of 250 patients who suffered an ischemic stroke with a prescription period of at least 6 months and no more than 1 year (late recovery period) were analyzed. The average age of 136 women and 114 men was 63.1 years (from 28 to 74 years). The patients were divided into two 1:1 groups: the main group (received, along with basic therapy and rehabilitation, Mexidol 500 mg (10 ml) parenterally for 14 days, followed by Mexidol FORTE 250 250 mg 3 times a day orally for 2 months) and the comparison group (only basic therapy and rehabilitation). The analysis of the dynamics of the state of functions, activity, and participation was determined according to a specific set of domains in the International Classification of Functioning (ICF) system. Results: In the main group of patients, after completing therapy, a statistically significantly larger number of patients exhibited no or mild impairments, and a statistically significantly smaller number of patients had severe and absolute impairments, compared to the comparison group, across most of the analyzed domains of function, task performance, and social engagement. Conclusions: The study has demonstrated the contribution of sequential …

title: Trade-offs/synergies and their optimization simulation of ecosystem services in mountain-urban complex watersheds from cluster perspective: a case study of the Tuojiang River Basin
Digital twin driven GAT and PPO for semantic fidelity preserving robotic embroidery path optimization of Mosuo costume patterns
abstract: Abstract In electrical automation systems, when using robots to process complex vector patterns, a short tool path may interrupt critical contours or compromise structural continuity, while unsuitable motion speeds can increase tracking error and process risk. Therefore, the processing sequence and robot speed need to be optimize d without violating the structural requirements of the pattern. DT-GAT-PPO is a digital twin-based framework that integrates a Graph Attention Network (GAT) with Proximal Policy optimization(PPO). Processing points and their contour connections, feasible transitions, and expert-defined structural relationships are presented in a semantic attributed graph. A multi-head GAT encodes the graph along with the current process state, and a hybrid-action PPO policy selects the next processing node and its corresponding motion velocity. Deposition stability and process window optimization of polycaprolactone in robotic pellet-based additive manufacturing
abstract: Purpose Polymer pellet-based additive manufacturing (PBAM) enables large-scale, high deposition-rate; however, geometric deposition stability and comprehensive manufacturing process windows for low-viscosity, semi-crystalline polymers remain poorly understood. This study aims to investigate and model geometric deposition stability in polycaprolactone (PCL) under high deposition-rate conditions. Design/methodology/approach A structured design of experiments was conducted to evaluate the effects of screw speed, robot travel speed and nominal layer height. Multivariate regression models were developed to quantify parameter interactions and predict key deposition metrics, including layer height deviation (Δzdiff), mean layer height (hzmean) and mean width (wdtmean). Findings The regression models showed high explanatory capability (R2 = 0.959–0.961) and statistically significant overall effects (p < 0.05). Distinct deposition regimes − under-extrusion, geometrically stable deposition and over-extrusion − were identified from the geometric responses and interpreted in terms of material throughput and robotic kinematic. Research limitations/implications This study is limited to the investigated PCL material, robotic PBAM configuration and parameter ranges, without direct rheological characterization, independent dimensional validation, mechanical testing or clinical evaluation. title: Optimization of PEG precipitation for macroprolactinemia screening
abstract: Abstract Objectives To determine whether 20 % or 25 % polyethylene glycol 6000 (PEG) is more suitable for macroprolactinemia screening and to investigate methodological factors affecting PEG precipitation. Methods Serum samples from five individuals with macroprolactinemia and five hyperprolactinemic controls were analyzed. Gel filtration chromatography quantified the precipitation of individual prolactin (PRL) molecular forms. Nonspecific monomeric PRL precipitation was assessed using an artificial serum matrix. Incubation time, temperature, pH, and PEG solvent were also investigated. Results In the artificial serum matrix, monomeric PRL precipitation was significantly lower with 20 % than with 25 % PEG (29.3 ± 5.0 % vs. 39.2 ± 6.2 %; p=0.0053). In macroprolactinemic sera, both PEG concentrations precipitated more than 90 % of macroPRL and big PRL, with no significant differences between the two concentrations. However, monomeric PRL precipitation was significantly lower with 20 % than with 25 % PEG (28.5 ± 9.4 % vs. 39.8 ± 11.0 %; p=0.0033). Despite this difference, the proportions of monomeric PRL in the PEG precipitates differed by only 3.0 percentage points. Incubation time and temperature had limited effects on the signal-to-noise ratio. Increasing pH reduced precipitation rates without substantially altering this ratio. A 0.1 mol/L phosphate buffer at pH 7.0 maintained h…

title: Management Control Optimization under Managerial Overconfidence: A Principal–Agent Model of Business Development Decisions
abstract: Business development decisions require resource commitments under uncertain opportunity quality, giving managerial judgment a central role in investment evaluation. This study develops an agency model to examine how managerial overconfidence shapes optimal incentive intensity and monitoring intensity. A behavioral parameter captures the manager's overestimation of opportunity value, while the board anticipates the investment response and selects both control instruments. Equilibrium analysis examines how biased beliefs, environmental uncertainty, effort costs, and monitoring costs influence control choices. Overconfidence raises perceived investment returns and increases managerial effort for given control choices. Comparative statics suggest that stronger bias reduces optimal incentive intensity and increases optimal monitoring intensity. Inflated expectations provide investment motivation and reduce the need for financial rewards. Monitoring reduces evaluation error losses outside the compensation measure. Numerical illustrations show lower optimal incentive shares and higher monitoring intensity as overconfidence increases. These findings connect managerial cognition with endogenous control design and clarify how behavioral and informational conditions shape business development decisions. The model distinguishes the motivational effects of overconfidence from evaluation los…

An inexact LPA for DC composite optimization and application to matrix completion with outliers
abstract: Abstract This paper concerns a class of DC composite optimization problems which, as an extension of convex composite optimization problems and DC programs with nonsmooth components, often arises in robust factorization models of low-rank matrix recovery. For this class of nonconvex and nonsmooth problems, we propose an inexact linearized proximal algorithm (iLPA) by computing at each step an inexact minimizer of a strongly convex majorization constructed with a partial linearization of their objective functions at the current iterate. We establish the full convergence of the generated iterate sequence under the Kurdyka–Łojasiewicz (KL) property of a potential function, and employ the composite structure to provide a verifiable condition for the potential function to satisfy the KL property of exponent $1/2$ at the limit point, so for the iterate sequence to have a local R-linear convergence rate. This condition is weaker than the one provided in Li & Pong (2018, Calculus of the exponent of Kurdyka–Łojasiewicz inequality and its applications to linear convergence of first-order methods. Found. Comput. Math., 18, 1199–1232, Theorem 3.2) for identifying the KL property of exponent $p\in [0,1)$ for a general composite function. title: Cervical Spondylosis (Waja ul Unuq): An Integrative Review of Unani and Modern Concepts
abstract: Cervical spondylosis is a chronic degenerative disorder of the cervical spine and an important cause of neck pain, disability, radiculopathy, and myelopathy. It involves progressive changes in intervertebral discs, vertebral bodies, facet and uncovertebral joints, ligaments, and adjacent soft tissues. Modern medicine considers age-related degeneration, biomechanical stress, occupational factors, trauma, posture, smoking, metabolic factors, and genetic predisposition among important contributors. In Unani medicine, the condition is understood within the broader framework of Waja ul Mafasil and, when involving the cervical region, is described as Waja ul Unuq. Classical explanations emphasize Su-e-Mizaj, accumulation of Mawad-e-Fasida, and predominance of Balgham. This review summarizes the historical background, Unani concept and pathogenesis, modern etiopathogenesis, clinical manifestations, diagnosis, and therapeutic approaches. It also compares the two perspectives and identifies areas where preventive, rehabilitative, and regimenal approaches may complement contemporary care. An integrative understanding may support patient-centred management while encouraging scientific evaluation of traditional interventions.

title: Becoming: movimentos da criação de uma proposta rizomática transdisciplinar para o ensino de inglês no Ensino Médio Integrado
abstract: Este trabalho se situa no campo da Linguística Aplicada e traz problematizações de uma pesquisa pós-doutoral em andamento, a qual investiga o processo de criação de uma proposta didática de ensino de inglês com conexões rizomáticas, voltada para o Ensino Médio Integrado. O estudo visa compreender possíveis reconfigurações epistemológicas, curriculares, subjetivas, e o surgimento de agenciamentos durante o percurso do planejamento. Os participantes são duas professoras de inglês e dois professores de informática de diferentes campi do Instituto Federal do Paraná (IFPR). De caráter transdisciplinar, a proposta didática considera o uso de tecnologias digitais de comunicação e informação, e tem como ponto de partida o componente curricular “Inglês Aplicado à Computação”, integrante da grade curricular do terceiro ano do curso Técnico em Informática, no IFPR, Campus Cascavel. A pesquisa baseia-se em pressupostos teóricos de perspectiva crítica que dialogam com o pós-estruturalismo, convergindo para os estudos deleuze-guattarianos sobre rizoma e cartografia. Trata-se de um estudo qualitativo que tem a cartografia como perspectiva teórico-epistemológica, pela qual o pesquisador compreende o mundo e com ele se relaciona, acompanhando os processos que acontecem no campo investigado. title: A Low-Cost Embedded System for Non-Technical Loss Detection in Low-Voltage Distribution Networks
abstract: A low-cost wireless embedded system was developed and evaluated for the local and real-time detection of non-technical losses caused by electrical bypasses in low-voltage service drops. The architecture consists of two ESP32-based measurement nodes equipped with PZEM-004T V3 modules and interconnected through ESP-NOW. Node A measures the electrical variables at the service connection point, whereas Node B acquires the billing-point variables, processes the received telemetry, and displays the operating status through a local web dashboard. The detection model incorporates the estimated resistive loss of the service drop and applies a current-dependent dynamic threshold to distinguish technical losses from unexplained power discrepancies. Measurement pairs are validated through sequence identification, timestamp-based synchronization, and wireless-link quality criteria before classification. The experimental campaign comprised 40 scenarios, including 20 controlled tests and 20 different residential service drops with conductor cross-sectional areas of 6 and 10 mm², lengths from 4 to 25 m, and different load profiles. Thirty-eight acquisitions satisfied the established quality criteria. The system obtained 9 true positives, 28 true negatives, 0 false positives, and 1 false negative, corresponding to an accuracy of 97.37%, sensitivity of 90.00%, specificity of 100.00%, and precisi…

Justification and Integrated Illegality: An Economic Framework for Criminal Law and Competition Law
abstract: Abstract This paper builds a common welfare architecture for legal permission rules in criminal law and competition law, and distinguishes throughout between doctrine it represents, normative premises it adopts, and results that follow from them. In criminal law, the received Japanese account on which an unlawful attacker’s interest forfeits protection is represented as a discount, bounded by the ratio of anticipated harms, on the harm borne by the source of a threat. Conditional on that representation, any incompleteness of the forfeiture reintroduces a balancing term of the same order; the three emergency justifications are distinguished by who bears the harm; and a defender’s prior provocation is separated from the attacker’s wrongfulness. In competition law, the paper models incentives to deliver benefits promised in green cooperation and derives a benchmark-specific threshold for cartel unsustainability. Both fields’ deterrence assessments share an untested assumption about substitution.

title: Full Pore System Characteristics, Fractal Dimensions, and Controlling Factors of Lacustrine Laminated Shale: Implications for Shale Oil Reservoirs in the Liaohe Depression, NE China
abstract: Abstract Clarifying the pore system of unconventional oil and gas reservoirs is essential for understanding hydrocarbon accumulation, improving recovery efficiency, and accurately assessing resource potential. However, research on pore systems in lacustrine shales remains limited, largely because the development of diverse laminas produces strong heterogeneity. In the current research, 20 samples from the fourth member of the Shahejie Formation in the Western Sag, Liaohe Depression of the Bohai Bay Basin were systematically characterized through a combined approach that includes CO2 adsorption, N2 adsorption, and high-pressure mercury intrusion (HPMI) experiments. Fractal dimensions for micropores (D1), mesopores (D2), and macropores (D3) were obtained using the V–S model for CO2 adsorption, the FHH model for N2 adsorption, and the MSP model for HPMI. The results demonstrate that the laminated shale is composed of light-colored layers rich in quartz, feldspar, calcite, and dolomite, which often alternate with darker layers primarily consisting of clay minerals and organic matter. The pore system of the laminated shale consists mainly of intergranular pores, intercrystalline pores, dissolution pores, and microfractures within the matrix, excluding pores associated with organic matter. In terms of pore volume, the pore system is primarily characterized by mesopores and macropores…

title: A 1951–1998 Lutao coral Pb isotope record reveals site-specific, marine-integrated anthropogenic Pb pollution signals in the Northwest Pacific
abstract: Coral lead (Pb) isotope records provide multi-decadal perspectives on marine Pb histories, but how individual records represent regional isotope histories remains an important interpretive question. We present a 1951–1998 Pb isotope record from a Porites coral at Lutao, southeast of Taiwan, and compare it with published records from Dongsha and Ogasawara in the Northwest Pacific. The three coral records exhibited substantial inter-site isotopic differences during 1953–1963, smaller differences in interval-mean 208 Pb/ 207 Pb during 1964–1984, and persistent site-specific characteristics. In 1985–1998, Lutao had a statistically distinguishable lower 208 Pb/ 207 Pb composition than Dongsha, whereas the middle-to-late change within Lutao itself was not statistically resolved. This contrast shows that inter-site isotopic differences need not imply an equivalent temporal shift at an individual site. Published Pb isotope reference fields are compatible with multiple possible source combinations but do not uniquely identify historical sources or marine transport mechanisms. Together, these results reveal spatial heterogeneity in coral Pb isotope histories, with smaller inter-site differences during 1964–1984, and highlight the need to evaluate the spatial representativeness of individual coral Pb isotope records before extrapolating site-specific signatures to regional historical inte…

title: Entre a avenida e o cubo branco: Vermelho-Mangue e reconfiguração da visualidade carnavalesca no sistema de arte
abstract: Resumo Este trabalho investiga a inserção da obra Vermelho-Mangue (2025), derivada de um carro alegórico concebido pelos carnavalescos Leonardo Bora e Gabriel Haddad para o desfile da Acadêmicos do Grande Rio (2025), no espaço expositivo do Centro Cultural Banco do Brasil, no Rio de Janeiro. A análise se concentra na transposição dessa visualidade carnavalesca – construída a partir de metodologias de criação coletiva e fortemente territorializadas — para o contexto museológico, buscando compreender de que maneira esse deslocamento produz efeitos institucionais e políticos, especialmente, ao tensionar hierarquias historicamente estabelecidas entre arte erudita e cultura popular. Em contraste com uma possível “visão tecnocrática”, centrada exclusivamente em resultados, o estudo propõe pensar a gestão dessa obra no museu como uma forma de ação política, entendendo seu processo de inserção como um campo de disputa no qual práticas, valores e modos de legitimação são continuamente reconfigurados. A partir das contribuições de Muniz Sodré, Françoise Vergès e Rita Segato, discute-se a carnavalização não apenas como um recurso estético, mas como um regime estético-político capaz de operar processos de descolonização das instituições artísticas e, ao mesmo tempo, de tensionar a lógica de mera “administração do existente”. title: Dos papéis às práticas: reflexões iniciais sobre as potencialidades e os desafios de consolidar o Sistema Nacional de Cultura em Pernambuco
abstract: Este ensaio tem como objetivo refletir sobre as potencialidades e os desafios de implementação do Sistema Nacional de Cultura em Pernambuco. Trata-se do trabalho de conclusão das disciplinas Políticas Culturais: trajetória e desafios contemporâneos; e Gestão Cultural: do tecnicismo ao engajamento, cursadas no âmbito da Especialização em Política e Gestão Cultural, realizada pela Universidade Federal do Recôncavo Baiano, em parceria com o Ministério da Cultura, por meio da Escola Solano Trindade de Formação e Qualificação Artística, Técnica e Cultural. A partir de revisão bibliográfica e análise documental, percorre-se a trajetória do SNC desde sua concepção até o atual marco regulatório (Lei nº 14.835/2024), destacando o papel catalisador das leis emergenciais da pandemia (Lei Aldir Blanc e Lei Paulo Gustavo) e da Política Nacional Aldir Blanc (PNAB). Como estratégia metodológica, as autorias partem das suas experiências laborais: ela, na Secretaria de Cultura do Estado de Pernambuco, e ele do Escritório Estadual do Ministério da Cultura em Pernambuco, para, em articulação aos conteúdos abordados nas duas matérias, analisar de forma crítica os diversos momentos da implementação do Sistema Nacional de Cultura no Estado, em busca de aprimorar sua consolidação como uma política estruturante. title: Linking the complement system to endometriosis pathogenesis: a systematic review of diagnostic potential
abstract: Endometriosis (EM) is a chronic gynecological disorder affecting roughly 5-10% of women in their reproductive age, with symptom onset often occurring during adolescence but diagnosis frequently delayed for several years. Its pathogenesis is multifactorial, involving immunological, hormonal, genetic, and environmental factors. Increasing evidence suggests that immune dysregulation, particularly involving the complement system, a key effector of innate immunity and mediator of inflammatory responses, contributes to EM pathogenesis by sustaining chronic inflammation, angiogenesis, and lesion development. This review summarizes the available evidence on the involvement of complement components in EM pathogenesis and evaluates their potential use as biomarkers. A systematic literature search was performed in PubMed, Scopus, and Embase following PRISMA guidelines, including all eligible studies published up to July 2026. After full-text screening, 64 of 652 studies were selected and included in the final analysis. Overall, evidence supported a predominant involvement of the alternative complement pathway in EM, with complement component C3 emerging as the most extensively investigated molecule (35/64 studies). Evidence for the classical and lectin pathways was comparatively limited and heterogeneous. Moreover, several complement regulators emerged as differentially expressed in trans…

title: Early detection of drug-resistant epilepsy via multi-domain EEG fusion with prefrontal candidate biomarkers
abstract: Drug-resistant epilepsy (DRE) is associated with poor clinical outcomes. Interictal scalp EEG-based DRE identification faces a methodological limitation: segment-level models often capture individual-specific EEG patterns rather than group-level pathological differences. In this retrospective study of 42 patients (21 DRE, 21 non-DRE), we constructed an EEG-based DRE recognition framework. Multi-domain features (temporal, spectral, nonlinear) were extracted, and a mutual validation strategy integrating patient-level statistical tests and machine learning was applied to verify the pathological discriminative validity of features. A multi-domain support vector machine was built with ReliefF feature selection, evaluated via leave-one-out cross-validation and hold-out validation, and further analyzed for interpretability and clinical correlations. Significant between-group differences were found in clinical and electrophysiological features, with prominent alterations in prefrontal temporal statistics, θ/β band power and entropy features. The multi-domain model consistently outperformed single-domain models; prefrontal β/γ power and entropy features were identified as core candidate biomarkers, significantly correlated with disease duration and seizure frequency. This study identifies prefrontal EEG features as candidate DRE biomarkers, and the combined validation framework supports…

title: Gut microbiota and metabolomic features associated with hemoglobin improvement in patients with aplastic anemia: an exploratory clinical multi-omics study
abstract: Background Hematologic recovery after treatment varies substantially among patients with aplastic anemia (AA). This exploratory clinical multi-omics study aimed to characterize gut microbial and metabolomic features associated with hemoglobin improvement in patients with AA. Methods Nineteen patients with AA who received kidney-nourishing and marrow-benefiting traditional Chinese medicine combined with conventional Western medical treatment were included. According to hematologic response at approximately 6 months, patients were classified as responders ( n = 14) or non-responders ( n = 5). Paired fecal and serum samples collected before and after treatment were analyzed using 16S rRNA sequencing and untargeted metabolomics. Hb_change, defined as post-treatment hemoglobin minus baseline hemoglobin, was used as the primary clinical variable. Associations between omics features and Hb_change were assessed using Spearman correlation with Benjamini–Hochberg correction. Leave-one-out analysis, bootstrap confidence intervals, baseline Hb-adjusted models, and paired longitudinal analyses were used to further examine selected associations. Results Hb_change was greater in responders than in non-responders (31.5 vs. 10.0 g/L, p = 0.006). title: Multi-channel discrimination of crystallographic defects in 4H-SiC epitaxial wafers using optical inspection, photoluminescence and X-ray topography
abstract: Accurate identification of crystallographic defects in 4H-SiC epitaxial wafers is essential for ensuring the yield and reliability of SiC power devices. Although a variety of inspection techniques have been developed, defect visibility varies substantially among characterization methods, making reliable automated defect classification challenging. In this study, a multi-channel defect identification framework that integrates optical inspection, photoluminescence, and X-ray topography using a convolutional neural network was developed. Images acquired by the three techniques were spatially registered and combined into multi-channel datasets for analysis. A Faster R-convolutional neural network was trained using annotated data collected from 18 epitaxial wafers. The trained model was evaluated using an independent test wafer containing reliability-relevant defects, including micropipes, basal plane dislocations, threading screw dislocations, stacking faults, stacking-fault complexes, polytype inclusions, and particle inclusions. Compared with models trained on individual inspection modalities, the multi-channel model exhibited improved classification performance by integrating complementary morphological, luminescence, and crystallographic information.

title: The TNG50-SKIRT Atlas: Multi-wavelength properties of galaxy discs in the TNG50 simulation
abstract: We investigate the wavelength dependence of disc scale lengths in galaxies from the TNG50–SKIRT Atlas (TSA), and assess whether the simulated galaxies reproduce the structural properties and scaling relations observed in real galaxies, as well as the physical origin of the wavelength dependence. We measure disc scale lengths from one-dimensional radial surface-brightness profiles of multi-wavelength synthetic images. The disc-dominated region is defined interactively per galaxy and applied consistently across bands. We restrict the analysis to nearly face-on, star-forming galaxies and retain only systems whose r -band profiles are well described by an exponential model. The resulting scale lengths are compared to observational samples and analysed using both dust-attenuated and dust-free images, as well as intrinsic stellar population maps. We find that the majority of TSA galaxies exhibit exponential discs in realistic mock observations. The TSA galaxies reproduce the observed disc scale length--stellar mass (luminosity) relation, but are systematically larger at fixed mass or luminosity. The dependence of disc scale length on morphology is weak. Disc scale lengths correlate strongly across wavelengths but decrease systematically with increasing wavelength. Multi-toxicant exposure to beauvericin, arsenic trioxide, and glyphosate enhances cytotoxicity and intracellular ROS levels in NIH-3T3 fibroblast cells
abstract: Introduction Human exposure to environmental contaminants typically occurs through complex chemical mixtures rather than individual compounds; however, the toxicological interactions among co-occurring contaminants remain poorly understood. This study investigated the cytotoxic interactions of the mycotoxin beauvericin (BEA), the pesticide glyphosate (GLY), and arsenic trioxide (ATO) in binary and ternary combinations using NIH‐3T3 fibroblasts. Methods Cell viability was assessed using the MTT assay. Toxicological interactions were quantitatively characterized using the Chou‐Talalay method based on combination index (CI) and dose reduction index (DRI) analyses. Intracellular reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation was measured to evaluate oxidative stress. Results Among the individual toxicants, ATO exhibited the greatest cytotoxicity, followed by BEA and GLY. Combination analysis revealed distinct interaction profiles depending on mixture composition. BEA + ATO and BEA + GLY consistently exhibited synergistic cytotoxicity, whereas ATO + GLY showed predominantly additive effects. Notably, the ternary mixture displayed a dose‐dependent interaction pattern, transitioning from antagonism at a low effect level (IC 10 ) to synergism at a high effect level (IC 50 ). These interaction profiles were accompanied by increased intracellular ROS generation, with synergistic combinations s…

Global trends and emerging frontiers in rectal neuroendocrine neoplasms: a multi-database bibliometric analysis
abstract: Background Research on rectal neuroendocrine neoplasms (R-NENs) has grown, but the development of this site-specific literature and the consistency of its main patterns across databases have not been examined together. Methods We mapped English-language articles and reviews from the Web of Science Core Collection (WoSCC), then used separately screened Scopus and PubMed records to compare publication trends, leading countries, and prespecified clinical themes. Author keywords and Keywords Plus were normalized and deduplicated within records. Results The primary WoSCC corpus included 875 publications. Of these, 803 met the direct title-and-abstract rule used for validation; the corresponding Scopus and PubMed sets contained 1,018 and 703 records. Annual output was strongly correlated across databases (Pearson r=0.979–0.992), although record overlap was moderate (Jaccard=0.531–0.545). Country and theme ranks showed partial agreement, while their absolute frequencies varied. Across time, the literature moved from historical ‘carcinoid’ terminology toward endoscopic resection, pathological risk, prognosis, and decisions after local treatment. Conclusion The analysis maps how R-NEN research has developed and where further clinical studies are needed. Cross-database agreement supports the overall growth pattern and some broad rankings, but it does not establish the validity of any tre…

title: Enhanced multi-object detection in brachial plexus ultrasound images using transformer-based semantic and spatial feature fusion
abstract: Abstract Advances in medical imaging have led to the widespread use of ultrasound for diagnosing and treating peripheral nerve blocks. However, challenges such as speckle noise and low spatial resolution hinder the accurate identification of neural structures. To address these issues, a model named transformer-based detection with semantic and spatial feature fusion (TDSS) was introduced, integrating spatial edge adaptive enhancement, multi-scale semantic fusion, and spatial distillation-assisted detection modules. These components improve edge perception, multi-scale semantic reasoning, and localization accuracy. Experiments on the Ultrasound Brachial Plexus Dataset demonstrated the superior performance of the model: TDSS achieved an AP of 0.407 for nerve detection and an overall mAP of 0.583, providing robust support for clinical medical image detection. The source code for the proposed TDSS framework is publicly available at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.18824199 .

title: Integrated Reactive CO2 and NH3 Capture and Conversion to Ammonium Carbamate: Material Design toward Low-Concentration Sources
abstract: Abstract Carbon dioxide (CO2) and ammonia (NH3) emissions are responsible for global warming and eutrophication, among other causes. Ionic liquids (ILs) stand out as versatile designer absorbent/catalyst materials that contribute to the capture and conversion of both gases. This work focuses on the efficient and innovative use of ILs in NH3 and CO2 integrated capture and conversion (ICC) to produce ammonium carbamate (AMC) using an efficient self-regenerating catalytic system operating at room temperature, with spontaneous product separation by precipitation. Experimental ICC tests were carried out using 10 ILs, with remarkable structural differences, and different NH3 and CO2 partial pressure and experimental times. Two different optimization routes were explored by tuning the IL material features through molecular design: (i) an NH3-driven mechanism using IL as the physical absorbent and (ii) a CO2-driven mechanism using IL as the reactive capture agent, selected to promote high CO2 chemical absorption and activation and easy IL regeneration and AMC removal. The use of an IL as a reactive capture agent strongly improves the process performance with fast ICC rates even at low NH3 and CO2 partial pressures, highlighting the CO2-driven approach as a versatile ICC technology capable of efficiently treating diluted NH3 and CO2 streams to produce value-added AMC products.

abstract: Addressing the needs of students majoring in Uyghur or Chinese who take Uzbek as a minor, this paper examines two language textbooks through content analysis and Uzbek–Uyghur comparison. It proposes principles based on communicative needs, explicit explanation of differences, differentiated support, and the recycling of language content. Contrastive analysis is incorporated into contextualized input, task performance, and revision following feedback, providing a basis for developing a textbook for beginning learners of Uzbek.

title: Estudos decoloniais da América Latina: interseções entre o design e o artesanato para novos futuros
abstract: O design decolonial emerge como uma resposta crítica à dominação eurocêntrica que historicamente moldou as práticas e os discursos do design na América Latina, influenciando modos de produzir, interpretar e valorizar objetos e saberes. Nesse contexto, este artigo analisa as interseções entre o design decolonial e o artesanato geracional, compreendendo-os como espaços de resistência, reexistência e produção de alternativas ao modelo hegemônico, com ênfase nas convergências entre o crochê e o bordado. Muito antes do processo de colonização, diversas comunidades latino-americanas já desenvolviam tradições artesanais têxteis, transmitidas intergeracionalmente como parte de sistemas simbólicos, culturais e identitários próprios. Essas práticas configuram-se como formas complexas de expressão e comunicação, articulando memória, pertencimento e modos de vida situados. No que se refere ao crochê, sua prática emerge em diferentes contextos históricos e se expande no período pós-colonial, sendo compreendida como espaço de construção de subjetividades, fortalecimento de vínculos sociais e constituição de redes afetivas. A pesquisa caracteriza-se como qualitativa, de natureza exploratória e interdisciplinar, orientada por uma perspectiva decolonial. Explainable AI-based framework for 3D structural as-built modeling of aging buildings in Korea using laser scanning
abstract: Purpose This study proposes a framework for automatically generating 3D structural as-built models of aging buildings by predicting the structural dimensions of members concealed behind finishes using laser scanning and machine learning, particularly when original construction drawings are unavailable. Design/methodology/approach Laser scanning captures building geometry but includes both structural components and non-structural finishes (e.g. plaster), making it unsuitable for directly extracting structural dimensions. To address this, the proposed framework extracts geometric features from point clouds and employs machine learning techniques to predict structural dimensions of columns, beams, walls and slabs. Six machine learning models – Random Forest, XGBoost, LightGBM, CatBoost, Linear Regression and Support Vector Regression (SVR) – were trained using data collected on 1,560 column elements, 2,875 beam elements, 870 wall elements and 148 slab elements across 50 buildings and validated through two real-world case studies. Findings The best-performing model achieved MAPE of 10.51% for column width (95%CI: 8.47–12.71), 12.98% for column depth (95% CI: 10.86–15.41), 14.91% for beam width (95% CI: 13.63–16.15), 18.91% for beam depth (95% CI: 17.94–19.90), 10.42% for walls (95% CI: 8.89–12.00) and 10.70% for slabs (95% CI: 7.11–14.50). The predicted dimensions enabled reconstru…

title: Health insurance shields families, yet inequalities still shape India's path toward financial protection and equity
O direito ao ócio e à criatividade: a pedagogia da capoeira angola como contraponto a uma educação mercantilizada
abstract: Este artigo analisa criticamente as políticas educacionais contemporâneas que, pautadas por avaliações em larga escala e pela mercantilização do ensino, reduzem a escola pública a um simulacro de adestramento para o mercado flexível e para a ideologia do empreendedorismo de si. Em contraposição a esse sequestro do tempo vital da juventude trabalhadora, propõe-se a pedagogia da Capoeira Angola como um contraponto político-epistêmico e metodológico. Metodologicamente, a pesquisa de natureza qualitativa e exploratória baseia-se em revisão bibliográfica e análise histórico-documental, com ênfase na criminalização histórica da “vadiagem” e da “capoeiragem” pelo Código Penal de 1890. Discute-se a vadiagem não como inércia, mas como categoria revolucionária que reivindica o direito inalienável ao ócio criador e à soberania temporal contra a lógica do “negócio” (nec-otium). Como resultado, caracteriza-se a Capoeira Angola como um sistema artístico-marcial autopoiético que recusa a competição e a esportivização da vida. Conclui-se que a transposição tática dos fundamentos da roda — como a mandinga, a malícia e a cooperação — para o cotidiano da escola formal oferece caminhos para que educadores transformem as salas de aula em trincheiras de resistência, instrumentalizando os estudantes com a agudeza cognitiva necessária para ler as contradições sociais e lutar pela emancipação coletiva.

title: Correcting stellar contamination in transmission spectroscopy with contemporaneous monitoring: Application to GJ 1214 b
abstract: Transmission spectroscopy has emerged as an essential tool for characterising the atmospheres of transiting exoplanets. However, stellar surface inhomogeneities contaminate transmission spectra, which poses a major challenge, particularly to high-precision observations such as those from the (JWST). James Webb Space Telescope We developed and applied a set of practical methodologies to correct for stellar contamination in transmission spectroscopy data, thereby improving the accuracy of exoplanet atmospheric characterisation. We obtained coordinated multi-band photometry and high-resolution spectroscopy around JWST observations of GJ,1214,b and applied two correction frameworks: (i) an inversion with the StarSim code, in which we infer stellar activity parameters from the monitoring data and propagate them to corrections; and (ii) , a data-driven approach in which neural networks (NNs) are trained on a large suite of simulations to learn the mapping from the monitoring data to the corrections. StarSim Both frameworks agree within the uncertainties and indicate that the JWST observations of GJ,1214 occurred at a favourable rotation phase with low stellar contamination. For , the inferred corrections can be constrained at the ∼10--30 ppm level across the JWST wavelength range, implying post-correction residuals of the same order. title: Climate shapes mosquito-borne disease transmission in africa: a scoping review of climatic determinants, biological responses and transmission dynamics
abstract: Abstract Background Mosquito-borne diseases remain a major public-health challenge in Africa, and their transmission is strongly influenced by climatic conditions. However, the evidence is geographically uneven and methodologically heterogeneous. Objective To map and synthesise evidence on the influence of temperature, rainfall/precipitation and relative humidity on mosquito-borne disease transmission in Africa, and to compare climatic patterns across major vector–pathogen systems. Methods A scoping review was conducted following PRISMA-ScR. Peer-reviewed primary studies conducted in Africa, or providing identifiable Africa-specific evidence, were included if they investigated malaria, dengue, chikungunya or Zika and assessed temperature, rainfall/precipitation and/or relative humidity in relation to biological, entomological, ecological, transmission-related or epidemiological outcomes. Results Eighteen primary studies were included: 10 on malaria, 6 on dengue and 2 on Zika; none specifically addressed chikungunya. Temperature was the most frequently assessed exposure. Malaria studies showed non-linear and context-dependent temperature relationships, including a field peak in malaria positivity near 25 °C. Dengue studies showed heterogeneous temperature signals, including stronger temperature–incidence relationships above approximately 21 °C and increased transmission-related …

title: Shock impedance mismatch and transmission loss in fiber–metal laminates: a computational and experimental study
abstract: Abstract The shielding performance of multi-layered sandwich structures is influenced by the shock impedance mismatch at material interfaces. In this study, an integrated computational, analytical, and experimental framework was developed to evaluate the acoustic transmission loss (TL) of fiber–metal laminates (FMLs) incorporating fabric-reinforced polymer core plies. A dimensionless shock-impedance formulation based on the Buckingham- $$\pi $$ theorem was employed to examine the influence of material properties, including Poisson’s ratio, on three-dimensional elastic wave propagation and aid in material selection. A mesoscale representative volume element (RVE) approach was used to derive the effective orthotropic properties of aramid-, basalt-, and Zylon-reinforced plies, which were subsequently incorporated into a macroscale finite-element (FE) harmonic-acoustics framework to evaluate TL over the 63–1300,Hz frequency range. In parallel, a multi-layer analytical formulation was developed to estimate insertion loss and the corresponding frequency-dependent TL response. The empirical parameters of the analytical model were calibrated using a single baseline configuration and subsequently applied to six additional stacking sequences, for which the mean TL difference from the corresponding FE predictions remained below $$3.06\%$$ . title: Financial Leverage, Profitability, and Firm Value: Evidence From Primary Consumer Goods Companies Listed on The Indonesia Stock Exchange
abstract: Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis dan menjelaskan pengaruh Financial Leverage dan Profitabilitas terhadap Nilai Perusahaan pada perusahaan sektor Barang Konsumen Primer yang terdaftar di Bursa Efek Indonesia (BEI) selama periode 2019–2024. Penelitian ini menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif. Populasi penelitian terdiri atas 125 perusahaan, dengan teknik pengambilan sampel menggunakan purposive sampling berdasarkan kriteria yang telah ditentukan, sehingga diperoleh 10 perusahaan sebagai sampel penelitian. Analisis data dilakukan menggunakan metode regresi linier berganda, sedangkan pengolahan data dilakukan dengan bantuan program EViews versi 13. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa Financial Leverage dan Profitabilitas secara simultan berpengaruh signifikan terhadap Nilai Perusahaan yang diproksikan dengan Price to Book Value (PBV). Secara parsial, Financial Leverage yang diproksikan dengan Debt to Equity Ratio (DER) berpengaruh signifikan terhadap Nilai Perusahaan. Demikian pula, Profitabilitas yang diproksikan dengan Return on Assets (ROA) berpengaruh signifikan terhadap Nilai Perusahaan.

title: Corporate GHG emissions and financial performances: the moderating role of CEO overconfidence
abstract: Purpose This study examines whether CEO overconfidence shapes the relationship between corporate greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions and firm financial performance. It asks whether emissions are uniformly value-destroying or whether their financial consequences depend on executive cognition and the operating scale embedded in emissions-intensive activity. Design/methodology/approach The analysis uses panel data on 1,816 US-listed firms over 2002–2020, with up to 33,179 firm-year observations depending on variable availability. GHG emissions are measured using total emissions, Scope 1, Scope 2, Scope 3, revenue-scaled emissions intensity and environmental cost indicators. Firm performance is captured by return on equity, return on assets and Tobin's Q. CEO overconfidence is measured mainly through the Holder67 option-based proxy. The study applies firm and year fixed-effects models, scale-sensitive robustness tests, an alternative overconfidence proxy based on overinvestment, two-stage least squares and dynamic panel generalized method of moments (GMM) diagnostics. Findings GHG emissions are positively associated with firm performance when firms are led by overconfident CEOs. This result holds across accounting and market-based measures and remains evident when emissions are separated by scope and when revenue-scaled intensity is examined. The positive association is stronger under h…

title: Artificial Intelligence Adoption and Financial Decision-Making Quality among SMEs in Freetown, Sierra Leone: The Moderating Role of Digital Capability
abstract: This study investigates the impact of artificial intelligence (AI) adoption on financial decision-making quality (FDMQ) among small and medium enterprises (SMEs) in Freetown, Sierra Leone. It examines the moderating role of digital capability. The study used a quantitative, cross-sectional survey design with a sample of 250 owner-managers and finance officers from SMEs in formal and semi-formal business clusters in Freetown, based on the Technology–Organization–Environment (TOE) framework and Resource-Based View (RBV). The data were analyzed using SPSS with descriptive statistics, correlation analysis, and hierarchical moderated multiple regression. Findings showed that AI adoption (β = .573, p .001) and digital capability (β = .283, p .001) were significant, positive predictors of FDMQ. The AI adoption–FDMQ relationship was also significantly moderated by digital capability (β = .195, ΔR² = .035, p .001). Simple slopes analysis showed that the effect of AI adoption was more than doubled when digital capability increased from low to high. AI adoption enhances SME financial decision-making, but its impact relies on supporting digital capabilities. The study builds on the TOE and RBV frameworks in an under-researched West African context. It emphasizes the importance of integrating AI provision with digital capability development. title: Physics-grounded sequence-domain graph learning for adaptive fault location in IBR-dominated offshore wind farm transmission networks
abstract: Abstract Fault location in offshore wind-farm networks dominated by inverter-based resources (IBRs) is complicated by converter-limited fault currents, cable charging currents and high fault resistance, which violate the assumptions of classical impedance-based estimators. This paper proposes PG-SDGL, a physics-grounded sequence-domain graph-learning framework that combines a graph-attention sequence-domain graph neural network (SeqGNN), a three-sequence physics-informed neural network (3Seq-PINN) for fault-resistance decoupling, sequence-residual split-conformal prediction intervals, cable charging-current compensation, an analytical IBR fault-current decomposition, a harmonic high-impedance-fault (HIF) gate with Dempster–Shafer fusion of two intelligent electronic devices and a protection-consistency index (PCI). The framework was evaluated in simulation on a 69 kV network with a 60 km overhead interconnection line and three 5–9 km submarine cable feeders, for four fault types and fault resistances of 2–150 Ω. Feeder-identification accuracy was 99.4–99.6%. Over 2–40 Ω, the average main-line mean relative error (MRE) was 0.195%, compared with 0.631% in the published random-forest benchmark on the same line model. title: Direito Humano à Água e Desigualdades Territoriais: uma análise crítica das políticas públicas de segurança hídrica no Brasil
abstract: O acesso à água potável constitui um direito humano fundamental reconhecido internacionalmente, porém sua efetivação permanece marcada por profundas desigualdades territoriais e socioambientais. No Brasil, apesar da ampla disponibilidade hídrica e da existência de marcos legais estruturantes, como a Política Nacional de Recursos Hídricos e o Marco Legal do Saneamento Básico, o acesso seguro e contínuo à água ainda não é garantido de forma universal. Este artigo analisa criticamente as políticas públicas nacionais voltadas à segurança hídrica, discutindo os avanços normativos, os instrumentos institucionais de gestão e os limites de sua implementação no território brasileiro. A partir de revisão bibliográfica, análise documental e abordagem geográfica crítica, o estudo examina a construção do direito humano à água no cenário internacional, sua incorporação ao arcabouço jurídico brasileiro e as tensões entre gestão técnica dos recursos hídricos e justiça socioambiental. A análise evidencia que a desigualdade no acesso à água resulta da interação entre fatores ambientais, sociais e institucionais, revelando como políticas públicas frequentemente reproduzem assimetrias históricas que afetam especialmente populações rurais, comunidades tradicionais e territórios periféricos. title: Scope 3 Emissions Framing and Corporate Climate Litigation: Encouraging the Right Narratives?
abstract: Abstract The article analyses the framing of scope 3 emissions in corporate climate litigation and the narratives they give rise to. It examines scope 3’s origins and its presence in legislative and other regulatory measures before analysing scope 3 emissions framing in a series of landmark cases globally. The case law on scope 3 is presented across five broad categories involving corporations: business challenges to climate disclosure legislation, and then greenwashing, project, due diligence and liability cases brought by the climate movement. How do we and how should we frame what a company’s emissions are, for which it is legally responsible? The article outlines how the case law reflects a framing contest over what emissions properly belong to a company. It then discusses narratives involved in some of the key scope 3 emissions categories. While finding that there are strategically positive narratives for the climate movement, it argues that some of its corporate climate litigation plays into problematic private governance and market-led narratives. A case is made for a carbon takeback obligation (CTBO) as part of a policy-led narrative to help resolve these tensions.

Out of the Mattresses and Into the Banks: Unpacking Financial Disintermediation and Liquidity Dynamics in South Sudan
abstract: This study investigates the behavioral, structural, and macroeconomic drivers of mattress banking, the widespread practice of hoarding cash outside formal financial institutions in South Sudan. Drawing on mixed-methods field data collected in 2026 (N=800), consisting of 650 structured survey respondents and 150 qualitative interview and focus group participants, the research identifies cultural attachment to traditional saving methods (12.1%) and fear of government scrutiny (11.3%) as the most salient factors, alongside systemic bank liquidity concerns (7.1%) and institutional distrust (6.7%). Macroeconomic impacts include weakened monetary policy, reduced access to private-sector credit, and significant losses to formal bank deposits, with households facing heightened risks of theft (8.3%) and asset destruction from disasters (7.5%). Regression and thematic analyses reveal that women, rural residents, the unbanked, and informal sector workers are particularly vulnerable to mattress banking, which is further exacerbated by chronic salary delays and low financial literacy. The study recommends a multi-pronged approach to reintegrate informal liquidity: expanding digital and mobile banking, strengthening regulatory oversight and deposit insurance, simplifying account opening, and fostering public trust through robust consumer protection and financial education. title: Crystal-axis dependence of nonreciprocal spin-wave transmission in asymmetric Fe/MgO/NiFe trilayers
abstract: We investigated the crystal-axis dependence of nonreciprocal spin-wave transmission in asymmetric Fe/MgO/NiFe trilayer waveguides. Spin-wave transmission was measured in the Damon–Eshbach geometry for two configurations: the easy-axis configuration, with the magnetic field applied along Fe[100], and the hard-axis configuration, with the field along Fe[110]. The transmission spectra exhibited propagation-direction-dependent differences in both amplitude and frequency. In particular, the directional amplitude difference of one experimentally observed branch reversed its polarity upon reversal of the external magnetic field in both configurations. Micromagnetic simulations showed propagation-direction-dependent localization of the dynamic magnetization and revealed that the spectral separation between the Fe-like and NiFe-like branches depended on the orientation relative to the Fe crystal axes. These results demonstrate the important role of the Fe crystal axes in nonreciprocal spin-wave transmission in asymmetric magnetic multilayers.

title: Forecasting High Electricity Demand Using Explainable Machine Learning
abstract: The objective of this study was to predict the onset of high demand, the highest half-hourly average power, and the total duration of high demand over the next two hours using historical electricity consumption data from residential households. Half-hourly measurements from 2013 for 200 standard-tariff residential households selected from the Low Carbon London dataset were used. High demand was defined as exceeding the 90th percentile of each household’s average power values during the January–February period. The models were developed using data from 160 households; transfer performance was evaluated on the 40 households not included in model training. The process was divided into a training period (March–June), model selection in July, calibration of prediction intervals in August, and a testing period (September–December). The selected models were retrained using March–July data. Separate models were built for the three targets; Random Forest, histogram-based gradient boosting (HistGB), XGBoost, LightGBM, and CatBoost were compared against a weekly seasonal reference. Model selection was initially based on average precision (AP) for the target and mean absolute error (MAE) for power and duration. title: Economic Policy Uncertainty as a Driver of Risk Premia in Emerging Market Swap Spreads
abstract: We examine the impact of domestic and global economic policy uncertainty (EPU) on interest rate swap spreads in the BRIC economies, representing the leading emerging markets. We mainly find that the impact of EPU is state-dependent and follows a regime-switching model. On applying the Markov regime-switching model, the effect of EPU was found to be statistically significant only in the relatively less volatile regime. During the high-volatility regime, the impact of EPU is surpassed by noise and other extraneous variables of the term structure and volatility index. When the impacts of domestic and global EPU are examined separately, global EPU is found to reduce swap spreads across all major maturities. This pattern suggests the relative resilience of these economies during periods of heightened global uncertainty and reflects investors’ tendency to drift toward safer fixed-income instruments. In contrast, the effects of domestic EPU are maturity-specific. During low-volatility regimes, higher levels of domestic EPU were causing widening of long-term swap spreads. This divergence indicates that domestic policy uncertainty is more potent in transmitting adverse credit and liquidity conditions over longer horizons, thereby increasing long-term risk premia in the swap market. JEL Codes: E42, E44, G12, G15, G21, G23

title: First Report of Neopestalotiopsis vacciniicola Causing Leaf Spot on Rhododendron delavayi in China
abstract: In March 2025, leaf spot was observed on nursery-grown Rhododendron delavayi in Dali, Yunnan, China (25°40′52″N, 100°18′01″E); of 300 plants randomly surveyed from the nursery population, 108 were affected. Adaxial lesions began as dark brown to purplish flecks, enlarged into tan-centered necrotic spots, coalesced, and caused premature leaf abscission; abaxial discoloration was less conspicuous. Nine symptomatic leaves were randomly collected from six plants showing typical symptoms. Lesion-margin pieces (ca. 5 × 5 mm) were disinfected in 70% ethanol for 30 s and 1% NaOCl for 1 min, rinsed, dried, and plated on potato dextrose agar (PDA). Twenty-one Neopestalotiopsis-like colonies were recovered from 27 pieces (77.8%); seven isolates were obtained. S1-1, S1-2, and S1-3 from different leaves had similar morphology. On PDA at 25°C, representative S1-1 formed white to creamy, cottony colonies after 7 d. Conidia of S1-1 were fusoid to slightly curved, mostly 4-septate, with three pigmented median cells and hyaline end cells, 13.5–26.0 × 5.9–8.4 μm (mean ± SD = 20.0 ± 3.2 × 7.0 ± 0.6 μm; n = 30), excluding appendages. They bore two to three tubular, unbranched, filiform apical appendages, 5.2–24.8 μm long, and one basal appendage. ITS, tef1-α, and tub2 were amplified from all three isolates using ITS1/ITS4 (White et al. 1990), EF1-728F/EF1-986R (Carbone and Kohn 1999), and Bt2a/Bt2b…

title: Expanding market shaping best practices to new contexts: Diagnosing insulin market health and charting a path forward
abstract: Market shaping tools such as the Healthy Market Framework (HMF) and associated Market Action Plans (MAPs) have supported access to essential health products in low- and middle-income countries by aligning partners around shared goals and driving progress forward. Despite their utility, these tools are rarely applied outside of the centralized, donor-financed markets they were designed for. Insulin is a fragmented market with persistent access gaps that market shaping efforts could address. In this viewpoint, we describe how the Insulin Healthy Markets Task Force (IHM-TF) developed the first HMF and MAP for insulin, adapting a methodology built for a fundamentally different market context. We outline the process for diagnosing market health, the stakeholder engagement needed to translate this into a prioritized MAP, and the lessons learned in applying these tools to markets lacking neutral coordinating bodies, adequate and sustained financing, and shared market data. Extending market shaping to fragmented markets depends on building the coordinating infrastructure these markets lack and sustaining a coalition around a shared purpose. As the global health architecture shifts toward greater country ownership, this approach can help country governments, civil society, and supply chain actors diagnose and act on barriers to insulin access in their own contexts.

Understanding the Evolution of Dairy Goat Farming in Mediterranean Systems: Market Volatility, Climate Stresses, and the Role of CAP Subsidies
abstract: Autochthonous breed dairy goat farming plays a key socio-ecological role in Andalusia (Spain); however, census and farm numbers have declined sharply over five decades (1974–2023). This study analyzes the drivers of this trajectory by combining official census statistics with a participatory workshop to conceptualize qualitative direct causal paths. The sector experienced structural restructuring, where technical efficiency gains were offset by farm-gate price setting asymmetries and supply cost volatility, aggravated by recurring droughts and reduced forage autonomy. Common Agricultural Policy direct payments were perceived merely as short-term liquidity supports. Crucially, a lack of generational renewal—driven by rural decline, quality-of-life concerns, heavy workloads, and low social recognition—constitutes one of the main risks to sector continuity. Participant scores reflect perceived factor importance rather than direct closure metrics. To overcome vulnerability, future resilience would require transformative strategies rather than incremental adjustments, such as farm automation to improve labor conditions, enhanced forage self-sufficiency, knowledge transfer on autochthonous breeds, and local value added through short supply chains and artisanal cheesemaking.

title: First Report of Leaf Spot Caused by Fusarium concentricum on Tea Plant ( Camellia sinensis ) in China
abstract: Tea plant [Camellia sinensis (L.) O. Kuntze] is one of the world’s important beverage crops with significant health benefits (Wei et al. 2018). In May 2024, leaf spot symptoms were observed in 11 representative tea plantations in Xixiang County, Shaanxi Province (107.77° E, 32.98° N). The disease occurred during a period of warm and humid conditions with frequent rainfall events. Among 100 surveyed tea plants, 15 showed typical symptoms, resulting in a disease incidence (DI) of 15%. Lesions covered 10% to 50% of leaf area. Symptoms were primarily observed on mature leaves. Initial symptoms appeared as small, water-soaked lesions along the leaf margins. As the disease progressed, these lesions gradually expanded, turning yellowish-brown and further developing into semicircular to irregular necrotic spots delineated by distinct dark-brown borders. Severe lesions exhibited concentric rings, and infected leaves became deformed and wilted (Fig. S1A). To isolate the pathogen, 30 symptomatic leaves were randomly collected and surface-sterilized in 75% ethanol for 30 s, followed by 1% sodium hypochlorite for 30 s, and rinsed three times with sterile water. Tissue pieces were excised from lesion areas of symptomatic leaves and cultured on potato dextrose agar (PDA) at 28°C in the dark for 72 h. title: The Role of Artificial Intelligence in Reshaping Consumer Behavior and Market Dynamics in the Digital Economy
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is a transformative technology in the digital economy, enabling businesses to analyze consumer behavior and enhance marketing strategies. The primary drawbacks of these social media platforms are lower data quality and a lack of advanced analytics to meet end users’ requirements. For that purpose, this article develops a novel computational model to analyze digital marketing trends using Machine Learning (ML) and Deep Learning (DL) techniques. The proposed methodology begins with a computational data model for efficient data collection and preprocessing steps, including sentiment labeling, geospatial analysis, ground-truth validation, and data augmentation. A hybrid classification approach is employed, integrating traditional ML models such as Support Vector Machine (SVM), Logistic Regression (LR), Decision Tree (DT), Random Forest (RF), and Multi-layer Perceptron (MLP) with deep learning models, including a CNN-LSTM architecture and the DeepNAO framework. The hybrid design enables effective extraction and improves classification accuracy. The model simulation, Pythsimulation, and the analysis parameters (including loss, accuracy, and precision) for both calculation models. Among the considered models, the DeepNAO model performs best in terms of accuracy and precision, offering optimized strategies for the competitive digital product market.

First report of Cercospora cf. sigesbeckiae causing Cercospora leaf spot of soybean in the Republic of Korea
abstract: During field trials conducted in 2022 and 2023, Cercospora leaf spot was observed on soybean ( Glycine max ) collected from Gimje-si, Jeollabuk-do; Yeoncheon-gun, Gyeonggi-do; and Muan-gun, Jeollanam-do, in the Republic of Korea. Lesions bearing black spore structures were observed on plants. To isolate the pathogen, infected tissues were surface-sterilized with 0.5% sodium hypochlorite for 1 min and cultured on potato dextrose agar (PDA). After seven days of incubation, white to gray fungal colonies with aerial mycelia were transferred to PDA and incubated at 25 °C under a 12-h photoperiod. Three isolates, 24YC2, MA35, and GJ3, were selected for morphological identification and pathogenicity testing. Conidiophores were brown to dark brown, straight to slightly curved, with multiple septa, measuring approximately 35–125 × 3.1–5.5 μm (n = 25). Conidiation was induced on soybean-based medium containing 16% (w/v) soybean tissue extract and 2% (w/v) agar under a 12-h photoperiod at 25 °C for 7 days. Conidia were hyaline to pale brown, cylindrical to filiform, and multicellular, measuring 45–120 × 3.5–5.7 μm (n = 25), consistent with previous descriptions of C. cf. sigesbeckiae . title: Energy-enstrophy balance and the evolving shape of Jupiter’s Great Red Spot
abstract: Abstract Inspired by the statistical mechanics approach to the organization of two-dimensional turbulence into a steady flow, we propose a variational principle to explain the observed tendency of Jupiter’s Great Red Spot (GRS) to become more circular. For this, we first derive, at leading order in the thin-shell parameter, a consistent set of nonlinear governing equations for the leading-order dynamics of flows confined to a thin zonal band in Jupiter’s upper troposphere, near the cloud tops. Jupiter’s internal heat source and interactions with the ambient flow may modify the kinetic energy of the GRS but its enstrophy is conserved at leading order. Within the framework of the leading-order dynamics, we show that the state of maximal kinetic energy at a fixed enstrophy for a prescribed area corresponds to a circular vortex and that this energetically optimal state is nonlinearly stable. This provides an energetic benchmark for interpreting the observed rounding trend of the GRS, with velocity and thermal features of the optimizer consistent with recent data. However, the discrepancy between the optimizer’s center-peaked vorticity profile and the observed hollow core shows that the optimizer is not an inevitable terminal state. Interactions with the ambient flow, radiative losses and three-dimensional stratified dynamics are factors that may prevent the GRS from attaining it.

title: A EFETIVIDADE DA LEI DE COTAS NA INCLUSÃO DA PESSOA COM DEFICIÊNCIA NO MERCADO DE TRABALHO FORMAL BRASILEIRO: OS DESAFIOS DA BAIXA ESCOLARIDADE E DA CONTRATAÇÃO PELAS EMPRESAS DE MENOR PORTE
abstract: O presente estudo analisa a efetividade da reserva legal de empregos para pessoas com deficiência no mercado de trabalho formal brasileiro, com ênfase em dois fatores que limitam o alcance da política: a desigualdade educacional e a participação das empresas de menor porte. A pesquisa é bibliográfica e documental, de abordagem qualitativa, com método dedutivo e análise de normas, dados oficiais e decisões da Justiça do Trabalho. O marco central é o art. 93 da Lei nº 8.213/1991, que obriga empresas com 100 ou mais empregados a reservar de 2% a 5% de seus cargos a pessoas com deficiência ou beneficiários reabilitados. Os dados examinados mostram que a política criou um canal relevante de inserção no emprego formal, pois mais de 93% dos vínculos de pessoas com deficiência identificados pelo eSocial em dezembro de 2025 estavam em empresas sujeitas à cota. Ao mesmo tempo, o cumprimento agregado permanece distante da universalidade, e a baixa escolaridade restringe o acesso a ocupações formais: em 2022, 63,3% das pessoas com deficiência de 25 anos ou mais estavam sem instrução ou com o ensino fundamental incompleto. A análise também evidencia que a exclusão das empresas com menos de 100 empregados da obrigação quantitativa reduz o alcance direto da política, embora não as afaste dos deveres de não discriminação e acessibilidade. Conclui-se que os resultados da Lei de Cotas devem ser …

title: Prevalence and Associated Factors of Musculoskeletal Conditions among Market Traders in Obio-Akpor Local Government Area, Rivers State
abstract: Background: Musculoskeletal conditions (MSCs) are an important cause of pain, disability and reduced productivity among informal-sector workers, particularly market traders exposed to prolonged standing, heavy lifting, repetitive movements, and inadequate rest breaks (da Costa & Vieira, 2010; Pega et al., 2021). This study determined the prevalence of MSCs and identified their sociodemographic and occupational determinants among traders in the Rumuokoro and Choba markets in Obio-Akpor Local Government Area, Rivers State, Nigeria. Methods: A descriptive cross-sectional design was employed, and 300 traders were recruited aged 30 years and above with at least six months of trading experience through random sampling across the two markets. Data were collected using structured, interviewer-administered questionnaires that incorporated a modified Nordic Musculoskeletal Questionnaire and sections on sociodemographic characteristics and occupational exposures. Data were analysed using IBM SPSS Version 25, with descriptive statistics, chi-square tests, and binary logistic regression at a 5% significance level. Results: The prevalence of musculoskeletal conditions was 81.7% (n=245), with the lower back (68.6%), knees (52.2%) and shoulders (44.5%) being the most affected regions. Almost half (45.3%) experienced pain daily, and 82.0% reported that pain interfered with their work. Significa…

Cyber-Resilient Dynamic EV Hosting-Capacity Control Against False Data Injection Attacks in Smart Distribution Systems
abstract: Dynamic hosting-capacity control lets electric vehicle (EV) charging stations use the voltage headroom of distribution feeders. Because charging power is set from voltage measurements, a false data injection attack (FDIA) that inflates the reported voltage makes the controller over-allocate power and drives the real voltage below its limit. This paper models the closed loop of measurement, estimation, control and feeder for a 0.6 MW station on the IEEE 33-bus system and proposes a physics-informed defense: a consistency test between the controller’s voltage and a reconstruction built only from protected substation measurements, the station’s revenue meter and load forecasts. For attacks confined to the field-meter set and chosen independently of the measurement noise, invariance to the attack allocation follows by design because the trusted reconstruction has zero gain from those field meters. Under the nominal 10% load pseudo-measurement uncertainty and the protected-meter noise levels used in the case study, the layered detector identifies 70–95% of stealthy 0.0075 p.u. attacks, against 34–66% for conventional residual-based detectors; over 30 simulated days, it cuts daily under-voltage time from about 180 min to 2–8 min for injections of 0.01 p.u. or more. This detection resolution degrades as forecast or protected-anchor uncertainty increases. A supervised neural classifier…

title: Regulatory measures to facilitate the development and registration of paediatric medicines: when market forces fail
abstract: Introduction. Paediatric drug development and registration are more complex than for adults and are rarely profitable. Finding solutions to improve access to paediatric medicines is a pressing global issue. A common approach is to stimulate the pharmaceutical industry with regulatory incentives, although these vary between countries. The World Health Organization is working to harmonise them. Aim. To compare regulatory measures adopted by the European Union (EU), the Eurasian Economic Union (EAEU) and the East African Community (EAC) to facilitate the development and registration of paediatric medicines. Materials and methods. Open-access regulatory databases of the EAEU, the EU and the EAC were searched for documents regulating the medicine registration process. A content analysis was conducted to identify regulatory provisions for paediatric medicines. These were categorised as either regulatory incentives or obligations. Results and discussion. Three documents were selected from the EAC, two from the EU and one from the EAEU. In the EU, 12 measures were identified in the form of incentives and obligations covering the development, registration and market placement stages. In the EAEU, one incentive measure at the registration stage was identified. No paediatric provisions were found in the EAC documents. The EAEU and the EAC may need to assess current mechanisms and expand r…

title: Logistics Service Providers as Compliance Intermediaries: Reallocating Traceability Obligations in Vietnam’s Agro-Forestry Export Supply Chains
abstract: The European Union Deforestation Regulation, applicable from 30 December 2026, shifts the market barrier facing Vietnam’s three leading agro-forestry exports, coffee, rubber and timber and timber products, from product attributes to an obligation of proof grounded in data. Existing scholarship concentrates on smallholders and exporting firms, leaving unanswered the question of who actually creates, holds and transmits traceability data once goods leave the processing plant. Using desk research with a four-tier source-reliability protocol, this study constructs a matrix contrasting statutory responsibility with de facto control over data. The findings reveal a structural misalignment: legal responsibility is concentrated in the EU importer, whereas the data determining compliance resides with collectors and logistics service providers, actors bearing no statutory duty. The study proposes the concept of the compliance intermediary, specifies three conditions for its emergence and four conditions for its effective operation, and cautions that low-risk country status exempts operators only from risk assessment, not from the underlying information requirements.
